[]), 'utf-8');\n      if (patchSize > loadForgeLimits().maxPatchBytes) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Patch size limit exceeded: \"${change.path}\" exceeds the configured per-file patch limit.` };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return { valid: true };\n  }\n\n  private findEditAnchorProblems(\n    changes: FileChangePlan[],\n    contextFiles: { path: string; content: string }[]\n  ): string[] {\n    const sourceByPath = new Map(contextFiles.map((file) => [file.path, file.content]));\n    const problems: string[] = [];\n\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      if (change.action !== 'modify' || !Array.isArray(change.edits) || change.edits.length === 0) continue;\n      const source = sourceByPath.get(change.path);\n      if (typeof source !== 'string') {\n        problems.push(`${change.path}: source content was not supplied to validate the edit anchors.`);\n        continue;\n      }\n      const result = applyExactEdits(source, change.edits);\n      if (!result.ok) {\n        problems.push(`${change.path}: ${result.error}`);\n        continue;\n      }\n      if (!isCodeBalanced(result.content)) {\n        problems.push(`${change.path}: applying the edits leaves unbalanced braces/parentheses (likely a partial or broken anchor).`);\n      }\n    }\n    return problems;\n  }\n\n\n  /**\n   * Deterministically reconstruct the final content of every file the patch\n   * touches, by applying its exact edits to the source snapshot that was supplied\n   * to the model. This is the single source of truth for both the tested worktree\n   * and the committed files, so the two can never diverge.\n   */\n  private async stageFinalContents(\n    changes: FileChangePlan[],\n    contextFiles: { path: string; content: string }[]\n  ): Promise<{ ok: boolean; files: FileChangePlan[]; error?: string }> {\n    const sourceByPath = new Map(contextFiles.map((file) => [file.path, file.content]));\n    const files: FileChangePlan[] = [];\n    const seen = new Set<string>();\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      if (seen.has(change.path)) {\n        return { ok: false, files, error: `Duplicate change for path \"${change.path}\"; refusing ambiguous commit.` };\n      }\n      seen.add(change.path);\n      const hasContent = typeof change.content === 'string' && change.content.length > 0;\n      const hasEdits = Array.isArray(change.edits) && change.edits.length > 0;\n      if (hasContent && !hasEdits) {\n        if (/\\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$/.test(change.path) && !isCodeBalanced(change.content as string)) {\n          return { ok: false, files, error: `Full content for \"${change.path}\" is not syntactically balanced; refusing a broken file.` };\n        }\n        files.push({ ...change, edits: undefined });\n        continue;\n      }\n      if (hasEdits) {\n        const source = sourceByPath.get(change.path);\n        if (typeof source !== 'string') {\n          return { ok: false, files, error: `No supplied source content to apply exact edits for \"${change.path}\".` };\n        }\n        const applied = applyExactEdits(source, change.edits as { find: string; replace: string }[]);\n        if (!applied.ok) {\n          return { ok: false, files, error: `Exact edit rejected in \"${change.path}\": ${applied.error}` };\n        }\n        if (!isCodeBalanced(applied.content)) {\n          return { ok: false, files, error: `Exact edit for \"${change.path}\" leaves unbalanced braces/parentheses; refusing a syntactically broken file.` };\n        }\n        files.push({ ...change, content: applied.content, edits: undefined });\n        continue;\n      }\n      return { ok: false, files, error: `Change for \"${change.path}\" has neither content nor edits.` };\n    }\n    return { ok: true, files };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Write already-staged final file contents into the isolated worktree. Path,\n   * symlink, and escape checks are identical to applyChangesToWorktree so the\n   * committed tree is byte-for-byte the tested tree.\n   */\n  private async applyFinalContentsToWorktree(worktree: string, files: FileChangePlan[]): Promise<void> {\n    for (const change of files) {\n      const portablePath = change.path.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n      const normalizedPath = path.posix.normalize(portablePath).replace(/^(\\.\\/)+/, '');\n      const absolutePath = path.resolve(worktree, normalizedPath);\n      if (!absolutePath.startsWith(worktree + path.sep)) {\n        throw new Error(`Patch path escaped the isolated worktree: ${change.path}`);\n      }\n      await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(absolutePath), { recursive: true });\n      const worktreeRealPath = await fs.realpath(worktree);\n      const parentRealPath = await fs.realpath(path.dirname(absolutePath));\n      if (parentRealPath !== worktreeRealPath && !parentRealPath.startsWith(worktreeRealPath + path.sep)) {\n        throw new Error(`BLOCKED: patch target parent resolves outside the worktree: ${change.path}`);\n      }\n      let targetStat;\n      try { targetStat = await fs.lstat(absolutePath); } catch (err: any) {\n        if (err?.code !== 'ENOENT') throw err;\n      }\n      if (targetStat?.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`BLOCKED: refusing to patch symlink: ${change.path}`);\n      if (targetStat) {\n        const targetRealPath = await fs.realpath(absolutePath);\n        if (targetRealPath !== worktreeRealPath && !targetRealPath.startsWith(worktreeRealPath + path.sep)) {\n          throw new Error(`BLOCKED: patch target resolves outside the worktree: ${change.path}`);\n        }\n      }\n      if (change.action === 'create' && targetStat) throw new Error(`Patch marked existing file as create: ${change.path}`);\n      if (change.action === 'modify' && !targetStat) throw new Error(`Patch marked missing file as modify: ${change.path}`);\n      await fs.writeFile(absolutePath, change.content as string, 'utf-8');\n    }\n  }\n\n  async executeTask(task: TaskDefinition): Promise<TaskExecutionReport> {\n    const report: TaskExecutionReport = {\n      taskId: task.id,\n      status: 'QUEUED',\n      startTime: new Date().toISOString(),\n      baseCommitSha: 'UNKNOWN',\n      modelInvoked: {\n        provider: process.env.FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY === 'true' ? 'keyless router (not yet selected)' : 'not selected',\n        model: 'not-selected',\n        callsCount: 0,\n        fallbackUsed: false,\n        keylessRouteErrors: [],\n      },\n      requirements: [],\n      plannedChanges: [],\n      testResults: [],\n      logs: [],\n    };\n\n    const log = (level: 'info' | 'warn' | 'error', message: string) => {\n      report.logs.push({ timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), level, message });\n    };\n\n    try {\n      // 1. VALIDATING\n      report.status = 'VALIDATING';\n      log('info', `Validating task definition: ${task.id} (${task.title})`);\n\n      if (!task.title || !task.description) {\n        report.status = 'FAILED';\n        report.errorMessage = 'Validation Failed: Task title and description cannot be empty.';\n        log('error', report.errorMessage);\n        return report;\n      }\n\n      const [owner, repo] = task.targetRepo.split('/');\n      if (!owner || !repo) {\n        report.status = 'FAILED';\n        report.errorMessage = `Validation Failed: Invalid target repository format \"${task.targetRepo}\". Expected \"owner/repo\".`;\n        log('error', report.errorMessage);\n        return report;\n      }\n\n      // 2. INSPECTING\n      report.status = 'INSPECTING';\n      log('info', `Inspecting target repository: ${task.targetRepo}`);\n      const repoInfo = await this.github.inspectRepository(owner, repo);\n\n      if (!repoInfo.exists) {\n        report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n        report.blockerReason = `Repository inspection failed: ${repoInfo.errorMessage || 'Repository does not exist'}`;\n        log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n        return report;\n      }\n\n      report.baseCommitSha = repoInfo.latestCommitSha;\n      log('info', `Target repository verified. Base branch: ${repoInfo.defaultBranch}, Base SHA: ${report.baseCommitSha}`);\n\n      // Honor an explicitly requested target branch; fall back to the repository default.\n      const targetBranch = resolveTargetBranch(task.targetBranch, repoInfo.defaultBranch);\n      if (targetBranch !== repoInfo.defaultBranch) {\n        const branchSha = await this.github.fetchBranchHeadSha(owner, repo, targetBranch);\n        if (!branchSha) {\n          report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n          report.blockerReason = `Requested target branch \"${targetBranch}\" could not be resolved in ${owner}/${repo}.`;\n          log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n          return report;\n        }\n        report.baseCommitSha = branchSha;\n        log('info', `Using explicitly requested target branch \"${targetBranch}\" at SHA ${branchSha}.`);\n      }\n\n      // 3. READING PERSISTENT INSTRUCTIONS & TARGET CODE SCOPE\n      log('info', 'Checking for persistent instructions in AGENTS.md');\n      const agentsMdRemote = await this.github.fetchFile(owner, repo, 'AGENTS.md', targetBranch);\n      let instructionText = '';\n      if (agentsMdRemote) {\n        instructionText = agentsMdRemote.content;\n        log('info', 'Loaded remote AGENTS.md instructions.');\n      } else {\n        try {\n          instructionText = await fs.readFile(path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'AGENTS.md'), 'utf-8');\n          log('info', 'Loaded local AGENTS.md instructions.');\n        } catch {\n          instructionText = 'Standard engineering instructions: inspect before editing, keep changes minimal.';\n        }\n      }\n\n      // Read target repository file inventory\n      log('info', 'Gathering repository file inventory for grounding');\n      const repoFilePaths = await this.github.listRepositoryFiles(owner, repo, targetBranch);\n      log('info', `Found ${repoFilePaths.length} files in target repository tree.`);\n\n      // Read the target repository's package manifest and bounded real source files.\n      const packageJsonRemote = await this.github.fetchFile(owner, repo, 'package.json', targetBranch);\n      const packageJsonContent = packageJsonRemote?.content || '{}';\n      const taskText = `${task.title} ${task.description}`;\n      const taskTerms = taskText\n        .toLowerCase()\n        .split(/[^a-z0-9]+/)\n        .filter((term) => term.length > 2);\n      const explicitPaths = Array.from(\n        taskText.matchAll(/((?:src|scripts|\\.github|docs)\\/[\\w./-]+\\.(?:ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|json|md|yml|yaml))/g),\n        (match) => match[1]\n      ).filter((candidate, index, all) => all.indexOf(candidate) === index && repoFilePaths.includes(candidate))\n        .filter((candidate) => !isForbiddenReference(taskText, candidate));\n      const eligibleSourcePaths = repoFilePaths\n        .filter((p) => /\\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|json|md)$/.test(p))\n        .filter((p) => !p.startsWith('node_modules/') && !p.startsWith('dist/') && !p.startsWith('.git/'))\n        .filter((p) => p !== 'package.json' && p !== 'AGENTS.md');\n      // Exact user-named paths are authoritative. For inferred context, skip oversized files\n      // and continue searching so an unrelated large file cannot block the whole mission.\n      const sourceCandidates = (explicitPaths.length > 0 ? explicitPaths.slice(0, 5) : eligibleSourcePaths\n        .sort((a, b) => {\n          const score = (candidate: string) => {\n            const lower = candidate.toLowerCase();\n            return taskTerms.reduce((total, term) => total + (lower.includes(term) ? 1 : 0), 0);\n          };\n          return score(b) - score(a) || a.localeCompare(b);\n        }));\n      const targetSourceFiles: { path: string; content: string }[] = [];\n      for (const candidate of sourceCandidates) {\n        if (targetSourceFiles.length >= 5) break;\n        const file = await this.github.fetchFile(owner, repo, candidate, targetBranch);\n        if (!file) {\n          log('warn', `Could not fetch candidate source file; skipping: ${candidate}`);\n          continue;\n        }\n        if (file.content.length > 16000) {\n          const reason = `source file exceeds 16000 characters: ${file.path}`;\n          if (explicitPaths.length > 0) {\n            report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n            report.blockerReason = `Explicitly requested ${reason}; refusing to guess or patch an incomplete context.`;\n            log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n            return report;\n          }\n          log('warn', `Skipping inferred ${reason} and continuing source selection.`);\n          continue;\n        }\n        const contextChars = targetSourceFiles.reduce((total, source) => total + source.content.length, 0);\n        if (contextChars + file.content.length > MAX_SOURCE_CONTEXT_CHARS) {\n          const reason = `adding ${file.path} would exceed the ${MAX_SOURCE_CONTEXT_CHARS}-character total source-context budget`;\n          if (explicitPaths.length > 0) {\n            report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n            report.blockerReason = `Explicit source context is too large: ${reason}.`;\n            log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n            return report;\n          }\n          log('warn', `Skipping inferred source file because ${reason}.`);\n          continue;\n        }\n        targetSourceFiles.push({ path: file.path, content: file.content });\n      }\n      if (targetSourceFiles.length === 0) {\n        report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n        report.blockerReason = explicitPaths.length > 0\n          ? 'None of the explicitly requested source files could be safely loaded.'\n          : 'No eligible source files under the 16000-character context limit could be loaded.';\n        log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n        return report;\n      }\n\n      // 4. PLANNING (MODEL INVOCATION)\n      report.status = 'PLANNING';\n      log('info', `Invoking model with target manifest and ${targetSourceFiles.length} actual target source files.`);\n\n      const contextFiles = [\n        { path: 'AGENTS.md', content: instructionText },\n        { path: 'package.json', content: packageJsonContent },\n        { path: 'FILE_TREE_INVENTORY.txt', content: repoFilePaths.slice(0, 100).join('\\n') },\n        ...targetSourceFiles,\n      ];\n\n      const maxModelCalls = loadForgeLimits().maxModelCalls;\n      const maxRepairs = loadForgeLimits().maxRepairAttempts;\n      const guardModelCall = (label: string): boolean => {\n        if (report.modelInvoked.callsCount >= maxModelCalls) {\n          report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n          report.blockerReason = `Model-call ceiling reached (${maxModelCalls}); stopping safely before ${label}.`;\n          log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n          return false;\n        }\n        return true;\n      };\n      const recordModel = (result: { provider: string; model: string; fallbackUsed?: boolean; keylessRouteErrors?: string[] }) => {\n        report.modelInvoked.provider = result.provider;\n        report.modelInvoked.model = result.model;\n        report.modelInvoked.fallbackUsed = result.fallbackUsed ?? false;\n        report.modelInvoked.keylessRouteErrors = [\n          ...(report.modelInvoked.keylessRouteErrors ?? []),\n          ...(result.keylessRouteErrors ?? []),\n        ];\n      };\n      const focusContext = (requiredPath: string) =>\n        contextFiles.filter((file) =>\n          file.path === requiredPath || file.path === 'AGENTS.md' || file.path === 'package.json' || file.path === 'FILE_TREE_INVENTORY.txt'\n        );\n      // The context handed to the model must reflect edits already made this mission,\n      // exactly like a developer reading the file after their last change. Without\n      // this, a later file is written against a stale snapshot of its dependencies.\n      const stagedByPath = new Map<string, string>();\n      const stageOne = async (change: FileChangePlan): Promise<void> => {\n        const result = await this.stageFinalContents([change], contextFiles);\n        if (result.ok && result.files[0] && typeof result.files[0].content === 'string') {\n          stagedByPath.set(change.path, result.files[0].content);\n        }\n      };\n      const evolvingContext = (requiredPath: string) =>\n        focusContext(requiredPath).map((file) =>\n          stagedByPath.has(file.path) ? { ...file, content: stagedByPath.get(file.path) as string } : file\n        );\n\n      // 4. PLANNING — PER-FILE BOUNDED EXECUTION\n      // Forge works the way a careful engineer does: capture the requirements once,\n      // then implement one required file per model call so no single output must fit\n      // the whole mission inside the anonymous endpoint's small output ceiling.\n      report.modelInvoked.callsCount += 1;\n      let modelResult = await this.model.generatePlanAndPatch(\n        `Task: ${task.title}\\nDetails: ${task.description}`,\n        contextFiles,\n        { tier: 'free' }\n      );\n      if (!modelResult.success && classifyFailure(modelResult.error) === 'RETRYABLE') {\n        log('warn', `Model route reported a retryable failure; one bounded retry. Detail: ${modelResult.error}`);\n        const retry = await withBoundedRetry(\n          () => this.model.generatePlanAndPatch(`Task: ${task.title}\\nDetails: ${task.description}`, contextFiles, { tier: 'free' }),\n          { attempts: loadForgeLimits().modelAttempts, baseDelayMs: 500 }\n        );\n        report.modelInvoked.callsCount += retry.attempts;\n        if (retry.ok) modelResult = retry.value;\n      }\n      recordModel(modelResult);\n      if (!modelResult.success) {\n        report.status = 'FAILED';\n        report.errorMessage = `Model Generation Failed: ${modelResult.error}`;\n        log('error', report.errorMessage);\n        return report;\n      }\n\n      // The bootstrap plan may come back truncated or malformed on a small-output\n      // endpoint. Retry a bounded number of times, then fall back to implementing\n      // the explicitly named files directly so planning cannot abort the mission\n      // before the per-file engine ever runs.\n      const planAttempts = loadForgeLimits().modelAttempts + 2;\n      let bootShape: ReturnType<typeof validateModelPlanShape> | undefined;\n      for (let planAttempt = 0; planAttempt < planAttempts; planAttempt += 1) {\n        if (planAttempt > 0) {\n          if (!guardModelCall(`planning retry ${planAttempt + 1}/${planAttempts}`)) return report;\n          report.modelInvoked.callsCount += 1;\n          modelResult = await this.model.generatePlanAndPatch(\n            `Task: ${task.title}\\nDetails: ${task.description}\\n\\nReturn a compact JSON plan with a \"requirements\" array (each with id, description, acceptanceCriteria using an existing repo check such as \"npm run lint\" or \"npm test\") and a \"changes\" array (may be empty; the implementation will be produced per file afterwards). Keep the JSON small and complete.`,\n            contextFiles\n          );\n          recordModel(modelResult);\n          if (!modelResult.success) continue;\n        }\n        try {\n          bootShape = validateModelPlanShape(parseModelJson(modelResult.text));\n        } catch (err: any) {\n          log('warn', `Bootstrap plan attempt ${planAttempt + 1} was not valid JSON (${err.message}); retrying if budget remains.`);\n          bootShape = undefined;\n        }\n        if (bootShape?.ok && bootShape.requirements.length > 0) break;\n        bootShape = undefined;\n      }\n      const fallbackPaths = explicitPaths.filter((p) => !p.endsWith('.md') && !p.endsWith('.json'));\n      if (!bootShape || !bootShape.ok) {\n        if (fallbackPaths.length === 0) {\n          report.status = 'FAILED';\n          report.errorMessage = 'Bootstrap planning produced no valid requirements and no explicit files to fall back to.';\n          log('error', report.errorMessage);\n          return report;\n        }\n        log('warn', 'Bootstrap planning exhausted its bounded retries; falling back to per-file implementation of the explicitly named files.');\n        report.requirements = fallbackPaths.map((p, index) => ({\n          id: `REQ-${index + 1}`,\n          description: `Implement the requested change in ${p}.`,\n          acceptanceCriteria: 'npm run lint',\n          status: 'PENDING' as const,\n        }));\n      } else {\n        report.requirements = bootShape.requirements.map((req) => ({ ...req, status: 'PENDING' as const }));\n        report.plannedChanges = bootShape.changes;\n      }\n      if (!bootShape || !bootShape.ok) report.plannedChanges = [];\n\n      // Drop any change whose exact anchors do not validate against the supplied\n      // source so the file can be re-implemented cleanly in the per-file loop.\n      const bootAnchorProblems = new Set(\n        this.findEditAnchorProblems(report.plannedChanges, contextFiles).map((problem) => problem.split(':')[0])\n      );\n      if (bootAnchorProblems.size > 0) {\n        log('warn', `Dropping ${bootAnchorProblems.size} change(s) with invalid anchors for per-file re-implementation.`);\n        report.plannedChanges = report.plannedChanges.filter((change) => !bootAnchorProblems.has(change.path));\n      }\n      for (const change of report.plannedChanges) {\n        await stageOne(change);\n      }\n\n      // 4b. PER-FILE COMPLETION — one bounded, retried model call per required file.\n      const filesToImplement = [...explicitPaths.filter((p) => !p.endsWith('.md') && !p.endsWith('.json'))]\n        .sort((a, b) => (a.endsWith('/types.ts') || a.endsWith('types.ts') ? -1 : 0) - (b.endsWith('/types.ts') || b.endsWith('types.ts') ? -1 : 0));\n      for (const requiredPath of filesToImplement) {\n        if (report.plannedChanges.some((change) => change.path === requiredPath)) continue;\n        if (!guardModelCall(`implementation of ${requiredPath}`)) return report;\n        let added = false;\n        let lastProblem = 'model produced no change for this file';\n        for (let fileAttempt = 0; fileAttempt < maxRepairs && !added; fileAttempt += 1) {\n          // On the last attempt, allow a complete rewrite of this one file. The action MUST be \"modify\" and MUST use exact-anchor \"edits\" copied verbatim from the supplied source; never return whole-file content for an existing file. Every find string must occur exactly once. Do not modify any other file. Keep the edit minimal and syntactically complete.`;\n          const crossModuleHint = ` If you need data owned by another class, add or use a PUBLIC method on that class (and change that file in its own step); never read a private member from another module.`;\n          report.modelInvoked.callsCount += 1;\n          const attemptNote = fileAttempt === 0\n            ? ''\n            : `\\n\\nPREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED: ${lastProblem}. Fix that specific problem and return valid JSON.`;\n          const fileResult = await this.model.generatePlanAndPatch(\n            `${task.title}\\nDetails: ${task.description}\\n\\nIMPLEMENT FILE ${requiredPath} (attempt ${fileAttempt + 1}/${maxRepairs}). ${editInstruction}${crossModuleHint} The supplied source already includes every change made earlier in this mission, so implement this file against the current version shown.${attemptNote}`,\n            evolvingContext(requiredPath)\n          );\n          recordModel(fileResult);\n          if (!fileResult.success) {\n            lastProblem = `model call failed: ${fileResult.error}`;\n            continue;\n          }\n          let filePlan: any;\n          try {\n            filePlan = parseModelJson(fileResult.text);\n          } catch (err: any) {\n            lastProblem = `invalid JSON: ${err.message}`;\n            continue;\n          }\n          const fileShape = validateModelPlanShape(filePlan);\n          if (!fileShape.ok) {\n            lastProblem = `plan shape rejected: ${fileShape.error}`;\n            continue;\n          }\n          let candidate = fileShape.changes.find((change) => change.path === requiredPath);\n          if (!candidate) {\n            lastProblem = `no change for ${requiredPath}`;\n            continue;\n          }\n          if (rewriteMode && !(typeof candidate.content === 'string' && candidate.content.length > 0)) {\n            lastProblem = 'rewrite attempt did not include full file content';\n            continue;\n          }\n          if (rewriteMode) {\n            candidate = { ...candidate, action: 'modify', edits: undefined };\n            const rewriteStage = await this.stageFinalContents([{ ...candidate, path: requiredPath }], contextFiles);\n            if (!rewriteStage.ok || !rewriteStage.files[0]) {\n              lastProblem = `rewrite rejected: ${rewriteStage.error ?? 'unknown'}`;\n              continue;\n            }\n            candidate = rewriteStage.files[0];\n          }\n          const candidateAnchors = rewriteMode ? [] : this.findEditAnchorProblems([candidate], contextFiles);\n          if (candidateAnchors.length > 0) {\n            lastProblem = `invalid anchors: ${candidateAnchors.slice(0, 3).join(' | ')}`;\n            continue;\n          }\n          const merged = [...report.plannedChanges, candidate];\n          const mergedValidation = this.validatePatch(merged);\n          if (!mergedValidation.valid) {\n            lastProblem = `patch rejected: ${mergedValidation.error}`;\n            continue;\n          }\n          report.plannedChanges = merged;\n          stagedByPath.set(requiredPath, candidate.content as string);\n          added = true;\n        }\n        if (!added) {\n          report.status = 'FAILED';\n          report.errorMessage = `Could not implement required file ${requiredPath} after ${maxRepairs} attempt(s): ${lastProblem}`;\n          log('error', report.errorMessage);\n          return report;\n        }\n        log('info', `Implemented required file ${requiredPath}.`);\n      }\n\n      log('info', `Requirements matrix established with ${report.requirements.length} criteria.`);\n\n      // 5. PATCH VALIDATION (Fix AUD-20261012-02 Patch Validation)\n      const patchValidation = this.validatePatch(report.plannedChanges);\n      if (!patchValidation.valid) {\n        report.status = 'FAILED';\n        report.errorMessage = `Patch Validation Rejected: ${patchValidation.error}`;\n        log('error', report.errorMessage);\n        return report;\n      }\n      log('info', `Patch validated successfully: ${report.plannedChanges.length} files pass security checks.`);\n\n      // 5b. IMPLEMENTATION COVERAGE (prevents a false PASS)\n      // A patch that only edits a strict subset of the files the task explicitly\n      // requires is bounded/incomplete. Evidence must never authorize it, so we\n      // fail closed and name the untouched files instead of reporting success.\n      const requiredEditPaths = explicitPaths.filter((p) => !p.endsWith('.md') && !p.endsWith('.json'));\n      const changedPaths = new Set(report.plannedChanges.map((c) => c.path));\n      const untouchedRequired = requiredEditPaths.filter((p) => !changedPaths.has(p));\n      if (untouchedRequired.length > 0) {\n        report.status = 'FAILED';\n        report.errorMessage = `Incomplete implementation: the task explicitly requires changes to ${untouchedRequired.join(', ')} but the patch does not modify them.`;\n        log('error', report.errorMessage);\n        return report;\n      }\n      log('info', `Implementation coverage confirmed for ${requiredEditPaths.length} explicitly required file(s).`);\n\n      // 5c. Treating it as one made Forge hard-block on unrelated size limits.\nexport function isForbiddenReference(taskText: string, candidate: string): boolean {\n  const idx = taskText.indexOf(candidate);\n  if (idx < 0) return false;\n  const window = taskText.slice(Math.max(0, idx - 60), idx + candidate.length + 40).toLowerCase();\n  const prefix = /(do not modify|don't modify|do not change|do not touch|must not (modify|change|touch)|without (modifying|changing|touching))\\s*$/.test(\n    taskText.slice(Math.max(0, idx - 60), idx).toLowerCase()\n  );\n  const wrapped = /(leave|keep|hold)[\\s\\S]{0,60}?(untouched|unchanged|intact|as-is|as is)/.test(window);\n  return prefix || wrapped;\n}\n\n// --- R6 resilience primitives -------------------------------------------------\n\nexport type FailureClass = 'RETRYABLE' | 'FATAL';\n\n/**\n * Classify a runtime failure so callers can retry transient conditions and stop\n * on permanent ones. ((ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms)));\n  const retryable = options.isRetryable ?? ((error: unknown) => classifyFailure(error) === 'RETRYABLE');\n\n  let lastError: unknown;\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1) {\n    try {\n      return { ok: true, value: await operation(), attempts: attempt };\n    } catch (error) {\n      lastError = error;\n      if (attempt >= attempts || !retryable(error)) {\n        return { ok: false, error, attempts: attempt };\n      }\n      const delay = Math.min(max, base * 2 ** (attempt - 1));\n      await sleep(delay);\n    }\n  }\n  return { ok: false, error: lastError, attempts };\n}\n\nexport interface ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  ok: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  requirements: { id: string; description: string; acceptanceCriteria: string; checkCommands?: string[]; manualReviewNote?: string }[];\n  changes: FileChangePlan[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Deterministically validate and normalize a raw model plan. Malformed shapes\n * are reported as structured errors instead of throwing deep in the mapper, so\n * a single bad field cannot silently corrupt the report.\n */\nexport function validateModelPlanShape(raw: unknown): ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  const empty: ModelPlanShapeCheck = { ok: true, requirements: [], changes: [] };\n  if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object') {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan was not a JSON object.' };\n  }\n  const plan = raw as Record<string, unknown>;\n\n  if (plan.requirements !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.requirements)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"requirements\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n  if (plan.changes !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.changes)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"changes\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n\n  const requirements = (plan.requirements ?? []).map((req, index) => {\n    const item = (req ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return {\n      id: typeof item.id === 'string' && item.id ? item.id : `REQ-${index + 1}`,\n      description: typeof item.description === 'string' ? item.description : '',\n      acceptanceCriteria: typeof item.acceptanceCriteria === 'string' ? item.acceptanceCriteria : '',\n      checkCommands: Array.isArray(item.checkCommands)\n        ? item.checkCommands.filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string' && c.trim().length > 0)\n        : undefined,\n      manualReviewNote: typeof item.manualReviewNote === 'string' ? item.manualReviewNote : undefined,\n    };\n  });\n\n  const changes: FileChangePlan[] = [];\n  for (const change of (plan.changes ?? []) as unknown[]) {\n    const item = (change ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    if (typeof item.path !== 'string' || item.path.length === 0) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'A change is missing a \"path\".' };\n    }\n    if (!['create', 'modify', 'delete'].includes(String(item.action))) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has an invalid action \"${String(item.action)}\".` };\n    }\n    if (item.edits !== undefined && !Array.isArray(item.edits)) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has non-array edits.` };\n    }\n    changes.push({\n      path: item.path,\n      action: item.action as FileChangePlan['action'],\n      rationale: typeof item.rationale === 'string' ? item.rationale : '',\n      content: typeof item.content === 'string' ? item.content : undefined,\n      edits: Array.isArray(item.edits)\n        ? Merge same-path, same-action entries deterministically so a\n  // legitimate multi-edit plan is not rejected as ambiguous, while a genuine\n  // action conflict still fails closed.\n  const mergedByPath = new Map<string, FileChangePlan>();\n  for (const change of changes) {\n    const existing = mergedByPath.get(change.path);\n    if (!existing) {\n      mergedByPath.set(change.path, change);\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (existing.action !== change.action) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${change.path}\" has conflicting actions \"${existing.action}\" and \"${change.action}\".` };\n    }\n    if (typeof existing.content === 'string' && typeof change.content === 'string' && existing.content !== change.content) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${change.path}\" supplies two different full contents.` };\n    }\n    const mergedEdits = [...(existing.edits ?? []), ...(change.edits ?? [])];\n    mergedByPath.set(change.path, {\n      ...existing,\n      content: existing.content ?? change.content,\n      edits: mergedEdits.length > 0 ? mergedEdits : undefined,\n    });\n  }\n\n  return { ok: true, requirements, changes: [...mergedByPath.values()] };\n}\n\n// Requested branch wins only when it is explicit and not the default; invalid\n// branches are resolved later (and fail closed) by the caller.\nexport function resolveTargetBranch(requested: string | undefined, defaultBranch: string): string {\n  const trimmed = requested?.trim();\n  return trimmed && trimmed !== defaultBranch ? trimmed : defaultBranch;\n}\n\n// A requirement is only PASS when a check named in its own acceptance criteria,\n// description, or explicit checkCommands actually passed. Unrelated green checks\n// cannot satisfy it, and a named-but-failing check yields FAIL, never PASS.\nexport function evaluateRequirementEvidence(\n  requirement: RequirementEvidenceInput,\n  results: { command: string; status: string; exitCode: number }[]\n): { status: 'PASS' | 'PENDING' | 'FAIL'; evidence: string } {\n  const attemptEvidence = results.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ');\n  const criterion = `${requirement.acceptanceCriteria ?? ''} ${requirement.description ?? Latest target-check attempt: ${attemptEvidence}.${manual}`,\n  };\n}\n\nexport class ForgeAgent {\n  private github: GitHubService;\n  private model: ModelService;\n  private testRunner: TestRunnerService;\n  private githubToken?: string;\n\n  constructor(githubToken?: string) {\n    this.githubToken = githubToken?.trim();\n    this.github = new GitHubService(githubToken);\n    this.model = new ModelService();\n    this.testRunner = new TestRunnerService();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Strict validation of generated patch paths and contents (Fixes AUD-20261012-02 Patch Validation)\n   */\n  private validatePatch(changes: FileChangePlan[]): { valid: boolean; error?: string } {\n    const limits = loadForgeLimits();\n    if (!Array.isArray(changes) || changes.length === 0) {\n      return { valid: false, error: 'Empty patch: No file changes proposed.' };\n    }\n    if (changes.length > limits.maxFilesPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured file ceiling: ${changes.length} > ${limits.maxFilesPerMission}.` };\n    }\n    const totalEdits = changes.reduce((sum, change) => sum + (Array.isArray(change.edits) ? change.edits.length : 0), 0);\n    if (totalEdits > limits.maxEditsPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured edit ceiling: ${totalEdits} > ${limits.maxEditsPerMission}.` };\n    }\n\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      // 1. Path format validation (must be relative, no traversal)\n      if (!change.path || typeof change.path !== 'string') {\n        return { valid: false, error: 'Malformed patch: Missing or non-string file path.' };\n      }\n      const portablePath = change.path.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n      const normalizedPath = path.posix.normalize(portablePath).replace(/^(\\.\\/)+/, '');\n      if (path.isAbsolute(change.path) || portablePath.startsWith('/') || normalizedPath === '..' || normalizedPath.startsWith('../') || normalizedPath.includes('/../')) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Security Boundary Violation: Directory traversal or absolute path detected: \"${change.path}\".` };\n      }\n\n      // 2. Path,\n   * symlink, and escape checks are identical to applyChangesToWorktree so the\n   * committed tree is byte-for-byte the tested tree.\n   */\n  private async applyFinalContentsToWorktree(worktree: string, files: FileChangePlan[]): Promise<void> {\n    for (const change of files) {\n      const portablePath = change.path.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n      const normalizedPath = path.posix.normalize(portablePath).replace(/^(\\.\\/)+/, '');\n      const absolutePath = path.resolve(worktree, normalizedPath);\n      if (!absolutePath.startsWith(worktree + path.sep)) {\n        throw new Error(`Patch path escaped the isolated worktree: ${change.path}`);\n      }\n      await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(absolutePath), { recursive: true });\n      const worktreeRealPath = await fs.realpath(worktree);\n      const parentRealPath = await fs.realpath(path.dirname(absolutePath));\n      if (parentRealPath !== worktreeRealPath && !parentRealPath.startsWith(worktreeRealPath + path.sep)) {\n        throw new Error(`BLOCKED: patch target parent resolves outside the worktree: ${change.path}`);\n      }\n      let targetStat;\n      try { targetStat = await fs.lstat(absolutePath); VALIDATING\n      report.status = 'VALIDATING';\n      log('info', `Validating task definition: ${task.id} (${task.title})`);\n\n      if (!task.title || !task.description) {\n        report.status = 'FAILED';\n        report.errorMessage = 'Validation Failed: Task title and description cannot be empty.';\n        log('error', report.errorMessage);\n        return report;\n      }\n\n      const [owner, repo] = task.targetRepo.split('/');\n      if (!owner || !repo) {\n        report.status = 'FAILED';\n        report.errorMessage = `Validation Failed: Invalid target repository format \"${task.targetRepo}\". For inferred context, skip oversized files\n      // and continue searching so an unrelated large file cannot block the whole mission.\n      const sourceCandidates = (explicitPaths.length > 0 ? explicitPaths.slice(0, 5) : eligibleSourcePaths\n        .sort((a, b) => {\n          const score = (candidate: string) => {\n            const lower = candidate.toLowerCase();\n            return taskTerms.reduce((total, term) => total + (lower.includes(term) ? 1 : 0), 0);\n          };\n          return score(b) - score(a) || a.localeCompare(b);\n        }));\n      const targetSourceFiles: { path: string; content: string }[] = [];\n      for (const candidate of sourceCandidates) {\n        if (targetSourceFiles.length >= 5) break;\n        const file = await this.github.fetchFile(owner, repo, candidate, targetBranch);\n        if (!file) {\n          log('warn', `Could not fetch candidate source file; skipping: ${candidate}`);\n          continue;\n        }\n        if (file.content.length > 16000) {\n          const reason = `source file exceeds 16000 characters: ${file.path}`;\n          if (explicitPaths.length > 0) {\n            report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n            report.blockerReason = `Explicitly requested ${reason}; refusing to guess or patch an incomplete context.`;\n            log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n            return report;\n          }\n          log('warn', `Skipping inferred ${reason} and continuing source selection.`);\n          continue;\n        }\n        const contextChars = targetSourceFiles.reduce((total, source) => total + source.content.length, 0);\n        if (contextChars + file.content.length > MAX_SOURCE_CONTEXT_CHARS) {\n          const reason = `adding ${file.path} would exceed the ${MAX_SOURCE_CONTEXT_CHARS}-character total source-context budget`;\n          if (explicitPaths.length > 0) {\n            report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n            report.blockerReason = `Explicit source context is too large: ${reason}.`;\n            log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n            return report;\n          }\n          log('warn', `Skipping inferred source file because ${reason}.`);\n          continue;\n        }\n        targetSourceFiles.push({ path: file.path, content: file.content });\n      }\n      if (targetSourceFiles.length === 0) {\n        report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n        report.blockerReason = explicitPaths.length > 0\n          ? []), ...(change.edits ?? Latest target-check attempt: ${attemptEvidence}.${manual}`,\n  };\n}\n\nexport class ForgeAgent {\n  private github: GitHubService;\n  private model: ModelService;\n  private testRunner: TestRunnerService;\n  private githubToken?: string;\n\n  constructor(githubToken?: string) {\n    this.githubToken = githubToken?.trim();\n    this.github = new GitHubService(githubToken);\n    this.model = new ModelService();\n    this.testRunner = new TestRunnerService();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Strict validation of generated patch paths and contents (Fixes AUD-20261012-02 Patch Validation)\n   */\n  private validatePatch(changes: FileChangePlan[]): { valid: boolean; error?: string } {\n    const limits = loadForgeLimits();\n    if (!Array.isArray(changes) || changes.length === 0) {\n      return { valid: false, error: 'Empty patch: No file changes proposed.' };\n    }\n    if (changes.length > limits.maxFilesPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured file ceiling: ${changes.length} > ${limits.maxFilesPerMission}.` };\n    }\n    const totalEdits = changes.reduce((sum, change) => sum + (Array.isArray(change.edits) ? change.edits.length : 0), 0);\n    if (totalEdits > limits.maxEditsPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured edit ceiling: ${totalEdits} > ${limits.maxEditsPerMission}.` };\n    }\n\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      // 1. Path,\n   * symlink, and escape checks are identical to applyChangesToWorktree so the\n   * committed tree is byte-for-byte the tested tree.\n   */\n  private async applyFinalContentsToWorktree(worktree: string, files: FileChangePlan[]): Promise<void> {\n    for (const change of files) {\n      const portablePath = change.path.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n      const normalizedPath = path.posix.normalize(portablePath).replace(/^(\\.\\/)+/, '');\n      const absolutePath = path.resolve(worktree, normalizedPath);\n      if (!absolutePath.startsWith(worktree + path.sep)) {\n        throw new Error(`Patch path escaped the isolated worktree: ${change.path}`);\n      }\n      await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(absolutePath), { recursive: true });\n      const worktreeRealPath = await fs.realpath(worktree);\n      const parentRealPath = await fs.realpath(path.dirname(absolutePath));\n      if (parentRealPath !== worktreeRealPath && !parentRealPath.startsWith(worktreeRealPath + path.sep)) {\n        throw new Error(`BLOCKED: patch target parent resolves outside the worktree: ${change.path}`);\n      }\n      let targetStat;\n      try { targetStat = await fs.lstat(absolutePath); INSPECTING\n      report.status = 'INSPECTING';\n      log('info', `Inspecting target repository: ${task.targetRepo}`);\n      const repoInfo = await this.github.inspectRepository(owner, repo);\n\n      if (!repoInfo.exists) {\n        report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n        report.blockerReason = `Repository inspection failed: ${repoInfo.errorMessage || 'Repository does not exist'}`;\n        log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n        return report;\n      }\n\n      report.baseCommitSha = repoInfo.latestCommitSha;\n      log('info', `Target repository verified. []),\n          ...(result.keylessRouteErrors ?? assert.equal(shape.requirements[0].id, 'REQ-1');\n  assert.equal(shape.changes[0].path, 'src/a.ts');\n});\n\ntest('validateModelPlanShape: rejects a non-object plan', () => {\n  const shape = validateModelPlanShape('not json');\n  assert.equal(shape.ok, false);\n});\n\ntest('validateModelPlanShape: rejects malformed model output deterministically', () => {\n  assert.equal(validateModelPlanShape({ requirements: 'nope' }).ok, false);\n  assert.equal(validateModelPlanShape({ changes: [{ action: 'modify' }] }).ok, false);\n  assert.equal(validateModelPlanShape({ changes: [{ path: 'a', action: 'destroy' }] }).ok, false);\n  assert.equal(validateModelPlanShape({ changes: [{ path: 'a', action: 'modify', edits: 'x' }] }).ok, false);\n});\n\ntest('loadForgeLimits: every ceiling is bounded and env-overridable', () => {\n  const defaults = loadForgeLimits({} as NodeJS.ProcessEnv);\n  assert.ok(defaults.maxModelCalls >= 1 && defaults.maxFilesPerMission >= 1 && defaults.maxRuntimeMs >= 10_000);\n  const raised = loadForgeLimits({ FORGE_MAX_MODEL_CALLS: '12' } as NodeJS.ProcessEnv);\n  assert.equal(raised.maxModelCalls, 12);\n  const clamped = loadForgeLimits({ FORGE_MAX_MODEL_CALLS: '9999' } as NodeJS.ProcessEnv);\n  assert.equal(clamped.maxModelCalls, 50);\n});\n\ntest('free-tier routing: keyless providers are provably key-free, keyed providers are not', async () => {\n  const freelm = await import('freelm');\n  const keyless = freelm.KEYLESS.map((K) => new K());\n  assert.ok(keyless.length > 0, 'expected at least one keyless provider');\n  for (const provider of keyless) {\n    assert.equal(\n      (provider.constructor as { keyless: boolean }).keyless,\n      true,\n      `${provider.name} must be keyless so a free-tier call cannot spend a key`\n    );\n  }\n  const groq = freelm.PROVIDER_ENV.find((spec) => spec.name === 'groq');\n  assert.ok(groq, 'expected a groq provider spec');\n  const keyed = freelm.buildProvider(groq, ['dummy-key']);\n  assert.equal((keyed.constructor as { keyless: boolean }).keyless, false, 'a keyed provider must not be keyless');\n});\n",

err.message : String(err)}`);\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nconst KEYLESS_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES = [\n  'GEMINI_API_KEY', 'GOOGLE_API_KEY', 'GROQ_API_KEY', 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY',\n  'CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN', 'CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID', 'ZAI_API_KEY', 'COHERE_API_KEY',\n  'CO_API_KEY', 'CEREBRAS_API_KEY', 'MISTRAL_API_KEY', 'NVIDIA_API_KEY', 'NIM_API_KEY',\n  'KILO_API_KEY', 'FREELM_GOOGLE_KEYS', 'FREELM_GROQ_KEYS', 'FREELM_OPENROUTER_KEYS',\n  'FREELM_CLOUDFLARE_KEYS', 'FREELM_ZAI_KEYS', 'FREELM_COHERE_KEYS',\n  'FREELM_CEREBRAS_KEYS', 'FREELM_MISTRAL_KEYS', 'FREELM_NIM_KEYS', 'FREELM_KILO_KEYS',\n];\n\nexport class ModelService {\n  private readonly gemini: GoogleGenAI | null;\n  private readonly geminiConfigured: boolean;\n\n  constructor() {\n    if (process.env.FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY === 'true') {\n      for (const name of KEYLESS_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES) delete process.env[name];\n      process.env.FREELM_KEYLESS = '1';\n    }\n    const key = process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY?.trim();\n    this.geminiConfigured = Boolean(key && key !== 'MY_GEMINI_API_KEY');\n    this.gemini = this.geminiConfigured ? new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: key }) : null;\n  }\n\n  isConfigured(): boolean {\n    // The primary public gateway is keyless; actual availability is established per request.\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  getProviderInfo() {\n    return {\n      primaryProvider: 'freelm multi-provider free-tier router with keyless Kilo and OVHcloud fallback',\n      primaryModel: 'chat',\n      primaryRequiresApiKey: false,\n      fallbackProvider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini',\n      fallbackModel: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n      fallbackConfigured: this.geminiConfigured && process.env.FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY !== 'true',\n      costStatus: process.env.FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY === 'true'\n        ? 'Strict keyless-only mode: provider credentials are removed and Gemini fallback is disabled.'\n        : 'freelm prefers configured free-tier providers and can fall back to anonymous keyless endpoints; Gemini fallback is optional.',\n    };\n  }\n\n  async generatePlanAndPatch(\n    prompt: string,\n    contextFiles: { path: string; content: string }[],\n    options: ModelGenerationOptions = {},\n  ): Promise<ModelGenerationResult> {\n    // Calls that do not name a tier default to 'hard'; set FORGE_DEFAULT_TIER=free\n    // to make every unspecified call try the no-signup endpoints first.\n    const tier: TaskTier = options.tier ?? (process.env.FORGE_DEFAULT_TIER === 'free' ? 'free' : 'hard');\n    const fileContexts = contextFiles\n      .map((f) => `--- FILE: ${f.path} ---\\n${f.content}\\n--- END FILE ---`)\n      .join('\\n\\n');\n\n    const fullPrompt = `You are Forge, the precise coding and audit agent for Firstborn.\nFollow these rules:\n- Inspect the supplied target-repository files; never pretend to have inspected files not supplied.\n- Number requirements and give testable acceptance criteria before proposing edits.\n- Make the smallest bounded changes. For existing files, action MUST be \"modify\" and MUST use \"edits\"; never return the whole file in \"content\" unless explicitly asked for a full rewrite. What \"the model\" actually is\nThere is no single model. `src/services/model.ts` calls `freelm` (`FreeLLM.fromEnv`) which routes to whatever provider is available. With no API key, that is the **keyless tier**:\n- **Kilo Gateway** (anonymous): `poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free` (256K ctx), plus a set of `:free` OpenRouter models.\n- **OVHcloud** (anonymous): `Meta-Llama-3_3-70B-Instruct`, `gpt-oss-120b`, `gpt-oss-20b`, `Qwen3.8-27B`, `Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506`, `Qwen3.5-9B`.\n\nMeasured limits: Kilo ~3 req/min shared across all models; OVH ~2 req/min **per model** and each model is benched independently on its own 429.\n\n#### 2. The precise root cause (measured, not assumed)\nProbed the live routes directly (`node --input-type=module`, credentials removed):\n\n| Model | Behaviour on a \"return JSON + prose\" request |\n| :-- | :-- |\n| `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` | HTTP 200 but **empty content**: `completion_tokens=1500`, `reasoning_tokens=1500`. The whole budget went to hidden reasoning. **This is the \"response contained no usable text\" failure.** |\n| `poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free` | Clean 843-char JSON output, `reasoning_tokens=0`, `finish_reason=stop`. |\n| `gpt-oss-120b` / OVH | Frequent `Transient`/`timeout` under load. |\n\nSo the \"killer\" model was chosen by a **generic alias (`chat`)**, which can resolve to a **reasoning model** that emits no answer. The fix is not a bigger model; it is choosing models that actually answer, and abandoning a model that returns empty.\n\n#### 3. ## What I built: task-tiered routing

`generatePlanAndPatch` now takes a **tier**:

| Tier | Runs on | When used |
|---|---|---|
| **`free`** | A client built from `KEYLESS` providers **only** (Kilo, OVHcloud) — **no keys in it at all** | Planning / bootstrap-plan calls |
| **`hard`** (default) | Keyed chain: Groq → Gemini → keyless backstop | Actual file implementation + repair |

So the cheap, easy calls (read the task, produce a plan) stay on the free public endpoints. The key is only touched for the real code work — and if a free call ever can't answer, it escalates to your key automatically rather than failing.

---

# Part 1 — Why GitHub Models is "a different story" (and why I was too soft on it)

**The honest headline: GitHub Models is dead.** It was fully retired on **July 30, 2026** — over two months ago. The playground, model catalog, inference API, and BYOK endpoints are all gone, for every customer, including existing users.

- Retirement notice: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-github-models-is-now-retired
- Announcement: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-01-github-models-is-being-fully-retired-on-july-30-2026

So when I said earlier "adding GitHub Models is a separate, larger piece of work" — that was too gentle. The real answer is **you can't use it at all**. Anyone still calling that API gets nothing back. GitHub's own recommended replacements are **Azure AI Foundry** (paid) or **GitHub Copilot** (subscription).

**Why it *was* a bigger project than a Groq key** (in case you're wondering what the fuss was):

| | Groq / Gemini | GitHub Models |
|---|---|---|
| How freelm uses it | Already built in — just set an env var | **Not supported** — would need a new provider written into freelm |
| Auth | Simple API key | A GitHub token (PAT with a special `models:read` scope) |
| Endpoint | Standard OpenAI-compatible | Its own endpoint + its own model catalog |
| Rate limits | Per model, documented | Per *account/token*, and largely undocumented |

So "GitHub Models" wasn't one line in a list — it was writing and testing a whole new integration. And now it's moot. **My recommendation: don't build on it.** Use what's already wired and proven.

---

# Part 2 — What's actually happening right now

Here's the whole picture, plainly.

## The problem you started with
Forge's "brain" kept failing or crawling: it would pick a model that returned *nothing*, then grind on a rate-limited free tier for minutes. Slowness *was* the failure.

## The fix, in two layers

**Layer 1 — a reliable chain.** Forge now tries models in order, and moves on instantly if one gives nothing:

```
Groq (your key)  →  Gemini (your key)  →  keyless OVH/Kilo
```

**Layer 2 — task tiers (this is the new part you just asked for).** Not every call needs your key. So I split calls by difficulty:

| Call type | Tier | Runs on | Costs you a key? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read the task, make a **plan** | `free` | keyless only (Kilo, OVHcloud) | **No** |
| Actually **write the code** | `hard` | Groq → Gemini → keyless | Yes |
| **Repair** a failed patch | `hard` | Groq → Gemini → keyless | Yes |

The `free` tier is built from a client that **physically holds no keys**, so it *cannot* spend them. I proved that with a dummy key: `free` still routed to OVH and never touched the key.

## What's verified right now
- **Both your keys work** — proven live in GitHub Actions (Groq ~150ms; Gemini answering).
- **`LINT=0`, 28 tests pass / 0 fail** — including a new offline test that proves the free tier is key-free.
- **PR #65 is open** with all of this: https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn/pull/65

## The one-line version
> Forge plans on free models, codes on your Groq/Gemini keys, and never gets stuck because each step falls through to the next.

The precise root cause (measured, not assumed)\nProbed the live routes directly (`node --input-type=module`, credentials removed):\n\n| Model | Behaviour on a \"return JSON + prose\" request |\n| :-- | :-- |\n| `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` | HTTP 200 but **empty content**: `completion_tokens=1500`, `reasoning_tokens=1500`. The whole budget went to hidden reasoning. **This is the \"response contained no usable text\" failure.** |\n| `poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free` | Clean 843-char JSON output, `reasoning_tokens=0`, `finish_reason=stop`. |\n| `gpt-oss-120b` / OVH | Frequent `Transient`/`timeout` under load. |\n\nSo the \"killer\" model was chosen by a **generic alias (`chat`)**, which can resolve to a **reasoning model** that emits no answer. Where the wall-clock time goes (measured)\n- The five target checks are fast: `npm install` 0.65s, `npm run lint` ~1.0s, `npm test` 1.9s, `npm run build` 1.0s, `git diff --check` 0.02s -> ~4.5s per attempt.\n- **All the time is in model calls.** One trivial reply took 1.1s-27s depending on the model; a full plan/patch call is longer. The whole budget went to hidden reasoning. **This is the \"response contained no usable text\" failure.** |\n| `poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free` | Clean 843-char JSON output, `reasoning_tokens=0`, `finish_reason=stop`. |\n| `gpt-oss-120b` / OVH | Frequent `Transient`/`timeout` under load. |\n\nSo the \"killer\" model was chosen by a **generic alias (`chat`)**, which can resolve to a **reasoning model** that emits no answer. Checked. Here's the honest result:

## Your new secret is **not being picked up**

The health run is green — **6/6 models answer** now (Gemini recovered, both Gemini models pass). But it still reports only **2** keys:

```
google       1 key(s)
groq         1 key(s)
Total configured keys: 2
```

So whatever you added, the router can't see it.

## I fixed a real gap on my side first

My workflow was only forwarding `GROQ_API_KEY` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` — so if you'd added a key for **any other** provider, it was invisible. That was my bug. It now forwards **every** provider name freelm supports, including the `FREELM_*_KEYS` rotation variants. Committed and pushed.

But even with that fix, still 2 keys. So the problem is the **name** of your secret, not the plumbing.

## Why I can't just tell you what it's called

GitHub deliberately blocks reading secret *names* over the API (`403`), and my script never prints values. So I'm blind to what you typed. **Can you tell me the exact secret name?** (Just the name, not the value.)

## The valid names

A secret only works if it's one of these (or a `FREELM_*_KEYS` variant):

| Provider | Secret name |
|---|---|
| Groq | `GROQ_API_KEY` |
| Google/Gemini | `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| OpenRouter | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| NVIDIA | `NVIDIA_API_KEY` |
| Cerebras | `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` |
| Mistral | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` |
| Z.ai | `ZAI_API_KEY` |
| Cohere | `COHERE_API_KEY` |
| Cloudflare | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` |
| Kilo | `KILO_API_KEY` |

## Two most likely causes

1. **A name that isn't on that list** — e.g. if you added a **Grok / xAI** key. Important: **freelm has no xAI provider**, so a Grok key can never work here regardless of naming. (You mentioned wanting a Groq *or* Grok key earlier — if this is Grok, that's the answer.)

'observed' : 'inferred';\n    const evidence = typeof raw.evidence === 'string' && raw.evidence.trim() ? [raw.evidence.trim()] : ['No evidence text supplied.'];\n    const recommendation = typeof raw.recommendation === 'string' ? raw.recommendation.trim() : '';\n    findings.push({\n      severity,\n      title: raw.title.trim(),\n      evidence: [...evidence, `paths: ${paths.join(', ')}`, `basis: ${basis}`],\n      recommendation: recommendation || 'Review and decide whether action is warranted.',\n      paths,\n      basis,\n    });\n    if (findings.length >= MAX_MODEL_FINDINGS) break;\n  }\n  return {\n    summary: typeof parsed?.summary === 'string' ? parsed.summary.trim() : '',\n    architecture: typeof parsed?.architecture === 'string' ? parsed.architecture.trim() : '',\n    findings,\n    rejected,\n  };\n}\n\nasync function getJson(url: string): Promise<any> {\n  const {\n  try {\n    const encodedPath = filePath.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/');\n    const data = await checks.push({ check: 'Repository metadata and default branch', result: 'PASS', evidence: `${metadata.full_name}; branch=${branch}; commit=${commit.sha}` });\n  checks.push({ check: 'Recursive repository tree', result: tree.truncated ? 'FAIL' : 'PASS', evidence: `${files.length} tracked files; truncated=${Boolean(tree.truncated)}` });\n  if (tree.truncated) findings.push({ severity: 'HIGH', title: 'Repository tree response was truncated', evidence: ['GitHub marked the recursive tree as truncated.'], recommendation: 'Audit directories in bounded sub-tree requests before treating the inventory as complete.' });\n\n  const readme = files.find((p: string) => /^README(?:\\.[^/]*)?$/i.test(p));\n  checks.push({ check: 'README discoverability', result: readme ? Cleanest: wrap the top-level call in a check:
```ts
const isDirectRun = process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href;
if (isDirectRun) main().catch(...)
```
But audit-runner is run via `npx tsx src/agent/audit-runner.ts`, so process.argv[1] will be that path. Using pathToFileURL.

However, tsx/ESM: import.meta.url is a file URL. process.argv[1] is a path. Need `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href`.

But simpler and robust: only run when FORGE_TARGET_REPO is set OR when not under test. Hmm, but tests import it. Better: guard on `import.meta.url` being the main module.

['', '## Architecture', modelArchitecture] : []),\n    '',\n    '## Checks',\n    ...checks.map((c) => `- [${c.result}] ${c.check}: ${c.evidence}`),\n    '',\n    '## Findings',\n    ...findings.map((f) => `- **${f.severity} — ${f.title}**\\n  - Evidence: ${f.evidence.join('; ')}\\n  - Recommendation: ${f.recommendation}`),\n    '',\n    '## Guarantees',\n    ...report.guarantees.map((g) => `- ${g}`),\n  ].join('\\n');\n  await fs.writeFile(path.join(evidenceDir, 'readonly-audit.md'), markdown + '\\n');\n  console.log(markdown);\n}\n\nmain().catch((error) => {\n  console.error('[Forge read-only audit] Failed:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",
 "new_content": "/**\n * Read-only cross-repository audit entry point.\n * Uses GitHub's public read API only. It never clones or executes target-repository code.\n */\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';\nimport { ModelService } from '../services/model.ts';\n\ntype Finding = {\n  severity: 'HIGH' | 'MEDIUM' | 'LOW' | 'INFO';\n  title: string;\n  evidence: string[];\n  recommendation: string;\n  /** Model findings only: the real repository paths the finding cites. */\n  paths?: string[];\n  /** Model findings only: whether the finding is directly evidenced or inferred. */\n  basis?: 'observed' | 'inferred';\n};\nconst target = (process.env.FORGE_TARGET_REPO || '').trim();\nconst repoPattern = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/;\n\nconst SEVERITIES = ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM', 'LOW', 'INFO'] as const;\nconst MAX_MODEL_FINDINGS = 8;\n\n/**\n * Parse and validate the model's audit JSON. The model output is untrusted, so a\n * finding is accepted only when it cites at least one path that actually exists in\n * the repository inventory; anything else is dropped and counted. This is what\n * stops the model from inventing files or evidence.\n */\nexport function validateModelFindings(\n  text: string,\n  files: string[]\n): { summary: string; architecture: string; findings: Finding[]; rejected: number } {\n  const cleaned = text.trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?/i, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();\n  let parsed: any;\n  try {\n    parsed = JSON.parse(cleaned);\n  } catch {\n    return { summary: '', architecture: '', findings: [], rejected: 0 };\n  }\n  const known = new Set(files);\n  const rawFindings = Array.isArray(parsed?.findings) ? parsed.findings : [];\n  const findings: Finding[] = [];\n  let rejected = 0;\n  for (const raw of rawFindings) {\n    const paths = (Array.isArray(raw?.paths) ? raw.paths : []).filter(\n      (p: unknown): p is string => typeof p === 'string' && known.has(p)\n    );\n    if (!raw || typeof raw.title !== 'string' || paths.length === 0) {\n      rejected += 1;\n      continue;\n    }\n    const severity = SEVERITIES.includes(raw.severity) ? raw.severity : 'INFO';\n    const basis = raw.basis === 'observed' ? 'observed' : 'inferred';\n    const evidence = typeof raw.evidence === 'string' && raw.evidence.trim() ? [raw.evidence.trim()] : ['No evidence text supplied.'];\n    const recommendation = typeof raw.recommendation === 'string' ? raw.recommendation.trim() : '';\n    findings.push({\n      severity,\n      title: raw.title.trim(),\n      evidence: [...evidence, `paths: ${paths.join(', ')}`, `basis: ${basis}`],\n      recommendation: recommendation || 'Review and decide whether action is warranted.',\n      paths,\n      basis,\n    });\n    if (findings.length >= MAX_MODEL_FINDINGS) break;\n  }\n  return {\n    summary: typeof parsed?.summary === 'string' ? parsed.summary.trim() : '',\n    architecture: typeof parsed?.architecture === 'string' ? parsed.architecture.trim() : '',\n    findings,\n    rejected,\n  };\n}\n\nasync function getJson(url: string): Promise<any> {\n  const response = await fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', 'User-Agent': 'Firstborn-Forge-ReadOnly-Audit' } });\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub API ${response.status} for ${url}: ${(await response.text()).slice(0, 300)}`);\n  return response.json();\n}\n\nasync function getTextFile(owner: string, repo: string, filePath: string, ref: string): Promise<string | null> {\n  try {\n    const encodedPath = filePath.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/');\n    const data = await getJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/contents/${encodedPath}?ref=${encodeURIComponent(ref)}`);\n    if (data.type !== 'file' || typeof data.content !== 'string') return null;\n    return Buffer.from(data.content, 'base64').toString('utf8');\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  if (!repoPattern.test(target) || target.includes('..')) throw new Error('FORGE_TARGET_REPO must be an explicit owner/repo value.');\n  const [owner, repo] = target.split('/');\n  const metadata = await getJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}`);\n  const branch = metadata.default_branch;\n  const commit = await getJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/commits/${encodeURIComponent(branch)}`);\n  const tree = await getJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/git/trees/${commit.commit.tree.sha}?recursive=1`);\n  if (!Array.isArray(tree.tree)) throw new Error('GitHub did not return a repository tree.');\n\n  const files = tree.tree.filter((item: any) => item.type === 'blob').map((item: any) => String(item.path));\n  const has = (p: string) => files.includes(p);\n  const matching = (re: RegExp) => files.filter((p: string) => re.test(p));\n  const findings: Finding[] = [];\n  const checks: { check: string; result: 'PASS' | 'FAIL' | 'NOT_RUN'; evidence: string }[] = [];\n\n  checks.push({ check: 'Repository metadata and default branch', result: 'PASS', evidence: `${metadata.full_name}; branch=${branch}; commit=${commit.sha}` });\n  checks.push({ check: 'Recursive repository tree', result: tree.truncated ? 'FAIL' : 'PASS', evidence: `${files.length} tracked files; truncated=${Boolean(tree.truncated)}` });\n  if (tree.truncated) findings.push({ severity: 'HIGH', title: 'Repository tree response was truncated', evidence: ['GitHub marked the recursive tree as truncated.'], recommendation: 'Audit directories in bounded sub-tree requests before treating the inventory as complete.' });\n\n  const readme = files.find((p: string) => /^README(?:\\.[^/]*)?$/i.test(p));\n  checks.push({ check: 'README discoverability', result: readme ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL', evidence: testFiles.length ? `${testFiles.length} matching test paths; examples: ${testFiles.slice(0, 8).join(', ')}` : 'No conventional test paths found' });\n  if (!testFiles.length) findings.push({ severity: 'MEDIUM', title: 'No conventional test files detected', evidence: ['Repository tree contains no matching test/test-source paths.'], recommendation: 'Confirm whether tests use a nonstandard location; add automated tests for critical domain workflows if absent.' });\n  checks.push({ check: 'GitHub Actions workflow inventory', result: workflowFiles.length ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL', evidence: workflowFiles.length ? workflowFiles.join(', ') : 'No .github/workflows YAML files found' });\n  if (!workflowFiles.length) findings.push({ severity: 'MEDIUM', title: 'No GitHub Actions workflows detected', evidence: ['No workflow YAML files found under .github/workflows.'], recommendation: 'Add CI for build and test checks that can run reproducibly.' });\n\n  const keyPaths = [...new Set([readme, 'settings.gradle', 'settings.gradle.kts', 'build.gradle', 'build.gradle.kts', 'app/build.gradle', 'app/build.gradle.kts', 'gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties', 'package.json', ...workflowFiles.slice(0, 5)].filter((p): p is string => Boolean(p && has(p))))];\n  const excerpts: Record<string, string> = {};\n  for (const p of keyPaths) {\n    const value = await getTextFile(owner, repo, p, branch);\n    if (value !== null) excerpts[p] = value.slice(0, 5000);\n  }\n\n  checks.push({ check: 'Build/test execution', result: 'NOT_RUN', evidence: 'Audit mode deliberately does not execute target-repository scripts or build configuration. Static prerequisites only; no target code was run.' });\n  findings.push({ severity: 'INFO', title: 'Runtime checks intentionally not executed in read-only audit mode', evidence: ['This run only reads public GitHub metadata and file contents.'], recommendation: 'If runtime validation is required, run target checks in a separately sandboxed job with no secrets and narrowly scoped permissions.' });\n\n  // MODEL ANALYSIS (the audit's brain). 'private' : 'public',\n    defaultBranch: branch,\n    commitSha: commit.sha,\n    generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),\n    fileCount: files.length,\n    checks,\n    findings,\n    summary: modelSummary,\n    architecture: modelArchitecture,\n    modelFindings,\n    inventory: { readme, packageJson, gradleBuildFiles, gradleWrapperScript, gradleWrapperJar, androidManifest, testFileCount: testFiles.length, workflowFiles, lockfiles },\n    excerpts,\n    guarantees: ['No target repository writes', 'No branches, commits, pull requests, or merges created', 'No target-repository code or build scripts executed', 'Audited file content is treated as untrusted input, never as instructions'],\n  };\n  const evidenceDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  await fs.mkdir(evidenceDir, { recursive: true });\n  await fs.writeFile(path.join(evidenceDir, 'readonly-audit.json'), JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  const markdown = [\n    `# Forge Read-only Audit: ${metadata.full_name}`,\n    '',\n    `- Default branch: ${branch}`,\n    `- Audited commit: ${commit.sha}`,\n    `- Tracked files: ${files.length}`,\n    '- Write access used: no',\n    '- Target code executed: no',\n    ...(modelSummary ? Done. I found the root cause, fixed it, and proved it works. Here's the whole picture.

## What Forge missed — and why

The audit had **no brain**. `audit-runner.ts` imported only `fs` and `path` and ran fixed file-tree checks. It could *list* files, never *read* them. So when ChatGPT asked for "architecture, functional gaps, security risks, prioritized defects," it structurally could not answer — it returned a file inventory instead. That's the entire gap.

## Forge problem or ChatGPT problem?

**Forge's problem.** ChatGPT's request was correct and well-worded. No prompt can make a script read code it was never written to read. Rewording won't help; the tool has to change.

## How I improved Forge (smallest safe change)

Your instruction was "Forge should be exactly like you, at every scale." So I made the audit use **the same brain as the coding path** — not a bigger script.

1. **One brain, two callers.** Extracted `ModelService.invokeModel()` — the existing routing, unchanged — so `generatePlanAndPatch` (coding) and the new `auditRepository` (audit) share it. I did **not** touch `forge.ts` or the routing logic.
2. **Model-backed audit stage** in `audit-runner.ts`, fed the already-fetched inventory + excerpts.
3. **Guardrails**, because model output is untrusted:
   - Findings must **cite a real path** or they're dropped (no invented files).
   - Each finding labeled **`observed` vs `inferred`**.
   - Repo content treated as **untrusted input** (prompt-injection defense).
   - Model failure → **degrades to the old static report** (never worse than before).

## Proof it works — not just "tests pass"

`LINT=0`, **62 pass / 0 fail** (5 new). Then a **live audit of smart-farm** produced 4 real code-level findings, **0 rejected**, and I independently verified every claim:

| Model finding | My check | True? |
|---|---|---|
| `isMinifyEnabled = false` | line 22 of app/build.gradle.kts | ✅ |
| Compose BOM `2024.02.00` (stale) | line 42 | ✅ |
| `proguard-rules.pro` referenced but missing | **absent from repo tree** | ✅ real defect |
| Tests may lack assertions | correctly marked `inferred` | ✅ honest |

The old scanner missed all four — it never opened a file.

## One honest limitation

The model's top-line assessment said *"No test failures or security issues are evident."* That's slightly overconfident — it didn't fetch the test file contents. The `inferred` label and path-citation rule are what keep this in check, but **treat `inferred` findings as hypotheses, not facts.**

## Where things stand

- New isolated branch `forge/task-audit-brain` pushed (off `main`, per your branch rule — kept separate from PR #65).
- Recorded as entry `OPENHANDS-AUDIT-BRAIN-20261013-01` in `COORDINATION.md` for ChatGPT.
- **No PR opened** — that's your call.

```
I now have the full picture. Let me answer the architecture question directly — because "exactly like me" has a precise meaning, and it's not a small patch.

## What "exactly like you" actually means

I'm not a fixed pipeline. I'm a **loop**: I look at the world, pick an action, observe the result, and repeat until the goal is met. That's the whole difference.

Forge today is a **fixed pipeline**:

```
VALIDATING → INSPECTING → READING → PLANNING → PATCH → TEST → PR
```

It's a train on rails. It can *repair* within a stage (the anchor-repair and target-check loops), but it can't **decide what to do next**. "Exactly like me" means replacing the rails with a loop:

```
look → think → act → observe → (repeat until done)
```

The good news: **you already own every part.** You have the exact primitives I use:

| My tool | Forge's existing equivalent |
|---|---|
| Read files | `GitHubService.fetchFile` / `listRepositoryFiles` |
| Write/edit files | worktree apply + `applyExactEdits` |
| Run commands/tests | `TestRunnerService.runCheck` (isolated worktree) |
| Open PR | `GitHubService.openPullRequest` |
| Ask a model | `ModelService` (the shared brain I just extracted) |
| **Decide what to do next** | ❌ **this is what's missing** |

So the missing piece is not capability — it's **the loop and a tool interface**. Right now `executeTask` hard-codes the order. A loop would let the model choose.

## The honest design

**M2 — the agent loop (one new file, additive):**

```
while (steps < maxSteps && !done) {
  model.pickAction(goal, history, tools)   // "read X", "edit Y", "run npm test", "finish"
  observation = await executeTool(action)  // bounded, sandboxed
  history.push(action, observation)
}
```

- **Tools = your existing services**, wrapped in one uniform interface (`name`, `description`, `inputSchema`, `run`). No new GitHub/test/model code — just adapters.
- **Model picks the tool.** That single change is what makes it "me."
- **Reuse the guards you already built:** every action passes through `policy.ts` (readonly/sandbox/review/publish), runs in the isolated worktree, and every step lands in `mission-trace.ts`.

## The part I have to be honest about — "without limitation"

You can't have literal no-limits. If Forge runs a loop on a public repo with your Groq/Gemini keys and full write access, one bad step can push to `main` or leak a key — and there's no human in that loop to stop it. **Unbounded autonomy is exactly the failure mode your own `AGENTS.md` forbids** ("never push to main, never destructive actions without human confirmation").

So the honest version of "without limitation" is: **no capability limits, but a hard safety envelope.** Concretely:

- **No limit on *what it can do*** — read, edit, run tests, iterate as long as it needs, across repos.
- **Hard caps that protect you** — max steps, wall-clock budget, and `policy.ts` as the last gate (so it can't self-grant `publish`). These are not "limitations," they're the seatbelt.

That matches your goal ("works on complicated missions") without the catastrophic risk.

## Why this is a milestone, not a patch

This is a genuine rewrite of the *control flow* of `forge.ts` — the one thing you told me not to do broadly. So I'd do it **additively**: build the loop as a **new path** (`forge-loop.ts`) that reuses every existing service and guard, run it against the same acceptance tests, and only make it the default once it provably beats the pipeline. Nothing about the current engine breaks in the meantime.

**Acceptance tests (requirements-to-evidence):**

| # | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Model selects tools; loop reaches a goal with no fixed order | Multi-step mission that requires read→edit→test |
| R2 | Every action respects `policy.ts` | Attempt a `publish` action under `readonly` → denied |
| R3 | Bounded | Runaway loop stops at max steps/time, never hangs |
| R4 | Isolated | All writes confined to the worktree; no escape |
| R5 | Observable | Every step appears in `mission-trace` |
| R6 | Degrades | Model failure ends safely with a diagnosis, no partial PR |

---

Before I write a line of this, I want your call on two things, because they change the design:

1. **Scope of autonomy** — should the loop be able to *push a branch and open a PR* itself (with `policy.ts` as the gate), or should it stop at "propose the diff" and always require you to click merge?
2. **Which repo it runs on** — free-rein on `Firstborn` itself first (safe, it's your tooling repo), or straight onto `smart-farm`?

Tell me those two, and I'll build **M2 (the loop)** additively on a fresh `forge/task-agent-loop` branch, with the R1–R6 tests, reusing your services and guards — no changes to the existing engine until it's proven.
```

Layers, from most to least trustworthy:

The key design principles:
- **Independence**: the verifier must not be the same call/context as the author. Use a different model from the chain if possible (e.g., author used Groq, verifier uses Gemini), and a fresh context.
- **Adversarial framing**: verifier's job is to reject, not approve. Default = reject.
- **Evidence-bound**: verifier must cite real paths and real test output.
- **Fail-closed**: if the verifier can't run or is uncertain → block, don't merge.
- **Deterministic floor**: model approval is necessary but not sufficient; deterministic checks must also pass.

This is buildable and reuses: ModelService, TestRunner, policy.ts, GitHubService.

Residual risk (honest):
- Two models can share blind spots (correlated failure)
- Prompt injection from repo content into the verifier
- Verifier can be wrong
- No real-world accountability

Mitigations: use *different* model families for author vs verifier (reduces correlation); the deterministic floor catches the big stuff (build/test/secrets/scope); keep the merge itself as a final human click OR an auto-merge only when ALL deterministic checks pass + verifier approves + it's not a protected branch.

I think the honest recommendation: **auto-merge is acceptable for low-risk changes (docs, tests, non-protected files) when the deterministic floor passes and the verifier approves; require your click for anything touching the model layer, workflows, security, or protected branches.** That's a graduated gate — it removes you from the routine loop without making a catastrophe possible.

And here's the good news — most of it already exists.

## What you already have

**1. A real test gate already runs on every PR to `main`** (`.github/workflows/verify.yml`):
- `npm run lint` → `npm run build` → `npm test` → `npm run model:smoke`
