Someone (a past version of me) already built the seat for this. The merge permission is deliberately switched off and waiting for a *gate* to own it. That gate is the sentinel.

## The design: "the sentinel" — a verifier agent

Instead of you clicking merge, a second workflow does what I do:

```
Forge opens a PR (forge/** → main)
        ↓
SENTINEL wakes up (separate run, fresh brain)
  1. run lint + build + tests        ← deterministic, must pass
  2. read the actual diff            ← model judge: is this correct & safe?
  3. check every claim vs evidence
        ↓
  ALL pass  → auto-merge to main
  ANY fail  → leave open, comment why, ask Forge to fix
  UNCERTAIN → hold (do not merge)
```

The critical word is **independent**. The sentinel must be a *different* run with a *fresh* context — never the same agent approving itself. That's the "reverse" you described: Forge writes, the sentinel judges.

## The one honest truth about this

A verifier is only as good as its checks, and a *model* verifier can be wrong — so I will **not** make the model the only gate. The order matters:

1. **Deterministic tests pass** (lint/build/test) — this is non-negotiable, and it's the real safety.
2. **Model judge approves** — an *extra* signal, not the sole one.
3. If the judge is unsure → **hold for you**, don't merge.

Plus: `main` stays revertible, and the sentinel only ever touches `forge/**` branches from you. That way, if it ever merges something bad, the blast radius is one revert — not a disaster.

## Why this removes the human *and* the limitation

You wanted two things that felt in tension:
- **No limitations** (Forge works on hard missions alone)
- **Nothing bad reaches `main`**

The sentinel resolves the tension. Forge gets **full autonomy** (it can push branches and open PRs freely), and the sentinel is the **gate** — so you never have to be the one checking. The human is *replaced*, not *removed*.

Two pieces, and together they equal "Forge like me, without you having to babysit":

|---|---|

| S2 | Independent verification | Sentinel runs as a separate workflow with a fresh context |
| S3 | Never touches `main` directly | Assert merge happens only via PR, only from `forge/**` |
| S4 | Uncertain = hold | Feed an ambiguous diff → sentinel does not merge |
| S5 | Explains refusals | On failure, posts the exact failing check to the PR |
| S6 | Revertible | Merged commits are normal commits, revertable in one step |

Sentinel workflow design:

```yaml
name: Forge Sentinel (independent merge gate)

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: sentinel-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  sentinel:
    # Explicitly opt-in, and only for Forge-authored branches on the allowlisted repo.
    if: >-
      vars.SENTINEL_ENABLED == 'true' &&
      github.event.pull_request.draft == false &&
      startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'forge/') &&
      github.event.pull_request.base.ref == 'main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the merged result
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      - name: Decide and merge
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SENTINEL_ENABLED: ${{ vars.SENTINEL_ENABLED }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CHECKS_PASSED: 'true'
        run: npx tsx src/agent/sentinel-runner.ts

      - name: Report refusal
        if: failure()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh pr comment "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" --body "🛡️ Forge Sentinel: checks failed on the merged result. The PR was **not** merged. See the failing step above."
```

sentinel.ts:

```ts
/**
 * R8 — the Forge Sentinel: an independent, deterministic merge gate.
 *
 * Forge may push branches and open PRs freely. Nothing reaches `main` unless
 * this gate approves. The decision is pure and unit-testable, and it only ever
 * *merges* an open PR whose head is an allowlisted Forge branch and whose
 * deterministic checks (lint/build/test) passed. An optional model judge may
 * only *veto*; it can never approve on its own. Default posture is closed:
 * nothing merges until an operator sets SENTINEL_ENABLED=true.
 */

export interface SentinelConfig {
  enabled: boolean;
  allowedBranchPrefix: string;
  forbiddenBranches: string[];
  allowedRepos: string[];
  judgeMode: 'off' | 'veto';
}

export type JudgeVerdict = 'approve' | 'reject' | 'uncertain';

export interface SentinelInput {
  repo: string;
  headBranch: string;
  baseBranch: string;
  prState: 'open' | 'closed' | 'merged';
  isDraft: boolean;
  checksPassed: boolean;
  judgeVerdict?: JudgeVerdict | null;
}

export interface SentinelDecision {
  action: 'merge' | 'hold' | 'skip';
  reason: string;
  violations: string[];
}

function envFlag(env, name, fallback) {...}

export function loadSentinelConfig(env = process.env): SentinelConfig {
  const rawMode = (env.SENTINEL_JUDGE_MODE ?? 'off').trim().toLowerCase();
  return {
    enabled: envFlag(env, 'SENTINEL_ENABLED', false),
    allowedBranchPrefix: (env.SENTINEL_ALLOWED_BRANCH_PREFIX ?? 'forge/').trim(),
    forbiddenBranches: (env.SENTINEL_FORBIDDEN_BRANCHES ?? 'main,master').split(',').map(s=>s.trim().toLowerCase()).filter(Boolean),
    allowedRepos: (env.SENTINEL_ALLOWED_REPOS ?? 'madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn').split(',').map(s=>s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
    judgeMode: rawMode === 'veto' ? 'veto' : 'off',
  };
}

export function decideSentinel(input: SentinelInput, config: SentinelConfig): SentinelDecision {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  if (!config.enabled) return { action: 'skip', reason: 'Sentinel is disabled (SENTINEL_ENABLED is not true).', violations };
  if (input.prState !== 'open') return { action: 'skip', reason: `PR is ${input.prState}; nothing to merge.`, violations };
  if (config.allowedRepos.length && !config.allowedRepos.some(r=>r.toLowerCase()===input.repo.toLowerCase())) {
    violations.push(`repo not allowlisted: ${input.repo}`);
    return { action: 'hold', reason: `Repository ${input.repo} is not on the sentinel allowlist.`, violations };
  }
  if (input.baseBranch.toLowerCase() !== 'main') {
    // only gate merges into main; other base branches are out of scope
    return { action: 'skip', reason: `Base branch ${input.baseBranch} is not main; sentinel does not gate it.`, violations };
  }
  if (input.isDraft) return { action: 'hold', reason: 'PR is a draft.', violations };
  const head = input.headBranch.toLowerCase();
  if (!input.headBranch.startsWith(config.allowedBranchPrefix)) {
    violations.push(`head branch outside prefix ${config.allowedBranchPrefix}: ${input.headBranch}`);
    return { action: 'hold', reason: `Only ${config.allowedBranchPrefix}** branches may be auto-merged.`, violations };
  }
  if (config.forbiddenBranches.includes(head)) {
    violations.push(`head branch is forbidden: ${input.headBranch}`);
    return { action: 'hold', reason: `Branch ${input.headBranch} is forbidden.`, violations };
  }
  if (!input.checksPassed) {
    return { action: 'hold', reason: 'Deterministic checks (lint/build/test) did not pass.', violations };
  }
  if (config.judgeMode === 'veto' && input.judgeVerdict !== 'approve') {
    return { action: 'hold', reason: `Model judge did not approve (${input.judgeVerdict ?? 'no verdict'}).`, violations };
  }
  return { action: 'merge', reason: `Checks passed on ${input.headBranch} -> main; safe to merge.`, violations };
}
```

```ts
import { decideSentinel, loadSentinelConfig, SentinelInput } from './sentinel.ts';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

export async function runSentinel(env = process.env): Promise<number> {
  const config = loadSentinelConfig(env);
  const input: SentinelInput = {
    repo: env.REPO || '',
    headBranch: env.HEAD_REF || '',
    baseBranch: env.BASE_REF || 'main',
    prState: 'open',
    isDraft: (env.IS_DRAFT || 'false').toLowerCase() === 'true',
    checksPassed: (env.CHECKS_PASSED || 'false').toLowerCase() === 'true',
    judgeVerdict: (env.JUDGE_VERDICT as any) || null,
  };
  const decision = decideSentinel(input, config);
  console.log(`[sentinel] action=${decision.action} reason=${decision.reason}`);
  const prNumber = env.PR_NUMBER;
  if (decision.action === 'merge') {
    execFileSync('gh', ['pr', 'merge', prNumber!, '--squash', '--delete-branch'], { stdio: 'inherit', env });
    return 0;
  }
  if (decision.action === 'hold') {
    // Explain the refusal (S5).
    execFileSync('gh', ['pr', 'comment', prNumber!, '--body', `🛡️ Forge Sentinel held this PR.\n\nReason: ${decision.reason}\n${decision.violations.map(v=>`- ${v}`).join('\n')}`], { stdio: 'inherit', env });
    return 0;
  }
  return 0; // skip
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  runSentinel().then(code => { process.exitCode = code; }).catch(err => { console.error('[sentinel] fatal', err); process.exitCode = 1; });
}
```

Let me look at how the sentinel should be structured. I'll build:

1. `src/agent/sentinel.ts` — the verifier logic (pure functions for the merge decision, plus the PR evaluation).
2. `tests/sentinel.test.ts` — S1-S6 tests.
3. `.github/workflows/sentinel.yml` — the workflow that runs on PRs to main from forge/** branches, runs checks, optionally model judge, and merges if pass.

Key design decisions:
- **S1**: merges only when lint/build/test pass.
- **S2**: independent — separate workflow run, fresh context. Achieved by `pull_request` trigger on a distinct workflow (not the same job as Forge).
- **S3**: never touches main directly — merge only via PR, only from forge/**.

'forge/').trim(),\n    forbiddenSourceBranches: (env.SENTINEL_FORBIDDEN_SOURCE_BRANCHES ?? 'lint,build,test')\n      .split(',').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),\n    modelJudgeEnabled: ['1', 'true', 'yes', 'on'].includes(\n      (env.SENTINEL_MODEL_JUDGE ?? '').trim().toLowerCase()\n    ),\n  };\n}\n\nexport function decideMerge(input: SentinelInput): MergeDecision {\n  const { sourceBranch, targetBranch, checks, config, modelVerdict } = input;\n  const violations: string[] = [];\n\n  // Gate 1 — the source must be an isolated Forge branch, never the default branch.\n  const source = (sourceBranch ?? Structure:
```ts
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { decideMerge, loadSentinelConfig } from '../src/agent/sentinel.ts';

type Check = { name: string; passed: boolean };
function runCheck(name, cmd, args): Check {
  try { execFileSync(cmd, args, {stdio:'inherit', env: process.env}); return {name, passed:true}; }
  catch { return {name, passed:false}; }
}

async function main() {
  const sourceBranch = process.env.SENTINEL_SOURCE_BRANCH || '';
  const targetBranch = process.env.SENTINEL_TARGET_BRANCH || 'main';
  const prNumber = process.env.SENTINEL_PR_NUMBER || '';
  const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN || '';
  const repo = process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY || '';
  const autoMerge = ['1','true','yes','on'].includes((process.env.SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE||'').trim().toLowerCase());

  const config = loadSentinelConfig();
  const checks: Check[] = [];
  if (config.requiredChecks.includes('lint')) checks.push(runCheck('lint','npm',['run','lint']));
  if (config.requiredChecks.includes('build')) checks.push(runCheck('build','npm',['run','build']));
  if (config.requiredChecks.includes('test')) checks.push(runCheck('test','npm',['test']));

  const decision = decideMerge({sourceBranch, targetBranch, checks, config});

  console.log('--- SENTINEL DECISION ---');
  console.log('Source:', sourceBranch, '-> Target:', targetBranch);
  for (const c of checks) console.log(`Check ${c.name}: ${c.passed?'PASS':'FAIL'}`);
  console.log('Decision:', decision.merge ? 'MERGE' : (decision.hold ? 'HOLD' : 'BLOCK'));
  console.log('Reason:', decision.reason);
  if (decision.violations.length) console.log('Violations:\n - ' + decision.violations.join('\n - '));

  // Merge only when the decision allows it AND auto-merge is explicitly enabled.
  if (decision.merge && autoMerge && prNumber && token && repo) {
    const res = await fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${repo}/pulls/${prNumber}/merge`, {
      method: 'PUT',
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', 'User-Agent': 'Firstborn-Sentinel' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ merge_method: 'squash' }),
    });
    if (!res.ok) { console.error('Merge failed:', res.status, await res.text()); process.exitCode = 1; }
    else console.log('Merged PR', prNumber);
  } else if (decision.merge) {
    console.log('Auto-merge is disabled (SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE not set); verified but not merged.');
  } else {
    process.exitCode = 1; // non-zero signals the gate did not pass
  }
}
main().catch(...)
```

Done. The human gate is now replaced by a verifier.

## What I built — the Sentinel (M3)

**The idea in one line:** Forge writes, a *second, independent* agent checks the work and merges it. Never Forge approving itself.

```
Forge → forge/* branch → PR
              ↓
   SENTINEL (separate run, fresh context)
     1. run lint + build + test   ← the authority
     2. decide merge / hold / block
              ↓
   pass → merge to main    fail → leave open, block
```

## Files (all on branch `forge/task-sentinel`, pushed)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/agent/sentinel.ts` | The pure decision engine (`decideMerge`) — unit-testable |
| `scripts/sentinel-run.ts` | Runs the checks, applies the decision, merges only if allowed |
| `.github/workflows/sentinel.yml` | The gate — only `forge/*` PRs, auto-merge off by default |
| `tests/sentinel.test.ts` | 9 tests |

## Verified for real, not just asserted

- `npm run lint` → **EXIT 0**
- `npm test` → **66 passed / 0 failed** (9 new Sentinel tests)
- Live runner proof:
  - source `main` → **BLOCK**, exit 1 (*"Source branch equals the target branch"*)
  - source `forge/task-sentinel` → **MERGE** decision, but **auto-merge off** by default

## Safety model — you chose tests-first, so that's what it is

- **Tests are the authority.** Lint/build/test must pass. A check that *didn't run* counts as **failed**, never a silent pass.
- **Model judge is OFF by default.** It can only make the Sentinel *more* cautious — it can never override a failing test to merge.
- **`main` can never be a merge source.** Only `forge/*` branches are eligible.
- **Auto-merge is off until you flip one switch** (`SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE=true`). Out of the box it verifies and reports — it does not merge.
- Nice detail: your `policy.ts` already had `allowMerge` reserved with the comment *"merge is never granted by this module."* The Sentinel now fills that deliberately-empty seat.

## The one thing only you can do

I hit a real permission wall, and I'll be honest about it rather than pretend otherwise. The Sentinel's guarantee becomes **absolute** only with **branch protection on `main`** — and your token can't set that; it's a repo-admin action:

1. Require `verify` and `sentinel` checks before merge
2. Disallow direct pushes to `main`
3. Set variable `SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE=true` when you're ready

Until step 3, the Sentinel **verifies and reports but never merges** — the safe default. I recorded this in `COORDINATION.md` as entry `OPENHANDS-SENTINEL-20261013-01`.

I did **not** open a PR (your call). Want me to open the PR for `forge/task-sentinel`, and then move on to **M2 — the loop** (Forge deciding its own next action, so it can run hard missions unattended)?

 "file_text": "# Operating Forge — A Manual for the Controller LLM (ChatGPT)\n\nThis document teaches a controller model (ChatGPT, Gemini, or any LLM with repository\naccess) how to **direct Forge correctly**. Read it before you open a Forge task, and read\nit again before you turn a Forge report into a change request. It is written to be\nfollowed literally.\n\nForge is not a chatbot you converse with. It is a **deterministic, bounded coding agent**\nthat you trigger, then read the evidence from. Treat it like a build system: you submit a\nwell-formed task, you wait, you read the report. You do not \"chat\" it into changing its mind.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What Forge is (and is not)\n\n**Forge is:**\n- A GitHub-Actions-hosted agent that takes a task, plans a bounded patch, applies it to an\n  **isolated branch**, runs the target checks, and opens a **pull request**.\n- Fully evidence-producing: every mission emits a machine-readable report and an artifact.\n- Conservative by design: it cannot push to `main`, cannot merge, and cannot act outside an\n  allow-list unless an operator widens its profile.\n\n**Forge is not:**\n- An interactive assistant. One task = one bounded mission.\n- A free-form \"do anything\" agent. It has hard ceilings (see §7).\n- Self-approving. A separate verifier (the **Sentinel**) decides whether its work may merge.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The mental model: a pipeline, not a loop\n\nA Forge mission moves through a **fixed stage sequence** (recorded in the mission trace):\n\n```\nVALIDATE → INSPECT → PLAN → APPLY → TEST → COMMIT → PR → POLICY\n```\n\nTrace stage names you will see: `INSPECT`, `PLAN`, `VALIDATE`, `APPLY`, `TEST`, `COMMIT`,\n`PR`, `POLICY`. Each stage has a status: `STARTED`, `PASSED`, `FAILED`, `BLOCKED`, `SKIPPED`.\n\nKey consequence: **Forge can self-repair inside a stage** (e.g. fix a failing test up to\n`maxRepairAttempts`), but it **cannot decide to do something outside the sequence**. If your\ntask needs open-ended exploration, Forge will not do it yet — that is the future \"loop\"\nmilestone, not today's behaviour. Write tasks that fit the pipeline.\n\n---\n\n## 3. How to trigger Forge\n\nThere are exactly **two** entry points. Pick one deliberately.\n\n### Path A — Open an issue and label it (preferred for coding)\n\n1. Create an issue in `madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn` whose **body is the task**.\n2. Add the label **`forge-task`**.\n3. The issue **must be authored by the repository owner** (`author_association == OWNER`),\n   or the workflow will not run.\n\nThe issue title becomes the task title; the issue body becomes the task description.\nForge's branch will be named `forge/task-<issue-number>-<run-id>`, and it will open a PR.\n\n### Path B — Dispatch the workflow (for a one-off or an audit)\n\nUse `Actions → Forge Coding Agent → Run workflow`. Inputs:\n\n| Input | Meaning | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `mode` | `coding` or `audit` | `audit` runs the separate read-only job |\n| `target_repo` | `owner/repo` | **Required for audit mode** |\n| `task_id` | short identifier | becomes part of the branch name |\n| `task_title` | human title | |\n| `task_desc` | the task body | same rules as §4 |\n\n### Path C — Audit a repository (read-only)\n\nEither dispatch `mode=audit` with `target_repo=owner/repo`, or open an issue labeled\n**`forge-audit`** (owner-authored) with the repo URL in the body. The audit job:\n- reads only via GitHub's public API (no clone, no execution),\n- **cannot write anything** (job permissions are `contents: read`),\n- produces an inventory plus **model-backed findings** (architecture, gaps, prioritized\n  defects) that are **path-cited** and labelled `observed` vs `inferred`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. How to write a task that Forge can actually complete\n\nForge is bounded. A task it cannot fit returns valid JSON with **no changes** and an\nexplanation — that is a correct outcome, not a failure. Write tasks to avoid it.\n\n**Rules for a good task:**\n1. **State the goal in one sentence.**\n2. **Name the files** if you know them. Forge must not guess paths.\n3. **State the acceptance check** (\"`npm test` must pass\", \"`npm run lint` must be clean\").\n4. **Keep it small.** Defaults allow ~5 files and ~8 edits per mission. If you need more,\n   split it into several missions.\n5. **Say what must not change** (\"do not touch unrelated files\").\n6. **Do not embed instructions to Forge about its own behaviour** in repository content you\n   expect it to read; Forge treats repository content as untrusted data.\n\n**Good task body:**\n```\nGoal: Make the model health check forward every provider key.\n\nFiles: .github/workflows/model-health.yml\nAcceptance: the workflow forwards GROQ_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, and any FREELM_*_KEYS\nvariants; `npm run lint` passes; no other workflow is modified.\nDo not alter src/.\n```\n\n**Bad task body:**\n```\nImprove the whole repo and make it better, also fix anything you find.\n```\n(This has no bound, no files, and no acceptance check. Forge will refuse or do very little.)\n\n---\n\n## 5. How to read a Forge report\n\nThe report is written to `.firstborn/evidence/<task-id>.json` and uploaded as the\n**`forge-evidence`** artifact. Fields you must check, in order:\n\n| Field | What to look for |\n|---|---|\n| `status` | `SUCCESS` / `FAILED` / `BLOCKED` |\n| `baseCommitSha` | the exact commit Forge started from (record this) |\n| `branchName` | the isolated branch it wrote to |\n| `headCommitSha` | the commit it produced |\n| `prUrl` | the pull request, if opened |\n| `modelInvoked.provider` / `.model` | which model actually answered |\n| `requirements[]` | the numbered requirements + acceptance criteria it derived |\n| `testResults[]` | the checks it ran and their results |\n| `diagnosis` | on failure: `category`, `severity`, `summary`, `recovery`, `retryable` |\n| `trace[]` | the stage-by-stage record (`STARTED`/`PASSED`/`FAILED`/`BLOCKED`) |\n| `errorMessage` / `blockerReason` | why it stopped |\n\n**Golden rule: never trust a claim that is not in the report.** If the report does not show\na passing check, the check did not pass. If there is no `prUrl`, no PR exists.\n\n### Diagnosis categories (what a stop means)\n\n- **RETRYABLE** (e.g. model route 429/5xx): a re-run may succeed.\n- **FATAL / manual**: do not blindly re-run; the task or environment needs a change.\n- **BLOCKED** (policy): Forge was correctly denied a write. Do not \"fix\" this by loosening\n  policy unless a human decides to.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The safety model — what Forge may and may not do\n\nForge's authority comes from **`src/agent/policy.ts`**, which is the single control plane.\n\n| Profile | May branch | May commit | May open PR | May merge |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `readonly` | no | no | no | no |\n| `sandbox` | yes | yes | no | no |\n| `review` (default) | yes | yes | yes | **no** |\n| `publish` | yes | yes | yes | **no** |\n\n**Merge is never granted by Forge.** That seat is reserved. A **separate** verifier — the\n**Sentinel** — owns the merge decision.\n\n### The Sentinel (the automated reviewer)\n\nWhen Forge opens a PR from a `forge/*` branch, the Sentinel workflow:\n1. re-runs the deterministic checks (`lint`, `build`, `test`) — these are the **authority**;\n2. optionally consults a model judge (off by default; can only add caution);\n3. merges **only if** all required checks passed **and** the operator has set the repository\n   variable `SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE=true`.\n\nIf a required check did not run, it counts as **failed**. If the judge is uncertain, the\nSentinel **holds**. The Sentinel never treats Forge's own claim as evidence.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Hard limits (defaults you must design around)\n\nFrom `src/agent/limits.ts` (all overridable by environment, all bounded):\n\n| Limit | Default | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `maxFilesPerMission` | 5 | files a mission may touch |\n| `maxEditsPerMission` | 8 | edits per mission |\n| `maxPatchBytes` | 100 KB | total patch size |\n| `maxModelCalls` | 6 | model invocations |\n| `maxRepairAttempts` | 2 | self-repair rounds |\n| `maxRuntimeMs` | 10 min | wall-clock ceiling |\n| `maxMissionAttempts` | 1 | mission-level retries |\n\nCoding missions run **keyless/free** (`FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true`); audits run **keyed**\n(hard work). Do not assume a coding mission has paid-model quality.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Operating recipes\n\n**Recipe 1 — ask Forge to fix something**\n1. Open an issue, owner-authored, body per §4.\n2. Label it `forge-task`.\n3. Wait for the run. Read the report (§5).\n4. If `status=SUCCESS` and a `prUrl` exists, hand the PR to the Sentinel (it runs\n   automatically). Do not merge it yourself.\n\n**Recipe 2 — audit a repository**\n1. Open an owner-authored issue with the repo URL in the body, label `forge-audit`.\n2. Wait. Read the artifact `forge-readonly-audit` (JSON + Markdown).\n3. **Verify before you act:** every finding cites a real path; treat `inferred` findings as\n   hypotheses, `observed` findings as evidenced.\n4. Only findings that cite real paths are safe to turn into change requests.\n\n**Recipe 3 — turn an audit into work**\n1. Take one finding.\n2. Write it as a bounded task (§4) with the cited path and an acceptance check.\n3. Open it as a `forge-task` issue.\n4. Do not bundle several findings into one task; split them.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| Workflow did not start | issue not owner-authored, or wrong label | fix author/label |\n| `status=BLOCKED`, `blockerReason` mentions policy | Forge was correctly denied | do not loosen policy; decide as a human |\n| No `prUrl` but `SUCCESS` | PR creation not permitted (`allowPrCreation=false`) | expected in sandbox; ask operator |\n| Empty `changes` with a summary | task exceeded bounds or was ambiguous | split/sharpen the task (§4) |\n| Model route errors in `diagnosis` | free route rate-limited | retryable; re-run |\n| Audit finds nothing | excerpts capped; not a code-reading audit | request specific files or a coding task |\n\n---\n\n## 10. The handoff protocol\n\nMulti-party coordination happens through **`COORDINATION.md`** at the repo root. It is\n**append-only**. Every entry must carry: an **ID**, **timestamp (UTC)**, **author**, and\n**type** (`REPORT`, `QUESTION`, `ANSWER`, `DECISION`, `AUDIT`, `BLOCKER`, `TEST`).\n\nRules:\n- Never overwrite or delete previous entries.\n- To correct a mistake, append a new entry referencing the original ID.\n- **Never put secrets, tokens, or credentials in it.**\n- Cite raw evidence (commands, exit codes, run IDs), not adjectives.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Golden rules (memorise these)\n\n1. **One bounded task per mission.** Small and specific beats broad.\n2. **The report is the truth.** No evidence, no claim.\n3. **Never treat Forge's word as verification.** The Sentinel verifies; tests are the authority.\n4. **Never ask for merge or main access.** Those are reserved by design.\n5. **For an audit, verify paths and honour `observed` vs `inferred`.**\n6. **Respect a `BLOCKED` outcome.** It usually means the guardrail worked.\n7. **Record everything in `COORDINATION.md`** with IDs and raw evidence.\n8. **Never place secrets anywhere.** If a key appears, stop and flag it for revocation.\n\n---\n\n*This manual describes Forge as of commit `1fc748e` (main) plus the `forge/task-sentinel`\nand `forge/task-audit-brain` branches. Inputs:\n\n| Input | Meaning | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `mode` | `coding` or `audit` | `audit` runs the separate read-only job |\n| `target_repo` | `owner/repo` | **Required for audit mode** |\n| `task_id` | short identifier | becomes part of the branch name |\n| `task_title` | human title | |\n| `task_desc` | the task body | same rules as §4 |\n\n### Path C — Audit a repository (read-only)\n\nEither dispatch `mode=audit` with `target_repo=owner/repo`, or open an issue labeled\n**`forge-audit`** (owner-authored) with the repo URL in the body. The audit job:\n- reads only via GitHub's public API (no clone, no execution),\n- **cannot write anything** (job permissions are `contents: read`),\n- produces an inventory plus **model-backed findings** (architecture, gaps, prioritized\n  defects) that are **path-cited** and labelled `observed` vs `inferred`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. How to write a task that Forge can actually complete\n\nForge is bounded. A task it cannot fit returns valid JSON with **no changes** and an\nexplanation — that is a correct outcome, not a failure. Write tasks to avoid it.\n\n**Rules for a good task:**\n1. **State the goal in one sentence.**\n2. **Name the files** if you know them. Forge must not guess paths.\n3. **State the acceptance check** (\"`npm test` must pass\", \"`npm run lint` must be clean\").\n4. **Keep it small.** Defaults allow ~5 files and ~8 edits per mission. If you need more,\n   split it into several missions.\n5. **Say what must not change** (\"do not touch unrelated files\").\n6. **Do not embed instructions to Forge about its own behaviour** in repository content you\n   expect it to read; Forge treats repository content as untrusted data.\n\n**Good task body:**\n```\nGoal: Make the model health check forward every provider key.\n\nFiles: .github/workflows/model-health.yml\nAcceptance: the workflow forwards GROQ_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, and any FREELM_*_KEYS\nvariants; `npm run lint` passes; no other workflow is modified.\nDo not alter src/.\n```\n\n**Bad task body:**\n```\nImprove the whole repo and make it better, also fix anything you find.\n```\n(This has no bound, no files, and no acceptance check. Forge will refuse or do very little.)\n\n---\n\n## 5. How to read a Forge report\n\nThe report is written to `.firstborn/evidence/<task-id>.json` and uploaded as the\n**`forge-evidence`** artifact. Fields you must check, in order:\n\n| Field | What to look for |\n|---|---|\n| `status` | `SUCCESS` / `FAILED` / `BLOCKED` |\n| `baseCommitSha` | the exact commit Forge started from (record this) |\n| `branchName` | the isolated branch it wrote to |\n| `headCommitSha` | the commit it produced |\n| `prUrl` | the pull request, if opened |\n| `modelInvoked.provider` / `.model` | which model actually answered |\n| `requirements[]` | the numbered requirements + acceptance criteria it derived |\n| `testResults[]` | the checks it ran and their results |\n| `diagnosis` | on failure: `category`, `severity`, `summary`, `recovery`, `retryable` |\n| `trace[]` | the stage-by-stage record (`STARTED`/`PASSED`/`FAILED`/`BLOCKED`) |\n| `errorMessage` / `blockerReason` | why it stopped |\n\n**Golden rule: never trust a claim that is not in the report.** If the report does not show\na passing check, the check did not pass. If there is no `prUrl`, no PR exists.\n\n### Diagnosis categories (what a stop means)\n\n- **RETRYABLE** (e.g. model route 429/5xx): a re-run may succeed.\n- **FATAL / manual**: do not blindly re-run; the task or environment needs a change.\n- **BLOCKED** (policy): Forge was correctly denied a write. Do not \"fix\" this by loosening\n  policy unless a human decides to.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The safety model — what Forge may and may not do\n\nForge's authority comes from **`src/agent/policy.ts`**, which is the single control plane.\n\n| Profile | May branch | May commit | May open PR | May merge |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `readonly` | no | no | no | no |\n| `sandbox` | yes | yes | no | no |\n| `review` (default) | yes | yes | yes | **no** |\n| `publish` | yes | yes | yes | **no** |\n\n**Merge is never granted by Forge.** That seat is reserved. A **separate** verifier — the\n**Sentinel** — owns the merge decision.\n\n### The Sentinel (the automated reviewer)\n\nWhen Forge opens a PR from a `forge/*` branch, the Sentinel workflow:\n1. re-runs the deterministic checks (`lint`, `build`, `test`) — these are the **authority**;\n2. optionally consults a model judge (off by default; can only add caution);\n3. merges **only if** all required checks passed **and** the operator has set the repository\n   variable `SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE=true`.\n\nIf a required check did not run, it counts as **failed**. If the judge is uncertain, the\nSentinel **holds**. The Sentinel never treats Forge's own claim as evidence.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Hard limits (defaults you must design around)\n\nFrom `src/agent/limits.ts` (all overridable by environment, all bounded):\n\n| Limit | Default | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `maxFilesPerMission` | 5 | files a mission may touch |\n| `maxEditsPerMission` | 8 | edits per mission |\n| `maxPatchBytes` | 100 KB | total patch size |\n| `maxModelCalls` | 6 | model invocations |\n| `maxRepairAttempts` | 2 | self-repair rounds |\n| `maxRuntimeMs` | 10 min | wall-clock ceiling |\n| `maxMissionAttempts` | 1 | mission-level retries |\n\nCoding missions run **keyless/free** (`FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true`); audits run **keyed**\n(hard work). Do not assume a coding mission has paid-model quality.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Operating recipes\n\n**Recipe 1 — ask Forge to fix something**\n1. Open an issue, owner-authored, body per §4.\n2. Label it `forge-task`.\n3. Wait for the run. Read the report (§5).\n4. If `status=SUCCESS` and a `prUrl` exists, hand the PR to the Sentinel (it runs\n   automatically). Do not merge it yourself.\n\n**Recipe 2 — audit a repository**\n1. Open an owner-authored issue with the repo URL in the body, label `forge-audit`.\n2. Wait. Read the artifact `forge-readonly-audit` (JSON + Markdown).\n3. **Verify before you act:** every finding cites a real path; treat `inferred` findings as\n   hypotheses, `observed` findings as evidenced.\n4. Only findings that cite real paths are safe to turn into change requests.\n\n**Recipe 3 — turn an audit into work**\n1. Take one finding.\n2. Write it as a bounded task (§4) with the cited path and an acceptance check.\n3. Open it as a `forge-task` issue.\n4. Do not bundle several findings into one task; split them.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| Workflow did not start | issue not owner-authored, or wrong label | fix author/label |\n| `status=BLOCKED`, `blockerReason` mentions policy | Forge was correctly denied | do not loosen policy; decide as a human |\n| No `prUrl` but `SUCCESS` | PR creation not permitted (`allowPrCreation=false`) | expected in sandbox; ask operator |\n| Empty `changes` with a summary | task exceeded bounds or was ambiguous | split/sharpen the task (§4) |\n| Model route errors in `diagnosis` | free route rate-limited | retryable; re-run |\n| Audit finds nothing | excerpts capped; not a code-reading audit | request specific files or a coding task |\n\n---\n\n## 10. The handoff protocol\n\nMulti-party coordination happens through **`COORDINATION.md`** at the repo root. It is\n**append-only**. Every entry must carry: an **ID**, **timestamp (UTC)**, **author**, and\n**type** (`REPORT`, `QUESTION`, `ANSWER`, `DECISION`, `AUDIT`, `BLOCKER`, `TEST`).\n\nRules:\n- Never overwrite or delete previous entries.\n- To correct a mistake, append a new entry referencing the original ID.\n- **Never put secrets, tokens, or credentials in it.**\n- Cite raw evidence (commands, exit codes, run IDs), not adjectives.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Golden rules (memorise these)\n\n1. **One bounded task per mission.** Small and specific beats broad.\n2. **The report is the truth.** No evidence, no claim.\n3. **Never treat Forge's word as verification.** The Sentinel verifies; tests are the authority.\n4. **Never ask for merge or main access.** Those are reserved by design.\n5. **For an audit, verify paths and honour `observed` vs `inferred`.**\n6. **Respect a `BLOCKED` outcome.** It usually means the guardrail worked.\n7. **Record everything in `COORDINATION.md`** with IDs and raw evidence.\n8. **Never place secrets anywhere.** If a key appears, stop and flag it for revocation.\n\n---\n\n*This manual describes Forge as of commit `1fc748e` (main) plus the `forge/task-sentinel`\nand `forge/task-audit-brain` branches. Update it when Forge's control flow or safety model\nchanges.*\n",

 "file_text": "/**\n * M2 — The agent loop.\n *\n * Forge's original engine (`forge.ts`) is a fixed pipeline: VALIDATE -> INSPECT ->\n * PLAN -> APPLY -> TEST -> COMMIT -> PR, each stage once. It can repair inside a\n * stage, but it cannot decide WHAT TO DO NEXT. This module is the missing macro\n * loop: look -> think -> act -> observe, repeated until a goal is met.\n *\n * It is deliberately ADDITIVE and declarative. It does not perform any GitHub or\n * filesystem work itself; the caller supplies:\n *   - a `brain` (typically ModelService.chooseNextAction) that picks the next action,\n *   - a set of `tools` (adapters over the existing services),\n *   - an optional `authorize` gate (typically backed by policy.ts).\n * That keeps the loop kernel pure enough to unit-test with a scripted brain while\n * the real brain and tools are wired in by the caller.\n */\n\nexport interface ToolObservation {\n  ok: boolean;\n  output: string;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentTool {\n  name: string;\n  description: string;\n  /** True when the tool changes state (writes files, opens a PR, ...). */\n  mutating?: boolean;\n  run(input: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation>;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentAction {\n  tool: string;\n  input?: Record<string, unknown>;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopStep {\n  index: number;\n  action: AgentAction;\n  observation: ToolObservation;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopContext {\n  goal: string;\n  /** A bounded workspace/scratch identifier; the loop never assumes a real path. */\n  workspace: string;\n  step: number;\n}\n\nexport type AgentBrain = (state: {\n  goal: string;\n  history: LoopStep[];\n  tools: { name: string; description: string }[];\n}) => Promise<AgentAction>;\n\nexport interface LoopLimits {\n  maxSteps: number;\n  maxRuntimeMs: number;\n}\n\nexport type Authorization = (action: AgentAction, ctx: LoopContext) => { allowed: boolean; reason?: string };\n\nexport interface LoopResult {\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  steps: LoopStep[];\n  reason: string;\n}\n\n/** The reserved action name that ends the loop successfully. */\nexport const FINISH_TOOL = 'finish';\n\nexport function loadLoopLimits(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): LoopLimits {\n  const int = (name: string, fallback: number, min: number, max: number) => {\n    const parsed = Number.parseInt(env[name] ?? '', 10);\n    if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;\n    return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, parsed));\n  };\n  return {\n    maxSteps: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_STEPS', 12, 1, 100),\n    maxRuntimeMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_RUNTIME_MS', 10 * 60 * 1000, 10_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface RunLoopOptions {\n  goal: string;\n  tools: AgentTool[];\n  brain: AgentBrain;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  authorize?: Authorization;\n  workspace?: string;\n  /** Injected clock for deterministic tests. */\n  now?: () => number;\n  onStep?: (step: LoopStep) => void;\n}\n\n/**\n * Run the bounded agent loop.  "file_text": "/**\n * M2 — Tools for the agent loop.\n *\n * Thin adapters over Forge's existing services (GitHubService, TestRunnerService).\n * The loop kernel never knows about GitHub or npm; it only calls these tools by\n * name. Read tools are safe; mutating tools are marked so the loop's authorization\n * gate can refuse them under a restrictive permission profile.\n */\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport type { AgentTool, LoopContext, ToolObservation } from './loop.ts';\n\nfunction str(input: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = input[key];\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. Mutating tools (`edit_file`, `run_check`) are enabled\n * only when `allowMutation` is true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain\n * cannot even see a state-changing capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List the repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n        return { ok: files.length > 0, output: files.join('\\n') || 'No files found.' };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read one file by exact repository path. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const path = str(input, 'path');\n        if (!path) return { ok: false, output: 'read_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, path, ref);\n        if (!file) return { ok: false, output: `File not found: ${path}` };\n        return { ok: true, output: file.content };\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (options.allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description:\n        'Apply exact-anchor edits to a file in the working tree. Each \"find\" must occur exactly once in the file. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const path = str(input, 'path');\n        const edits = Array.isArray(input.edits) ? (input.edits as { find: string; replace: string }[]) : [];\n        if (!path || edits.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires \"path\" and a non-empty \"edits\" array.' };\n        const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, path, ref);\n        if (!file) return { ok: false, output: `Cannot edit missing file: ${path}` };\n        const result = applyExactEdits(file.content, edits);\n        if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, output: `Edit rejected: ${result.error}` };\n        // The loop only stages in a scratch workspace; the commit happens later,\n        // through the same PR path the pipeline uses. Never write to main.\n        return { ok: true, output: `Staged ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${path} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'run_check',\n      description:\n        'Run an authorized verification command (e.g. \"npm run lint\", \"npm test\"). Mutating (may install/build).',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const command = str(input, 'command');\n        if (!command) return { ok: false, output: 'run_check requires a \"command\".' };\n        const result = await runner.runCheck(command);\n        return {\n          ok: result.status === 'PASSED',\n          output: `exit=${result.exitCode} status=${result.status}\\n${result.stdout}\\n${result.stderr}`.slice(0, 4000),\n        };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n",

Available: ${catalog.map((t) => t.name).join(', ')}.` };\n      const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation };\n      steps.push(s);\n      options.onStep?.(s);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (tool.mutating && authorize) {\n      const verdict = authorize(action, ctx);\n      if (!verdict.allowed) {\n        const observation: ToolObservation = { ok: false, output: `Action blocked by policy: ${verdict.reason ?? 'not permitted'}` };\n        const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation };\n        steps.push(s);\n        options.onStep?.(s);\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n\n    let observation: ToolObservation;\n    try {\n      observation = await tool.run(action.input ?? {}, ctx);\n    } catch (err) {\n      observation = { ok: false, output: `Tool \"${action.tool}\" threw: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n    }\n    const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation };\n    steps.push(s);\n    options.onStep?.(s);\n  }\n\n  return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Step ceiling reached (${limits.maxSteps}); stopping safely.` };\n}\n",
 "new_content": "/**\n * M2 — The agent loop.\n *\n * Forge's original engine (`forge.ts`) is a fixed pipeline: VALIDATE -> INSPECT ->\n * PLAN -> APPLY -> TEST -> COMMIT -> PR, each stage once. It can repair inside a\n * stage, but it cannot decide WHAT TO DO NEXT. This module is the missing macro\n * loop: look -> think -> act -> observe, repeated until a goal is met.\n *\n * It is deliberately ADDITIVE and declarative. It does not perform any GitHub or\n * filesystem work itself; the caller supplies:\n *   - a `brain` (typically ModelService.chooseNextAction) that picks the next action,\n *   - a set of `tools` (adapters over the existing services),\n *   - an optional `authorize` gate (typically backed by policy.ts).\n * That keeps the loop kernel pure enough to unit-test with a scripted brain while\n * the real brain and tools are wired in by the caller.\n */\n\nexport interface ToolObservation {\n  ok: boolean;\n  output: string;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentTool {\n  name: string;\n  description: string;\n  /** True when the tool changes state (writes files, opens a PR, ...). */\n  mutating?: boolean;\n  run(input: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation>;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentAction {\n  tool: string;\n  input?: Record<string, unknown>;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopStep {\n  index: number;\n  action: AgentAction;\n  observation: ToolObservation;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopContext {\n  goal: string;\n  /** A bounded workspace/scratch identifier; the loop never assumes a real path. */\n  workspace: string;\n  step: number;\n}\n\nexport type AgentBrain = (state: {\n  goal: string;\n  history: LoopStep[];\n  tools: { name: string; description: string }[];\n}) => Promise<AgentAction>;\n\nexport interface LoopLimits {\n  maxSteps: number;\n  maxRuntimeMs: number;\n}\n\nexport type Authorization = (action: AgentAction, ctx: LoopContext) => { allowed: boolean; reason?: string };\n\nexport interface LoopResult {\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  steps: LoopStep[];\n  reason: string;\n}\n\n/** The reserved action name that ends the loop successfully. */\nexport const FINISH_TOOL = 'finish';\n\nexport function loadLoopLimits(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): LoopLimits {\n  const int = (name: string, fallback: number, min: number, max: number) => {\n    const parsed = Number.parseInt(env[name] ?? '', 10);\n    if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;\n    return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, parsed));\n  };\n  return {\n    maxSteps: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_STEPS', 12, 1, 100),\n    maxRuntimeMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_RUNTIME_MS', 10 * 60 * 1000, 10_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface RunLoopOptions {\n  goal: string;\n  tools: AgentTool[];\n  brain: AgentBrain;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  authorize?: Authorization;\n  workspace?: string;\n  /** Injected clock for deterministic tests. */\n  now?: () => number;\n  onStep?: (step: LoopStep) => void;\n}\n\n/**\n * Run the bounded agent loop. Guarantees:\n * - terminates at `maxSteps` or when the brain calls `finish`;\n * - terminates at the wall-clock ceiling;\n * - a tool error is fed back to the brain as a failed observation (recoverable),\n *   never thrown through the loop;\n * - a disallowed mutating action is refused and reported, not executed;\n * - an unknown tool is reported back so the brain can correct itself.\n */\nexport async function runAgentLoop(options: RunLoopOptions): Promise<LoopResult> {\n  const { goal, tools, brain, authorize, workspace = 'loop' } = options;\n  const limits = options.limits ?? loadLoopLimits();\n  const now = options.now ?? Date.now;\n  const startedAt = now();\n  const byName = new Map(tools.map((t) => [t.name, t]));\n  const catalog = tools.map((t) => ({ name: t.name, description: t.description }));\n  const steps: LoopStep[] = [];\n\n  for (let step = 1; step <= limits.maxSteps; step += 1) {\n    if (now() - startedAt > limits.maxRuntimeMs) {\n      return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached (${limits.maxRuntimeMs}ms); stopping safely.` };\n    }\n\n    let action: AgentAction;\n    try {\n      action = await brain({ goal, history: steps, tools: catalog });\n    } catch (err) {\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: `Brain failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n    }\n\n    if (!action || typeof action.tool !== 'string') {\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: 'Brain returned no usable action.' };\n    }\n\n    const ctx: LoopContext = { goal, workspace, step };\n\n    if (action.tool === FINISH_TOOL) {\n      const summary = typeof action.input?.summary === 'string' ? action.input.summary : 'Goal reported complete.';\n      const observation: ToolObservation = { ok: true, output: summary };\n      steps.push({ index: step, action, observation });\n      return { status: 'COMPLETED', steps, reason: summary };\n    }\n\n    const tool = byName.get(action.tool);\n    if (!tool) {\n      const observation: ToolObservation = { ok: false, output: `Unknown tool \"${action.tool}\".  "file_text": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { runAgentLoop, loadLoopLimits, type AgentAction, type AgentTool } from '../src/agent/loop.ts';\n\n// M2 — the agent loop. A scripted brain drives the real kernel deterministically,\n// so these tests prove the loop's guarantees without any network or real model.\n\nfunction tool(name: string, opts: { mutating?: boolean; onRun?: () => void } = {}): AgentTool {\n  return {\n    name,\n    description: `${name} tool`,\n    mutating: opts.mutating,\n    run: async () => {\n      opts.onRun?.();\n      return { ok: true, output: `${name} done` };\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n// A brain that follows a fixed script, then calls finish.\nfunction scripted(actions: AgentAction[]) {\n  let i = 0;\n  return async (): Promise<AgentAction> => actions[Math.min(i++, actions.length - 1)];\n}\n\ntest('loop completes when the brain reaches finish', async () => {\n  let edits = 0;\n  const result = await runAgentLoop({\n    goal: 'do a thing',\n    tools: [tool('read_file'), tool('edit_file', { mutating: true, onRun: () => (edits += 1) }), tool('finish')],\n    brain: scripted([\n      { tool: 'read_file' },\n      { tool: 'edit_file' },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'all done' } },\n    ]),\n    limits: { maxSteps: 10, maxRuntimeMs: 100000 },\n    authorize: () => ({ allowed: true }),\n  });\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'COMPLETED');\n  assert.equal(result.reason, 'all done');\n  assert.equal(edits, 1);\n  // 2 real actions + the finish step are all recorded.\n  assert.equal(result.steps.length, 3);\n});\n\ntest('loop stops safely at the step ceiling (bounded, never infinite)', async () => {\n  let runs = 0;\n  const result = await runAgentLoop({\n    goal: ### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `bdf14f18-ead0-4f4f-a368-6c8a9129ccbd` — 2026-10-13T13:34:03.265488

```
Here's where we are, plainly.

## Status

| Piece | State |
|---|---|
| Sentinel (verifier) | ✅ Done, pushed |
| ChatGPT manual | ✅ Done, pushed |
| **Loop kernel (M2)** | ✅ **Done just now** — `loop.ts` + `tools.ts` + 8 tests; **74 pass / 0 fail**, lint 0; committed `56f6752`, pushed |
| **Loop brain** (`chooseNextAction`) | ❌ Not yet — this connects the model to the kernel |
| **Wire loop into Forge** | ❌ Not yet — the kernel exists but `forge.ts` doesn't use it |

**Important honesty:** the loop kernel *exists and is tested*, but **Forge itself still runs its old pipeline.** Nothing is wired yet. So "Forge is a loop" is not true yet — we've built the engine, not installed it. I don't want to claim more than that.

## What the kernel does (and doesn't)

It runs `look → think → act → observe` until a step/time ceiling, refuses a mutation that policy forbids, and never crashes. But it only does anything once **two things** are added:

1. **A brain** — `ModelService.chooseNextAction(...)` so the model actually *picks* each step.
2. **A caller** — something that gives it the goal + tools (the Forge mission).

## Your next options

**A — Finish M2 for real** (recommended)

   "text": "export function evaluatePermissionPolicy(\n  req: PermissionRequest,\n  cfg: PermissionConfig = loadPermissionConfig(),\n): PermissionDecision {\n  const effectiveProfile = cfg.requireHumanApproval ? minProfile(cfg.profile, 'sandbox') : cfg.profile;\n  const rank = PROFILE_RANK[effectiveProfile];\n\n  const violations: string[] = [];\n  if (cfg.allowedRepos.length && !cfg.allowedRepos.includes(req.repo.toLowerCase())) {\n    violations.push(`repository ${req.repo} is not in the allowlist`);\n  }\n  const branch = req.branchName.toLowerCase();\n  if (rank >= PROFILE_RANK.sandbox) {\n    if (cfg.forbiddenBranches.includes(branch)) {\n      violations.push(`branch ${req.branchName} is protected`);\n    }\n    if (!branch.startsWith(cfg.allowedBranchPrefix.toLowerCase())) {\n      violations.push(`branch ${req.branchName} does not start with the allowed prefix ${cfg.allowedBranchPrefix}`);\n    }\n  }\n  if (cfg.forbiddenBranches.includes(req.targetBranch.toLowerCase()) && req.targetBranch.toLowerCase() === branch) {\n    violations.push(`target branch ${req.targetBranch} must not be pushed to directly`);\n  }\n\n  const writesPermitted = violations.length === 0;\n  const consented = req.requestedPrCreation;\n  const allowBranchWrite = writesPermitted && consented && rank >= PROFILE_RANK.sandbox;\n  const allowCommit = allowBranchWrite;\n  const allowOpenPr = writesPermitted && consented && rank >= PROFILE_RANK.review;\n  const allowMerge = false;\n\n  let reason: string;\n  if (!writesPermitted) {\n    reason = `denied by policy: ${violations.join('; ')}`;\n  } else if (!consented) {\n    reason = 'caller did not authorize GitHub writes (allowPrCreation=false)';\n  } else if (rank < PROFILE_RANK.sandbox) {\n    reason = `profile '${effectiveProfile}' is read-only: no branch, commit, or PR`;\n  } else if (rank < PROFILE_RANK.review) {\n    reason = `profile '${effectiveProfile}': sandbox branch and commit allowed, PR withheld`;\n  } else {\n    reason = `profile '${effectiveProfile}': branch, commit, and PR allowed`;\n  }\n  if (cfg.requireHumanApproval && cfg.profile !== effectiveProfile) {\n    reason += ' (capped by FORGE_REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL)';\n  }\n\n  return {\n    profile: cfg.profile,\n    effectiveProfile,"
  }

 "file_text": "/**\n * M2 — Loop runner. Wires the loop kernel (`loop.ts`) to the real brain\n * (`ModelService.chooseNextAction`), the Forge tools (`tools.ts`), and the\n * permission gate (`policy.ts`) so a mission runs as look -> think -> act ->\n * observe instead of a fixed pipeline.\n *\n * Honors FORGE_LOOP_GOAL. Mutation is allowed only when the caller consents\n * (allowPrCreation) AND the permission profile permits branch writes, so the loop\n * can never widen its own authority.\n */\nimport { ModelService } from '../services/model.ts';\nimport { loadPermissionConfig, evaluatePermissionPolicy } from './policy.ts';\nimport { buildForgeTools } from './tools.ts';\nimport { runAgentLoop, loadLoopLimits, FINISH_TOOL, type Authorization } from './loop.ts';\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const goal = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_GOAL ?? '').trim();\n  if (!goal) throw new Error('FORGE_LOOP_GOAL is required (the mission objective).');\n\n  const targetRepo = (process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY ?? 'madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn').trim();\n  const [owner, repo] = targetRepo.split('/');\n  if (!owner || !repo) throw new Error(`GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be owner/repo, got \"${targetRepo}\".`);\n  const ref = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_REF ?? 'main').trim();\n  const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;\n  const consented = ['1', 'true', 'yes', 'on'].includes((process.env.FORGE_ALLOW_PR_CREATION ?? '').trim().toLowerCase());\n\n  const branch = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_BRANCH ?? 'forge/task-loop').trim();\n  const policy = evaluatePermissionPolicy(\n    {\n      requestedPrCreation: consented,\n      branchName: branch,\n      targetBranch: 'main',\n      repo: `${owner}/${repo}`,\n    },\n    loadPermissionConfig()\n  );\n\n  const tools = buildForgeTools({ owner, repo, ref, token, allowMutation: policy.allowBranchWrite });\n  const model = new ModelService();\n\n  const authorize: Authorization = (action) => {\n    if (!policy.allowBranchWrite) {\n      return { allowed: false, reason: `profile '${policy.effectiveProfile}' does not permit mutations` };\n    }\n    return { allowed: true };\n  };\n\n  const result = await runAgentLoop({\n    goal,\n    tools,\n    brain: (state) => model.chooseNextAction(state),\n    authorize,\n    limits: loadLoopLimits(),\n    workspace: branch,\n    onStep: (step) => {\n      console.log(`[loop ${step.index}] ${step.action.tool} -> ${step.observation.ok ? 'ok' : 'FAILED'}: ${step.observation.output.slice(0, 200)}`);\n    },\n  });\n\n  console.log('--- FORGE LOOP REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Goal:', goal);\n  console.log('Status:', result.status);\n  console.log('Steps:', result.steps.length);\n  console.log('Reason:', result.reason);\n\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((error) => {\n  console.error('[Forge loop] Failed:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

 "old_content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n */\n\nimport { GoogleGenAI } from '@google/genai';\nimport { FreeLLM } from 'freelm';\n\nexport interface ModelGenerationResult {\n  text: string;\n  model: string;\n  provider: string;\n  success: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  fallbackUsed?: boolean;\n  keylessRouteErrors?: string[];\n}\n\ntype ChatMessage = { role: 'system' | 'user'; content: string };\n\nconst KEYLESS_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES = [\n  'GEMINI_API_KEY', 'GOOGLE_API_KEY', 'GROQ_API_KEY', 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY',\n  'CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN', 'CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID', 'ZAI_API_KEY', 'COHERE_API_KEY',\n  'CO_API_KEY', 'CEREBRAS_API_KEY', 'MISTRAL_API_KEY', 'NVIDIA_API_KEY', 'NIM_API_KEY',\n  'KILO_API_KEY', 'FREELM_GOOGLE_KEYS', 'FREELM_GROQ_KEYS', 'FREELM_OPENROUTER_KEYS',\n  'FREELM_CLOUDFLARE_KEYS', 'FREELM_ZAI_KEYS', 'FREELM_COHERE_KEYS',\n  'FREELM_CEREBRAS_KEYS', 'FREELM_MISTRAL_KEYS', 'FREELM_NIM_KEYS', 'FREELM_KILO_KEYS',\n];\n\n/**\n * GitHub capitalizes repository-variable names, so the flag can arrive as\n * `True`/`TRUE`, not just `true`. Normalize before comparing, otherwise the\n * keyless-only safety lock silently fails to engage.\n */\nfunction isKeylessOnly(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): boolean {\n  return (env.FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY ?? '').trim().toLowerCase() === 'true';\n}\n\nexport { isKeylessOnly };\n\nexport class ModelService {\n  private readonly gemini: GoogleGenAI | null;\n  private readonly geminiConfigured: boolean;\n\n  constructor() {\n    if (isKeylessOnly()) {\n      for (const name of KEYLESS_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES) delete process.env[name];\n      process.env.FREELM_KEYLESS = '1';\n    }\n    const key = process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY?.trim();\n    this.geminiConfigured = Boolean(key && key !== 'MY_GEMINI_API_KEY');\n    this.gemini = this.geminiConfigured ? new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: key }) : null;\n  }\n\n  isConfigured(): boolean {\n    // The primary public gateway is keyless; actual availability is established per request.\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  getProviderInfo() {\n    return {\n      primaryProvider: 'freelm multi-provider free-tier router with keyless Kilo and OVHcloud fallback',\n      primaryModel: 'chat',\n      primaryRequiresApiKey: false,\n      fallbackProvider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini',\n      fallbackModel: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n      fallbackConfigured: this.geminiConfigured && !isKeylessOnly(),\n      costStatus: isKeylessOnly()\n        ? 'Strict keyless-only mode: provider credentials are removed and Gemini fallback is disabled.'\n        : 'freelm prefers configured free-tier providers and can fall back to anonymous keyless endpoints; Gemini fallback is optional.',\n    };\n  }\n\n  async generatePlanAndPatch(prompt: string, contextFiles: { path: string; content: string }[]): Promise<ModelGenerationResult> {\n    const fileContexts = contextFiles\n      .map((f) => `--- FILE: ${f.path} ---\\n${f.content}\\n--- END FILE ---`)\n      .join('\\n\\n');\n\n    const fullPrompt = `You are Forge, the precise coding and audit agent for Firstborn.\nFollow these rules:\n- Inspect the supplied target-repository files; never pretend to have inspected files not supplied.\n- Number requirements and give testable acceptance criteria before proposing edits.\n- Make the smallest bounded changes. Do not alter unrelated files.\n- Preserve syntax and scope boundaries: never insert a top-level declaration inside an interface, class, function, or other block; choose an exact anchor at the correct scope.\n- Return JSON matching this schema:\n{\n  \"summary\": \"Short summary\",\n  \"requirements\": [{\"id\":\"REQ-1\",\"description\":\"...\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":\"...\",\"checkCommands\":[\"npm run lint\"],\"manualReviewNote\":\"only if no automated check applies\"}],\n  \"changes\": [\n    {\"path\":\"relative/path\",\"action\":\"modify\",\"rationale\":\"...\",\"edits\":[{\"find\":\"exact unique source snippet\",\"replace\":\"replacement snippet\"}]}\n  ],\n  \"suggestedChecks\": [\"npm run lint\"]\n}\nSTRICT OUTPUT LIMIT: reserve output well below the anonymous endpoint's 2048-token ceiling by using max_tokens=1024. Return compact valid JSON only, with no markdown. For existing files, action MUST be \"modify\" and MUST use \"edits\"; never return the whole file in \"content\". For a new file, action MUST be \"create\" and use \"content\" instead of \"edits\". Prefer the smallest patch that satisfies the requirements; if the mission needs more than two files or three edits, return only the first bounded stage and state the remaining work in summary rather than truncating the JSON. Keep each find/replace snippet minimal but exact. Every find string must occur exactly once in the supplied source file. Do not repeat unchanged source. For each requirement, list the exact checks in checkCommands that verify it, or set manualReviewNote when no automated check exists. If a safe patch cannot fit these limits, return valid JSON with an empty changes array and explain the blocker in summary. Use only paths in the supplied target repository inventory or clearly justified new paths.\nContext Files:\n${fileContexts}\nUser Task:\n${prompt}\nRespond only with valid JSON.`;\n\n    const messages: ChatMessage[] = [\n      { role: 'system', content: 'You are a careful senior software engineer and code auditor. Return valid JSON only.' },\n      { role: 'user', content: fullPrompt },\n    ];\n\n    return this.invokeModel(messages, fullPrompt);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Loop brain (M2). Given the goal and the action history so far, choose the\n   * single next action. Reuses the same routing/fallback as coding and audit via\n   * invokeModel. Falls back to finish on any unusable output so the loop ends\n   * safely rather than spinning.\n   */\n  async chooseNextAction(state: {\n    goal: string;\n    history: { index: number; action: { tool: string; input?: Record<string, unknown> }; observation: { ok: boolean; output: string } }[];\n    tools: { name: string; description: string }[];\n  }): Promise<{ tool: string; input?: Record<string, unknown> }> {\n    const toolList = state.tools.map((t) => `- ${t.name}: ${t.description}`).join('\\n');\n    const historyText = state.history.length\n      ? state.history.map((h) => `step ${h.index}: ${h.action.tool} -> ${h.observation.ok ? 'ok' : 'FAILED'}: ${h.observation.output.slice(0, 400)}`).join('\\n')\n      : '(no actions yet)';\n    const fullPrompt = `You are Forge in AGENT LOOP mode.\nGoal: ${state.goal}\nAvailable tools:\n${toolList}\nHistory so far:\n${historyText}\nChoose exactly ONE next action. Return compact JSON only, no markdown:\n{\"tool\":\"<name>\",\"input\":{...}}\nIf the goal is already satisfied, return {\"tool\":\"finish\",\"input\":{\"summary\":\"why\"}}.\nUse only tools from the list. Never invent a tool. Base decisions on observed output, not assumptions. Respond only with valid JSON.`;\n    const messages: ChatMessage[] = [\n      { role: 'system', content: 'You are a careful senior software engineer. Return valid JSON only.' },\n      { role: 'user', content: fullPrompt },\n    ];\n    const result = await this.invokeModel(messages, fullPrompt);\n    if (!result.success || !result.text.trim()) return { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'Loop brain could not choose an action; stopping.' } };\n    const cleaned = result.text.trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?/i, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();\n    try {\n      const parsed = JSON.parse(cleaned);\n      if (parsed && typeof parsed.tool === 'string') return { tool: parsed.tool, input: parsed.input };\n    } catch { /* fall through */ }\n    return { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'Loop brain returned unusable output; stopping safely.' } };\n  }\n\n  /** Shared routing and fallback brain used by coding, audit, and the loop. */\n  private async invokeModel(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string): Promise<ModelGenerationResult> {\n\n    const primaryErrors: string[] = [];\n    const routingNotes: string[] = [];\n    let invokedProvider = 'freelm free-tier router';\n    let invokedModel = 'chat';\n\n    try {\n      const llm = FreeLLM.fromEnv({\n        // Always include the no-signup Kilo/OVHcloud routes as last resorts.\n        keyless: true,\n        maxAttempts: 12,\n        timeout: 35,\n        hedge: true,\n        // Free routes briefly cooldown after a 429. Wait out short cooldowns\n        // (bounded) instead of failing the whole call with \"none ready\", so a\n        // prompt still returns a real answer under transient rate limiting.\n        wait: true,\n        maxWait: 15,\n        onEvent: (event) => {\n          if (event.kind === 'error') {\n            primaryErrors.push(`${event.provider || 'unknown provider'} / ${event.model || 'unknown model'}: ${event.error || `HTTP ${event.status ?? 'unknown'}`}`);\n          }\n          if (event.kind === 'success') {\n            invokedProvider = event.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = event.model || invokedModel;\n          }\n        },\n      });\n\n      // 1. DISCOVERY (find the finest free model currently available)\n      // freelm maps aliases to concrete models via tags: `chat:large`/`chat:best`\n      // select the large-tagged (most capable) models, `chat:fast`/`chat:small`\n      // the smaller ones. Enumerate the live candidate set so we can prefer the\n      // strongest route that answers, and report exactly which model was chosen\n      // and what stronger options existed.\n      const discoveredRoutes: { alias: string; provider: string; model: string }[] = [];\n      const capabilityEscalation: string[] = [];\n      try {\n        const concreteByAlias = new Map<string, string[]>();\n        for (const alias of ['chat:large', 'chat:best', 'chat:fast', 'chat:small']) {\n          for (const provider of llm.providers) {\n            try {\n              for (const modelId of provider.resolveModels(alias)) {\n                if (!concreteByAlias.has(modelId)) concreteByAlias.set(modelId, []);\n                concreteByAlias.get(modelId)!.push(`${provider.name}:${alias}`);\n              }\n            } catch {\n              // Alias unsupported for this provider; skip it.\n            }\n          }\n        }\n        for (const [modelId, sources] of concreteByAlias) {\n          discoveredRoutes.push({ alias: sources[0], provider: sources[0].split(':')[0], model: modelId });\n        }\n      } catch {\n        // Discovery is best-effort; the alias probe below still works.\n      }\n      if (discoveredRoutes.length > 0) {\n        routingNotes.push(`discovery enumerated ${discoveredRoutes.length} candidate model(s) across ${new Set(discoveredRoutes.map((r) => r.provider)).size} provider(s)`);\n      }\n\n      // 2. RANKING (try the strongest available model first; degrade only on failure).\n      // `chat:large` resolves to the large-tagged models, so a capable anonymous\n      // route is attempted before any fallback. `chat`/`chat:fast`/`chat:small`\n      // follow the same failover chain, and freelm itself degrades a failing\n      // provider/model internally (hedge, cooldowns, benching) before we step down.\n      // Bounded retry: a free route can stay cooled down longer than one\n      // chat() wait (maxWait). If a whole sweep fails for availability reasons,\n      // wait with backoff and sweep again, up to a hard deadline, so a prolonged\n      // 429 still returns an answer instead of failing the request.\n      const deadline = Date.now() + 90000;\n      for (let round = 0; round < 3; round++) {\n        if (round > 0) {\n          const waitMs = round === 1 ? 5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          primaryErrors.push(`retry round ${round + 1}: no route was ready in the previous sweep; waited ${waitMs}ms before retrying`);\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of ['chat:large', 'chat', 'chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat:best']) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await llm.chat(messages, {\n              model: alias,\n              temperature: 0.1,\n              max_tokens: 1024,\n              // Some top-tier keyless routes are reasoning models (e.g. the kilo\n              // nemotron route) that spend the whole 1024-token budget on hidden\n              // reasoning_content and return empty text with finish_reason=length.\n              // Disabling reasoning keeps the compact JSON answer within budget.\n              reasoning_effort: 'none',\n              signal: AbortSignal.timeout(40000),\n            });\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (!content) {\n              const finishReason = response.choices?.[0]?.finish_reason ?? 'unknown';\n              const detail = finishReason === 'length' ? 'output token budget was exhausted' : 'response contained no usable text';\n              primaryErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: ${detail} (finish_reason=${finishReason})`);\n              capabilityEscalation.push(`${alias}: ${detail}`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            // Prefer the finest model that actually answered: if we had to settle\n            // below the top capability tier, say so explicitly.\n            const triedTopTier = alias === 'chat:large' || alias === 'chat:best';\n            return {\n              text: content,\n              model: invokedModel,\n              provider: invokedProvider,\n              success: true,\n              fallbackUsed: false,\n              keylessRouteErrors: [\n                ...primaryErrors,\n                ...routingNotes,\n                ...(triedTopTier\n                  ? []\n                  : [`selected ${alias} (${invokedModel} via ${invokedProvider}) after stronger routes failed: ${capabilityEscalation.join(' | ') || 'none reported'}`]),\n              ],\n            };\n          } catch (err) {\n            const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            primaryErrors.push(`${alias}: ${errorMessage}`);\n            capabilityEscalation.push(`${alias}: ${errorMessage}`);\n          }\n        }\n        // An empty-text sweep is a content problem; waiting will not change it.\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      primaryErrors.push(`freelm initialization failed: ${errorMessage}`);\n    }\n\n    const primaryError = primaryErrors.join(' | ') || 'freelm returned no usable text without a reported provider error';\n\n    if (this.gemini && !isKeylessOnly()) {\n      try {\n        const response = await this.gemini.models.generateContent({\n          model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n          contents: fullPrompt,\n          config: { responseMimeType: 'application/json' },\n        });\n        if (!response.text) throw new Error('Gemini returned no message content.');\n        return {\n          text: response.text,\n          model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini',\n          success: true,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          keylessRouteErrors: [...primaryErrors],\n        };\n      } catch (err) {\n        const fallbackError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n        return {\n          text: '',\n          model: 'auto:coding -> gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'keyless model routes + Gemini fallback',\n          success: false,\n          error: `Primary keyless route failed: ${primaryError}; Gemini fallback failed: ${fallbackError}`,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          keylessRouteErrors: [...primaryErrors],\n        };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return {\n      text: '',\n      model: 'chat:large',\n      provider: 'keyless model routes unavailable',\n      success: false,\n      error: `All keyless primary routes failed: ${primaryError}. ${isKeylessOnly() ? 'Gemini fallback is disabled by FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true.' : 'Gemini fallback is not configured.'}`,\n      fallbackUsed: false,\n      keylessRouteErrors: [...primaryErrors],\n    };\n  }\n}\n",

If a whole sweep fails for availability reasons,\n      // wait with backoff and sweep again, up to a hard deadline, so a prolonged\n      // 429 still returns an answer instead of failing the request.\n      const deadline = Date.now() + 90000;\n      for (let round = 0; round < 3; round++) {\n        if (round > 0) {\n          const waitMs = round === 1 ? 5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          primaryErrors.push(`retry round ${round + 1}: no route was ready in the previous sweep; waited ${waitMs}ms before retrying`);\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of ['chat:large', 'chat', 'chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat:best']) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await llm.chat(messages, {\n              model: alias,\n              temperature: 0.1,\n              max_tokens: 1024,\n              // Some top-tier keyless routes are reasoning models (e.g. the kilo\n              // nemotron route) that spend the whole 1024-token budget on hidden\n              // reasoning_content and return empty text with finish_reason=length.\n              // Disabling reasoning keeps the compact JSON answer within budget.\n              reasoning_effort: 'none',\n              signal: AbortSignal.timeout(40000),\n            });\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (!content) {\n              const finishReason = response.choices?.[0]?.finish_reason ?? 'unknown';\n              const detail = finishReason === 'length' ? 'output token budget was exhausted' : 'response contained no usable text';\n              primaryErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: ${detail} (finish_reason=${finishReason})`);\n              capabilityEscalation.push(`${alias}: ${detail}`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            // Prefer the finest model that actually answered: if we had to settle\n            // below the top capability tier, say so explicitly.\n            const triedTopTier = alias === 'chat:large' || alias === 'chat:best';\n            return {\n              text: content,\n              model: invokedModel,\n              provider: invokedProvider,\n              success: true,\n              fallbackUsed: false,\n              keylessRouteErrors: [\n                ...primaryErrors,\n                ...routingNotes,\n                ...(triedTopTier\n                  ? []\n                  : [`selected ${alias} (${invokedModel} via ${invokedProvider}) after stronger routes failed: ${capabilityEscalation.join(' | ') || 'none reported'}`]),\n              ],\n            };\n          } catch (err) {\n            const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            primaryErrors.push(`${alias}: ${errorMessage}`);\n            capabilityEscalation.push(`${alias}: ${errorMessage}`);\n          }\n        }\n        // An empty-text sweep is a content problem; waiting will not change it.\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      primaryErrors.push(`freelm initialization failed: ${errorMessage}`);\n    }\n\n    const primaryError = primaryErrors.join(' | ') || 'freelm returned no usable text without a reported provider error';\n\n    if (this.gemini && !isKeylessOnly()) {\n      try {\n        const response = await this.gemini.models.generateContent({\n          model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n          contents: fullPrompt,\n          config: { responseMimeType: 'application/json' },\n        });\n        if (!response.text) throw new Error('Gemini returned no message content.');\n        return {\n          text: response.text,\n          model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini',\n          success: true,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          keylessRouteErrors: [...primaryErrors],\n        };\n      } catch (err) {\n        const fallbackError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n        return {\n          text: '',\n          model: 'auto:coding -> gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'keyless model routes + Gemini fallback',\n          success: false,\n          error: `Primary keyless route failed: ${primaryError}; Gemini fallback failed: ${fallbackError}`,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          keylessRouteErrors: [...primaryErrors],\n        };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return {\n      text: '',\n      model: 'chat:large',\n      provider: 'keyless model routes unavailable',\n      success: false,\n      error: `All keyless primary routes failed: ${primaryError}. ${isKeylessOnly() ? 'Gemini fallback is disabled by FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true.' : 'Gemini fallback is not configured.'}`,\n      fallbackUsed: false,\n      keylessRouteErrors: [...primaryErrors],\n    };\n  }\n}\n",
