| Module | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/agent/loop.ts` | The loop kernel: **look → think → act → observe**, bounded by steps and time |
| `src/agent/tools.ts` | Tool adapters over your existing services (read/list/edit/run-check) |
| `src/services/model.ts` | **`chooseNextAction()`** — the brain pick; plus one shared `invokeModel()` for coding + audit + loop |
| `src/agent/loop-runner.ts` | Wires brain + tools + `policy.ts` as the authorization gate |

## Proof — not just claims

- `npm run lint` → **EXIT 0**
- `npm test` → **74 passed / 0 failed** (8 new loop tests: completion, step ceiling, runtime ceiling, policy-blocked mutation, unknown tool, throwing tool, failing brain, bounded defaults)

  > **COMPLETED in 3 steps** → `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts` ✅ correct

## The honest part — I found a real defect

My **first** live run got **stuck**: the brain kept calling `list_files` and never moved on, ending at the step ceiling. The loop was *safe* (it stopped), but not *useful*. I fixed the two causes — the file list wasn't visible in the observation, and the prompt lacked "don't repeat, build on results" rules — then re-ran to a clean completion. I'm telling you because a working loop that silently loops forever would be worse than useless.

## Where this leaves us

- Loop **mechanism**: ✅ proven
- Loop **as Forge's default engine**: ❌ not yet — `forge.ts` still runs the old pipeline. Wiring the loop in is the next bounded step, and should be proven against the pipeline before it replaces it.

Read-only by default; set allow_writes to\n# let it stage edits (still bounded by policy and the loop ceilings).\n\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      goal:\n        description: 'Mission goal for the loop (e.g. \"read package.json and report the test script\")'\n        required: true\n        default: 'List the repository files, then read README.md and summarize the project in one sentence.'\n      max_steps:\n        description: 'Maximum loop steps'\n        required: true\n        default: '6'\n      allow_writes:\n        description: 'Allow the loop to stage edits (requires a writable profile)'\n        type: boolean\n        required: false\n        default: false\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\njobs:\n  loop:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    timeout-minutes: 15\n    steps:\n      - name: Checkout Repository\n        uses: actions/checkout@v4\n\n      - name: Setup Node.js 22\n        uses: actions/setup-node@v4\n        with:\n          node-version: 22\n\n      - name: Install Dependencies\n        run: npm ci\n\n      - name: Run Forge loop\n        env:\n          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}\n          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}\n          FORGE_LOOP_GOAL: ${{ github.event.inputs.goal }}\n          FORGE_LOOP_MAX_STEPS: ${{ github.event.inputs.max_steps }}\n          FORGE_LOOP_REF: main\n          FORGE_ALLOW_PR_CREATION: ${{ github.event.inputs.allow_writes }}\n        run: npx tsx src/agent/loop-runner.ts\n\n      - name: Upload loop evidence\n        if: always()\n        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4\n        with:\n          name: forge-loop-evidence\n          path: .firstborn/evidence/\n          if-no-files-found: warn\n",

Read-only by default; set allow_writes to\n# let it stage edits (still bounded by policy and the loop ceilings).\n\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      goal:\n        description: 'Mission goal for the loop (e.g. \"read package.json and report the test script\")'\n        required: true\n        default: 'List the repository files, then read README.md and summarize the project in one sentence.'\n      max_steps:\n        description: 'Maximum loop steps'\n        required: true\n        default: '6'\n      allow_writes:\n        description: 'Allow the loop to stage edits (requires a writable profile)'\n        type: boolean\n        required: false\n        default: false\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\njobs:\n  loop:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    timeout-minutes: 15\n    steps:\n      - name: Checkout Repository\n        uses: actions/checkout@v4\n\n      - name: Setup Node.js 22\n        uses: actions/setup-node@v4\n        with:\n          node-version: 22\n\n      - name: Install Dependencies\n        run: npm ci\n\n      - name: Run Forge loop\n        env:\n          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}\n          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}\n          FORGE_LOOP_GOAL: ${{ github.event.inputs.goal }}\n          FORGE_LOOP_MAX_STEPS: ${{ github.event.inputs.max_steps }}\n          FORGE_LOOP_REF: main\n          FORGE_ALLOW_PR_CREATION: ${{ github.event.inputs.allow_writes }}\n        run: npx tsx src/agent/loop-runner.ts\n\n      - name: Upload loop evidence\n        if: always()\n        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4\n        with:\n          name: forge-loop-evidence\n          path: .firstborn/evidence/\n          if-no-files-found: warn\n",

'').trim();\n  if (!goal) throw new Error('FORGE_LOOP_GOAL is required (the mission objective).');\n\n  const targetRepo = (process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY ?? 'madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn').trim();\n  const [owner, repo] = targetRepo.split('/');\n  if (!owner || !repo) throw new Error(`GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be owner/repo, got \"${targetRepo}\".`);\n  const ref = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_REF ?? 'main').trim();\n  const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;\n  const consented = ['1', 'true', 'yes', 'on'].includes((process.env.FORGE_ALLOW_PR_CREATION ?? '').trim().toLowerCase());\n\n  const branch = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_BRANCH ?? 'forge/task-loop').trim();\n  const policy = evaluatePermissionPolicy(\n    {\n      requestedPrCreation: consented,\n      branchName: branch,\n      targetBranch: 'main',\n      repo: `${owner}/${repo}`,\n    },\n    loadPermissionConfig()\n  );\n\n  const tools = buildForgeTools({ owner, repo, ref, token, allowMutation: policy.allowBranchWrite });\n  const model = new ModelService();\n\n  const authorize: Authorization = (action) => {\n    if (!policy.allowBranchWrite) {\n      return { allowed: false, reason: `profile '${policy.effectiveProfile}' does not permit mutations` };\n    }\n    return { allowed: true };\n  };\n\n  const result = await runAgentLoop({\n    goal,\n    tools,\n    brain: (state) => model.chooseNextAction(state),\n    authorize,\n    limits: loadLoopLimits(),\n    workspace: branch,\n    onStep: (step) => {\n      console.log(`[loop ${step.index}] ${step.action.tool} -> ${step.observation.ok ? 'ok' : 'FAILED'}: ${step.observation.output.slice(0, 200)}`);\n    },\n  });\n\n  console.log('--- FORGE LOOP REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Goal:', goal);\n  console.log('Status:', result.status);\n  console.log('Steps:', result.steps.length);\n  console.log('Reason:', result.reason);\n\n  const evidenceDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  mkdirSync(evidenceDir, { recursive: true });\n  writeFileSync(\n    path.join(evidenceDir, 'forge-loop.json'),\n    JSON.stringify({ generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(), goal, status: result.status, steps: result.steps, reason: result.reason }, null, 2) + '\\n'\n  );\n\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((error) => {\n  console.error('[Forge loop] Failed:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

'').trim().toLowerCase());\n\n  const branch = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_BRANCH ?? 'forge/task-loop').trim();\n  const policy = evaluatePermissionPolicy(\n    {\n      requestedPrCreation: consented,\n      branchName: branch,\n      targetBranch: 'main',\n      repo: `${owner}/${repo}`,\n    },\n    loadPermissionConfig()\n  );\n\n  const tools = buildForgeTools({ owner, repo, ref, token, allowMutation: policy.allowBranchWrite });\n  const model = new ModelService();\n\n  const authorize: Authorization = (action) => {\n    if (!policy.allowBranchWrite) {\n      return { allowed: false, reason: `profile '${policy.effectiveProfile}' does not permit mutations` };\n    }\n    return { allowed: true };\n  };\n\n  const result = await runAgentLoop({\n    goal,\n    tools,\n    brain: (state) => model.chooseNextAction(state),\n    authorize,\n    limits: loadLoopLimits(),\n    workspace: branch,\n    onStep: (step) => {\n      console.log(`[loop ${step.index}] ${step.action.tool} -> ${step.observation.ok ? ## Forge vs. OpenHands — the capability gap

**Forge's whole toolset is four tools:**

| Tool | Kind |

### The four dimensions that separate them

1. **Tool breadth** — 4 vs. dozens. Forge can list, read, edit, and run an allowlisted check. It cannot search, grep, install, browse, or run arbitrary commands.
2. **Execution environment** — Forge runs in a **GitHub Actions runner** on one repo checkout and reads files through the GitHub API. 4. **Planning depth** — Forge's loop picks **one action at a time** with step/time ceilings. I keep a task list and can spawn sub-agents for parallel work.

### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `e12608fe-897e-4f14-988e-fc464b01f7fe` — 2026-10-13T15:08:21.057392

```
Got it — "general agent" (your voice-to-text mangled it twice, but I follow you). Here's what I mean, and what else OpenHands can do. I pulled this from the live docs so it's accurate, not vibes.

## What "general agent" means

A **general agent** is one system that can handle *many different kinds of tasks* because it has a broad toolset and reasons about which to use — rather than being hard-wired to one workflow.

- **Forge is a specialist.** It does one job: take a task, edit code in a repo, run checks, open a PR. Four tools. One pipeline. Bounded on purpose.
- **OpenHands is a generalist.** Same agent can debug a flaky test, write a migration, review a PR, triage an incident, or research an API — because it has a real computer and dozens of tools, and picks among them itself.

Same core loop (think → act → observe). The difference is **breadth of tools and freedom to choose**. That's the whole distinction.

## What OpenHands can actually do — by category

**1. Execution (the "real computer" part)**
Full shell/terminal, filesystem, run any code, install packages, browse the web. This is the biggest gap versus Forge.

**2. Tools**
Built-in tools, **custom tools** you write, **parallel tool execution**, and **structured output** (typed, validated fields). → [Custom Tools](https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/custom-tools.md)

**3. Extensibility — how you teach it new tricks**
- **Skills** — reusable instructions/knowledge that load on keywords, file paths, org, or globally → [Skills Overview](https://docs.openhands.dev/overview/skills.md)
- **MCP servers** — plug in external tools dynamically → [MCP](https://docs.openhands.dev/overview/model-context-protocol.md)
- **Hooks** — block dangerous commands, enforce checks before stopping, inject context → [Hooks](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/customization/hooks.md)
- **Plugins** — bundle skills + hooks + MCP + commands into one package → [Plugins](https://docs.openhands.dev/overview/plugins.md)

**4. Automations — running on its own**
- **Scheduled** (cron) and **event-based** (GitHub events, custom webhooks) → [Automations](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/automations/overview.md)
- **Software Factory** — four automations chaining an issue through dev → review → test → merge → [Software Factory](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/use-cases/software-factory.md)

**5. Integrations**
GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Slack, Discord, Linear, Jira, Notion, Datadog, Vercel — I have skills for each.

**6. Ways to run it**

/** Convert a glob (supports **, *, ?) to an anchored RegExp over repo paths. */
export function globToRegExp(pattern: string): RegExp {
  let re = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < pattern.length; i++) {
    const c = pattern[i];
    if (c === '*') {
      if (pattern[i+1] === '*') {
        // ** matches across path separators
        re += '.*';
        i++;
        if (pattern[i+1] === '/') i++; // consume slash after **
      } else {
        re += '[^/]*';
      }
    } else if (c === '?') re += '[^/]';
    else if ('\\^$.|+()[]{}'.includes(c)) re += '\\' + c;
    else re += c;
  }
  return new RegExp('^' + re + '$');
}
```

export interface GrepMatch { path: string; line: number; text: string }
export function grepText(path: string, content: string, pattern: RegExp, maxPerFile = 20): GrepMatch[] {
  const out: GrepMatch[] = [];
  const lines = content.split('\n');
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length && out.length < maxPerFile; i++) {
    if (pattern.test(lines[i])) out.push({ path, line: i+1, text: lines[i].slice(0, 300) });
  }
  return out;
}
```

export function htmlToText(html: string): string {
  return html
    .replace(/<script[\s\S]*?<\/script>/gi, '')
    .replace(/<style[\s\S]*?<\/style>/gi, '')
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ' ')
    .replace(/&nbsp;/g, ' ')  // minimal entities
    .replace(/&amp;/g,'&').replace(/&lt;/g,'<').replace(/&gt;/g,'>').replace(/&quot;/g,'"').replace(/&#39;/g,"'")
    .replace(/[ \t]+/g,' ')
    .replace(/\n\s*\n\s*\n+/g,'\n\n')
    .trim();
}

export function capText(text: string, max = 4000): string {
  return text.length <= max ? text : text.slice(0, max) + `\n... [truncated ${text.length - max} chars]`;
}

' (capped)' : ''}:\\n${matches.join('\\n')}`,\n        };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'find_files',\n      description:\n        'Find files by glob pattern, e.g. {\"glob\":\"src/**/*.ts\"} or {\"glob\":\"*.json\"}. Returns matching paths. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        if (!glob) return { ok: false, output: 'find_files requires a \"glob\".' };\n        const matcher = globToRegExp(glob);\n        const matches = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => matcher.test(p));\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No files match ${glob}.` };\n        return { ok: true, output: `${matches.length} file(s):\\n${matches.slice(0, 100).join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'think',\n      description:\n        'Record a reasoning step without changing anything (use to plan before acting). Mutation is allowed only when the caller consents\n * (allowPrCreation) AND the permission profile permits branch writes, so the loop\n * can never widen its own authority.\n */\nimport { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { ModelService } from '../services/model.ts';\nimport { loadPermissionConfig, evaluatePermissionPolicy } from './policy.ts';\nimport { buildForgeTools } from './tools.ts';\nimport { runAgentLoop, loadLoopLimits, FINISH_TOOL, type Authorization } from './loop.ts';\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const goal = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_GOAL ?? '').trim();\n  if (!goal) throw new Error('FORGE_LOOP_GOAL is required (the mission objective).');\n\n  const targetRepo = (process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY ?? 'madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn').trim();\n  const [owner, repo] = targetRepo.split('/');\n  if (!owner || !repo) throw new Error(`GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be owner/repo, got \"${targetRepo}\".`);\n  const ref = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_REF ?? 'main').trim();\n  const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;\n  const consented = ['1', 'true', 'yes', 'on'].includes((process.env.FORGE_ALLOW_PR_CREATION ?? '').trim().toLowerCase());\n\n  const branch = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_BRANCH ?? 'forge/task-loop').trim();\n  // Operate on the real checkout when present (CI checks the repo out here), so\n  // search/read/edit act on actual files and run_check can see installed deps.\n  const workspace = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_WORKSPACE ?? process.cwd()).trim();\n  const policy = evaluatePermissionPolicy(\n    {\n      requestedPrCreation: consented,\n      branchName: branch,\n      targetBranch: 'main',\n      repo: `${owner}/${repo}`,\n    },\n    loadPermissionConfig()\n  );\n\n  const tools = buildForgeTools({ owner, repo, ref, token, allowMutation: policy.allowBranchWrite, workspace });\n  const model = new ModelService();\n\n  const authorize: Authorization = (action) => {\n    if (!policy.allowBranchWrite) {\n      return { allowed: false, reason: `profile '${policy.effectiveProfile}' does not permit mutations` };\n    }\n    return { allowed: true };\n  };\n\n  const result = await runAgentLoop({\n    goal,\n    tools,\n    brain: (state) => model.chooseNextAction(state),\n    authorize,\n    limits: loadLoopLimits(),\n    workspace: branch,\n    onStep: (step) => {\n      console.log(`[loop ${step.index}] ${step.action.tool} -> ${step.observation.ok ? 'ok' : 'FAILED'}: ${step.observation.output.slice(0, 200)}`);\n    },\n  });\n\n  console.log('--- FORGE LOOP REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Goal:', goal);\n  console.log('Status:', result.status);\n  console.log('Steps:', result.steps.length);\n  console.log('Reason:', result.reason);\n\n  const evidenceDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  mkdirSync(evidenceDir, { recursive: true });\n  writeFileSync(\n    path.join(evidenceDir, 'forge-loop.json'),\n    JSON.stringify({ generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(), goal, status: result.status, steps: result.steps, reason: result.reason }, null, 2) + '\\n'\n  );\n\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((error) => {\n  console.error('[Forge loop] Failed:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

If a whole sweep fails for availability reasons,\n      // wait with backoff and sweep again, up to a hard deadline, so a prolonged\n      // 429 still returns an answer instead of failing the request.\n      const deadline = Date.now() + 90000;\n      for (let round = 0; round < 3; round++) {\n        if (round > 0) {\n          const waitMs = round === 1 ? 5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          primaryErrors.push(`retry round ${round + 1}: no route was ready in the previous sweep; waited ${waitMs}ms before retrying`);\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of ['chat:large', 'chat', 'chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat:best']) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await llm.chat(messages, {\n              model: alias,\n              temperature: 0.1,\n              max_tokens: 1024,\n              // Some top-tier keyless routes are reasoning models (e.g. the kilo\n              // nemotron route) that spend the whole 1024-token budget on hidden\n              // reasoning_content and return empty text with finish_reason=length.\n              // Disabling reasoning keeps the compact JSON answer within budget.\n              reasoning_effort: 'none',\n              signal: AbortSignal.timeout(40000),\n            });\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (!content) {\n              const finishReason = response.choices?.[0]?.finish_reason ?? 'unknown';\n              const detail = finishReason === 'length' ? 'output token budget was exhausted' : 'response contained no usable text';\n              primaryErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: ${detail} (finish_reason=${finishReason})`);\n              capabilityEscalation.push(`${alias}: ${detail}`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            // Prefer the finest model that actually answered: if we had to settle\n            // below the top capability tier, say so explicitly.\n            const triedTopTier = alias === 'chat:large' || alias === 'chat:best';\n            return {\n              text: content,\n              model: invokedModel,\n              provider: invokedProvider,\n              success: true,\n              fallbackUsed: false,\n              keylessRouteErrors: [\n                ...primaryErrors,\n                ...routingNotes,\n                ...(triedTopTier\n                  ? []\n                  : [`selected ${alias} (${invokedModel} via ${invokedProvider}) after stronger routes failed: ${capabilityEscalation.join(' | ') || 'none reported'}`]),\n              ],\n            };\n          } catch (err) {\n            const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            primaryErrors.push(`${alias}: ${errorMessage}`);\n            capabilityEscalation.push(`${alias}: ${errorMessage}`);\n          }\n        }\n        // An empty-text sweep is a content problem; waiting will not change it.\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? }\\n}\\n');\n  writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'src', 'app.ts'), 'export function greet(name: string) {\\n  return `hi ${name}`;\\n}\\n');\n  writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'src', 'util.ts'), 'export const VERSION = \"1.2.3\";\\n');\n  return dir;\n}\n\nfunction tools(workspace: string, allowMutation = false): AgentTool[] {\n  return buildForgeTools({ owner: 'o', repo: 'r', ref: 'main', workspace, allowMutation });\n}\n\nfunction byName(list: AgentTool[]): Map<string, AgentTool> {\n  return new Map(list.map((t) => [t.name, t]));\n}\n\nconst ctx: LoopContext = { goal: 'test', workspace: 'ws', step: 1 };\n\ntest('read-only toolset exposes the discovery tools and hides mutating ones', () => {\n  const names = tools(makeWorkspace()).map((t) => t.name).sort();\n  assert.deepEqual(names, assert.ok(!names.includes('run_check'));\n});\n\ntest('allowMutation adds the mutating tools', () => {\n  const names = tools(makeWorkspace(), true).map((t) => t.name).sort();\n  assert.ok(names.includes('edit_file'));\n  assert.ok(names.includes('write_file'));\n  assert.ok(names.includes('run_check'));\n});\n\ntest('list_files lists real workspace files', async () => {\n  const t = byName(tools(makeWorkspace()));\n  const obs = await t.get('list_files')!.run({}, ctx);\n  assert.equal(obs.ok, true);\n  assert.match(obs.output, /package\\.json/);\n  assert.match(obs.output, /src\\/app\\.ts/);\n});\n\ntest('read_file returns content, and reports a missing file', async () => {\n  const t = byName(tools(makeWorkspace()));\n  const found = await t.get('read_file')!.run({ path: 'src/util.ts' }, ctx);\n  assert.equal(found.ok, true);\n  assert.match(found.output, /VERSION/);\n  const missing = await t.get('read_file')!.run({ path: 'nope.ts' }, The loop kernel never knows about GitHub or npm;\n * it only calls these tools by name.\n *\n * Capability tiers:\n *  - read-only tools (list_files, read_file, search, find_files, think, fetch_url)\n *    are always available;\n *  - mutating tools (edit_file, write_file, run_check) are only registered when the\n *    permission profile permits branch writes, so the brain cannot even see a\n *    state-changing capability it is not permitted to use.\n *\n * File tools prefer the mission workspace when one exists (so edits can be made and\n * then verified), and fall back to reading the repository through GitHub.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService, AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport type { AgentTool, LoopContext, ToolObservation } from './loop.ts';\n\nfunction str(input: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = input[key];\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\nfunction walkFiles(root: string): string[] {\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const stack = [''];\n  while (stack.length && out.length < MAX_SCAN_FILES) {\n    const rel = stack.pop() as string;\n    const abs = path.join(root, rel);\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;\n      const childRel = rel ? path.join(rel, entry.name) : entry.name;\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) stack.push(childRel);\n      else if (entry.isFile()) out.push(childRel.split(path.sep).join('/'));\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {\n  const escaped = glob.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n  const pattern = escaped\n    .replace(/\\*\\*/g, '\\u0000')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '[^/]*')\n    .replace(/\\u0000/g, '.*')\n    .replace(/\\?/g, '.');\n  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. Mutating tools are enabled only when `allowMutation` is\n * true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain cannot even see a state-changing\n * capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  /** Absolute path to the mission workspace, when one exists. */\n  workspace?: string;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n      if (!safe) return null;\n      const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await listPaths();\n        if (files.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'No files found.' };\n        const shown = files.slice(0, 80);\n        return { ok: true, output: `${files.length} files total. First ${shown.length}:\\n${shown.join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read one file by exact repository path. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'read_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `File not found: ${rel}` };\n        return { ok: true, output: content.slice(0, MAX_FILE_BYTES) };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'search',\n      description:\n        'Search file contents by regular expression (like grep). Input: {\"pattern\":\"...\", \"glob\":\"*.ts\" (optional)}. Returns matching file:line: text. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const pattern = str(input, 'pattern');\n        if (!pattern) return { ok: false, output: 'search requires a \"pattern\" (regular expression).' };\n        let re: RegExp;\n        try {\n          re = new RegExp(pattern, 'i');\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Invalid pattern: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        }\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        const matcher = glob ? globToRegExp(glob) : null;\n        const paths = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        const matches: string[] = [];\n        let scanned = 0;\n        for (const rel of paths) {\n          if (matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES || scanned >= MAX_SCAN_FILES) break;\n          scanned += 1;\n          const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n          if (content === null) continue;\n          const lines = content.split('\\n');\n          for (let i = 0; i < lines.length && matches.length < MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES; i += 1) {\n            if (re.test(lines[i])) matches.push(`${rel}:${i + 1}: ${lines[i].trim().slice(0, 200)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No matches for /${pattern}/ in ${paths.length} file(s).` };\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          output: `${matches.length} match(es)${matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES ? ' (capped)' : ''}:\\n${matches.join('\\n')}`,\n        };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'find_files',\n      description:\n        'Find files by glob pattern, e.g. {\"glob\":\"src/**/*.ts\"} or {\"glob\":\"*.json\"}. Returns matching paths. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        if (!glob) return { ok: false, output: 'find_files requires a \"glob\".' };\n        const matcher = globToRegExp(glob);\n        const matches = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => matcher.test(p));\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No files match ${glob}.` };\n        return { ok: true, output: `${matches.length} file(s):\\n${matches.slice(0, 100).join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'think',\n      description:\n        'Record a reasoning step without changing anything (use to plan before acting). Input: {\"thought\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const thought = str(input, 'thought');\n        if (!thought) return { ok: false, output: 'think requires a \"thought\".' };\n        return { ok: true, output: `Noted: ${thought.slice(0, 1000)}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'fetch_url',\n      description:\n        'Fetch the text of an http(s) URL (e.g. docs, a raw file). Input: {\"url\":\"https://...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!/^https?:\\/\\//i.test(url)) return { ok: false, output: 'fetch_url requires an http(s) \"url\".' };\n        const controller = new AbortController();\n        const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15_000);\n        try {\n          const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, headers: { 'user-agent': 'forge-agent' } });\n          const text = await res.text();\n          return { ok: res.ok, output: `HTTP ${res.status}\\n${text.slice(0, 20_000)}` };\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Fetch failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        } finally {\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (options.allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description:\n        'Apply exact-anchor edits to a file. Each \"find\" must occur exactly once. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"edits\":[{\"find\":\"...\",\"replace\":\"...\"}]}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const rawEdits = Array.isArray(input.edits) ? input.edits : [];\n        const edits = rawEdits.filter(\n          (e): e is { find: string; replace: string } =>\n            Boolean(e) && typeof (e as any).find === 'string' && typeof (e as any).replace === 'string'\n        );\n        if (!rel || edits.length === 0) {\n          return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires \"path\" and a non-empty \"edits\" array of {find, replace}.' };\n        }\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `Cannot edit missing file: ${rel}` };\n        const result = applyExactEdits(content, edits);\n        if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, output: `Edit rejected: ${result.error}` };\n        if (ws) {\n          const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n          if (!safe) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n          const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, result.content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Applied ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n        }\n        // No workspace: the pipeline stages the change later through the PR path.\n        return { ok: true, output: `Staged ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Mutating (may install/build).`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const command = str(input, 'command');\n        if (!command) return { ok: false, output: 'run_check requires a \"command\".' };\n        const cwd = ws ?? ctx.workspace ?? process.cwd();\n        const result = await runner.runCheck(command, cwd);\n        return {\n          ok: result.status === 'PASSED',\n          output: `exit=${result.exitCode} status=${result.status}\\n${result.stdout}\\n${result.stderr}`.slice(0, 4000),\n        };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n",

 "old_content": "/**\n * M2 — Tools for the agent loop.\n *\n * Thin adapters over Forge's existing services (GitHubService, TestRunnerService)\n * plus a bounded local workspace. The loop kernel never knows about GitHub or npm;\n * it only calls these tools by name.\n *\n * Capability tiers:\n *  - read-only tools (list_files, read_file, search, find_files, think, fetch_url)\n *    are always available;\n *  - mutating tools (edit_file, write_file, run_check) are only registered when the\n *    permission profile permits branch writes, so the brain cannot even see a\n *    state-changing capability it is not permitted to use.\n *\n * File tools prefer the mission workspace when one exists (so edits can be made and\n * then verified), and fall back to reading the repository through GitHub.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService, AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport type { AgentTool, LoopContext, ToolObservation } from './loop.ts';\n\nfunction str(input: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = input[key];\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\nfunction walkFiles(root: string): string[] {\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const stack = [''];\n  while (stack.length && out.length < MAX_SCAN_FILES) {\n    const rel = stack.pop() as string;\n    const abs = path.join(root, rel);\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;\n      const childRel = rel ? path.join(rel, entry.name) : entry.name;\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) stack.push(childRel);\n      else if (entry.isFile()) out.push(childRel.split(path.sep).join('/'));\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {\n  const escaped = glob.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n  const pattern = escaped\n    .replace(/\\*\\*\\//g, '\\u0001')\n    .replace(/\\*\\*/g, '\\u0000')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '[^/]*')\n    .replace(/\\?/g, '.')\n    .replace(/\\u0001/g, '(?:.*/)?')\n    .replace(/\\u0000/g, '.*');\n  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. Mutating tools are enabled only when `allowMutation` is\n * true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain cannot even see a state-changing\n * capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  /** Absolute path to the mission workspace, when one exists. */\n  workspace?: string;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n      if (!safe) return null;\n      const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await listPaths();\n        if (files.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'No files found.' };\n        const shown = files.slice(0, 80);\n        return { ok: true, output: `${files.length} files total. First ${shown.length}:\\n${shown.join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read one file by exact repository path. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'read_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `File not found: ${rel}` };\n        return { ok: true, output: content.slice(0, MAX_FILE_BYTES) };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'search',\n      description:\n        'Search file contents by regular expression (like grep). Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const pattern = str(input, 'pattern');\n        if (!pattern) return { ok: false, output: 'search requires a \"pattern\" (regular expression).' };\n        let re: RegExp;\n        try {\n          re = new RegExp(pattern, 'i');\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Invalid pattern: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        }\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        const matcher = glob ? globToRegExp(glob) : null;\n        const paths = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        const matches: string[] = [];\n        let scanned = 0;\n        for (const rel of paths) {\n          if (matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES || scanned >= MAX_SCAN_FILES) break;\n          scanned += 1;\n          const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n          if (content === null) continue;\n          const lines = content.split('\\n');\n          for (let i = 0; i < lines.length && matches.length < MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES; i += 1) {\n            if (re.test(lines[i])) matches.push(`${rel}:${i + 1}: ${lines[i].trim().slice(0, 200)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No matches for /${pattern}/ in ${paths.length} file(s).` };\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          output: `${matches.length} match(es)${matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES ? ' (capped)' : ''}:\\n${matches.join('\\n')}`,\n        };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'find_files',\n      description:\n        'Find files by glob pattern, e.g. {\"glob\":\"src/**/*.ts\"} or {\"glob\":\"*.json\"}. Returns matching paths. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        if (!glob) return { ok: false, output: 'find_files requires a \"glob\".' };\n        const matcher = globToRegExp(glob);\n        const matches = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => matcher.test(p));\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No files match ${glob}.` };\n        return { ok: true, output: `${matches.length} file(s):\\n${matches.slice(0, 100).join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'think',\n      description:\n        'Record a reasoning step without changing anything (use to plan before acting). Input: {\"thought\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const thought = str(input, 'thought');\n        if (!thought) return { ok: false, output: 'think requires a \"thought\".' };\n        return { ok: true, output: `Noted: ${thought.slice(0, 1000)}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'fetch_url',\n      description:\n        'Fetch the text of an http(s) URL (e.g. docs, a raw file). Input: {\"url\":\"https://...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!/^https?:\\/\\//i.test(url)) return { ok: false, output: 'fetch_url requires an http(s) \"url\".' };\n        const controller = new AbortController();\n        const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15_000);\n        try {\n          const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, headers: { 'user-agent': 'forge-agent' } });\n          const text = await res.text();\n          return { ok: res.ok, output: `HTTP ${res.status}\\n${text.slice(0, 20_000)}` };\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Fetch failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        } finally {\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (options.allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description:\n        'Apply exact-anchor edits to a file. Each \"find\" must occur exactly once. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"edits\":[{\"find\":\"...\",\"replace\":\"...\"}]}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const rawEdits = Array.isArray(input.edits) ? input.edits : [];\n        const edits = rawEdits.filter(\n          (e): e is { find: string; replace: string } =>\n            Boolean(e) && typeof (e as any).find === 'string' && typeof (e as any).replace === 'string'\n        );\n        if (!rel || edits.length === 0) {\n          return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires \"path\" and a non-empty \"edits\" array of {find, replace}.' };\n        }\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `Cannot edit missing file: ${rel}` };\n        const result = applyExactEdits(content, edits);\n        if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, output: `Edit rejected: ${result.error}` };\n        if (ws) {\n          const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n          if (!safe) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n          const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, result.content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Applied ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n        }\n        // No workspace: the pipeline stages the change later through the PR path.\n        return { ok: true, output: `Staged ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"content\":\"...\"}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const content = typeof input.content === 'string' ? input.content : '';\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'write_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        if (!ws) return { ok: false, output: 'No workspace available; cannot write files.' };\n        const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n        if (!safe) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n        writeFileSync(abs, content);\n        return { ok: true, output: `Wrote ${content.length} byte(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'run_check',\n      description: `Run an authorized verification command. Allowed commands: ${Object.keys(AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS).join(\n        ', '\n      )}. Mutating (may install/build).`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const command = str(input, 'command');\n        if (!command) return { ok: false, output: 'run_check requires a \"command\".' };\n        const cwd = ws ?? ctx.workspace ?? process.cwd();\n        const result = await runner.runCheck(command, cwd);\n        return {\n          ok: result.status === 'PASSED',\n          output: `exit=${result.exitCode} status=${result.status}\\n${result.stdout}\\n${result.stderr}`.slice(0, 4000),\n        };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n",

The loop kernel never knows about GitHub or npm;\n * it only calls these tools by name.\n *\n * Capability tiers:\n *  - read-only tools (list_files, read_file, search, find_files, think, fetch_url)\n *    are always available;\n *  - mutating tools (edit_file, write_file, run_check) are only registered when the\n *    permission profile permits branch writes, so the brain cannot even see a\n *    state-changing capability it is not permitted to use.\n *\n * File tools prefer the mission workspace when one exists (so edits can be made and\n * then verified), and fall back to reading the repository through GitHub.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService, AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport type { AgentTool, LoopContext, ToolObservation } from './loop.ts';\n\nfunction str(input: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = input[key];\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\nfunction walkFiles(root: string): string[] {\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const stack = [''];\n  while (stack.length && out.length < MAX_SCAN_FILES) {\n    const rel = stack.pop() as string;\n    const abs = path.join(root, rel);\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;\n      const childRel = rel ? path.join(rel, entry.name) : entry.name;\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) stack.push(childRel);\n      else if (entry.isFile()) out.push(childRel.split(path.sep).join('/'));\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {\n  const escaped = glob.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n  const pattern = escaped\n    .replace(/\\*\\*\\//g, '\\u0001')\n    .replace(/\\*\\*/g, '\\u0000')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '[^/]*')\n    .replace(/\\?/g, '.')\n    .replace(/\\u0001/g, '(?:.*/)?')\n    .replace(/\\u0000/g, '.*');\n  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);\n}\n\n/** `*`, `**`, and `**/*` are the common \"everything\" shorthands; treat them as all files. */\nfunction matchesAll(glob: string): boolean {\n  const g = glob.trim();\n  return g === '' || g === '*' || g === '**' || g === '**/*';\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. Mutating tools are enabled only when `allowMutation` is\n * true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain cannot even see a state-changing\n * capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  /** Absolute path to the mission workspace, when one exists. */\n  workspace?: string;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n      if (!safe) return null;\n      const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await listPaths();\n        if (files.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'No files found.' };\n        const shown = files.slice(0, 80);\n        return { ok: true, output: `${files.length} files total. First ${shown.length}:\\n${shown.join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read one file by exact repository path. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'read_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `File not found: ${rel}` };\n        return { ok: true, output: content.slice(0, MAX_FILE_BYTES) };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'search',\n      description:\n        'Search file contents by regular expression (like grep). Input: {\"pattern\":\"...\", \"glob\":\"*.ts\" (optional)}. Returns matching file:line: text. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const pattern = str(input, 'pattern');\n        if (!pattern) return { ok: false, output: 'search requires a \"pattern\" (regular expression).' };\n        let re: RegExp;\n        try {\n          re = new RegExp(pattern, 'i');\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Invalid pattern: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        }\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        const matcher = glob && !matchesAll(glob) ? globToRegExp(glob) : null;\n        const paths = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        const matches: string[] = [];\n        let scanned = 0;\n        for (const rel of paths) {\n          if (matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES || scanned >= MAX_SCAN_FILES) break;\n          scanned += 1;\n          const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n          if (content === null) continue;\n          const lines = content.split('\\n');\n          for (let i = 0; i < lines.length && matches.length < MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES; i += 1) {\n            if (re.test(lines[i])) matches.push(`${rel}:${i + 1}: ${lines[i].trim().slice(0, 200)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No matches for /${pattern}/ in ${paths.length} file(s).` };\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          output: `${matches.length} match(es)${matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES ? ' (capped)' : ''}:\\n${matches.join('\\n')}`,\n        };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'find_files',\n      description:\n        'Find files by glob pattern, e.g. {\"glob\":\"src/**/*.ts\"} or {\"glob\":\"*.json\"}. Returns matching paths. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        if (!glob) return { ok: false, output: 'find_files requires a \"glob\".' };\n        const matcher = matchesAll(glob) ? null : globToRegExp(glob);\n        const matches = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No files match ${glob}.` };\n        return { ok: true, output: `${matches.length} file(s):\\n${matches.slice(0, 100).join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'think',\n      description:\n        'Record a reasoning step without changing anything (use to plan before acting). Input: {\"thought\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const thought = str(input, 'thought');\n        if (!thought) return { ok: false, output: 'think requires a \"thought\".' };\n        return { ok: true, output: `Noted: ${thought.slice(0, 1000)}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'fetch_url',\n      description:\n        'Fetch the text of an http(s) URL (e.g. docs, a raw file). Input: {\"url\":\"https://...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!/^https?:\\/\\//i.test(url)) return { ok: false, output: 'fetch_url requires an http(s) \"url\".' };\n        const controller = new AbortController();\n        const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15_000);\n        try {\n          const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, headers: { 'user-agent': 'forge-agent' } });\n          const text = await res.text();\n          return { ok: res.ok, output: `HTTP ${res.status}\\n${text.slice(0, 20_000)}` };\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Fetch failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        } finally {\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (options.allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description:\n        'Apply exact-anchor edits to a file. Each \"find\" must occur exactly once. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"edits\":[{\"find\":\"...\",\"replace\":\"...\"}]}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const rawEdits = Array.isArray(input.edits) ? input.edits : [];\n        const edits = rawEdits.filter(\n          (e): e is { find: string; replace: string } =>\n            Boolean(e) && typeof (e as any).find === 'string' && typeof (e as any).replace === 'string'\n        );\n        if (!rel || edits.length === 0) {\n          return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires \"path\" and a non-empty \"edits\" array of {find, replace}.' };\n        }\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `Cannot edit missing file: ${rel}` };\n        const result = applyExactEdits(content, edits);\n        if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, output: `Edit rejected: ${result.error}` };\n        if (ws) {\n          const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n          if (!safe) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n          const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, result.content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Applied ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n        }\n        // No workspace: the pipeline stages the change later through the PR path.\n        return { ok: true, output: `Staged ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"content\":\"...\"}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const content = typeof input.content === 'string' ? input.content : '';\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'write_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        if (!ws) return { ok: false, output: 'No workspace available; cannot write files.' };\n        const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n        if (!safe) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n        writeFileSync(abs, content);\n        return { ok: true, output: `Wrote ${content.length} byte(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'run_check',\n      description: `Run an authorized verification command. Allowed commands: ${Object.keys(AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS).join(\n        ', '\n      )}. Mutating (may install/build).`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const command = str(input, 'command');\n        if (!command) return { ok: false, output: 'run_check requires a \"command\".' };\n        const cwd = ws ?? ctx.workspace ?? process.cwd();\n        const result = await runner.runCheck(command, cwd);\n        return {\n          ok: result.status === 'PASSED',\n          output: `exit=${result.exitCode} status=${result.status}\\n${result.stdout}\\n${result.stderr}`.slice(0, 4000),\n        };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n",

If a whole sweep fails for availability reasons,\n      // wait with backoff and sweep again, up to a hard deadline, so a prolonged\n      // 429 still returns an answer instead of failing the request.\n      const deadline = Date.now() + 90000;\n      for (let round = 0; round < 3; round++) {\n        if (round > 0) {\n          const waitMs = round === 1 ? 5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          primaryErrors.push(`retry round ${round + 1}: no route was ready in the previous sweep; waited ${waitMs}ms before retrying`);\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of ['chat:large', 'chat', 'chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat:best']) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await llm.chat(messages, {\n              model: alias,\n              temperature: 0.1,\n              max_tokens: 1024,\n              // Some top-tier keyless routes are reasoning models (e.g. the kilo\n              // nemotron route) that spend the whole 1024-token budget on hidden\n              // reasoning_content and return empty text with finish_reason=length.\n              // Disabling reasoning keeps the compact JSON answer within budget.\n              reasoning_effort: 'none',\n              signal: AbortSignal.timeout(40000),\n            });\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (!content) {\n              const finishReason = response.choices?.[0]?.finish_reason ?? 'unknown';\n              const detail = finishReason === 'length' ? 'output token budget was exhausted' : 'response contained no usable text';\n              primaryErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: ${detail} (finish_reason=${finishReason})`);\n              capabilityEscalation.push(`${alias}: ${detail}`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            // Prefer the finest model that actually answered: if we had to settle\n            // below the top capability tier, say so explicitly.\n            const triedTopTier = alias === 'chat:large' || alias === 'chat:best';\n            return {\n              text: content,\n              model: invokedModel,\n              provider: invokedProvider,\n              success: true,\n              fallbackUsed: false,\n              keylessRouteErrors: [\n                ...primaryErrors,\n                ...routingNotes,\n                ...(triedTopTier\n                  ? []\n                  : [`selected ${alias} (${invokedModel} via ${invokedProvider}) after stronger routes failed: ${capabilityEscalation.join(' | ') || 'none reported'}`]),\n              ],\n            };\n          } catch (err) {\n            const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            primaryErrors.push(`${alias}: ${errorMessage}`);\n            capabilityEscalation.push(`${alias}: ${errorMessage}`);\n          }\n        }\n        // An empty-text sweep is a content problem; waiting will not change it.\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n        return {\n          text: '',\n          model: 'auto:coding -> gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'keyless model routes + Gemini fallback',\n          success: false,\n          error: `Primary keyless route failed: ${primaryError}; Gemini fallback failed: ${fallbackError}`,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          keylessRouteErrors: [...primaryErrors],\n        };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return {\n      text: '',\n      model: 'chat:large',\n      provider: 'keyless model routes unavailable',\n      success: false,\n      error: `All keyless primary routes failed: ${primaryError}. ${isKeylessOnly() ? Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!/^https?:\\/\\//i.test(url)) return { ok: false, output: 'fetch_url requires an http(s) \"url\".' };\n        const controller = new AbortController();\n        const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15_000);\n        try {\n          const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, headers: { 'user-agent': 'forge-agent' } });\n          const text = await res.text();\n          return { ok: res.ok, output: `HTTP ${res.status}\\n${text.slice(0, 20_000)}` };\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Fetch failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        } finally {\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (options.allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description:\n        'Apply exact-anchor edits to a file. Each \"find\" must occur exactly once. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"edits\":[{\"find\":\"...\",\"replace\":\"...\"}]}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const rawEdits = Array.isArray(input.edits) ? input.edits : [];\n        const edits = rawEdits.filter(\n          (e): e is { find: string; replace: string } =>\n            Boolean(e) && typeof (e as any).find === 'string' && typeof (e as any).replace === 'string'\n        );\n        if (!rel || edits.length === 0) {\n          return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires \"path\" and a non-empty \"edits\" array of {find, replace}.' };\n        }\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `Cannot edit missing file: ${rel}` };\n        const result = applyExactEdits(content, edits);\n        if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, output: `Edit rejected: ${result.error}` };\n        if (ws) {\n          const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n          if (!safe) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n          const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, result.content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Applied ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n        }\n        // No workspace: the pipeline stages the change later through the PR path.\n        return { ok: true, output: `Staged ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"content\":\"...\"}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const content = typeof input.content === 'string' ? input.content : '';\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'write_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        if (!ws) return { ok: false, output: 'No workspace available; cannot write files.' };\n        const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n        if (!safe) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n        writeFileSync(abs, content);\n        return { ok: true, output: `Wrote ${content.length} byte(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'run_check',\n      description: `Run an authorized verification command. Allowed commands: ${Object.keys(AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS).join(\n        ', '\n      )}. Mutating (may install/build).`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const command = str(input, 'command');\n        if (!command) return { ok: false, output: 'run_check requires a \"command\".' };\n        const cwd = ws ?? ctx.workspace ?? process.cwd();\n        const result = await runner.runCheck(command, cwd);\n        return {\n          ok: result.status === 'PASSED',\n          output: `exit=${result.exitCode} status=${result.status}\\n${result.stdout}\\n${result.stderr}`.slice(0, 4000),\n        };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n",
 "kind": "FileEditorObservation"
}

```
{
 "data": {
  "repo_name": "madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn",
  "source_branch": "forge/task-tools-expand",
  "target_branch": "main",
  "title": "feat(tools): give the loop real discovery and workspace tools (4 → 9)",
  "body": "## What this does\n\nExpands the Forge loop toolset from **4 tools to 9**, so the loop can actually navigate a repository and act on a real checkout — closing most of the tool gap with a general agent.\n\n### New tools\n\n| Tool | Kind | What it does |\n|---|---|---|\n| `search` | read | Regex grep over file contents, returns `file:line: text` |\n| `find_files` | read | Glob-based path search (`**/` handling; `*` = all files) |\n| `think` | read | A no-op planning step (plan before acting) |\n| `fetch_url` | read | Read docs / raw files over http(s) |\n| `write_file` | mutate | Create or overwrite a file in the workspace |\n\n### Changed behavior\n\n- `read_file` / `edit_file` / `run_check` now **prefer the mission workspace** and fall back to GitHub. Edits are written to disk, so they can be verified by a follow-up read or check.\n- Path guards reject absolute and `..` traversal; file sizes and match counts are capped.\n- Mutating tools (`edit_file`, `write_file`, `run_check`) stay **hidden** unless the permission profile allows branch writes — the brain can't see a capability it can't use.\n- Runner passes a workspace (`FORGE_LOOP_WORKSPACE`, defaults to the checkout); `run_check` runs there.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `npm run lint` → **EXIT 0**\n- `npm test` → **93 passed / 0 failed** (new `tests/tools.test.ts`, 14 cases, run against a real temp workspace — no mocks)\n- **Live run 1**: search for `AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS` → **COMPLETED in 2 steps**, correct `file:line` hits\n- **Live run 2**: edit `src/math.ts` (41 → 42) → **COMPLETED in 4 steps**; file on disk reads `42`\n\n## Two bugs the tests caught and I fixed\n\n1. `**/` didn't match zero directories (`src/**/*.ts` missed `src/app.ts`).\n2. A bare `*` glob matched only top-level files, so the model's `glob:\"*\"` silently searched 13 of 61 files. Now `*` / `**` / `**/*` mean all files, and the brain prompt explains it.\n\n_This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Ahmed._",
  "labels": [
   "enhancement"
  ]
 },
 "kind": "MCPToolAction"
}
```
