The anti-repeat\nguard also covers `browser_view`, `browser_extract`, and `browser_scroll`, so a\nrepeated identical read can never burn the step budget.\n\n---\n\n## 3. As a library\n\n```ts\nimport { BrowserService } from './src/services/browser.ts';\n\nconst browser = new BrowserService();\nconst snap = await browser.open('https://example.com');\nconsole.log(snap.title, snap.elements);\n\nawait browser.click(0);          // click element [0]\nawait browser.type(1, 'hello');  // type into element [1]\nawait browser.press('Enter');\nawait browser.scroll('down');\nconsole.log(await browser.extract('price'));\nawait browser.close();\n```\n\n`BrowserSnapshot` = `{ url, title, elements, text }`, where each element is\n`{ i, tag, type?, text, href? }`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. As an MCP server\n\nForreyra runs as a **Model Context Protocol** server over stdio, so any MCP client\n(Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, the OpenHands agent) can drive the browser with\nthe same look-then-act model.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra:mcp\n```\n\nIt exposes nine tools: `browser_open`, `browser_view`, `browser_click`,\n`browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_extract`,\n`browser_screenshot` (returns a PNG image), `browser_close`.\n\n### Client configuration\n\nClaude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"forreyra\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"tsx\", \"src/mcp/forreyra-server.ts\"],\n      \"cwd\": \"/absolute/path/to/Firstborn\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nCursor / VS Code use the same `command` + `args` + `cwd` shape.\n\n### Verify the connection\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/mcp-client-smoke.mjs\n```\n\nThis uses the official MCP client SDK to connect, list the tools, open\n`https://example.com`, and close.\n\n---\n\n## Setup\n\n- Chromium is auto-detected at `/usr/bin/chromium`, `/usr/bin/chromium-browser`,\n  or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`. To point at a specific binary, set\n  `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/path/to/chrome`.\n- Installed with the repo: `npm install` (the `playwright` package).\n- Headless by default. Runs with `--no-sandbox` and `--disable-dev-shm-usage` so\n  it works in CI containers.\n\n## How it behaves\n\n- **One browser per session.** A page opened once stays open for later actions.\n- **Look, then act.** Every action returns a fresh snapshot, mirroring how a\n  person re-reads a page after each step.\n- **Basic stealth.** A real Chrome user agent and the `navigator.webdriver` flag\n  hidden at start.\n\n## Limits\n\n- Interactive elements are the standard clickable/typable set (`a`, `button`,\n  `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `[role=button]`, `[onclick]`, `[contenteditable]`),\n  capped at 120 per view.\n- Page text is capped at 4000 characters per snapshot.\n- No persistent profile or cookie jar across runs yet — each run starts clean.\n\n## Tests\n\n`tests/browser.test.ts` drives a real headless Chromium against a real local HTTP\nserver (no mocks) and covers open, type-then-submit, click-through navigation, and\nregex extract.\n\n```bash\nnpm test\n```\n",

  "body": "## What this does\n\nExposes **Forreyra** over the **Model Context Protocol** (stdio), so any MCP client — Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, the OpenHands agent — can drive a real Chromium session with the same look-then-act model as the CLI and the agent tools.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra:mcp\n```\n\n## Tools exposed\n\n`browser_open`, `browser_view`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_extract`, `browser_screenshot` (returns a real PNG image block), `browser_close`.\n\nBuilt on `McpServer` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` + zod input schemas, reusing `BrowserService` — no new browser logic.\n\n## Client config\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"forreyra\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"tsx\", \"src/mcp/forreyra-server.ts\"],\n      \"cwd\": \"/absolute/path/to/Firstborn\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `npm run lint` → **EXIT 0**; `npm test` → **113 passed / 0 failed** (+6 MCP tests).\n- `tests/mcp.test.ts` **spawns the real server and speaks real stdio JSON-RPC**, then drives a real headless Chromium against a real local HTTP server: initialize handshake, `tools/list`, `browser_open`, `browser_extract`, `browser_screenshot` (asserts PNG bytes), `browser_close`.\n- **Interop proof with the official SDK:** `node scripts/mcp-client-smoke.mjs` connected with `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client`, listed all nine tools, and opened `https://example.com` → *Example Domain*. Output: `OFFICIAL CLIENT OK`.\n\n_This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Ahmed._",

### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `c901dbf7-8b0f-46ae-9145-96f67eba4509` — 2026-10-13T16:30:12.167094

```
Done — the MCP server is built, verified, and merged. Forreyra now plugs into any MCP client.

## Shipped: **[#79](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn/pull/79)** (`ac2c042`)

`npm run forreyra:mcp` starts a **Model Context Protocol** server over stdio. Any MCP client — Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, the OpenHands agent — can now drive a real Chromium session with the same look-then-act model as the CLI.

### Tools exposed (9)
`browser_open` · `browser_view` · `browser_click` · `browser_type` · `browser_press` · `browser_scroll` · `browser_extract` · `browser_screenshot` (returns a real PNG image block) · `browser_close`

Built on `McpServer` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` with zod input schemas, reusing `BrowserService` — no duplicated browser logic.

### Client config
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "forreyra": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["tsx", "src/mcp/forreyra-server.ts"],
      "cwd": "/absolute/path/to/Firstborn"
    }
  }
}
```
Documented in `FORREYRA.md` §4, with `node scripts/mcp-client-smoke.mjs` to verify the connection.

### Proof (real, not claimed)
- `tests/mcp.test.ts` **spawns the actual server and speaks real stdio JSON-RPC**, then drives a real headless Chromium against a real local HTTP server — initialize handshake, `tools/list`, `browser_open`, `browser_extract`, `browser_screenshot` (asserts real PNG bytes), `browser_close`.
- **Interop with the official SDK:** `node scripts/mcp-client-smoke.mjs` connected via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client`, listed all nine tools, opened `https://example.com` → *Example Domain* → `OFFICIAL CLIENT OK`.
- CI: verify + sentinel success, **113 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped** — I pulled the job log to confirm the MCP tests actually executed.

### Where this leaves Forreyra
Four ways in, one engine: **CLI** → **agent tools** → **library** → **MCP server**.

Next rung for the TinyFish-style mission would be **natural-language extraction** — ask for "the price" instead of a regex — so the MCP tool can return structured data, not just page text. Want me to start there?

Now I'll build a deterministic NL query planner. Design: pure module `src/services/query.ts` that:
- `planQuery(query: string): QueryPlan` — classify into a kind + params.
- `runQuery(data: PageData, plan: QueryPlan): QueryResult` — resolve to structured matches.

PageData collected from the DOM: title, headings (h1-h3), links ({text, href}), text, tables (rows), labeled fields (label + input value?), emails/phones/prices via regex over text.

Kinds:
- title: page title
- headings: list headings (optionally filtered by keyword)
- links: list links (optionally filtered by keyword, e.g. "links about docs")
- emails: regex emails
- phones: regex phones
- prices: regex currency amounts
- table: first table as rows (optionally the table matching a keyword)
- count: count of something
- text/search: sentences matching keywords
- labeled: "the value of <label>" → find label text then nearby input value or sibling text
- meta: description

Let me design it cleanly and deterministically:

```ts
export type QueryKind =
  | 'title' | 'headings' | 'links' | 'emails' | 'phones' | 'prices'
  | 'table' | 'count' | 'labeled' | 'search';

export interface QueryPlan { kind: QueryKind; term?: string; raw: string; }
export interface QueryMatch { value: string; context?: string; href?: string; }
export interface QueryResult { kind: QueryKind; query: string; matches: QueryMatch[]; note?: string; }
export interface PageData {
  url: string; title: string; text: string;
  headings: string[];
  links: { text: string; href: string }[];
  tables: string[][][]; // list of tables, each a list of rows (cells)
  fields: { label: string; value: string }[];
}
```

Planner rules (ordered):
- /^\s*(title|page title|what.*title)/ → title
- headings: "headings", "sections", "headers"
- links: "links", "urls", "hyperlinks" (+ optional term from "about X" / "for X" / "containing X")
- emails: "email", "e-mail", "mail"
- phones: "phone", "tel", "telephone"
- prices: "price", "cost", "how much"
- count: "how many" → count of a noun (links/rows/headings)
- table: "table", "rows"
- labeled: "value of X", "what is X", "X field", "X value" → term
- default → search over text with keywords.

For term extraction: strip stopwords and known nouns. Keep it deterministic.

Now, code for gather:

```ts
async gather(): Promise<PageData> {
  const page = await this.ensurePage();
  const data = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const norm = (s: string | null | undefined) => (s ?? '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    const title = document.title || '';
    const headings = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3')).map(h => norm(h.textContent)).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 100);
    const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a[href]')).map(a => ({ text: norm(a.textContent), href: (a as HTMLAnchorElement).href })).filter(l => l.text || l.href).slice(0, 300);
    const tables = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('table')).slice(0, 10).map(t =>
      Array.from(t.querySelectorAll('tr')).slice(0, 50).map(tr =>
        Array.from(tr.querySelectorAll('th,td')).map(td => norm(td.textContent))
      )
    );
    const fields: {label:string;value:string}[] = [];
    document.querySelectorAll('label').forEach(l => {
      const forId = l.getAttribute('for');
      const ctrl = forId ? document.getElementById(forId) : l.querySelector('input,select,textarea');
      const value = ctrl ? ((ctrl as HTMLInputElement).value ?? '') : '';
      fields.push({ label: norm(l.textContent), value: norm(value) });
    });
    document.querySelectorAll('input,select,textarea').forEach(el => {
      const id = el.getAttribute('id'); const name = el.getAttribute('name');
      const label = id ? document.querySelector(`label[for="${id}"]`) : null;
      if (!label) fields.push({ label: norm(name || el.getAttribute('placeholder') || el.getAttribute('aria-label')), value: norm((el as HTMLInputElement).value) });
    });
    const text = norm(document.body?.innerText || document.body?.textContent);
    return { url: location.href, title, headings, links, tables, fields: fields.filter(f=>f.label), text: text.slice(0, 20000) };
  });
  return data as PageData;
}
```

Then query:

```ts
async query(nl: string): Promise<QueryResult> {
  const data = await this.gather();
  return runQuery(data, planQuery(nl));
}
```

const NOUNS = ['links','link','urls','url','headings','heading','headers','header','sections','section','emails','email','e-mail','phones','phone','prices','price','cost','tables','table','rows','row','title'];
```

planQuery logic:

```ts
export function planQuery(raw: string): QueryPlan {
  const q = raw.trim();
  const lc = q.toLowerCase();
  const term = extractTerm(lc);
  if (/\bhow many\b/.test(lc)) return { kind: 'count', term: nounTerm(lc), raw: q };
  if (/\b(title|page title|headline)\b/.test(lc)) return { kind: 'title', raw: q };
  if (/\b(email|e-mail|mail address|emails)\b/.test(lc)) return { kind: 'emails', raw: q };
  if (/\b(phone|telephone|tel number|phone number|phones)\b/.test(lc)) return { kind: 'phones', raw: q };
  if (/\b(price|cost|how much|prices)\b/.test(lc)) return { kind: 'prices', raw: q };
  if (/\b(headings|headlines|sections|headers)\b/.test(lc)) return { kind: 'headings', term, raw: q };
  if (/\b(table|rows)\b/.test(lc)) return { kind: 'table', term, raw: q };
  if (/\b(links|urls|hyperlinks)\b/.test(lc)) return { kind: 'links', term, raw: q };
  const labeled = /(?:value of|what is|what's|whats)\s+(.+)$/.exec(lc);
  if (labeled) return { kind: 'labeled', term: cleanTerm(labeled[1]), raw: q };
  if (/\b(list|show|find|get|extract|give)\b/.test(lc) && term) return { kind: 'search', term, raw: q };
  return { kind: 'search', term: term || lc, raw: q };
}
```

- table: if term, find table containing term in first row; else first table. matches rows joined by ' | '.
- count: count noun.
- labeled: find field whose label includes term; value.
- search: sentences containing term.

Return QueryResult with note when empty.

async gather(): Promise<PageData> {
  const page = await this.ensurePage();
  const title = await page.title().catch(() => '');
  const bodyText = ((await page.textContent('body').catch(() => '')) ?? '').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim().slice(0, MAX_TEXT * 4);
  const dom = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const headings = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6')).map(h => (h.textContent||'').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim()).filter(Boolean);
    const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a[href]')).map(a => ({ text: (a.textContent||'').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim().slice(0,120), href: (a as HTMLAnchorElement).href })).filter(l => l.href);
    const tables = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('table')).map(t => Array.from(t.querySelectorAll('tr')).map(r => Array.from(r.querySelectorAll('th,td')).map(c => (c.textContent||'').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim())));
    const fields: {label:string;value:string}[] = [];
    document.querySelectorAll('dl').forEach(dl => {
      const dts = Array.from(dl.querySelectorAll('dt'));
      const dds = Array.from(dl.querySelectorAll('dd'));
      dts.forEach((dt, i) => { if (dds[i]) fields.push({ label:(dt.textContent||'').trim(), value:(dds[i].textContent||'').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim() }); });
    });
    // label[for] + input
    document.querySelectorAll('label[for]').forEach(l => {
      const id = l.getAttribute('for'); const input = id ? document.getElementById(id) : null;
      if (input) fields.push({ label:(l.textContent||'').trim(), value: (input as HTMLInputElement).value || input.getAttribute('placeholder') || '' });
    });
    return { headings, links, tables, fields };
  }).catch(() => ({ headings: [], links: [], tables: [], fields: [] }));
  return { url: page.url(), title, text: bodyText, ...dom };
}

this.browser = await chromium.launch({\n      executablePath: this.executablePath,\n      args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-dev-shm-usage'],\n    });\n    this.context = await 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n      if (!safe) return null;\n      const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). ' (capped)' : ''}:\\n${matches.join('\\n')}`,\n        };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'find_files',\n      description:\n        'Find files by glob pattern, e.g. {\"glob\":\"src/**/*.ts\"} or {\"glob\":\"*.json\"}. 'up' : 'down';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.scroll(direction)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_scroll failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_extract',\n      description: 'Return the visible text of the current page, optionally only sentences matching a regex.  "new_content": "/**\n * M2 — Tools for the agent loop.\n *\n * Thin adapters over Forge's existing services (GitHubService, TestRunnerService)\n * plus a bounded local workspace. The loop kernel never knows about GitHub or npm;\n * it only calls these tools by name.\n *\n * Capability tiers:\n *  - read-only tools (list_files, read_file, search, find_files, think, fetch_url)\n *    are always available;\n *  - mutating tools (edit_file, write_file, run_check) are only registered when the\n *    permission profile permits branch writes, so the brain cannot even see a\n *    state-changing capability it is not permitted to use.\n *\n * File tools prefer the mission workspace when one exists (so edits can be made and\n * then verified), and fall back to reading the repository through GitHub.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService, AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { BrowserService } from '../services/browser.ts';\nimport { renderQueryResult } from '../services/query.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport type { AgentTool, LoopContext, ToolObservation } from './loop.ts';\n\nfunction str(input: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = input[key];\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\nfunction walkFiles(root: string): string[] {\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const stack = [''];\n  while (stack.length && out.length < MAX_SCAN_FILES) {\n    const rel = stack.pop() as string;\n    const abs = path.join(root, rel);\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;\n      const childRel = rel ? path.join(rel, entry.name) : entry.name;\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) stack.push(childRel);\n      else if (entry.isFile()) out.push(childRel.split(path.sep).join('/'));\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {\n  const escaped = glob.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n  const pattern = escaped\n    .replace(/\\*\\*\\//g, '\\u0001')\n    .replace(/\\*\\*/g, '\\u0000')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '[^/]*')\n    .replace(/\\?/g, '.')\n    .replace(/\\u0001/g, '(?:.*/)?')\n    .replace(/\\u0000/g, '.*');\n  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);\n}\n\n/** Common \"everything\" shorthands (star, double-star, double-star-slash-star) mean all files. */\nfunction matchesAll(glob: string): boolean {\n  const g = glob.trim();\n  return g === '' || g === '*' || g === '**' || g === '**/*';\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. Mutating tools are enabled only when `allowMutation` is\n * true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain cannot even see a state-changing\n * capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  /** Absolute path to the mission workspace, when one exists. */\n  workspace?: string;\n  /** Include the real-browser tools (open/view/click/type/scroll/extract/close). */\n  allowBrowser?: boolean;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n      if (!safe) return null;\n      const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await listPaths();\n        if (files.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'No files found.' };\n        const shown = files.slice(0, 80);\n        return { ok: true, output: `${files.length} files total. 0 : 1);\n  }\n\n  const browser = new BrowserService();\n  try {\n    let snap = await browser.open(url);\n    showElements(snap);\n\n    for (const action of actions) {\n      const [verb, rest] = action.split(/:(.*)/s);\n      if (verb === 'click') {\n        snap = await browser.click(Number(rest));\n      } else if (verb === 'type') {\n        const [idx, text] = (rest ?? An identical call to a\n * read-only tool cannot yield new information, so it is replaced with a `think`\n * nudge to change course; mutating actions are never altered. Pure, so it can be\n * unit-tested without a model.\n */\nexport function guardRepeatedReadOnly(\n  action: { tool: string; input?: Record<string, unknown> },\n  history: { action: { tool: string; input?: Record<string, unknown> } }[]\n): { tool: string; input?: Record<string, unknown> } {\n  if (!READ_ONLY_TOOLS.has(action.tool)) return action;\n  const key = JSON.stringify({ tool: action.tool, input: action.input });\n  const repeated = history.some((h) => JSON.stringify({ tool: h.action.tool, input: h.action.input }) === key);\n  if (!repeated) return action;\n  return { tool: 'think', input: { thought: `Already ran ${key}; that result will not change. Choose a different tool or finish.` } };\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the audit prompt. Exported and pure so the untrusted-input guard and the\n * inventory/excerpt injection can be asserted without calling a model.\n */\nexport function buildAuditPrompt(input: AuditModelInput): string {\n  const inventory = input.files.join('\\n');\n  const excerptBlocks = Object.entries(input.excerpts)\n    .map(([p, content]) => `--- FILE: ${p} ---\\n${content}\\n--- END FILE ---`)\n    .join('\\n\\n');\n  return `You are Forge, the precise READ-ONLY audit agent for Firstborn.\nYou are auditing the repository ${input.targetRepository} at commit ${input.commitSha}.\nFollow these rules:\n- Base every statement ONLY on the supplied repository inventory and file excerpts.  "old_content": "/**\n * Natural-language query planner for Forreyra.\n *\n * Turns a plain-English request (\"what is the price\", \"list the links about\n * docs\", \"how many rows are in the table\") into a deterministic, typed plan, then\n * resolves that plan against structured page data.  "old_content": "# Forreyra — the browser\n\n**Forreyra** is Forge's real browser. It drives an actual Chromium session, so the\nagent can open pages, look at them, click, type, scroll, and read the text — the\nsame way a person uses a browser. It is named for Foryra, the missions repo.\n\nThere are three ways to use it, from simplest to most integrated.\n\n---\n\n## 1. One-command CLI\n\nNo code. One command opens a page, prints its interactive elements, and can run a\nchain of actions left to right against that one open page.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra -- https://example.com\n```\n\n```\nurl:   https://example.com/\ntitle: Example Domain\nelements:\n  [0] a Learn more -> https://iana.org/help/example-domains\n```\n\n### Actions\n\n| Action | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `click:<n>` | click element `[n]` from the last view |\n| `type:<n>=<text>` | type text into element `[n]` |\n| `press:<key>` | press a key, e.g. `press:Enter` |\n| `scroll:up` / `scroll:down` | scroll one screen |\n| `extract[:<regex>]` | print the page text (optionally only matching sentences) |\n| `view` | re-print the element list |\n\n### Examples\n\n```bash\n# read the top story headline from Hacker News\nnpm run forreyra -- https://news.ycombinator.com extract:Apple\n\n# click a link, then read the page it lands on\nnpm run forreyra -- https://example.com click:0 extract:IANA\n\n# search: type into the search box, press Enter, read the results\nnpm run forreyra -- https://duckduckgo.com type:1=playwright press:Enter\n```\n\nElements are numbered in document order. A `view` (or `open`) is always followed\nby a fresh element list, so the `[n]` you click is exactly the element you saw.\n\n---\n\n## 2. As agent tools (Forge uses it like a person)\n\nWhen the loop runs with the browser enabled, Forge gets eight tools:\n\n`browser_open`, `browser_view`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`,\n`browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_extract`, `browser_close`.\n\nA goal like *\"open news.ycombinator.com and report the top story\"* makes Forge\ncall `browser_open`, read the numbered elements, and finish with the answer.\n\nEnable it by setting `FORGE_ALLOW_BROWSER` (default on; set to `false` to remove\nthe tools entirely):\n\n```bash\nFORGE_ALLOW_BROWSER=true \\\nFORGE_LOOP_GOAL=\"Open https://example.com and report the title.\" \\\nnpx tsx src/agent/loop-runner.ts\n```\n\nThe tools are opt-in so the read-only tool list stays unchanged. The anti-repeat\nguard also covers `browser_view`, `browser_extract`, and `browser_scroll`, so a\nrepeated identical read can never burn the step budget.\n\n---\n\n## 3. As a library\n\n```ts\nimport { BrowserService } from './src/services/browser.ts';\n\nconst browser = new BrowserService();\nconst snap = await browser.open('https://example.com');\nconsole.log(snap.title, snap.elements);\n\nawait browser.click(0);          // click element [0]\nawait browser.type(1, 'hello');  // type into element [1]\nawait browser.press('Enter');\nawait browser.scroll('down');\nconsole.log(await browser.extract('price'));\nawait browser.close();\n```\n\n`BrowserSnapshot` = `{ url, title, elements, text }`, where each element is\n`{ i, tag, type?, text, href? }`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. As an MCP server\n\nForreyra runs as a **Model Context Protocol** server over stdio, so any MCP client\n(Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, the OpenHands agent) can drive the browser with\nthe same look-then-act model.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra:mcp\n```\n\nIt exposes nine tools: `browser_open`, `browser_view`, `browser_click`,\n`browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_extract`,\n`browser_screenshot` (returns a PNG image), `browser_close`.\n\n### Client configuration\n\nClaude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"forreyra\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"tsx\", \"src/mcp/forreyra-server.ts\"],\n      \"cwd\": \"/absolute/path/to/Firstborn\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nCursor / VS Code use the same `command` + `args` + `cwd` shape.\n\n### Verify the connection\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/mcp-client-smoke.mjs\n```\n\nThis uses the official MCP client SDK to connect, list the tools, open\n`https://example.com`, and close.\n\n---\n\n## Setup\n\n- Chromium is auto-detected at `/usr/bin/chromium`, `/usr/bin/chromium-browser`,\n  or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`. As an MCP server\n\nForreyra runs as a **Model Context Protocol** server over stdio, so any MCP client\n(Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, the OpenHands agent) can drive the browser with\nthe same look-then-act model.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra:mcp\n```\n\nIt exposes nine tools: `browser_open`, `browser_view`, `browser_click`,\n`browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_extract`,\n`browser_screenshot` (returns a PNG image), `browser_close`.\n\n### Client configuration\n\nClaude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"forreyra\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"tsx\", \"src/mcp/forreyra-server.ts\"],\n      \"cwd\": \"/absolute/path/to/Firstborn\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nCursor / VS Code use the same `command` + `args` + `cwd` shape.\n\n### Verify the connection\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/mcp-client-smoke.mjs\n```\n\nThis uses the official MCP client SDK to connect, list the tools, open\n`https://example.com`, and close.\n\n---\n\n## Setup\n\n- Chromium is auto-detected at `/usr/bin/chromium`, `/usr/bin/chromium-browser`,\n  or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`.  "old_content": "# Forreyra — the browser\n\n**Forreyra** is Forge's real browser. It drives an actual Chromium session, so the\nagent can open pages, look at them, click, type, scroll, and read the text — the\nsame way a person uses a browser. It is named for Foryra, the missions repo.\n\nThere are three ways to use it, from simplest to most integrated.\n\n---\n\n## 1. One-command CLI\n\nNo code. One command opens a page, prints its interactive elements, and can run a\nchain of actions left to right against that one open page.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra -- https://example.com\n```\n\n```\nurl:   https://example.com/\ntitle: Example Domain\nelements:\n  [0] a Learn more -> https://iana.org/help/example-domains\n```\n\n### Actions\n\n| Action | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `click:<n>` | click element `[n]` from the last view |\n| `type:<n>=<text>` | type text into element `[n]` |\n| `press:<key>` | press a key, e.g. `press:Enter` |\n| `scroll:up` / `scroll:down` | scroll one screen |\n| `extract[:<regex>]` | print the page text (optionally only matching sentences) |\n| `query:<question>` | answer a plain-English question, e.g. `query:what is the price` |\n| `view` | re-print the element list |\n\n### Examples\n\n```bash\n# read the top story headline from Hacker News\nnpm run forreyra -- https://news.ycombinator.com extract:Apple\n\n# click a link, then read the page it lands on\nnpm run forreyra -- https://example.com click:0 extract:IANA\n\n# search: type into the search box, press Enter, read the results\nnpm run forreyra -- https://duckduckgo.com type:1=playwright press:Enter\n\n# ask a question in plain English — no regex\nnpm run forreyra -- https://example.com query:what is the title\nnpm run forreyra -- https://books.toscrape.com query:what is the price\n```\n\nElements are numbered in document order. A `view` (or `open`) is always followed\nby a fresh element list, so the `[n]` you click is exactly the element you saw.\n\n---\n\n## 2. As agent tools (Forge uses it like a person)\n\nWhen the loop runs with the browser enabled, Forge gets eight tools:\n\n`browser_open`, `browser_view`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`,\n`browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_extract`, `browser_query`,\n`browser_screenshot`, `browser_close`.\n\nA goal like *\"open news.ycombinator.com and report the top story\"* makes Forge\ncall `browser_open`, read the numbered elements, and finish with the answer.\n\nEnable it by setting `FORGE_ALLOW_BROWSER` (default on; set to `false` to remove\nthe tools entirely):\n\n```bash\nFORGE_ALLOW_BROWSER=true \\\nFORGE_LOOP_GOAL=\"Open https://example.com and report the title.\" \\\nnpx tsx src/agent/loop-runner.ts\n```\n\nThe tools are opt-in so the read-only tool list stays unchanged. The anti-repeat\nguard also covers `browser_view`, `browser_extract`, and `browser_scroll`, so a\nrepeated identical read can never burn the step budget.\n\n---\n\n## 3. As a library\n\n```ts\nimport { BrowserService } from './src/services/browser.ts';\n\nconst browser = new BrowserService();\nconst snap = await browser.open('https://example.com');\nconsole.log(snap.title, snap.elements);\n\nawait browser.click(0);          // click element [0]\nawait browser.type(1, 'hello');  // type into element [1]\nawait browser.press('Enter');\nawait browser.scroll('down');\nconsole.log(await browser.extract('price'));\nawait browser.close();\n```\n\n`BrowserSnapshot` = `{ url, title, elements, text }`, where each element is\n`{ i, tag, type?, text, href? }`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. As an MCP server\n\nForreyra runs as a **Model Context Protocol** server over stdio, so any MCP client\n(Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, the OpenHands agent) can drive the browser with\nthe same look-then-act model.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra:mcp\n```\n\nIt exposes nine tools: `browser_open`, `browser_view`, `browser_click`,\n`browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_extract`,\n`browser_screenshot` (returns a PNG image), `browser_close`.\n\n### Client configuration\n\nClaude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"forreyra\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"tsx\", \"src/mcp/forreyra-server.ts\"],\n      \"cwd\": \"/absolute/path/to/Firstborn\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nCursor / VS Code use the same `command` + `args` + `cwd` shape.\n\n### Verify the connection\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/mcp-client-smoke.mjs\n```\n\nThis uses the official MCP client SDK to connect, list the tools, open\n`https://example.com`, and close.\n\n---\n\n## Setup\n\n- Chromium is auto-detected at `/usr/bin/chromium`, `/usr/bin/chromium-browser`,\n  or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`. To point at a specific binary, set\n  `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/path/to/chrome`.\n- Installed with the repo: `npm install` (the `playwright` package).\n- Headless by default. Runs with `--no-sandbox` and `--disable-dev-shm-usage` so\n  it works in CI containers.\n\n## How it behaves\n\n- **One browser per session.** A page opened once stays open for later actions.\n- **Look, then act.** Every action returns a fresh snapshot, mirroring how a\n  person re-reads a page after each step.\n- **Basic stealth.** A real Chrome user agent and the `navigator.webdriver` flag\n  hidden at start.\n\n## Limits\n\n- Interactive elements are the standard clickable/typable set (`a`, `button`,\n  `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `[role=button]`, `[onclick]`, `[contenteditable]`),\n  capped at 120 per view.\n- Page text is capped at 4000 characters per snapshot.\n- No persistent profile or cookie jar across runs yet — each run starts clean.\n\n## Tests\n\n`tests/browser.test.ts` drives a real headless Chromium against a real local HTTP\nserver (no mocks) and covers open, type-then-submit, click-through navigation, and\nregex extract.\n\n```bash\nnpm test\n```\n",

{
 "data": {
  "repo_name": "madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn",
  "source_branch": "forge/forreyra-query",
  "target_branch": "main",
  "title": "feat(forreyra): query the page in plain English",
  "body": "## What this does\n\nAdds a **deterministic natural-language query layer** to Forreyra: ask a plain-English question and get **structured data** back — no regex.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra -- https://books.toscrape.com \"query:what is the price\"\n```\n```\nquery: what is the price\nkind: prices\nmatches: 20\n- £51.77\n- £53.74\n...\n```\n\n## How\n\n`src/services/query.ts` is a **pure planner + resolver**:\n- `planQuery(\"what is the price\")` → `{ kind: 'prices' }`\n- `runQuery(pageData, plan)` → `{ kind, matches, note }`\n\nSame question → same plan → same result. No model call, so it's explainable and fully testable.\n\nHandles: **title, headings, links** (keyword-filtered), **emails, phones, prices, table rows, counts** (`how many rows…`), **labelled values** (`what is the value of weight`), and **free-text search**.\n\n`BrowserService.gather()` collects structured DOM data (headings, links, tables, `dt`/`label` fields); `BrowserService.query()` resolves the plan against it.\n\nExposed three ways: the `browser_query` **MCP tool**, the `query:<nl>` **CLI action**, and a `browser_query` **agent tool** — which is also covered by the anti-repeat guard.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `npm run lint` → **EXIT 0**; `npm test` → **128 passed / 0 failed** (+13 planner, +1 real-browser query, +1 MCP query).\n- `tests/query.test.ts` — 13 pure tests over a fixed page fixture.\n- `tests/browser.test.ts` — `browser_query` drives **real Chromium** against a **real local shop page** and returns the price, email, row count, and title.\n- `tests/mcp.test.ts` — `browser_query` over **real stdio JSON-RPC**.\n- **Live, just now:** `query:what is the price` on `books.toscrape.com` → 20 real prices.\n- A miss is **reported, never invented** (`No email addresses found.`).\n\n_This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Ahmed._",
  "labels": [
   "enhancement"
  ]
 },
 "kind": "MCPToolAction"
}
```

It runs as a SEPARATE job with a fresh context, never Forge approving\n# itself.\n#\n# Safety model:\n#   - Only forge/* source branches are eligible (enforced here and in the engine).\n#   - main can never be a merge source.\n#   - The model judge is OFF by default; the deterministic checks are the authority.\n#   - Auto-merge only happens when the repository variable SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE is\n#     \"true\". Out of the box this workflow verifies and reports only.\n#   - For the guarantee to be real, `main` must be protected (see README note):\n#     require this check and the `verify` check, and disallow direct pushes.\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n    branches: [main]\n  workflow_dispatch:\n\npermissions:\n  contents: write\n  pull-requests: write\n\njobs:\n  sentinel:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    # Only verifier-eligible branches reach the checks. Anything else is skipped.\n    if: startsWith(github.head_ref, 'forge/')\n    steps:\n      - name: Checkout the pull request head (the code under test)\n        uses: actions/checkout@v4\n        with:\n          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}\n          fetch-depth: 0\n\n      - name: Setup Node.js 22\n        uses: actions/setup-node@v4\n        with:\n          node-version: 22\n\n      - name: Install dependencies\n        run: npm ci\n\n      - name: Run Sentinel verification\n        id: sentinel\n        env:\n          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}\n          SENTINEL_SOURCE_BRANCH: ${{ github.head_ref }}\n          SENTINEL_TARGET_BRANCH: ${{ github.base_ref || 'main' }}\n          SENTINEL_PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}\n          SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE: ${{ vars.SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE }}\n          SENTINEL_MODEL_JUDGE: ${{ vars.SENTINEL_MODEL_JUDGE }}\n        run: npx tsx scripts/sentinel-run.ts\n\n      - name: Upload Sentinel decision evidence\n        if: always()\n        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4"
  }

### ObservationEvent — tool: `finish` — source: `environment` — id: `f6c2bf14-dcc2-42f5-9370-a19180f0276b` — 2026-10-13T23:01:49.603974

```
## Orbit report — this triple

Three PRs, all merged to `main`, all gated by Sentinel + verify:

| PR | Commit | What | Files |
|----|--------|------|-------|
| **#80** | `82c498b` | Plain-English query layer | 10 files, +458 / −4 |
| **#81** | `237d785` | Forreyra map in `AGENTS.md` | 1 file, +28 |
| **#82** | `68f559f` | Coordination report entry | 1 file |

`main` HEAD = `68f559f`. Working tree clean. `main` verify: **success**.

### What I changed

**1. `src/services/query.ts` (new) — the answer to "get the price", no regex.**
A deterministic, pure two-stage layer:
- `planQuery("what is the price")` → `{ kind: 'prices' }` — maps a question to a typed plan: `title`, `headings`, `links`, `emails`, `phones`, `prices`, `table`, `count`, `labeled`, `search`.
- `runQuery(pageData, plan)` → `{ kind, matches, note }` — resolves it against structured page data.

Same question → same plan → same result. No model call, so it is explainable and fully unit-testable. **A miss is reported, never invented** (`No email addresses found.`).

**2. `BrowserService.gather()` / `query()`** — collect structured DOM data (headings, links, tables, `dt`/`label` fields), then resolve the plan. Exposed three ways: the `browser_query` **MCP tool**, the `query:<question>` **CLI action**, and a `browser_query` **agent tool**. Added to the read-only anti-repeat guard so identical repeats steer to `think`.

**3. `AGENTS.md`** — durable Forreyra capability map (agent tools, CLI actions, MCP tools, the query layer) plus the verification commands, so Forge's own map matches the code.

**4. `COORDINATION.md`** — one append-only entry, `OPENHANDS-FORREYRA-QUERY-20261013-01`, reporting the above.

### Evidence (observed, not claimed)

- `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → **EXIT 0**.
- `npm test` → **128 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped** (up from 113). Added `tests/query.test.ts` (13 pure cases), a real-Chromium `browser_query` case, and an MCP stdio case.
- **Live, just now:** `npm run forreyra -- https://books.toscrape.com "query:what is the price"` → `kind: prices`, **20 real prices** (£51.77 … £57.25). EXIT 0.
- #80 / #81 / #82: Sentinel + verify **success**; #80 merged after its Sentinel re-run.

### Two things worth your attention

1. **A Sentinel run hung** on a dead runner (0 steps, `in_progress` ~25 min) while PR #78's workflows held capacity. Cancelling and re-running it passed cleanly — infrastructure, not code. Worth knowing if you see a stuck sentinel again.
2. **No LLM key in this environment**, so the keyless router is what runs. That's why the query layer is deliberately model-free — it works with or without a brain.

### Not touched
PR **#78** (the earlier Forreyra end-to-end verification branch) is still open and unmerged. I left it alone.
```

```ts
function withDeadline<T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`Deadline exceeded (${ms}ms)`)), ms);
    timer.unref?.();
    p.then(
      (v) => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(v); },
      (e) => { clearTimeout(timer); reject(e); },
    );
  });
}
```

Mutation is allowed only when the caller consents\n * (allowPrCreation) AND the permission profile permits branch writes, so the loop\n * can never widen its own authority.\n */\nimport { mkdirSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { ModelService } from '../services/model.ts';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { loadPermissionConfig, evaluatePermissionPolicy } from './policy.ts';\nimport { buildForgeTools } from './tools.ts';\nimport { runAgentLoop, loadLoopLimits, FINISH_TOOL, type Authorization } from './loop.ts';\n\nconst MEMORY_FILE = 'AGENTS.md';\n\n/** Load repository guidance (AGENTS.md) from the workspace, falling back to GitHub. */\nasync function loadMemory(workspace: string, owner: string, repo: string, ref: string, token?: string): Promise<string | undefined> {\n  const local = path.join(workspace, MEMORY_FILE);\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(local)) return readFileSync(local, 'utf8');\n  } catch {\n    /* fall through to GitHub */\n  }\n  const remote = await new GitHubService(token).fetchFile(owner, repo, MEMORY_FILE, ref);\n  return remote?.content;\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const goal = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_GOAL ?? '').trim();\n  if (!goal) throw new Error('FORGE_LOOP_GOAL is required (the mission objective).');\n\n  const targetRepo = (process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY ?? 'madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn').trim();\n  const [owner, repo] = targetRepo.split('/');\n  if (!owner || !repo) throw new Error(`GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be owner/repo, got \"${targetRepo}\".`);\n  const ref = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_REF ?? '').trim().toLowerCase());\n\n  const branch = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_BRANCH ?? 'forge/task-loop').trim();\n  // Operate on the real checkout when present (CI checks the repo out here), so\n  // search/read/edit act on actual files and run_check can see installed deps.\n  const workspace = (process.env.FORGE_LOOP_WORKSPACE ?? process.cwd()).trim();\n  const policy = evaluatePermissionPolicy(\n    {\n      requestedPrCreation: consented,\n      branchName: branch,\n      targetBranch: 'main',\n      repo: `${owner}/${repo}`,\n    },\n    loadPermissionConfig()\n  );\n\n  const allowBrowser = process.env.FORGE_ALLOW_BROWSER !== 'false';\n  const tools = buildForgeTools({\n    owner,\n    repo,\n    ref,\n    token,\n    allowMutation: policy.allowBranchWrite,\n    workspace,\n    allowBrowser,\n  });\n  const memory = await loadMemory(workspace, owner, repo, ref, token);\n  const model = new ModelService();\n\n  const authorize: Authorization = (action) => {\n    if (!policy.allowBranchWrite) {\n      return { allowed: false, reason: `profile '${policy.effectiveProfile}' does not permit mutations` };\n    }\n    return { allowed: true };\n  };\n\n  const result = await runAgentLoop({\n    goal,\n    tools,\n    brain: (state) => model.chooseNextAction(state),\n    authorize,\n    limits: loadLoopLimits(),\n    workspace: branch,\n    memory,\n    onStep: (step) => {\n      console.log(`[loop ${step.index}] ${step.action.tool} -> ${step.observation.ok ? async function withDeadline<T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<{ done: true; value: T } | { done: false }> {
  if (ms <= 0) return { done: false };
  return await new Promise((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve({ done: false }), ms);
    p.then((value) => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve({ done: true, value }); },
           () => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve({ done: true, value: undefined as any }); });
  });
}
```

async function raceDeadline<T>(work: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<{ timedOut: false; value: T } | { timedOut: true }> {
  if (!Number.isFinite(ms) || ms <= 0) return { timedOut: true };
  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
  const timeout = new Promise<{ timedOut: true }>((resolve) => { timer = setTimeout(() => resolve({ timedOut: true }), ms); });

      work.then((value) => ({ timedOut: false as const, value })),
      timeout,
    ]);
    return result;
  } finally {
    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

**Fix #2 (symlink escape):** After lexical check, resolve the real path and confirm it stays within the real workspace root. Use `fs.realpathSync` on the workspace root (cached) and on the target's existing ancestor. Implementation:

```ts
function containedReal(ws: string, abs: string): boolean {
  let realRoot: string;
  try { realRoot = realpathSync(ws); } catch { return false; }
  // resolve the longest existing ancestor of abs, then the rest lexically
  let cur = abs;
  const tail: string[] = [];
  while (!existsSync(cur)) {
    tail.unshift(path.basename(cur));
    const parent = path.dirname(cur);
    if (parent === cur) break;
    cur = parent;
  }
  let realCur: string;
  try { realCur = realpathSync(cur); } catch { return false; }
  const realTarget = path.resolve(realCur, ...tail);
  const rel = path.relative(realRoot, realTarget);
  return rel === '' || (!rel.startsWith('..') && !path.isAbsolute(rel));
}
```

It can repair inside a\n * stage, but it cannot decide WHAT TO DO NEXT. This module is the missing macro\n * loop: look -> think -> act -> observe, repeated until a goal is met.\n *\n * It is deliberately ADDITIVE and declarative. It does not perform any GitHub or\n * filesystem work itself; the caller supplies:\n *   - a `brain` (typically ModelService.chooseNextAction) that picks the next action,\n *   - a set of `tools` (adapters over the existing services),\n *   - an optional `authorize` gate (typically backed by policy.ts).\n * That keeps the loop kernel pure enough to unit-test with a scripted brain while\n * the real brain and tools are wired in by the caller.\n */\n\nexport interface ToolObservation {\n  ok: boolean;\n  output: string;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentTool {\n  name: string;\n  description: string;\n  /** True when the tool changes state (writes files, opens a PR, ...). */\n  mutating?: boolean;\n  run(input: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation>;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentAction {\n  tool: string;\n  input?: Record<string, unknown>;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopStep {\n  index: number;\n  action: AgentAction;\n  observation: ToolObservation;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopContext {\n  goal: string;\n  /** A bounded workspace/scratch identifier; the loop never assumes a real path. */\n  workspace: string;\n  step: number;\n  /** Wall-clock budget (ms) for this single action; the loop enforces it. */\n  deadlineMs?: number;\n}\n\nexport type AgentBrain = (state: {\n  goal: string;\n  history: LoopStep[];\n  tools: { name: string; description: string }[];\n  /** Repository guidance (e.g. AGENTS.md), loaded once per run. */\n  memory?: string;\n}) => Promise<AgentAction>;\n\nexport interface LoopLimits {\n  maxSteps: number;\n  maxRuntimeMs: number;\n  /** Ceiling (ms) for a single brain or tool call. /**
 * Resolve a workspace-relative path and confirm it stays inside the workspace,
 * even through symlinks. Returns the absolute path, or null if the path is
 * absolute, escapes lexically, or resolves (via a symlink) outside the root.
 */
function resolveInWorkspace(root: string, rel: string): string | null {
  if (!rel) return null;
  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;
  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);
  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;
  const abs = path.join(root, normalized);

  // Real paths: resolve the workspace root and the nearest existing ancestor of
  // the target. A symlink that leaves the workspace is refused.
  let realRoot: string;
  try {
    realRoot = realpathSync(root);
  } catch {
    return null; // no real workspace root -> refuse rather than guess
  }
  let probe = abs;
  while (!existsSync(probe)) {
    const parent = path.dirname(probe);
    if (parent === probe) break;
    probe = parent;
  }
  let realProbe: string;
  try {
    realProbe = realpathSync(probe);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  if (realProbe !== realRoot && !realProbe.startsWith(realRoot + path.sep)) return null;
  return abs;
}

Input: {\"index\":3}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const index = Number(input.index);\n        if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_click requires an integer \"index\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.click(index)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_click failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_type',\n      description: 'Type text into the element at an index from the latest view. 'up' : 'down';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.scroll(direction)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_scroll failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_extract',\n      description: 'Return the visible text of the current page, optionally only sentences matching a regex.  "new_content": "/**\n * M2 — Tools for the agent loop.\n *\n * Thin adapters over Forge's existing services (GitHubService, TestRunnerService)\n * plus a bounded local workspace. The loop kernel never knows about GitHub or npm;\n * it only calls these tools by name.\n *\n * Capability tiers:\n *  - read-only tools (list_files, read_file, search, find_files, think, fetch_url)\n *    are always available;\n *  - mutating tools (edit_file, write_file, run_check) are only registered when the\n *    permission profile permits branch writes, so the brain cannot even see a\n *    state-changing capability it is not permitted to use.\n *\n * File tools prefer the mission workspace when one exists (so edits can be made and\n * then verified), and fall back to reading the repository through GitHub.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService, AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { BrowserService } from '../services/browser.ts';\nimport { renderQueryResult } from '../services/query.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport type { AgentTool, LoopContext, ToolObservation } from './loop.ts';\n\nfunction str(input: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = input[key];\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\nfunction walkFiles(root: string): string[] {\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const stack = [''];\n  while (stack.length && out.length < MAX_SCAN_FILES) {\n    const rel = stack.pop() as string;\n    const abs = path.join(root, rel);\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;\n      const childRel = rel ? path.join(rel, entry.name) : entry.name;\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) stack.push(childRel);\n      else if (entry.isFile()) out.push(childRel.split(path.sep).join('/'));\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {\n  const escaped = glob.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n  const pattern = escaped\n    .replace(/\\*\\*\\//g, '\\u0001')\n    .replace(/\\*\\*/g, '\\u0000')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '[^/]*')\n    .replace(/\\?/g, '.')\n    .replace(/\\u0001/g, '(?:.*/)?')\n    .replace(/\\u0000/g, '.*');\n  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);\n}\n\n/** Common \"everything\" shorthands (star, double-star, double-star-slash-star) mean all files. */\nfunction matchesAll(glob: string): boolean {\n  const g = glob.trim();\n  return g === '' || g === '*' || g === '**' || g === '**/*';\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. Mutating tools are enabled only when `allowMutation` is\n * true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain cannot even see a state-changing\n * capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  /** Absolute path to the mission workspace, when one exists. */\n  workspace?: string;\n  /** Include the real-browser tools (open/view/click/type/scroll/extract/close). */\n  allowBrowser?: boolean;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n      if (!safe) return null;\n      const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await listPaths();\n        if (files.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'No files found.' };\n        const shown = files.slice(0, 80);\n        return { ok: true, output: `${files.length} files total.  "new_str": "/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `rel` under `ws` and confirm the result stays inside the workspace.\n * Lexical checks alone cannot catch a symlink inside the workspace that points\n * outside it, so the parent directory is resolved through the real filesystem.\n * Returns the absolute path, or null when the target escapes or cannot be\n * resolved safely.\n */\nfunction resolveInWorkspace(ws: string, rel: string): string | null {\n  const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n  if (!safe) return null;\n  const root = realpathSync(ws);\n  const abs = path.join(root, safe);\n  const parent = realpathSync(path.dirname(abs));\n  if (parent !== root && !parent.startsWith(root + path.sep)) return null;\n  return abs;\n}",

value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\nfunction walkFiles(root: string): string[] {\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const stack = [''];\n  while (stack.length && out.length < MAX_SCAN_FILES) {\n    const rel = stack.pop() as string;\n    const abs = path.join(root, rel);\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;\n      const childRel = rel ? path.join(rel, entry.name) : entry.name;\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) stack.push(childRel);\n      else if (entry.isFile()) out.push(childRel.split(path.sep).join('/'));\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {\n  const escaped = glob.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n  const pattern = escaped\n    .replace(/\\*\\*\\//g, '\\u0001')\n    .replace(/\\*\\*/g, '\\u0000')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '[^/]*')\n    .replace(/\\?/g, '.')\n    .replace(/\\u0001/g, '(?:.*/)?')\n    .replace(/\\u0000/g, '.*');\n  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);\n}\n\n/** Common \"everything\" shorthands (star, double-star, double-star-slash-star) mean all files. */\nfunction matchesAll(glob: string): boolean {\n  const g = glob.trim();\n  return g === '' || g === '*' || g === '**' || g === '**/*';\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n      if (!safe) return null;\n      const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await listPaths();\n        if (files.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'No files found.' };\n        const shown = files.slice(0, 80);\n        return { ok: true, output: `${files.length} files total. First ${shown.length}:\\n${shown.join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read one file by exact repository path. Input: {\"pattern\":\"...\", \"glob\":\"*.ts\" (optional)}. Returns matching file:line: text. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const pattern = str(input, 'pattern');\n        if (!pattern) return { ok: false, output: 'search requires a \"pattern\" (regular expression).' };\n        let re: RegExp;\n        try {\n          re = new RegExp(pattern, 'i');\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Invalid pattern: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        }\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        const matcher = glob && !matchesAll(glob) ? globToRegExp(glob) : null;\n        const paths = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        const matches: string[] = [];\n        let scanned = 0;\n        for (const rel of paths) {\n          if (matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES || scanned >= MAX_SCAN_FILES) break;\n          scanned += 1;\n          const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n          if (content === null) continue;\n          const lines = content.split('\\n');\n          for (let i = 0; i < lines.length && matches.length < MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES; i += 1) {\n            if (re.test(lines[i])) matches.push(`${rel}:${i + 1}: ${lines[i].trim().slice(0, 200)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No matches for /${pattern}/ in ${paths.length} file(s).` };\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          output: `${matches.length} match(es)${matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES ? Mutating (may install/build).`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const command = str(input, 'command');\n        if (!command) return { ok: false, output: 'run_check requires a \"command\".' };\n        const cwd = ws ?? ctx.workspace ?? process.cwd();\n        const result = await runner.runCheck(command, cwd);\n        return {\n          ok: result.status === 'PASSED',\n          output: `exit=${result.exitCode} status=${result.status}\\n${result.stdout}\\n${result.stderr}`.slice(0, 4000),\n        };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  if (options.allowBrowser) {\n    tools.push(...buildBrowserTools());\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n\n/** Render a browser snapshot as compact text the brain can act on. */\nexport function renderSnapshot(snap: { url: string; title: string; elements: { i: number; tag: string; type?: string; text: string; href?: string }[]; text: string }): string {\n  const lines = snap.elements.map((e) => `[${e.i}] ${e.tag}${e.type ? `(${e.type})` : ''} ${e.text}${e.href ? ` -> ${e.href}` : ''}`.trimEnd());\n  return `url: ${snap.url}\\ntitle: ${snap.title}\\nelements:\\n${lines.join('\\n')}\\ntext: ${snap.text}`.slice(0, 6000);\n}\n\n/**\n * Real-browser tools. Input: {\"index\":2,\"text\":\"hello\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const index = Number(input.index);\n        const text = str(input, 'text');\n        if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_type requires an integer \"index\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.type(index, text)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_type failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_press',\n      description: 'Press a keyboard key on the focused element, e.g. {\"key\":\"Enter\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const key = str(input, 'key') || 'Enter';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.press(key)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_press failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_scroll',\n      description: 'Scroll the page one screen. Input: {\"direction\":\"down\"} or {\"direction\":\"up\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const direction = str(input, 'direction') === 'up' ? 'up' : 'down';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.scroll(direction)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_scroll failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_extract',\n      description: 'Return the visible text of the current page, optionally only sentences matching a regex.
