Input: {}.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.view()) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_view failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_click',\n      description: 'Click the interactive element at an index from the latest view. Input: {\"index\":3}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const index = Number(input.index);\n        if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_click requires an integer \"index\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.click(index)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_click failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_type',\n      description: 'Type text into the element at an index from the latest view. Input: {\"index\":2,\"text\":\"hello\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const index = Number(input.index);\n        const text = str(input, 'text');\n        if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_type requires an integer \"index\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.type(index, text)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_type failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_press',\n      description: 'Press a keyboard key on the focused element, e.g. {\"key\":\"Enter\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const key = str(input, 'key') || 'Enter';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.press(key)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_press failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_scroll',\n      description: 'Scroll the page one screen. Input: {\"direction\":\"down\"} or {\"direction\":\"up\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const direction = str(input, 'direction') === 'up' ? 'up' : 'down';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.scroll(direction)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_scroll failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_extract',\n      description: 'Return the visible text of the current page, optionally only sentences matching a regex. Input: {\"pattern\":\"price\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: await browser.extract(str(input, 'pattern') || undefined) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_extract failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_query',\n      description:\n        'Answer a plain-English question about the current page with structured data (no regex). Input: {\"question\":\"what is the price\"}. Handles title, headings, links, emails, phones, prices, table rows, counts, labelled values.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderQueryResult(await browser.query(str(input, 'question'))) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_query failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_close',\n      description: 'Close the browser session and free the resources. Input: {}.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        await browser.close();\n        return { ok: true, output: 'Browser closed.' };\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n}\n",

 "old_content": "/**\n * M2 — Tools for the agent loop.\n *\n * Thin adapters over Forge's existing services (GitHubService, TestRunnerService)\n * plus a bounded local workspace. The loop kernel never knows about GitHub or npm;\n * it only calls these tools by name.\n *\n * Capability tiers:\n *  - read-only tools (list_files, read_file, search, find_files, think, fetch_url)\n *    are always available;\n *  - mutating tools (edit_file, write_file, run_check) are only registered when the\n *    permission profile permits branch writes, so the brain cannot even see a\n *    state-changing capability it is not permitted to use.\n *\n * File tools prefer the mission workspace when one exists (so edits can be made and\n * then verified), and fall back to reading the repository through GitHub.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService, AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { BrowserService } from '../services/browser.ts';\nimport { renderQueryResult } from '../services/query.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport type { AgentTool, LoopContext, ToolObservation } from './loop.ts';\n\nfunction str(input: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = input[key];\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `rel` under `ws` and confirm the result stays inside the workspace.\n * Lexical checks alone cannot catch a symlink inside the workspace that points\n * outside it, so the parent directory is resolved through the real filesystem.\n * Returns the absolute path, or null when the target escapes or cannot be\n * resolved safely.\n */\nfunction resolveInWorkspace(ws: string, rel: string): string | null {\n  const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n  if (!safe) return null;\n  let root: string;\n  try {\n    root = realpathSync(ws);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const abs = path.join(root, safe);\n\n  const inside = (real: string) => real === root || real.startsWith(root + path.sep);\n\n  // The deepest existing ancestor is the only part that can contain a symlink;\n  // realpath resolves every symlinked component along the way. Any components\n  // below it do not exist yet, so they can only be plain names.\n  let probe = path.dirname(abs);\n  while (!existsSync(probe)) {\n    const next = path.dirname(probe);\n    if (next === probe) break;\n    probe = next;\n  }\n  try {\n    if (!inside(realpathSync(probe))) return null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  // If the target itself already exists, it may be a symlink pointing outside.\n  if (existsSync(abs)) {\n    try {\n      if (!inside(realpathSync(abs))) return null;\n    } catch {\n      return null;\n    }\n  }\n  return abs;\n}\n\nfunction walkFiles(root: string): string[] {\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const stack = [''];\n  while (stack.length && out.length < MAX_SCAN_FILES) {\n    const rel = stack.pop() as string;\n    const abs = path.join(root, rel);\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;\n      const childRel = rel ? path.join(rel, entry.name) : entry.name;\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) stack.push(childRel);\n      else if (entry.isFile()) out.push(childRel.split(path.sep).join('/'));\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {\n  const escaped = glob.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n  const pattern = escaped\n    .replace(/\\*\\*\\//g, '\\u0001')\n    .replace(/\\*\\*/g, '\\u0000')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '[^/]*')\n    .replace(/\\?/g, '.')\n    .replace(/\\u0001/g, '(?:.*/)?')\n    .replace(/\\u0000/g, '.*');\n  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);\n}\n\n/** Common \"everything\" shorthands (star, double-star, double-star-slash-star) mean all files. */\nfunction matchesAll(glob: string): boolean {\n  const g = glob.trim();\n  return g === '' || g === '*' || g === '**' || g === '**/*';\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. Mutating tools are enabled only when `allowMutation` is\n * true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain cannot even see a state-changing\n * capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  /** Absolute path to the mission workspace, when one exists. */\n  workspace?: string;\n  /** Include the real-browser tools (open/view/click/type/scroll/extract/close). */\n  allowBrowser?: boolean;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n      if (!safe) return null;\n      const abs = path.join(ws, safe);\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await listPaths();\n        if (files.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'No files found.' };\n        const shown = files.slice(0, 80);\n        return { ok: true, output: `${files.length} files total. First ${shown.length}:\\n${shown.join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read one file by exact repository path. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'read_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `File not found: ${rel}` };\n        return { ok: true, output: content.slice(0, MAX_FILE_BYTES) };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'search',\n      description:\n        'Search file contents by regular expression (like grep). Input: {\"pattern\":\"...\", \"glob\":\"*.ts\" (optional)}. Returns matching file:line: text. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const pattern = str(input, 'pattern');\n        if (!pattern) return { ok: false, output: 'search requires a \"pattern\" (regular expression).' };\n        let re: RegExp;\n        try {\n          re = new RegExp(pattern, 'i');\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Invalid pattern: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        }\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        const matcher = glob && !matchesAll(glob) ? globToRegExp(glob) : null;\n        const paths = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        const matches: string[] = [];\n        let scanned = 0;\n        for (const rel of paths) {\n          if (matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES || scanned >= MAX_SCAN_FILES) break;\n          scanned += 1;\n          const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n          if (content === null) continue;\n          const lines = content.split('\\n');\n          for (let i = 0; i < lines.length && matches.length < MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES; i += 1) {\n            if (re.test(lines[i])) matches.push(`${rel}:${i + 1}: ${lines[i].trim().slice(0, 200)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No matches for /${pattern}/ in ${paths.length} file(s).` };\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          output: `${matches.length} match(es)${matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES ? ' (capped)' : ''}:\\n${matches.join('\\n')}`,\n        };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'find_files',\n      description:\n        'Find files by glob pattern, e.g. {\"glob\":\"src/**/*.ts\"} or {\"glob\":\"*.json\"}. Returns matching paths. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        if (!glob) return { ok: false, output: 'find_files requires a \"glob\".' };\n        const matcher = matchesAll(glob) ? null : globToRegExp(glob);\n        const matches = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No files match ${glob}.` };\n        return { ok: true, output: `${matches.length} file(s):\\n${matches.slice(0, 100).join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'think',\n      description:\n        'Record a reasoning step without changing anything (use to plan before acting). Input: {\"thought\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const thought = str(input, 'thought');\n        if (!thought) return { ok: false, output: 'think requires a \"thought\".' };\n        return { ok: true, output: `Noted: ${thought.slice(0, 1000)}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'fetch_url',\n      description:\n        'Fetch the text of an http(s) URL (e.g. docs, a raw file). Input: {\"url\":\"https://...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!/^https?:\\/\\//i.test(url)) return { ok: false, output: 'fetch_url requires an http(s) \"url\".' };\n        const controller = new AbortController();\n        const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15_000);\n        try {\n          const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, headers: { 'user-agent': 'forge-agent' } });\n          const text = await res.text();\n          return { ok: res.ok, output: `HTTP ${res.status}\\n${text.slice(0, 20_000)}` };\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Fetch failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        } finally {\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (options.allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description:\n        'Apply exact-anchor edits to a file. Each \"find\" must occur exactly once. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"edits\":[{\"find\":\"...\",\"replace\":\"...\"}]}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const rawEdits = Array.isArray(input.edits) ? input.edits : [];\n        const edits = rawEdits.filter(\n          (e): e is { find: string; replace: string } =>\n            Boolean(e) && typeof (e as any).find === 'string' && typeof (e as any).replace === 'string'\n        );\n        if (!rel || edits.length === 0) {\n          return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires \"path\" and a non-empty \"edits\" array of {find, replace}.' };\n        }\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `Cannot edit missing file: ${rel}` };\n        const result = applyExactEdits(content, edits);\n        if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, output: `Edit rejected: ${result.error}` };\n        if (ws) {\n          const abs = resolveInWorkspace(ws, rel);\n          if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, result.content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Applied ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n        }\n        // No workspace: the pipeline stages the change later through the PR path.\n        return { ok: true, output: `Staged ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"content\":\"...\"}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const content = typeof input.content === 'string' ? input.content : '';\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'write_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        if (!ws) return { ok: false, output: 'No workspace available; cannot write files.' };\n        const abs = resolveInWorkspace(ws, rel);\n        if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n        writeFileSync(abs, content);\n        return { ok: true, output: `Wrote ${content.length} byte(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'run_check',\n      description: `Run an authorized verification command. Allowed commands: ${Object.keys(AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS).join(\n        ', '\n      )}. Mutating (may install/build).`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const command = str(input, 'command');\n        if (!command) return { ok: false, output: 'run_check requires a \"command\".' };\n        const cwd = ws ?? ctx.workspace ?? process.cwd();\n        const result = await runner.runCheck(command, cwd);\n        return {\n          ok: result.status === 'PASSED',\n          output: `exit=${result.exitCode} status=${result.status}\\n${result.stdout}\\n${result.stderr}`.slice(0, 4000),\n        };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  if (options.allowBrowser) {\n    tools.push(...buildBrowserTools());\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n\n/** Render a browser snapshot as compact text the brain can act on. */\nexport function renderSnapshot(snap: { url: string; title: string; elements: { i: number; tag: string; type?: string; text: string; href?: string }[]; text: string }): string {\n  const lines = snap.elements.map((e) => `[${e.i}] ${e.tag}${e.type ? `(${e.type})` : ''} ${e.text}${e.href ? ` -> ${e.href}` : ''}`.trimEnd());\n  return `url: ${snap.url}\\ntitle: ${snap.title}\\nelements:\\n${lines.join('\\n')}\\ntext: ${snap.text}`.slice(0, 6000);\n}\n\n/**\n * Real-browser tools. A single BrowserService is shared across the toolset so a\n * page opened by `browser_open` stays open for later `browser_click`/`browser_view`\n * calls — the brain navigates the way a person would.\n */\nexport function buildBrowserTools(executablePath?: string): AgentTool[] {\n  const browser = new BrowserService(executablePath);\n  return [\n    {\n      name: 'browser_open',\n      description:\n        'Open a real web page in a browser and return its interactive elements and text. Input: {\"url\":\"https://...\"}. Use the [i] index of an element with browser_click/browser_type.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!url) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_open requires a \"url\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.open(url)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_open failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_view',\n      description: 'Re-read the current page: url, title, interactive elements (with [i] indices) and visible text. Input: {}.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.view()) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_view failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_click',\n      description: 'Click the interactive element at an index from the latest view. Input: {\"index\":3}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const index = Number(input.index);\n        if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_click requires an integer \"index\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.click(index)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_click failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_type',\n      description: 'Type text into the element at an index from the latest view. Input: {\"index\":2,\"text\":\"hello\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const index = Number(input.index);\n        const text = str(input, 'text');\n        if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_type requires an integer \"index\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.type(index, text)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_type failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_press',\n      description: 'Press a keyboard key on the focused element, e.g. {\"key\":\"Enter\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const key = str(input, 'key') || 'Enter';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.press(key)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_press failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_scroll',\n      description: 'Scroll the page one screen. Input: {\"direction\":\"down\"} or {\"direction\":\"up\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const direction = str(input, 'direction') === 'up' ? 'up' : 'down';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.scroll(direction)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_scroll failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_extract',\n      description: 'Return the visible text of the current page, optionally only sentences matching a regex. Input: {\"pattern\":\"price\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: await browser.extract(str(input, 'pattern') || undefined) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_extract failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_query',\n      description:\n        'Answer a plain-English question about the current page with structured data (no regex). Input: {\"question\":\"what is the price\"}. Handles title, headings, links, emails, phones, prices, table rows, counts, labelled values.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderQueryResult(await browser.query(str(input, 'question'))) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_query failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_close',\n      description: 'Close the browser session and free the resources. Input: {}.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        await browser.close();\n        return { ok: true, output: 'Browser closed.' };\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n}\n",

value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `rel` under `ws` and confirm the result stays inside the workspace.\n * Lexical checks alone cannot catch a symlink inside the workspace that points\n * outside it, so the parent directory is resolved through the real filesystem.\n * Returns the absolute path, or null when the target escapes or cannot be\n * resolved safely.\n */\nfunction resolveInWorkspace(ws: string, rel: string): string | null {\n  const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n  if (!safe) return null;\n  let root: string;\n  try {\n    root = realpathSync(ws);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const abs = path.join(root, safe);\n\n  const inside = (real: string) => real === root || real.startsWith(root + path.sep);\n\n  // The deepest existing ancestor is the only part that can contain a symlink;\n  // realpath resolves every symlinked component along the way. ' (capped)' : ''}:\\n${matches.join('\\n')}`,\n        };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'find_files',\n      description:\n        'Find files by glob pattern, e.g. {\"glob\":\"src/**/*.ts\"} or {\"glob\":\"*.json\"}. A single BrowserService is shared across the toolset so a\n * page opened by `browser_open` stays open for later `browser_click`/`browser_view`\n * calls — the brain navigates the way a person would.\n */\nexport function buildBrowserTools(executablePath?: string): AgentTool[] {\n  const browser = new BrowserService(executablePath);\n  return [\n    {\n      name: 'browser_open',\n      description:\n        'Open a real web page in a browser and return its interactive elements and text. 'up' : 'down';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.scroll(direction)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_scroll failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_extract',\n      description: 'Return the visible text of the current page, optionally only sentences matching a regex.  "new_content": "/**\n * M2 — Tools for the agent loop.\n *\n * Thin adapters over Forge's existing services (GitHubService, TestRunnerService)\n * plus a bounded local workspace. The loop kernel never knows about GitHub or npm;\n * it only calls these tools by name.\n *\n * Capability tiers:\n *  - read-only tools (list_files, read_file, search, find_files, think, fetch_url)\n *    are always available;\n *  - mutating tools (edit_file, write_file, run_check) are only registered when the\n *    permission profile permits branch writes, so the brain cannot even see a\n *    state-changing capability it is not permitted to use.\n *\n * File tools prefer the mission workspace when one exists (so edits can be made and\n * then verified), and fall back to reading the repository through GitHub.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService, AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { BrowserService } from '../services/browser.ts';\nimport { renderQueryResult } from '../services/query.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport type { AgentTool, LoopContext, ToolObservation } from './loop.ts';\n\nfunction str(input: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = input[key];\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `rel` under `ws` and confirm the result stays inside the workspace.\n * Lexical checks alone cannot catch a symlink inside the workspace that points\n * outside it, so the parent directory is resolved through the real filesystem.\n * Returns the absolute path, or null when the target escapes or cannot be\n * resolved safely.\n */\nfunction resolveInWorkspace(ws: string, rel: string): string | null {\n  const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n  if (!safe) return null;\n  let root: string;\n  try {\n    root = realpathSync(ws);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const abs = path.join(root, safe);\n\n  const inside = (real: string) => real === root || real.startsWith(root + path.sep);\n\n  // The deepest existing ancestor is the only part that can contain a symlink;\n  // realpath resolves every symlinked component along the way. Any components\n  // below it do not exist yet, so they can only be plain names.\n  let probe = path.dirname(abs);\n  while (!existsSync(probe)) {\n    const next = path.dirname(probe);\n    if (next === probe) break;\n    probe = next;\n  }\n  try {\n    if (!inside(realpathSync(probe))) return null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  // If the target itself already exists, it may be a symlink pointing outside.\n  if (existsSync(abs)) {\n    try {\n      if (!inside(realpathSync(abs))) return null;\n    } catch {\n      return null;\n    }\n  }\n  return abs;\n}\n\nfunction walkFiles(root: string): string[] {\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const stack = [''];\n  while (stack.length && out.length < MAX_SCAN_FILES) {\n    const rel = stack.pop() as string;\n    const abs = path.join(root, rel);\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;\n      const childRel = rel ? path.join(rel, entry.name) : entry.name;\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) stack.push(childRel);\n      else if (entry.isFile()) out.push(childRel.split(path.sep).join('/'));\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {\n  const escaped = glob.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n  const pattern = escaped\n    .replace(/\\*\\*\\//g, '\\u0001')\n    .replace(/\\*\\*/g, '\\u0000')\n    .replace(/\\*/g, '[^/]*')\n    .replace(/\\?/g, '.')\n    .replace(/\\u0001/g, '(?:.*/)?')\n    .replace(/\\u0000/g, '.*');\n  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);\n}\n\n/** Common \"everything\" shorthands (star, double-star, double-star-slash-star) mean all files. */\nfunction matchesAll(glob: string): boolean {\n  const g = glob.trim();\n  return g === '' || g === '*' || g === '**' || g === '**/*';\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Forge toolset. Mutating tools are enabled only when `allowMutation` is\n * true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain cannot even see a state-changing\n * capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  /** Absolute path to the mission workspace, when one exists. */\n  workspace?: string;\n  /** Include the real-browser tools (open/view/click/type/scroll/extract/close). */\n  allowBrowser?: boolean;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const abs = resolveInWorkspace(ws, rel);\n      if (!abs) return null;\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!/^https?:\\/\\//i.test(url)) return { ok: false, output: 'fetch_url requires an http(s) \"url\".' };\n        const controller = new AbortController();\n        const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15_000);\n        try {\n          const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, headers: { 'user-agent': 'forge-agent' } });\n          const text = await res.text();\n          return { ok: res.ok, output: `HTTP ${res.status}\\n${text.slice(0, 20_000)}` };\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Fetch failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        } finally {\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (options.allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description:\n        'Apply exact-anchor edits to a file. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const rawEdits = Array.isArray(input.edits) ? input.edits : [];\n        const edits = rawEdits.filter(\n          (e): e is { find: string; replace: string } =>\n            Boolean(e) && typeof (e as any).find === 'string' && typeof (e as any).replace === 'string'\n        );\n        if (!rel || edits.length === 0) {\n          return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires \"path\" and a non-empty \"edits\" array of {find, replace}.' };\n        }\n        // Reject an escaping path up front so a symlink escape reads as a refusal,\n        // not as a confusing \"missing file\".\n        const target = ws ? resolveInWorkspace(ws, rel) : null;\n        if (ws && !target) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `Cannot edit missing file: ${rel}` };\n        const result = applyExactEdits(content, edits);\n        if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, output: `Edit rejected: ${result.error}` };\n        if (ws) {\n          const abs = target as string;\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, result.content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Applied ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n        }\n        // No workspace: the pipeline stages the change later through the PR path.\n        return { ok: true, output: `Staged ${edits.length} edit(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"content\":\"...\"}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        const content = typeof input.content === 'string' ? input.content : '';\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'write_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        if (!ws) return { ok: false, output: 'No workspace available; cannot write files.' };\n        const abs = resolveInWorkspace(ws, rel);\n        if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n        writeFileSync(abs, content);\n        return { ok: true, output: `Wrote ${content.length} byte(s) to ${rel} in ${ctx.workspace}.` };\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'run_check',\n      description: `Run an authorized verification command. Allowed commands: ${Object.keys(AUTHORIZED_COMMANDS).join(\n        ', '\n      )}. Mutating (may install/build).`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const command = str(input, 'command');\n        if (!command) return { ok: false, output: 'run_check requires a \"command\".' };\n        const cwd = ws ?? ctx.workspace ?? process.cwd();\n        const result = await runner.runCheck(command, cwd);\n        return {\n          ok: result.status === 'PASSED',\n          output: `exit=${result.exitCode} status=${result.status}\\n${result.stdout}\\n${result.stderr}`.slice(0, 4000),\n        };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  if (options.allowBrowser) {\n    tools.push(...buildBrowserTools());\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n\n/** Render a browser snapshot as compact text the brain can act on. */\nexport function renderSnapshot(snap: { url: string; title: string; elements: { i: number; tag: string; type?: string; text: string; href?: string }[]; text: string }): string {\n  const lines = snap.elements.map((e) => `[${e.i}] ${e.tag}${e.type ? `(${e.type})` : ''} ${e.text}${e.href ? ` -> ${e.href}` : ''}`.trimEnd());\n  return `url: ${snap.url}\\ntitle: ${snap.title}\\nelements:\\n${lines.join('\\n')}\\ntext: ${snap.text}`.slice(0, 6000);\n}\n\n/**\n * Real-browser tools. A single BrowserService is shared across the toolset so a\n * page opened by `browser_open` stays open for later `browser_click`/`browser_view`\n * calls — the brain navigates the way a person would.\n */\nexport function buildBrowserTools(executablePath?: string): AgentTool[] {\n  const browser = new BrowserService(executablePath);\n  return [\n    {\n      name: 'browser_open',\n      description:\n        'Open a real web page in a browser and return its interactive elements and text. Input: {\"url\":\"https://...\"}. Use the [i] index of an element with browser_click/browser_type.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!url) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_open requires a \"url\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.open(url)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_open failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_view',\n      description: 'Re-read the current page: url, title, interactive elements (with [i] indices) and visible text. Input: {}.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.view()) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_view failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_click',\n      description: 'Click the interactive element at an index from the latest view. Input: {\"index\":3}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const index = Number(input.index);\n        if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_click requires an integer \"index\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.click(index)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_click failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_type',\n      description: 'Type text into the element at an index from the latest view. Input: {\"index\":2,\"text\":\"hello\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const index = Number(input.index);\n        const text = str(input, 'text');\n        if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) return { ok: false, output: 'browser_type requires an integer \"index\".' };\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.type(index, text)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_type failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_press',\n      description: 'Press a keyboard key on the focused element, e.g. {\"key\":\"Enter\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const key = str(input, 'key') || 'Enter';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.press(key)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_press failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_scroll',\n      description: 'Scroll the page one screen. Input: {\"direction\":\"down\"} or {\"direction\":\"up\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const direction = str(input, 'direction') === 'up' ? 'up' : 'down';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.scroll(direction)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_scroll failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_extract',\n      description: 'Return the visible text of the current page, optionally only sentences matching a regex. Input: {\"pattern\":\"price\"}.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: await browser.extract(str(input, 'pattern') || undefined) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_extract failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_query',\n      description:\n        'Answer a plain-English question about the current page with structured data (no regex).   "body": "## What this does\n\nCloses the three adversarial gaps ChatGPT raised in the PR #78 review. Each defect was **reproduced first**, then fixed, then locked with a regression test in `tests/adversarial.test.ts` (real promises, real temp filesystem, real symlinks — no mocks).\n\n### 1. Runtime limits — *reproduced*\nThe wall-clock ceiling was only checked **between** steps, so a brain or tool that never resolved hung the loop forever. Probe: a tool returning `new Promise(() => {})` with a 30ms ceiling never returned; an outer 1500ms timeout fired instead.\n**Fix:** every brain and tool call now runs under a per-call deadline (`LoopLimits.maxCallMs`, env `FORGE_LOOP_MAX_CALL_MS`, default 2 min, never exceeding the remaining run budget). A hung call is cut off and the loop returns `BLOCKED`.\n\n### 2. Completion integrity\n`finish` was always treated as success. **Fix:** optional `verifyCompletion` gate. If it refuses, the refusal is fed back to the brain and the loop continues, bounded by `maxSteps`. Default behaviour is unchanged, so existing callers are unaffected.\n\n### 3. Workspace isolation — *reproduced*\nA symlink **inside** the workspace pointing **outside** it let `write_file`/`edit_file` escape. Probe: `write_file {path:\"escape/pwned.txt\"}` wrote a real file outside the workspace (`landed OUTSIDE workspace: true`).\n**Fix:** `resolveInWorkspace()` resolves the real path of the target and its deepest existing ancestor and refuses anything that lands outside. Ordinary `../` traversal is still refused (regression-tested).\n\n## Evidence\n- `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`): **EXIT 0**\n- `npm test`: **137 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped** (+9 adversarial)\n- New `tests/adversarial.test.ts`: hanging tool, hanging brain, slow-but-finite tool, verifier refuse/accept, symlink escape (write + edit), inside-workspace symlink allowed, `../` regression.\n\n## Scope\nOnly `src/agent/loop.ts`, `src/agent/tools.ts`, and the new test file. No change to default loop behaviour, no unrelated refactors.\n\n_This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Ahmed._",

Good. The architecture is clean and composable. I have enough to propose a design.

Let me check the CI for PR #83 first, then write the design proposal. Let me poll.

Actually, let me think about the design proposal content — this is the important deliverable.

**Forge as a software company — design**

Goal: Forge should be able to run a job the way a real software company does: multiple roles/agents that can *integrate* together to finish a job, and can *compete* (multiple candidates, best wins).

Key existing building blocks:
- `runAgentLoop(goal, tools, brain, authorize, limits, verifyCompletion)` — a bounded single-worker loop. Pure kernel, testable.
- `ModelService.chooseNextAction(state)` — a brain.
- `buildForgeTools({owner,repo,ref,token,allowMutation,workspace,allowBrowser})` — the worker's toolbox.
- `policy.ts` — permission gate (branch-write only).
- `loop-runner.ts` — wires one loop.

What's missing for a "company":
1. **Roles** — each agent has a job function, a tool subset, a prompt/persona, and a permission profile. E.g.:
   - Product/Planner → turns goal into numbered requirements + acceptance criteria (no mutations)
   - Architect → designs approach (read-only)
   - Developer → implements on a branch (mutation allowed)
   - Tester/QA → writes & runs verification, checks acceptance criteria (mutation to test files only)
   - Reviewer/Security → adversarial review of the diff (read-only)
   - Integrator → merges the work, resolves conflicts, opens the PR
2. **Collaboration (integrate together)** — a job is a pipeline/blackboard: Planner → Architect → Developer → Tester → Reviewer → Integrator. Each role reads a shared job artifact (requirements, plan, diff, test results) and appends its output. The loop kernel already supports `memory` + history; we add a `Blackboard` (shared JSON artifact) as the handoff medium.
3. **Competition** — the same role can be run N times in parallel with different strategies/seeds ("teams"), and a **judge** picks the winner by objective criteria (tests pass, acceptance criteria met, smallest diff, lint clean). This maps naturally onto: run N loops in isolated workspaces → score each → keep the best. Deterministic scoring, no LLM needed for the decision (though an LLM judge can rank ties).
4. **Integration** — the Integrator merges winning artifacts, runs the full suite, and opens the PR. Conflicts are surfaced, never silently resolved.

Design principles to keep it honest and safe (matching AGENTS.md):
- Deterministic: every stage produces an artifact; the judge uses objective signals first.
- Bounded: each role has its own step/time/cost ceiling; the whole job has a global ceiling.
- Isolated: each competing candidate gets its own git worktree/branch so they cannot clobber each other.
- Human authority: Integrator can open a PR but never auto-merge; policy gate still applies.
- Evidence: every role's output and exit codes are recorded in the job artifact.

Proposed new modules (additive, testable):
- `src/company/roles.ts` — role definitions (name, toolset, permission profile, prompt template, acceptance).
- `src/company/blackboard.ts` — the shared job artifact (requirements, plan, candidates, results, verdicts).
- `src/company/judge.ts` — pure scoring/selection of competing candidates.
- `src/company/orchestrator.ts` — runs the pipeline, fans out competitions, calls the judge, hands to the integrator.
- `src/company/company-runner.ts` — CLI/CI entry, like loop-runner.ts.
- tests: `tests/company-*.test.ts` with scripted brains (no model) so it's deterministic.

I should present this as a plan and ask for confirmation on scope/roles before building — per AGENTS.md rule (bounded changes, confirm plan on major work) and the troubleshooting guidance.

Let me be concise but concrete. I'll also mention the "compete" mechanism and "integrate" mechanism clearly.

#83 merged (`1ebd7ce`). The three defects ChatGPT found are now closed and locked with tests. Now the big one — **Forge as a whole software company**.

Let me lay out a concrete design before I build, because "whole software company" has a few possible shapes and I want to build the right one.

## The company model

The key insight: **a role is just the existing hardened loop with a different mandate, toolset, and judge.** I don't need a new engine — I need an *org layer* on top of `runAgentLoop`.

**1. Roles** (`src/company/roles.ts`) — each a named employee with:
- a mandate (what it owns), a scoped toolset, a policy profile (read-only vs branch-write), and a brain (model-backed, or scripted/deterministic for tests)
- an output contract: it must hand the next role a *typed artifact* (plan, diff, test evidence, review verdict)
- The roster: **PM** (decompose the ask into requirements), **Architect** (design), **Implementer** (write the code), **Reviewer** (read the diff, find flaws), **QA** (run real tests), **Security** (adversarial checks — the ChatGPT role), **Release** (branch/PR), **Docs**.

**2. Teams** (`src/company/team.ts`) — a team is an ordered roster + handoff contract. It runs each role through the loop, passing artifacts forward. Same shape as `stages.ts`, but the roster is configurable and each role has its own brain and authority. Produces a `TeamRun`: artifacts + evidence + status.

**3. Competition** (`src/company/compete.ts`) — the "they can compete" part. Spawn **N independent attempts** at the same work item (different roles, strategies, or models), each producing a diff + evidence. Then **judges** score them.

**4. Judges / "teachers"** (`src/company/judge.ts`) — the graders that decide who wins:
- deterministic rubrics first: tests pass, lint clean, smaller diff, no security regressions, acceptance criteria met
- optional model reviewer as a tie-breaker
- **a winner is only ever chosen on evidence** — a claim without a passing test doesn't score. Ties break deterministically.

**5. Supervisor / "CEO"** (`src/company/company.ts`) — takes one goal, decomposes it into work items, assigns a team to each, runs them (optionally in parallel), then runs an **integration** pass that merges the winners and re-verifies the whole. Bounded by a company-wide budget (steps, runtime, attempts).

**6. Shared artifact bus** (`src/company/bus.ts`) — how roles "integrate together": a typed, append-only artifact log (same discipline as `COORDINATION.md`) so every handoff is inspectable.

## Why this is real, not a demo
- It **reuses** the hardened loop, so every role inherits the timeout ceiling, completion verifier, and symlink-safe tools I just merged.
- The whole org kernel is **deterministic and unit-testable with scripted roles** — no LLM needed to prove collaboration, competition, judging, and integration.
- Model-backed brains plug in at the role boundary, exactly like `ModelService.chooseNextAction` does today.

## Phased plan (each slice ships green)
1. **Kernel (no LLM):** roles registry + team pipeline + competition + judges + supervisor, driven by scripted roles. Fully unit-tested. *This is the foundation and I can build it now.*
2. **Real brains:** wire `ModelService` per role with role-specific prompts; deterministic fallback retained.
3. **Real work:** supervisor decomposes a goal; teams work on real workspaces/branches; evidence persisted; PR opened only for the winning attempt.
4. **Surface:** `forge company:<goal>` CLI + MCP tools + `AGENTS.md`/`COORDINATION.md` + an end-to-end test.

There's **no LLM key in this environment**, so Slice 2+ can't be exercised live here — but Slice 1 and the judging/competition logic can be fully proven with real tests, and that's the part most likely to have bugs.

{
 "command": "create",
 "path": "/workspace/project/forge-company/src/kernel/loop.ts",
 "file_text": "/**\n * The company's kernel: a bounded, hardened agent loop plus a workspace-safe\n * tool registry. It is self-contained on purpose so Forge-the-company carries\n * its own engine and never depends on the Firstborn repository.\n *\n * Hardening carried over from the Firstborn review (PR #83):\n * - a per-call deadline, so a hung brain or tool cannot defeat the ceiling;\n * - an optional completion verifier, so `finish` is not automatically success;\n * - symlink-aware workspace containment for every file read and write.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, realpathSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\n\nexport interface ToolObservation {\n  ok: boolean;\n  output: string;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopContext {\n  goal: string;\n  workspace: string;\n  step: number;\n  deadlineMs?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentTool {\n  name: string;\n  description: string;\n  mutating?: boolean;\n  run(input: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation>;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentAction {\n  tool: string;\n  input?: Record<string, unknown>;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopStep {\n  index: number;\n  action: AgentAction;\n  observation: ToolObservation;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentBrainState {\n  goal: string;\n  history: LoopStep[];\n  tools: { name: string; description: string }[];\n  memory?: string;\n}\n\nexport type AgentBrain = (state: AgentBrainState) => Promise<AgentAction>;\n\nexport interface LoopLimits {\n  maxSteps: number;\n  maxRuntimeMs: number;\n  /** Ceiling (ms) for a single brain or tool call. Defaults to maxRuntimeMs. */\n  maxCallMs?: number;\n}\n\nexport type Authorization = (action: AgentAction, ctx: LoopContext) => { allowed: boolean; reason?: string };\n\nexport interface LoopResult {\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  steps: LoopStep[];\n  reason: string;\n}\n\nexport const FINISH_TOOL = 'finish';\n\nexport function loadLoopLimits(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): LoopLimits {\n  const int = (name: string, fallback: number, min: number, max: number) => {\n    const parsed = Number.parseInt(env[name] ?? '', 10);\n    if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;\n    return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, parsed));\n  };\n  return {\n    maxSteps: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_STEPS', 12, 1, 100),\n    maxRuntimeMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_RUNTIME_MS', 10 * 60 * 1000, 10_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n    maxCallMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_CALL_MS', 2 * 60 * 1000, 1_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n  };\n}\n\nasync function withDeadline<T>(promise: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {\n  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;\n  try {\n    return await Promise.race([\n      promise,\n      new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {\n        timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${label} exceeded its ${ms}ms deadline`)), ms);\n      }),\n    ]);\n  } finally {\n    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface RunLoopOptions {\n  goal: string;\n  tools: AgentTool[];\n  brain: AgentBrain;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  authorize?: Authorization;\n  workspace?: string;\n  memory?: string;\n  now?: () => number;\n  onStep?: (step: LoopStep) => void;\n  verifyCompletion?: (state: { goal: string; summary: string; history: LoopStep[] }) => { ok: boolean; reason?: string };\n}\n\nexport async function runAgentLoop(options: RunLoopOptions): Promise<LoopResult> {\n  const { goal, tools, brain, authorize, workspace = 'loop', memory } = options;\n  const limits = options.limits ?? loadLoopLimits();\n  const now = options.now ?? Date.now;\n  const startedAt = now();\n  const maxCallMs = limits.maxCallMs ?? limits.maxRuntimeMs;\n  const byName = new Map(tools.map((t) => [t.name, t]));\n  const catalog = tools.map((t) => ({ name: t.name, description: t.description }));\n  const steps: LoopStep[] = [];\n\n  for (let step = 1; step <= limits.maxSteps; step += 1) {\n    if (now() - startedAt > limits.maxRuntimeMs) {\n      return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached (${limits.maxRuntimeMs}ms); stopping safely.` };\n    }\n    const remaining = Math.max(1, limits.maxRuntimeMs - (now() - startedAt));\n    const deadlineMs = Math.min(maxCallMs, remaining);\n\n    let action: AgentAction;\n    try {\n      action = await withDeadline(brain({ goal, history: steps, tools: catalog, memory }), deadlineMs, 'Brain call');\n    } catch (err) {\n      const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      if (/deadline/.test(message)) {\n        return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached: ${message}; stopping safely.` };\n      }\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: `Brain failed: ${message}` };\n    }\n\n    if (!action || typeof action.tool !== 'string') {\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: 'Brain returned no usable action.' };\n    }\n\n    const ctx: LoopContext = { goal, workspace, step, deadlineMs };\n\n    if (action.tool === FINISH_TOOL) {\n      const summary = typeof action.input?.summary === 'string' ? action.input.summary : 'Goal reported complete.';\n      const verdict = options.verifyCompletion ? options.verifyCompletion({ goal, summary, history: steps }) : { ok: true };\n      if (verdict.ok) {\n        steps.push({ index: step, action, observation: { ok: true, output: summary } });\n        return { status: 'COMPLETED', steps, reason: summary };\n      }\n      const refused: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation: { ok: false, output: `Completion refused: ${verdict.reason ?? 'acceptance criteria not met'}` } };\n      steps.push(refused);\n      options.onStep?.(refused);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    const tool = byName.get(action.tool);\n    if (!tool) {\n      const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation: { ok: false, output: `Unknown tool \"${action.tool}\". Available: ${catalog.map((t) => t.name).join(', ')}.` } };\n      steps.push(s);\n      options.onStep?.(s);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (tool.mutating && authorize) {\n      const verdict = authorize(action, ctx);\n      if (!verdict.allowed) {\n        const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation: { ok: false, output: `Action blocked by policy: ${verdict.reason ?? 'not permitted'}` } };\n        steps.push(s);\n        options.onStep?.(s);\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n\n    let observation: ToolObservation;\n    try {\n      observation = await withDeadline(tool.run(action.input ?? {}, ctx), deadlineMs, `Tool \"${action.tool}\"`);\n    } catch (err) {\n      observation = { ok: false, output: `Tool \"${action.tool}\" threw: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n    }\n    const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation };\n    steps.push(s);\n    options.onStep?.(s);\n  }\n\n  return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Step ceiling reached (${limits.maxSteps}); stopping safely.` };\n}\n\n// --- Workspace-safe file tools ------------------------------------------------\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nexport function safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `rel` under `ws` and confirm the real path stays inside the workspace.\n * Lexical checks miss a symlink inside the workspace that points outside it, so\n * the target and its deepest existing ancestor are resolved through the real FS.\n */\nexport function resolveInWorkspace(ws: string, rel: string): string | null {\n  const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n  if (!safe) return null;\n  let root: string;\n  try {\n    root = realpathSync(ws);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const abs = path.join(root, safe);\n  const inside = (real: string) => real === root || real.startsWith(root + path.sep);\n\n  let probe = path.dirname(abs);\n  while (!existsSync(probe)) {\n    const next = path.dirname(probe);\n    if (next === probe) break;\n    probe = next;\n  }\n  try {\n    if (!inside(realpathSync(probe))) return null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  if (existsSync(abs)) {\n    try {\n      if (!inside(realpathSync(abs))) return null;\n    } catch {\n      return null;\n    }\n  }\n  return abs;\n}\n\n/**\n * A minimal, real, workspace-contained toolset every employee shares. Reads and\n * writes go through the symlink-aware resolver; `run_check` is a bounded shell\n * runner restricted to an allowlist.\n */\nexport interface WorkspaceToolsOptions {\n  workspace: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  runner?: (command: string, cwd: string) => Promise<{ status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }>;\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_AUTHORIZED: Record<string, string> = {\n  test: 'npm test',\n  lint: 'npm run lint',\n};\n\nexport function buildWorkspaceTools(options: WorkspaceToolsOptions): AgentTool[] {\n  const { workspace, allowMutation = false } = options;\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? DEFAULT_AUTHORIZED;\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read a file inside the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        const abs = resolveInWorkspace(workspace, rel);\n        if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to read outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        try {\n          if (!existsSync(abs)) return { ok: false, output: `No such file: ${rel}` };\n          return { ok: true, output: readFileSync(abs, 'utf8') };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Read failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'think',\n      description: 'Record a reasoning step without changing anything. Input: {\"thought\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input) => ({ ok: true, output: `Noted: ${typeof input.thought === 'string' ? input.thought : '(empty)'}` }),\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"content\":\"...\"}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        const content = typeof input.content === 'string' ? input.content : '';\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'write_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const abs = resolveInWorkspace(workspace, rel);\n        if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        try {\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Wrote ${content.length} byte(s) to ${rel}.` };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Write failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'run_check',\n      description: `Run an authorized verification command (${Object.keys(authorized).join(', ')}). Mutating.`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input) => {\n        const command = typeof input.command === 'string' ? input.command : '';\n        if (!(command in authorized)) return { ok: false, output: `Command \"${command}\" is not authorized. Allowed: ${Object.keys(authorized).join(', ')}.` };\n        if (!options.runner) return { ok: false, output: 'No runner configured.' };\n        const result = await options.runner(authorized[command], workspace);\n        return { ok: result.status === 'PASSED', output: `[${command}] ${result.status}: ${result.output}` };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n",

'', 10);\n    if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;\n    return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, parsed));\n  };\n  return {\n    maxSteps: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_STEPS', 12, 1, 100),\n    maxRuntimeMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_RUNTIME_MS', 10 * 60 * 1000, 10_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n    maxCallMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_CALL_MS', 2 * 60 * 1000, 1_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n  };\n}\n\nasync function withDeadline<T>(promise: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {\n  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;\n  try {\n    return await Promise.race([\n      promise,\n      new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {\n        timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${label} exceeded its ${ms}ms deadline`)), ms);\n      }),\n    ]);\n  } finally {\n    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface RunLoopOptions {\n  goal: string;\n  tools: AgentTool[];\n  brain: AgentBrain;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  authorize?: Authorization;\n  workspace?: string;\n  memory?: string;\n  now?: () => number;\n  onStep?: (step: LoopStep) => void;\n  verifyCompletion?: (state: { goal: string; summary: string; history: LoopStep[] }) => { ok: boolean; reason?: string };\n}\n\nexport async function runAgentLoop(options: RunLoopOptions): Promise<LoopResult> {\n  const { goal, tools, brain, authorize, workspace = 'loop', memory } = options;\n  const limits = options.limits ?? loadLoopLimits();\n  const now = options.now ?? Date.now;\n  const startedAt = now();\n  const maxCallMs = limits.maxCallMs ?? limits.maxRuntimeMs;\n  const byName = new Map(tools.map((t) => [t.name, t]));\n  const catalog = tools.map((t) => ({ name: t.name, description: t.description }));\n  const steps: LoopStep[] = [];\n\n  for (let step = 1; step <= limits.maxSteps; step += 1) {\n    if (now() - startedAt > limits.maxRuntimeMs) {\n      return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached (${limits.maxRuntimeMs}ms); stopping safely.` };\n    }\n    const remaining = Math.max(1, limits.maxRuntimeMs - (now() - startedAt));\n    const deadlineMs = Math.min(maxCallMs, remaining);\n\n    let action: AgentAction;\n    try {\n      action = await withDeadline(brain({ goal, history: steps, tools: catalog, memory }), deadlineMs, 'Brain call');\n    } catch (err) {\n      const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      if (/deadline/.test(message)) {\n        return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached: ${message}; stopping safely.` };\n      }\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: `Brain failed: ${message}` };\n    }\n\n    if (!action || typeof action.tool !== 'string') {\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: 'Brain returned no usable action.' };\n    }\n\n    const ctx: LoopContext = { goal, workspace, step, deadlineMs };\n\n    if (action.tool === FINISH_TOOL) {\n      const summary = typeof action.input?.summary === 'string' ? action.input.summary : 'Goal reported complete.';\n      const verdict = options.verifyCompletion ? options.verifyCompletion({ goal, summary, history: steps }) : { ok: true };\n      if (verdict.ok) {\n        steps.push({ index: step, action, observation: { ok: true, output: summary } });\n        return { status: 'COMPLETED', steps, reason: summary };\n      }\n      const refused: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation: { ok: false, output: `Completion refused: ${verdict.reason ?? 'acceptance criteria not met'}` } };\n      steps.push(refused);\n      options.onStep?.(refused);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    const tool = byName.get(action.tool);\n    if (!tool) {\n      const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation: { ok: false, output: `Unknown tool \"${action.tool}\". Available: ${catalog.map((t) => t.name).join(', ')}.` } };\n      steps.push(s);\n      options.onStep?.(s);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (tool.mutating && authorize) {\n      const verdict = authorize(action, ctx);\n      if (!verdict.allowed) {\n        const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation: { ok: false, output: `Action blocked by policy: ${verdict.reason ?? 'not permitted'}` } };\n        steps.push(s);\n        options.onStep?.(s);\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n\n    let observation: ToolObservation;\n    try {\n      observation = await withDeadline(tool.run(action.input ?? {}, ctx), deadlineMs, `Tool \"${action.tool}\"`);\n    } catch (err) {\n      observation = { ok: false, output: `Tool \"${action.tool}\" threw: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n    }\n    const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation };\n    steps.push(s);\n    options.onStep?.(s);\n  }\n\n  return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Step ceiling reached (${limits.maxSteps}); stopping safely.` };\n}\n\n// --- Workspace-safe file tools ------------------------------------------------\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nexport function safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `rel` under `ws` and confirm the real path stays inside the workspace.\n * Lexical checks miss a symlink inside the workspace that points outside it, so\n * the target and its deepest existing ancestor are resolved through the real FS.\n */\nexport function resolveInWorkspace(ws: string, rel: string): string | null {\n  const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n  if (!safe) return null;\n  let root: string;\n  try {\n    root = realpathSync(ws);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const abs = path.join(root, safe);\n  const inside = (real: string) => real === root || real.startsWith(root + path.sep);\n\n  let probe = path.dirname(abs);\n  while (!existsSync(probe)) {\n    const next = path.dirname(probe);\n    if (next === probe) break;\n    probe = next;\n  }\n  try {\n    if (!inside(realpathSync(probe))) return null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  if (existsSync(abs)) {\n    try {\n      if (!inside(realpathSync(abs))) return null;\n    } catch {\n      return null;\n    }\n  }\n  return abs;\n}\n\n/**\n * A minimal, real, workspace-contained toolset every employee shares. Reads and\n * writes go through the symlink-aware resolver; `run_check` is a bounded shell\n * runner restricted to an allowlist.\n */\nexport interface WorkspaceToolsOptions {\n  workspace: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  runner?: (command: string, cwd: string) => Promise<{ status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }>;\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_AUTHORIZED: Record<string, string> = {\n  test: 'npm test',\n  lint: 'npm run lint',\n};\n\nexport function buildWorkspaceTools(options: WorkspaceToolsOptions): AgentTool[] {\n  const { workspace, allowMutation = false } = options;\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? DEFAULT_AUTHORIZED;\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read a file inside the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        const abs = resolveInWorkspace(workspace, rel);\n        if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to read outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        try {\n          if (!existsSync(abs)) return { ok: false, output: `No such file: ${rel}` };\n          return { ok: true, output: readFileSync(abs, 'utf8') };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Read failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'think',\n      description: 'Record a reasoning step without changing anything. Input: {\"thought\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input) => ({ ok: true, output: `Noted: ${typeof input.thought === 'string' ? input.thought : '(empty)'}` }),\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"content\":\"...\"}. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        const content = typeof input.content === 'string' ? input.content : '';\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'write_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const abs = resolveInWorkspace(workspace, rel);\n        if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        try {\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Wrote ${content.length} byte(s) to ${rel}.` };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Write failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'run_check',\n      description: `Run an authorized verification command (${Object.keys(authorized).join(', ')}). Mutating.`,\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input) => {\n        const command = typeof input.command === 'string' ? input.command : '';\n        if (!(command in authorized)) return { ok: false, output: `Command \"${command}\" is not authorized. Allowed: ${Object.keys(authorized).join(', ')}.` };\n        if (!options.runner) return { ok: false, output: 'No runner configured.' };\n        const result = await options.runner(authorized[command], workspace);\n        return { ok: result.status === 'PASSED', output: `[${command}] ${result.status}: ${result.output}` };\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return tools;\n}\n",

{
 "command": "create",
 "path": "/workspace/project/forge-company/src/company/bus.ts",
 "file_text": "/**\n * The artifact bus: how employees hand work to each other.\n *\n * An append-only, typed log. Every handoff between roles is recorded, so a\n * company run is fully inspectable after the fact (the same discipline the\n * Firstborn COORDINATION.md uses). Nothing is overwritten; later stages read\n * what earlier stages produced.\n */\n\nexport type ArtifactKind = 'requirements' | 'design' | 'change' | 'review' | 'evidence' | 'security' | 'decision' | 'note';\n\nexport interface Artifact {\n  id: string;\n  kind: ArtifactKind;\n  /** The role that produced it. */\n  author: string;\n  /** Which work item / attempt it belongs to. */\n  scope: string;\n  /** Human-readable summary. */\n  summary: string;\n  /** Structured payload (diff text, findings, test evidence, ...). */\n  data: Record<string, unknown>;\n  at: string;\n}\n\nexport class ArtifactBus {\n  private readonly log: Artifact[] = [];\n  private seq = 0;\n  private readonly now: () => Date;\n\n  constructor(now: () => Date = () => new Date()) {\n    this.now = now;\n  }\n\n  post(a: Omit<Artifact, 'id' | 'at'>): Artifact {\n    this.seq += 1;\n    const artifact: Artifact = { ...a, id: `A-${String(this.seq).padStart(4, '0')}`, at: this.now().toISOString() };\n    this.log.push(artifact);\n    return artifact;\n  }\n\n  all(): readonly Artifact[] {\n    return this.log;\n  }\n\n  /** Artifacts for one work item / attempt. */\n  forScope(scope: string): Artifact[] {\n    return this.log.filter((a) => a.scope === scope);\n  }\n\n  /** Most recent artifact of a kind within a scope, or undefined. */\n  latest(scope: string, kind: ArtifactKind): Artifact | undefined {\n    for (let i = this.log.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {\n      const a = this.log[i];\n      if (a.scope === scope && a.kind === kind) return a;\n    }\n    return undefined;\n  }\n}\n",

}
