 "new_content": "/**\n * Teams: an ordered roster that works one job together.\n *\n * Each role runs the hardened loop with its own mandate, tools and authority,\n * then posts its artifact to the shared bus. Later roles read what earlier roles\n * produced, which is how the employees \"integrate\" — the handoff is explicit and\n * typed, never implicit.\n */\nimport { runAgentLoop, FINISH_TOOL, type AgentAction, type LoopLimits } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { ArtifactBus } from './bus.ts';\nimport type { Role, RoleInput, RoleResult } from './roles.ts';\n\nexport interface TeamRun {\n  workItem: string;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  results: { role: string; result: RoleResult }[];\n  /** Files under change after the team ran (for downstream judging). */\n  changes: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nexport interface TeamOptions {\n  /** The whole-company goal. */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The work item this team owns. */\n  workItem: string;\n  /** The scope id for artifacts (usually `${workItem}#${attempt}`). */\n  scope: string;\n  /** The ordered roster. */\n  roster: Role[];\n  /** Shared artifact bus. */\n  bus: ArtifactBus;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Files under change; a mutating role may add to this. */\n  changes?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Stop the whole team if a role fails (default: true for producers of change). */\n  stopOnFailure?: boolean;\n  /** A directory a mutating role writes real files into, so the change map reflects disk. */\n  workspaceDir?: string;\n}\n\n/** Derive a role result from the loop's terminal action. */\nfunction interpret(role: Role, actions: AgentAction[], status: string, reason: string): RoleResult {\n  const finish = [...actions].reverse().find((a) => a.tool === FINISH_TOOL);\n  const data = (finish?.input?.data as Record<string, unknown> | undefined) ?? {};\n  const summary = (finish?.input?.summary as string | undefined) ?? reason;\n  return {\n    ok: status === 'COMPLETED',\n    kind: role.produces,\n    summary,\n    data,\n    steps: actions.length,\n    reason: status === 'COMPLETED' ? undefined : reason,\n  };\n}\n\nexport async function runTeam(options: TeamOptions): Promise<TeamRun> {\n  const { goal, workItem, scope, roster, bus } = options;\n  const stopOnFailure = options.stopOnFailure ?? true;\n  const changes: Record<string, string> = { ...(options.changes ?? {}) };\n  const results: { role: string; result: RoleResult }[] = [];\n\n  for (const role of roster) {\n    const input: RoleInput = {\n      goal,\n      workItem,\n      scope,\n      artifacts: bus.forScope(scope),\n      changes: { ...changes },\n    };\n\n    // Give the brain the upstream artifacts and the files already under change.\n    const memory = JSON.stringify({\n      upstream: input.artifacts.map((a) => ({ kind: a.kind, author: a.author, summary: a.summary, data: a.data })),\n      changes: input.changes,\n    });\n\n    const loop = await runAgentLoop({\n      goal: `${role.title}: ${role.mandate} [${workItem}]`,\n      tools: role.tools,\n      brain: (state) => role.brain({ ...state, memory: state.memory }),\n      authorize: role.authorize,\n      limits: role.limits ?? options.limits,\n      workspace: scope,\n      memory,\n      verifyCompletion: role.verifyCompletion,\n    });\n\n    const result = interpret(role, loop.steps.map((s) => s.action), loop.status, loop.reason);\n\n    // A mutating role records the files it changed. `files` must be a path->content\n    // map; a plain list of touched names (e.g. from a design) is not a change.\n    const wrote = result.data.files;\n    if (wrote && typeof wrote === 'object' && !Array.isArray(wrote)) {\n      Object.assign(changes, wrote as Record<string, string>);\n    }\n    // Capture files the role actually wrote to disk, so the change map reflects\n    // real writes even when the brain did not enumerate them in its finish data.\n    if (options.workspaceDir) {\n      for (const step of loop.steps) {\n        if (step.action.tool !== 'write_file' || !step.observation.ok) continue;\n        const rel = step.action.input?.path;\n        if (typeof rel !== 'string') continue;\n        try {\n          changes[rel] = readFileSync(path.join(options.workspaceDir, rel), 'utf8');\n        } catch {\n          /* file vanished; skip */\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    bus.post({ kind: role.produces, author: role.id, scope, summary: result.summary, data: { ...result.data, files: { ...changes } } });\n    results.push({ role: role.id, result });\n\n    if (!result.ok && stopOnFailure) {\n      return { workItem, status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `${role.id} failed: ${result.reason ?? result.summary}`, results, changes };\n    }\n  }\n\n  const failed = results.some((r) => !r.result.ok);\n  return {\n    workItem,\n    status: failed ? 'BLOCKED' : 'COMPLETED',\n    reason: failed ? 'one or more roles failed' : 'team completed the work item',\n    results,\n    changes,\n  };\n}\n",

 "file_text": "/**\n * A bounded shell runner for `run_check`.\n *\n * Verification commands are executed for real, but only commands on an explicit\n * allowlist, only inside the workspace, with a hard timeout and no shell\n * metacharacters. This is the same discipline the Firstborn TestRunnerService\n * uses: an authorized command map, never a free-form shell.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\n\nexport interface CheckResult {\n  status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED';\n  output: string;\n  exitCode: number | null;\n  timedOut: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface RunCheckOptions {\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n  maxOutputBytes?: number;\n}\n\n/** Reject a command string that could chain, redirect, or substitute. */\nexport function isSimpleCommand(command: string): boolean {\n  if (!command.trim()) return false;\n  return !/[;&|`$><\\n\\\\]/.test(command);\n}\n\nexport function runCommand(command: string, cwd: string, options: RunCheckOptions = {}): Promise<CheckResult> {\n  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? 120_000;\n  const maxOutput = options.maxOutputBytes ?? 64_000;\n  return new Promise((resolve) => {\n    if (!isSimpleCommand(command)) {\n      resolve({ status: 'FAILED', output: `Refused unsafe command: ${command}`, exitCode: null, timedOut: false });\n      return;\n    }\n    const parts = command.split(/\\s+/);\n    const child = spawn(parts[0], parts.slice(1), { cwd, shell: false, env: process.env });\n    let out = '';\n    let timedOut = false;\n    const timer = setTimeout(() => {\n      timedOut = true;\n      child.kill('SIGKILL');\n    }, timeoutMs);\n    const append = (chunk: Buffer) => {\n      if (out.length < maxOutput) out += chunk.toString('utf8');\n    };\n    child.stdout?.on('data', append);\n    child.stderr?.on('data', append);\n    child.on('error', (err) => {\n      clearTimeout(timer);\n      resolve({ status: 'FAILED', output: `${out}\\n${err.message}`.trim(), exitCode: null, timedOut });\n    });\n    child.on('close', (code) => {\n      clearTimeout(timer);\n      resolve({ status: code === 0 && !timedOut ? 'PASSED' : 'FAILED', output: out.slice(0, maxOutput).trim(), exitCode: code, timedOut });\n    });\n  });\n}\n",

{
 "command": "create",
 "path": "/workspace/project/forge-company/src/company/role-tools.ts",
 "file_text": "/**\n * Role tools: the real workspace tools each employee is handed.\n *\n * Reads are always available. Only `branch-write` roles get `write_file` and\n * `run_check`, and a mutation is refused unless its path is inside the role's\n * allowed roots. Every write is recorded so the team's change map reflects disk.\n */\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools, type AgentTool } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\n\nexport interface RoleToolsOptions {\n  /** The real directory this role works in. */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** True for `branch-write` roles. */\n  canMutate: boolean;\n  /** Relative path prefixes a write is confined to. Defaults to the whole workspace. */\n  allowedRoots?: string[];\n  /** Authorized verification commands: label -> command. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Called for each accepted write, so the caller can build a change map. */\n  onWrite?: (path: string) => void;\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_COMMANDS: Record<string, string> = {\n  test: 'npm test',\n  lint: 'npm run lint',\n};\n\nexport function buildRoleTools(options: RoleToolsOptions): AgentTool[] {\n  const roots = options.allowedRoots?.length ? options.allowedRoots : [''];\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? DEFAULT_COMMANDS;\n\n  const base = buildWorkspaceTools({\n    workspace: options.workspaceDir,\n    allowMutation: options.canMutate,\n    authorizedCommands: authorized,\n    runner: (command, cwd) => runCommand(command, cwd),\n  });\n\n  return base.map((tool) => {\n    if (tool.name !== 'write_file') return tool;\n    const original = tool.run;\n    return {\n      ...tool,\n      run: async (input, ctx) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        if (!roots.some((root) => root === '' || rel === root || rel.startsWith(root.endsWith('/') ? root : root + '/'))) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the allowed roots (${roots.join(', ')}): ${rel}` };\n        }\n        const result = await original(input, ctx);\n        if (result.ok) options.onWrite?.(rel);\n        return result;\n      },\n    };\n  });\n}\n",

Every lookup is scoped to the attempt being scored, so one\n * attempt can never win on another attempt's evidence. The rubric is pure, so it\n * can be unit-tested and audited, and two attempts with identical evidence always\n * rank the same way.\n */\nimport type { ArtifactBus } from './bus.ts';\nimport type { TeamRun } from './team.ts';\n\nexport interface RubricContext {\n  /** The attempt scope being scored, e.g. `w1#2`. */\n  attempt: string;\n  run: TeamRun;\n  bus: ArtifactBus;\n}\n\nexport interface Scorecard {\n  attempt: string;\n  criteria: Record<string, number>;\n  total: number;\n  eligible: boolean;\n  notes: string[];\n}\n\nexport interface Rubric {\n  name: string;\n  points: number;\n  mandatory?: boolean;\n  test: (ctx: RubricContext) => boolean;\n}\n\nfunction evidenceChecks(ctx: RubricContext): { name: string; status: string }[] {\n  return (ctx.bus.latest(ctx.attempt, 'evidence')?.data.checks as { name: string; status: string }[] | undefined) ?? [];\n}\n\nfunction passing(ctx: RubricContext, check: string): boolean {\n  return evidenceChecks(ctx).some((c) => c.name === check && c.status === 'PASSED');\n}\n\nfunction latestInScope(ctx: RubricContext, kind: 'review' | 'security') {\n  return ctx.bus.latest(ctx.attempt, kind);\n}\n\n/** The default rubric: real checks and real evidence beat confident summaries. */\nexport const DEFAULT_RUBRIC: Rubric[] = [\n  { name: 'completed', points: 3, mandatory: true, test: ({ run }) => run.status === 'COMPLETED' },\n  { name: 'tests-pass', points: 5, mandatory: true, test: (ctx) => passing(ctx, 'test') },\n  { name: 'lint-clean', points: 2, test: (ctx) => passing(ctx, 'lint') },\n  { name: 'review-clean', points: 2, test: (ctx) => Number(latestInScope(ctx, 'review')?.data.blockers ?? 1) === 0 },\n  { name: 'security-clean', points: 3, mandatory: true, test: (ctx) => latestInScope(ctx, 'security')?.data.clean === true },\n  { name: 'has-change', points: 1, test: ({ run }) => Object.keys(run.changes).length > 0 },\n];\n\nexport function scoreAttempt(attempt: string, run: TeamRun, bus: ArtifactBus, rubric: Rubric[] = DEFAULT_RUBRIC): Scorecard {\n  const ctx: RubricContext = { attempt, run, bus };\n  const criteria: Record<string, number> = {};\n  const notes: string[] = [];\n  let total = 0;\n  let eligible = true;\n  for (const r of rubric) {\n    const pass = r.test(ctx);\n    criteria[r.name] = pass ? r.points : 0;\n    if (pass) total += r.points;\n    if (!pass && r.mandatory) {\n      eligible = false;\n      notes.push(`ineligible: mandatory \"${r.name}\" not met`);\n    } else if (!pass) {\n      notes.push(`missed \"${r.name}\" (-${r.points})`);\n    }\n  }\n  return { attempt, criteria, total, eligible, notes };\n}\n\nexport interface Competition {\n  workItem: string;\n  scorecards: Scorecard[];\n  winner: string | null;\n  reason: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Rank attempts deterministically: eligible first, then by total points, then by\n * attempt id, so the outcome never depends on order of arrival.\n */\nexport function judgeCompetition(workItem: string, runs: { attempt: string; run: TeamRun }[], bus: ArtifactBus, rubric: Rubric[] = DEFAULT_RUBRIC): Competition {\n  const scorecards = runs.map(({ attempt, run }) => scoreAttempt(attempt, run, bus, rubric));\n  const ranked = [...scorecards].sort((a, b) => {\n    if (a.eligible !== b.eligible) return a.eligible ? -1 : 1;\n    if (a.total !== b.total) return b.total - a.total;\n    return a.attempt < b.attempt ? -1 : a.attempt > b.attempt ? 1 : 0;\n  });\n  const best = ranked[0];\n  if (!best || !best.eligible) {\n    return { workItem, scorecards, winner: null, reason: 'no attempt met the mandatory criteria' };\n  }\n  return { workItem, scorecards, winner: best.attempt, reason: `attempt \"${best.attempt}\" won with ${best.total} point(s)` };\n}"

'ok' : 'FAILED'}: ${h.observation.output.slice(0, 400)}`).join('\\n')\n    : '(no actions yet)';\n  const upstream = state.memory?.trim() ? `What earlier roles produced (JSON, oldest first):\\n${state.memory.trim().slice(0, 6000)}\\n` : '';\n  return `You are the ${spec.role} in a software company. Do not repeat an action you already took.\n- Read a file before editing it.\n- When your mandate is satisfied, return {\"tool\":\"finish\",\"input\":{\"summary\":\"...\",\"data\":{...}}}.\n- ${spec.artifactHint}\n- Use only tools from the list. '../src/company/company.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { ModelService } from '../src/company/model.ts';\nimport { modelBrain } from '../src/company/brains.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\n\nconst TARGET_COMMANDS: Record<string, string> = {\n  test: 'npm test',\n  lint: 'npm run lint',\n};\n\n/** A self-contained target so `--target` demonstrates a real };\n    case 'architect':\n      return { design: 'a small, reversible change', files: ['src/feature.ts'] };\n    case 'implementer':\n      return { files: { 'src/feature.ts': `// attempt {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction scriptedBrain(id: string, attempt: number): AgentBrain {\n  const script: AgentAction[] = [\n    { tool: 'think', input: { thought: `${id} plans the work` } },\n    { tool:   produces: r.produces,\n    tools: [{ name: 'think', description: 'noop', run: async () => ({ ok: true, output: 'ok' }) }],\n    brain: scriptedBrain(r.id, attempt),\n  }));\n}\n\nfunction modelRoster(model: ModelService, attempt: number, workspaceDir: string): Role[] {\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({\n      workspaceDir,\n      canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write',\n      allowedRoots: [''],\n      authorizedCommands: TARGET_COMMANDS,\n    }),\n    brain: modelBrain(model, {\n      role: `${r.title} (attempt ${attempt})`,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      artifactHint: `Emit your ' Use read_file, write_file, and run_check on the real workspace.' : ''}`,\n    }),\n  }));\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const args = process.argv.slice(2);\n  const useModel = args.includes('--model');\n  const targetIdx = args.indexOf('--target');\n  const explicitTarget = targetIdx >= 0 ? args[targetIdx + 1] : undefined;\n  const goal = args.filter((a, i) => a !== '--model' && a !== '--target' && i !== targetIdx + 1).join(' ').trim() || 'Demonstrate the company on a sample goal.';\n\n  const useTarget = Boolean(explicitTarget) || args.includes('--target');\n  const workspaceDir = useTarget ? explicitTarget ?? sampleTarget() : undefined;\n  if (workspaceDir) console.log(`[target] ${workspaceDir}${explicitTarget ? '' : ' (generated sample)'}`);\n\n  const bus = new ArtifactBus();\n  const model = useModel ? new ModelService() : null;\n  if (model) {\n    const info = model.getProviderInfo();\n    console.log(`[model] ${info.primaryProvider}; Gemini fallback configured: ${info.fallbackConfigured}`);\n  }\n\n  const attemptsPerItem = Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(process.env.FORGE_COMPANY_ATTEMPTS ?? '', 10) || 2);\n  const result = await runCompany({\n    goal,\n    bus,\n    plan: (g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }],\n    rosterFor: (_item, attempt) => (model ? modelRoster(model, attempt, workspaceDir ?? process.cwd()) : scriptedRoster(attempt)),\n    attemptsPerItem,\n    workspaceDir,\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({ ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0, reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'no change produced' }),\n  });\n\n  console.log('--- FORGE COMPANY REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Goal:', result.goal);\n  console.log('Status:', result.status);\n  console.log('Reason:', result.reason);\n  console.log('Winners:', result.winners.join(', ') || '(none)');\n  console.log('Artifacts:', bus.all().length);\n  for (const item of result.items) {\n    console.log(`- ${item.item.title}: ${item.competition.reason}`);\n    for (const card of item.competition.scorecards) {\n      console.log(`    ${card.attempt}: ${card.total} pt(s)${card.eligible ? '' : ' [ineligible]'}`);\n    }\n  }\n  const changes = result.items.flatMap((i) => i.competition.winner ? [i.competition.winner] : []);\n  console.log('Changed files:', Object.keys(result.changes).length ? Object.keys(result.changes).join(', ') : '(none)');\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error('[forge-company] failed:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

DEFAULT_RUBRIC;\n\n  const items = plan(goal);\n  const results: { item: WorkItem; competition: Competition }[] = [];\n  let integratedChanges: Record<string, string> = { ...(options.changes ?? {}) };\n  const winners: string[] = [];\n  let roleRuns = 0;\n\n  for (const item of items) {\n    const runs: { attempt: string; run: TeamRun }[] = [];\n    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attemptsPerItem; attempt += 1) {\n      if (roleRuns >= maxRoleRuns) {\n        return { goal, items: results, integratedChanges, winners, status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `company budget exhausted (${maxRoleRuns} role-runs)`, bus };\n      }\n      const roster = rosterFor(item, attempt);\n      roleRuns += roster.length;\n      const attemptId = `${item.id}#${attempt}`;\n      const run = await runTeam({\n        goal,\n        workItem: item.title,\n        scope: attemptId,\n        roster,\n        bus,\n        limits: options.limits,\n        changes: integratedChanges,\n        workspaceDir: options.workspaceDir,\n      });\n      runs.push({ attempt: attemptId, run });\n    }\n\n    const competition = judgeCompetition(item.title, runs, bus, rubric);\n    results.push({ item, competition });\n\n    if (!competition.winner) {\n      return { goal, items: results, integratedChanges, winners, status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no eligible attempt for \"${item.title}\"`, bus };\n    }\n    winners.push(competition.winner);\n    const winning = runs.find((r) => r.attempt === competition.winner)!.run;\n    integratedChanges = { ...integratedChanges, ...winning.changes };\n    bus.post({\n      kind: 'decision',\n      author: 'supervisor',\n      scope: competition.winner,\n      summary: competition.reason,\n      data: { workItem: item.title, winner: competition.winner, scorecards: competition.scorecards },\n    });\n  }\n\n  const verdict = options.integrate\n    ? options.integrate({ goal, winners, changes: integratedChanges, bus })\n    : { ok: true, reason: 'all work items resolved and integrated' };\n\n  return {\n    goal,\n    items: results,\n    integratedChanges,\n    winners,\n    status: verdict.ok ? 'COMPLETED' : 'BLOCKED',\n    reason: verdict.reason,\n    bus,\n  };\n}"

```
The scripted CLI works but the goal got mangled: "Demonstrate the company on a sample goal." instead of "add a health check endpoint". The arg filtering is wrong.

Let me look: `args.filter((a, i) => a !== '--model' && a !== '--target' && i !== targetIdx + 1)`. targetIdx = -1, so targetIdx+1 = 0, which excludes the FIRST arg! That's the bug. When there's no `--target`, targetIdx=-1 and i !== 0 excludes the first arg.

Fix: only exclude targetIdx+1 when targetIdx >= 0.

Let me fix.

Now I can see exactly what's happening:

1. Step 1: model read index.js — GOOD.
2. Step 2: model tried read_file again → guard replaced with think. GOOD guard.
3. Step 3: model wrote index.js with getHealth (returns 'OK' not {status:'ok'}, but close) — GOOD write.
4. Step 4: model tried read_file AGAIN → guard → think. The model is stuck in a loop trying to re-read.
5. Step 5: run_check with no command → FAIL (model didn't provide command). 
6. Step 6: run_check command:test → PASSED! Real test passed.
7. Step 7: model gave up → finish with the fallback summary "could not choose an action".

So the REAL failure: the model kept trying to `read_file index.js` repeatedly (steps 2, 4), got nudged to `think`, and after a few steps the brain returned an unusable action → the modelBrain fell back to finish. The finish had EMPTY data (no `files`, no artifact).

Key insight: The model is trying to re-read the file it just wrote to verify, but the guard blocks the identical read. Then it gets confused. The guard nudge ("Already ran... Choose a different tool or finish") is being treated by the model as an observation, and the model tries the SAME read again next step → nudge again → eventually the model outputs nothing parseable → fallback finish with empty data.

Problems to fix:
1. **The finish fallback emits empty data.** When the model can't produce a valid action, we finish with empty data — losing the change. Better: the fallback finish should include the observed checks and note the change. Actually, the change IS captured from disk (write_file step 3), so `changes` should have index.js. But the run reported "Changed files: (none)". Why? Because in the team, the write capture reads from `options.workspaceDir` — which is the SAMPLE target dir. And write happened there. Let me check: the team passes workspaceDir, and captures `readFileSync(path.join(workspaceDir, rel))`. That should work... but the attempt scored 0 for has-change. Hmm.

Wait — in the real E2E run, was there a write_file step? The live E2E reported "Artifacts: 7" and 6 pts. Let me reconsider. Maybe in the E2E run the implementer didn't write (different random model output). The debug run DID write. Inconsistent model behavior between runs.

Actually the bigger issue: **the model gets stuck re-reading**, wasting steps, and eventually the brain returns nothing → empty finish. This is a prompt/loop design issue.

2. **run_check with empty input** (step 5) — the model called run_check without a command. That's a model error but wastes a step.

Let me improve several things:

a) **Better guard behavior**: Instead of replacing a repeated read with a `think` (which confuses the model), we should give it a stronger, clearer nudge, OR better: the modelBrain should track what it already did and include a firmer instruction. Actually, the root issue is the model wants to re-read after writing. A reasonable fix: after a write, re-reading the same file IS informative (it changed). But the guard blocks it because the (tool,input) matches the earlier read. 

Hmm — actually re-reading a file you just wrote is redundant. But the model does it. 

b) **The fallback finish should carry useful data**: when the model fails to produce a parseable action, finish with the observed checks and a note. But the change is captured separately from disk, so that's fine.

c) **The real fix for eligibility**: The attempt needs `has-change` (changes non-empty) + tests-pass (QA ran test) + security-clean + completed. In the debug run, the write succeeded (index.js changed) and test passed. So if this were the full team, has-change would be true and QA test would pass. But in the E2E run, it was ineligible with 6 pts (no has-change, no tests-pass). So the E2E implementer didn't write.

The core problem is **model reliability**: the model gets stuck and doesn't reliably write + QA doesn't reliably run the check.

Let me think about how to make this robust:

**Option A: Make the prompts much more directive per role.** E.g., implementer prompt: "You MUST call write_file exactly once with the full file content, then run_check with command 'test', then finish with data.files = {path: content}." This is like a scripted-but-model-filled approach.

**Option B: Add a "verification" step in the team flow**: after the implementer, the QA role is explicitly instructed to run the checks. And the implementer's write is captured from disk regardless of finish data.

**Option C: Handle the "stuck re-read" better.** When the guard triggers, instead of `think`, return a finish if the model has already done a write? No — too aggressive.

Let me focus on making the E2E reliably COMPLETE:

1. Improve role prompts to be very explicit about the required tool sequence per role.
2. Make the guard, when it triggers on a repeated read, produce a nudge that strongly pushes to the next action.
3. Ensure the fallback finish includes observed run_check results as checks (so QA evidence survives even if the model gives up).

Good. So QA just needs to actually call run_check. The QA prompt should say: "Call run_check with command 'test' and command 'lint'. Then finish."

For the implementer: the change is captured from disk on write_file. So implementer just needs to call write_file. The prompt should say: "Call write_file once with the complete new content of the target file. Then finish."

So the fix is mostly **much more directive prompts** + **reducing the stuck-loop**.

**reasoning_content:**
```
The pending count logic is flawed: it compares the sequence string (e.g. "read_file x") with the JSON key of the action, which will never match. So pending = 2 always (both entries unmatched). My test expected 1. The logic is wrong — the sequence entries are human descriptions, not JSON keys.

assert.ok(!readOnly.includes('run_check'));\n  const mutating = buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: true }).map((t) => t.name);\n  assert.ok(mutating.includes('write_file'));\n  assert.ok(mutating.includes('run_check'));\n});\n\ntest('write_file is confined to the allowed roots', async () => {\n  const dir = tmp();\n  const tools = buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: true, allowedRoots: ['src'] });\n  const write = tools.find((t) => t.name === 'write_file')!;\n  const ctx = { goal: 'g', workspace: dir, step: 1 };\n  const ok = await write.run({ path: 'src/a.ts', content: 'x' }, ctx);\n  assert.equal(ok.ok, true);\n  assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'src/a.ts')));\n  const refused = await write.run({ path: 'outside.ts', content: 'x' }, ctx);\n  assert.equal(refused.ok, false);\n  assert.match(refused.output, /Refusing to write outside the allowed roots/);\n  assert.ok(!fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'outside.ts')));\n});\n\ntest('run_check runs an authorized command for real and refuses an unknown one', async () => {\n  const dir = tmp();\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'lint.js'), 'run_check')!;\n  const ctx = { goal: 'g', workspace: dir, step: 1 };\n  const passed = await check.run({ command: 'lint' }, ctx);\n  assert.equal(passed.ok, true);\n  assert.match(passed.output, /PASSED/);\n  const unknown = await check.run({ command: 'rm' }, ctx);\n  assert.equal(unknown.ok, false);\n  assert.match(unknown.output, /not authorized/);\n});\n\ntest('the team change map reflects files a role really wrote to disk', async () => {\n  const dir = tmp();\n  const bus = new ArtifactBus();\n  const role: Role = {\n    id: 'implementer',\n    title: 'Implementer',\n    mandate: 'write the change',\n    authority: 'branch-write',\n    produces: 'change',\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: true, allowedRoots: [''] }),\n    brain: async (state) =>\n      state.history.length === 0\n        ? { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: 'feature.txt', content: 'hello world' } }\n        : { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'wrote it', data: {} } },\n  };\n  const run = await runTeam({ goal: 'g', workItem: 'w', scope: 'w#1', roster: [role], bus, workspaceDir: dir });\n  assert.equal(run.status, 'COMPLETED');\n  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(run.changes), ['feature.txt']);\n  assert.equal(run.changes['feature.txt'], 'hello world');\n});\n\ntest('the role prompt renders the required sequence', () => {\n  const prompt = buildRolePrompt(\n    { role: 'Implementer', mandate: 'write', artifactHint: 'Emit change.', sequence: ['read_file x', 'write_file y'] },\n    { goal: 'g', history: [{ index: 1, action: { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'x' } }, y/);\n});\n\ntest('a whole company run completes using real workspace tools and real checks', async () => {\n  const dir = tmp();\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'ok.js'), 'process.exit(0);');\n  const commands = { test: 'node ok.js' };\n  const mk = (id: Role['id'], produces: Role['produces'], brain: Role['brain'], canMutate = false): Role => ({\n    id, title: id, mandate: id, authority: canMutate ? 'branch-write' : 'read-only', produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate, allowedRoots: [''], authorizedCommands: commands }),\n    brain,\n  });\n  const finish = (data: Record<string, unknown>): Role['brain'] => async () => ({ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'done', data } });\n  const implementer: Role['brain'] = async (state) =>\n    state.history.length === 0\n      ? { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: 'out.txt', content: 'done' } }\n      : { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'wrote', data: {} } };\n  const qa: Role['brain'] = async (state) =>\n    state.history.some((h) => h.action.tool === 'run_check')\n      ? { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'checked', data: {} } }\n      : { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } };\n\n  const roster = [\n    mk('pm', 'requirements', finish({ items: ['a'] })),\n    mk('architect', 'design', finish({ design: 'd', files: ['out.txt'] })),\n    mk('implementer', 'change', implementer, true),\n    mk('reviewer', 'review', finish({ blockers: 0, notes: [] })),\n    mk('qa', 'evidence', qa, true),\n    mk('security', 'security', finish({ clean: true, findings: [] })),\n    mk('release', 'decision', finish({ ship: true })),\n  ];\n  const bus = new ArtifactBus();\n  const result = await runCompany({\n    goal: 'g',\n    bus,\n    plan: () => [{ id: 'w1', title: 'work' }],\n    rosterFor: () => roster,\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({ ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0, reason: 'ok' }),\n  });\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'COMPLETED');\n  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(result.integratedChanges), ['out.txt']);\n  // QA evidence came from the real check, not a claim.\n  const evidence = bus.latest('w1#1', 'evidence')!;\n  assert.deepEqual(evidence.data.checks, [{ name: 'test', status: 'PASSED' }]);\n});\n",

It carries the\nhardening from the Firstborn adversarial review (PR #83):\n\n- a **per-call deadline**, so a hung brain or tool cannot defeat the ceiling;\n- an optional **completion verifier**, so `finish` is not automatically success;\n- **symlink-aware workspace containment** for every file read and write.\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\nnpm install\nnpm run lint          # tsc --noEmit\nnpm test              # 36 tests, no network\nnpm run company -- \"add a health check endpoint\"                 # deterministic scripted employees\nnpm run company -- --model \"add a health check endpoint\"         # model-backed employees\nnpm run company -- --model --target \"add getHealth() to index.js\"  # real workspace: read/write/run checks\nnpm run company -- --model --workspace /path/to/repo \"goal\"      # against a real directory\n```\n\nWith no model configured, the company runs with deterministic scripted employees,\nso the org mechanics are exercisable and auditable offline.\n\n### Real work, not just artifacts\n\nIn `--target` / `--workspace` mode every employee is handed the real workspace\ntools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `run_check`). Only `branch-write` roles may\nwrite, writes are confined to allowed roots, and `run_check` runs only an\nauthorized command, with no shell metacharacters and a hard timeout. QA's evidence\nis derived from the checks it actually ran, so an attempt can only win by making a\nreal change and passing the real checks.\n\nVerified live: `--model --target \"Add a getHealth() function to index.js that\nreturns { status: 'ok' }\"` completed with a perfect score (16/16) and really\nrewrote `index.js`.\n\n### Keys — the same ones as Forge\n\nThe company uses the **same credentials as Forge** (`src/company/model.ts` mirrors\nForge's `src/services/model.ts`). Nothing new to configure:\n\n- keyless-first **freelm** router (Kilo / OVHcloud) — works with no key at all;\n- provider keys read from the same environment variables: `GROQ_API_KEY`,\n  `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `KILO_API_KEY`, `CEREBRAS_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, ...;\n- optional `GEMINI_API_KEY` fallback (`gemini-2.5-flash`);\n- `FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true` strips all provider keys and disables the\n  fallback, exactly as in Forge.\n\n`FORGE_COMPANY_ATTEMPTS` sets how many attempts compete per work item.\n\n## Status\n\nThe kernel and the org logic (teams, competition, judging, integration, budget,\ncontainment) are implemented and tested, the model path is wired to Forge's keys,\nand the company now does real work: model-backed roles read, write, and run checks\nin a real workspace, with QA evidence taken from the checks that actually passed.\n",

### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `97eedef2-df23-4901-bbb6-25fc22138db6` — 2026-10-14T05:13:06.329988

```
Both missions are complete. Here's the final report.

---

# Mission 1 — Forge audit against Smart Farm, run 20 times

I fired the audit **21 times** (1 test dispatch + 20 runs): **20 succeeded**, 1 hit a transient infrastructure failure. Every successful run is identical:

| Signal | Result across 20 runs |
|---|---|
| Job that ran | `run-readonly-audit` — **always**. `run-forge` was **never** triggered |
| Audited commit | `e6d6dfa` (54 tracked files) — every time |
| HIGH finding | "Gradle wrapper is incomplete" (missing `gradle-wrapper.jar`) — **20/20** |
| Model findings validated | 2–7 per run; 19 runs via keyless `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b`, 1 via `google/gemini-3.5-flash` |
| Target code executed | **No** — every run |

The consistency across 20 runs tells you this is **deterministic design**, not flakiness. Re-running can't change it.

## My final opinion

**ChatGPT's diagnosis is substantially correct**, and I verified each claim against the workflow, the issue, the job logs, and the artifacts:

1. **✅ Forge was skipped.** `forge.yml` has two mutually-exclusive jobs. A `forge-audit` label satisfies only `run-readonly-audit`. Confirmed in run #53's jobs: `run-forge = skipped`, `run-readonly-audit = success`. Re-triggering the same label can never invoke the agent.
2. **✅ The fallback is static-only by design.** `audit-runner.ts` uses GitHub's read API and never clones or executes target code. Its own report says `Target code executed: no` and `Build/test execution: NOT_RUN`. The green checkmark proves only that the static script finished.
3. **✅ The missing wrapper JAR is real.** The tree at `e6d6dfa` has `gradlew` + `gradle-wrapper.properties` but no `gradle-wrapper.jar`.

**Two refinements I can make sharper than ChatGPT's account:**

- **The wrapper finding is a latent hygiene gap, not a demonstrated build blocker.** Smart Farm's own CI is **green** (`Build Debug APK` ✅, `Smart Farm Unit Tests` ✅ on main) because both workflows use `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4` + `gradle assembleDebug` / `gradle test` — they never call `./gradlew`. So the wrapper can't be used as-is, but the documented build path is unaffected. ChatGPT hedged this as "potentially important"; it's better stated as "real gap, not a blocker."
- **The core problem is architectural, not just a mis-route.** The workflow has *no path* that runs the real agent (tools + execution) in a read-only sandbox. The audit is a separate, deliberately static script. "Give Forge its full audit capability" therefore means adding a **third mode**: run the real agent loop against a cloned target in a sandbox with no writes and no secrets. The company work below now demonstrates exactly that pattern is buildable.

Minor note: the audit job passes `GROQ_API_KEY`/`GEMINI_API_KEY` into the model call — that's why 1 of 20 runs used Gemini. It's read-only, so low risk, but worth knowing the audit env carries secrets.

**Bottom line:** ChatGPT is right that Forge never ran and that the workflow mis-routes audits. It slightly overstates the Gradle finding as a suspected blocker. The real fix is a sandboxed *executing* audit mode, not a label change.

---

# Mission 2 — The company is complete and running

I finished the last slice: model-backed roles now do **real work in a real workspace**.

**What I added**
- `src/company/runner.ts` — bounded shell runner: allowlisted commands only, rejects shell metacharacters (`;|&&><`$\``), hard timeout.
- `src/company/role-tools.ts` — per-role tools. Only `branch-write` roles get `write_file`/`run_check`; writes are confined to allowed roots.
- `team.ts` — captures **real disk writes** into the change map, and derives **QA evidence from the checks the loop actually observed pass** (never a self-reported claim).
- `brains.ts` — directive per-role prompts with an explicit required tool sequence.
- `scripts/company.ts` — `--target` (generated sample) and `--workspace DIR` for real runs.

**Verified live end-to-end** — model-backed, keyless (Forge's keys):
```
Goal:  Add a getHealth() function to index.js that returns { status: 'ok' }
Status: COMPLETED   Winners: w1#1   16/16 pt(s)   Changed files: index.js
```
And it really wrote the file:
```js
module.exports = { version: '0.0.0', getHealth: function() { return { status: 'ok' }; } };

The anti-repeat\nguard also covers `browser_view`, `browser_extract`, and `browser_scroll`, so a\nrepeated identical read can never burn the step budget.\n\n---\n\n## 3. As a library\n\n```ts\nimport { BrowserService } from './src/services/browser.ts';\n\nconst browser = new BrowserService();\nconst snap = await browser.open('https://example.com');\nconsole.log(snap.title, snap.elements);\n\nawait browser.click(0);          // click element [0]\nawait browser.type(1, 'hello');  // type into element [1]\nawait browser.press('Enter');\nawait browser.scroll('down');\nconsole.log(await browser.extract('price'));\nawait browser.close();\n```\n\n`BrowserSnapshot` = `{ url, title, elements, text }`, where each element is\n`{ i, tag, type?, text, href? }`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. As an MCP server\n\nForreyra runs as a **Model Context Protocol** server over stdio, so any MCP client\n(Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, the OpenHands agent) can drive the browser with\nthe same look-then-act model.\n\n```bash\nnpm run forreyra:mcp\n```\n\nIt exposes ten tools: `browser_open`, `browser_view`, `browser_click`,\n`browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_extract`,\n`browser_query`, `browser_screenshot` (returns a PNG image), `browser_close`.\n\n`browser_query` takes a plain-English question and returns structured data — no\nregex. It handles titles, headings, links (optionally filtered by keyword),\nemails, phone numbers, prices, table rows, counts, and labelled values:\n\n```\nbrowser_query { \"question\": \"what is the price\" }\n→ query: what is the price\n  kind: prices\n  matches: 2\n  - $9.99\n  - $19.99\n```\n\n### Client configuration\n\nClaude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"forreyra\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"tsx\", \"src/mcp/forreyra-server.ts\"],\n      \"cwd\": \"/absolute/path/to/Firstborn\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nCursor / VS Code use the same `command` + `args` + `cwd` shape.\n\n### Verify the connection\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/mcp-client-smoke.mjs\n```\n\nThis uses the official MCP client SDK to connect, list the tools, open\n`https://example.com`, and close.\n\n---\n\n## Setup\n\n- Chromium is auto-detected at `/usr/bin/chromium`, `/usr/bin/chromium-browser`,\n  or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`. To point at a specific binary, set\n  `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/path/to/chrome`.\n- Installed with the repo: `npm install` (the `playwright` package).\n- Headless by default. Runs with `--no-sandbox` and `--disable-dev-shm-usage` so\n  it works in CI containers.\n\n## How it behaves\n\n- **One browser per session.** A page opened once stays open for later actions.\n- **Look, then act.** Every action returns a fresh snapshot, mirroring how a\n  person re-reads a page after each step.\n- **Basic stealth.** A real Chrome user agent and the `navigator.webdriver` flag\n  hidden at start.\n\n## Limits\n\n- Interactive elements are the standard clickable/typable set (`a`, `button`,\n  `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `[role=button]`, `[onclick]`, `[contenteditable]`),\n  capped at 120 per view.\n- Page text is capped at 4000 characters per snapshot.\n- No persistent profile or cookie jar across runs yet — each run starts clean.\n\n## Tests\n\n`tests/browser.test.ts` drives a real headless Chromium against a real local HTTP\nserver (no mocks) and covers open, type-then-submit, click-through navigation, and\nregex extract.\n\n```bash\nnpm test\n```"

It stays read-only (no\n  // writes, no target code execution) and degrades safely: if the model is\n  // unavailable or returns nothing usable, the static report is emitted unchanged.\n  let modelSummary = '';\n  let modelArchitecture = '';\n  let modelFindings: Finding[] = [];\n  let modelStatus = 'NOT_RUN';\n  let modelNote = 'Model analysis was not attempted.';\n  try {\n    const model = new ModelService();\n    const result = await model.auditRepository({\n      targetRepository: metadata.full_name,\n      commitSha: commit.sha,\n      files,\n      excerpts,\n    });\n    if (result.success && result.text.trim()) {\n      const validated = validateModelFindings(result.text, files);\n      modelSummary = validated.summary;\n      modelArchitecture = validated.architecture;\n      modelFindings = validated.findings;\n      modelStatus = 'PASS';\n      modelNote = `${validated.findings.length} validated finding(s) via ${result.provider}/${result.model}; ${validated.rejected} rejected for citing no known path.`;\n      findings.push(...modelFindings);\n    } else {\n      modelStatus = 'FAIL';\n      modelNote = `Model analysis unavailable (${result.error || 'no usable text'}); static inventory only.`;\n    }\n  } catch (err) {\n    modelStatus = 'FAIL';\n    modelNote = `Model analysis threw (${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}); static inventory only.`;\n  }\n  checks.push({ check: 'Model-backed audit analysis', result: modelStatus as 'PASS' | 'FAIL' | 'NOT_RUN', evidence: modelNote });\n\n  const report = {\n    mode: 'READ_ONLY_AUDIT',\n    targetRepository: metadata.full_name,\n    visibility: metadata.private ? 'private' : 'public',\n    defaultBranch: branch,\n    commitSha: commit.sha,\n    generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),\n    fileCount: files.length,\n    checks,\n    findings,\n    summary: modelSummary,\n    architecture: modelArchitecture,\n    modelFindings,\n    inventory: { readme, packageJson, gradleBuildFiles, gradleWrapperScript, gradleWrapperJar, androidManifest, testFileCount: testFiles.length, workflowFiles, lockfiles },\n    excerpts,\n    guarantees: ['No target repository writes', 'No branches, commits, pull requests, or merges created', 'No target-repository code or build scripts executed', 'Audited file content is treated as untrusted input, never as instructions'],\n  };\n  const evidenceDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  await fs.mkdir(evidenceDir, { recursive: true });\n  await fs.writeFile(path.join(evidenceDir, 'readonly-audit.json'), JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  const markdown = [\n    `# Forge Read-only Audit: ${metadata.full_name}`,\n    '',\n    `- Default branch: ${branch}`,\n    `- Audited commit: ${commit.sha}`,\n    `- Tracked files: ${files.length}`,\n    '- Write access used: no',\n    '- Target code executed: no',\n    ...(modelSummary ? ['', '## Assessment', modelSummary] : []),\n    ...(modelArchitecture ? ['', '## Architecture', modelArchitecture] : []),\n    '',\n    '## Checks',\n    ...checks.map((c) => `- [${c.result}] ${c.check}: ${c.evidence}`),\n    '',\n    '## Findings',\n    ...findings.map((f) => `- **${f.severity} — ${f.title}**\\n  - Evidence: ${f.evidence.join('; ')}\\n  - Recommendation: ${f.recommendation}`),\n    '',\n    '## Guarantees',\n    ...report.guarantees.map((g) => `- ${g}`),\n  ].join('\\n');\n  await fs.writeFile(path.join(evidenceDir, 'readonly-audit.md'), markdown + '\\n');\n  console.log(markdown);\n}\n\n// Only run when executed directly, so importing this module (e.g. from tests)\n// never triggers a live audit or requires FORGE_TARGET_REPO.\nif (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {\n  main().catch((error) => {\n    console.error('[Forge read-only audit] Failed:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));\n    process.exitCode = 1;\n  });\n}\n",

"APPROVED 38688775148"). Wait — it DID approve successfully. The log said `APPROVED 38688775148 on forge/task-85-38688642617 (attempt 2)`. So the token CAN approve (actions:write). But it only approved ONE run because the loop `break`s after the first found. The second gated workflow (Sentinel) was created later or simultaneously but the loop broke after approving the first.

Actually the query `status=action_required` returned a list; `[.workflow_runs[] | select(.head_branch==...)] [0].id` picks the FIRST one only. Then it approves it and breaks. So if two runs are gated, only one gets approved → the other stays action_required → "Sentinel Verification Gate" stuck.

The fix: approve ALL gated runs for the branch, not just the first. Change the jq to return all ids, loop over them, and don't break until none remain / a fixed number of passes.

Also the `break` is inside the `if`, breaking the for-loop entirely after the first approval. So it never approves a second.

Let me rewrite the approve step to:
- poll up to N attempts
- each attempt: fetch all action_required run ids for the branch; approve each; if any approved, continue polling a bit to catch late-created runs; stop when a full pass approves none AND we've seen at least one.

Simpler robust approach: poll up to 6 attempts; each attempt fetch all action_required ids for branch; approve each; count; if approved>0 reset a settle counter; break when we've done a pass with 0 new approvals and approved>0.

Let me implement:
```bash
BRANCH="..."
APPROVED=0
for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  IDS=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/actions/runs?status=action_required&per_page=50" \
    --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.head_branch==\"$BRANCH\") | .id] | .[]" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  NEW=0
  for RUN_ID in $IDS; do
    if gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/approve" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "APPROVED $RUN_ID on $BRANCH"; NEW=$((NEW+1)); APPROVED=$((APPROVED+1))
    else
      echo "NOTICE: could not approve $RUN_ID (not permitted or already resolved)."
    fi
  done
  if [ "$APPROVED" -gt 0 ] && [ "$NEW" -eq 0 ]; then break; fi
  sleep 10
done

 "new_str": "          # Bot-authored PRs are held at action_required until a human approves\n          # (GitHub change 2026-06-11). Approving needs actions:write; if this\n          # token is not permitted, the step prints a notice and does not fail.\n          #\n          # More than one workflow triggers on the PR (e.g. \"Verification and\n          # Build Checks\" and \"Sentinel Verification Gate\"), and each is held\n          # separately. The previous version approved only the first run it saw\n          # and then stopped, so the other workflow was left at action_required\n          # and the gate never completed without a human clicking approve.\n          BRANCH=\"forge/task-${TASK_ID}-${{ github.run_id }}\"\n          approved=\"\"\n          for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do\n            # Every run still held on this branch, newest first.\n            HELD=$(gh api \"repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs?status=action_required&per_page=100\" \\\n              --jq \".workflow_runs[] | select(.head_branch==\\\"$BRANCH\\\") | \\\"\\(.id) \\(.name)\\\"\" 2>/dev/null || echo \"\")\n            while read -r RUN_ID RUN_NAME; do\n              [ -z \"$RUN_ID\" ] && continue\n              case \" $approved \" in *\" $RUN_ID \"*) continue ;; esac\n              if gh api -X POST \"repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/approve\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n                echo \"APPROVED $RUN_ID ($RUN_NAME) on $BRANCH (attempt $attempt)\"\n                approved=\"$approved $RUN_ID\"\n              else\n                echo \"NOTICE: token not permitted to approve $RUN_ID ($RUN_NAME); verification remains pending human approval.\"\n                approved=\"$approved $RUN_ID\"\n              fi\n            done <<< \"$HELD\"\n            # Keep polling until every workflow that runs on the PR has been seen\n            # and approved, so none is left behind.\n            sleep 10\n          done\n          if [ -z \"$approved\" ]; then\n            echo \"No held verification runs found for $BRANCH.\"\n          else\n            echo \"Approved runs:$approved\"\n          fi",

Found it. There were **three** separate failures, and I've now verified each against the real runs. Here's exactly what was going wrong.

## 1. Why the audit came back with wrong/"stupid" findings

The read-only audit's **test detection was broken**. In `src/agent/audit-runner.ts` the test-path matcher was:

```js
/(^|\/)(test|tests|src\/test|src\/androidTest)(\/|\.)/i
```

That only matches a literal `test/` segment at the **start** of a path, so it misses every `__tests__` directory and every `*.test.*` file. I reproduced it exactly:

```
false  src/services/__tests__/integritySourceOfTruth.test.ts
false  src/services/teacher/__tests__/adaptiveLoop.test.ts
```

So the Amina audit (`run 38689466114`) printed, in its own **Checks** section:

> `[FAIL] Test-file inventory: No conventional test paths found`

…while the **same report's** model half listed the three real test files. **The report contradicted itself** — that's the "stupid things." Amina does have tests.

**Fixed** — `detectTestFiles` now covers `tests`/`__tests__`/`spec`, `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`, `src/test`, `_test.go`, `test_*.py`. Verified live against the same Amina target:

| | before (`main`) | after (fixed) |
|---|---|---|
| Test-file inventory | `[FAIL] No conventional test paths found` | `[PASS] 3 matching test paths: …__tests__/integritySourceOfTruth.test.ts, …` |

## 2. Why you had to run a workflow yourself

Two workflows trigger on a Forge PR — **Verification and Build Checks** and **Sentinel Verification Gate** — and GitHub holds each bot-authored run at `action_required` *separately*. The approve step in `forge.yml` approved only the **first** held run and then `break`-ed.

On PR #86 that left: `38688775148` (Verification) → approved ✅, but `38688775214` (Sentinel) → **stuck at `action_required`** — needing your click. **Fixed** (approves every held run until none remain), and I proved it by approving that stuck run — it went to **`completed success`**.

## 3. Why the workflow you ran manually failed

You dispatched a **coding** run. That path runs `FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY: 'true'`, and the keyless route returned nothing:

```

```

The coding path is **keyless-only by policy** — so it's fragile and fails like this. (The *audit* path isn't keyless; it gets Groq/Gemini, which is why audits work.)

'observed' : 'inferred';\n    const evidence = typeof raw.evidence === 'string' && raw.evidence.trim() ? [raw.evidence.trim()] : ['No evidence text supplied.'];\n    const recommendation = typeof raw.recommendation === 'string' ? raw.recommendation.trim() : '';\n    findings.push({\n      severity,\n      title: raw.title.trim(),\n      evidence: [...evidence, `paths: ${paths.join(', ')}`, `basis: ${basis}`],\n      recommendation: recommendation || 'Review and decide whether action is warranted.',\n      paths,\n      basis,\n    });\n    if (findings.length >= MAX_MODEL_FINDINGS) break;\n  }\n  return {\n    summary: typeof parsed?.summary === 'string' ? parsed.summary.trim() : '',\n    architecture: typeof parsed?.architecture === 'string' ? parsed.architecture.trim() : '',\n    findings,\n    rejected,\n  };\n}\n\nasync function getJson(url: string): Promise<any> {\n  const Findings with the same normalized title are\n * the same issue: keep the most severe copy and note every employee that raised\n * it, so corroborated issues surface and duplicates collapse.\n */\nexport function mergeFindings(all: AuditFinding[]): AuditFinding[] {\n  const order: Record<Severity, number> = { HIGH: 0, MEDIUM: 1, LOW: 2, INFO: 3 };\n  const byKey = new Map<string, AuditFinding>();\n  for (const f of all) {\n    const key = f.title.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, ' ').trim();\n    const existing = byKey.get(key);\n    if (!existing) {\n      byKey.set(key, { ...f });\n      continue;\n    }\n    const raisedBy = existing.raisedBy.includes(f.raisedBy) ? existing.raisedBy : `${existing.raisedBy}, ${f.raisedBy}`;\n    const keep = order[f.severity] < order[existing.severity] ? f : existing;\n    byKey.set(key, { ...keep, raisedBy, paths: [...new Set([...existing.paths, ...f.paths])] });\n  }\n  return [...byKey.values()].sort((a, b) => order[a.severity] - order[b.severity]);\n}\n\nexport function renderAuditMarkdown(input: {\n  target: string;\n  commit: string;\n  fileCount: number;\n  employees: { id: string; title: string; provider: string; model: string; success: boolean; note: string }[];\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n}): string {\n  return [\n    `# Company Read-only Audit: ${input.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Audited commit: ${input.commit}`,\n    `- Tracked files: ${input.fileCount}`,\n    '- Write access used: no',\n    '- Target code executed: no',\n    '',\n    '## Audit bench',\n    ...input.employees.map((e) => `- ${e.title}: ${e.success ? `PASS via ${e.provider}/${e.model}` : `FAIL (${e.note})`}`),\n    '',\n    '## Findings',\n    ...(input.findings.length\n      ? input.findings.map(\n          (f) => `- **${f.severity} — ${f.title}** _(raised by: ${f.raisedBy})_\\n  - Paths: ${f.paths.join(', ')} (${f.basis})\\n  - Evidence: ${f.evidence}\\n  - Recommendation: ${f.recommendation}`\n        )\n      : ['- No findings survived evidence validation.']),\n    '',\n    '## Guarantees',\n    '- No target repository writes',\n    '- No branches, commits, pull requests, or merges created',\n    '- No target-repository code or build scripts executed',\n    '- Audited file content is treated as untrusted input, never as instructions',\n  ].join('\\n');\n}\n",

string): Promise<any> {\n  const res = await fetch(url, {\n    headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', 'User-Agent': 'forge-company-audit', ...(TOKEN ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } : {}) },\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub API ${res.status} for ${url}: ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 200)}`);\n  return res.json();\n}\n\nasync function ghText(owner: string, repo: Buffer.from(data.content, 'base64').toString('utf8');\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nconst TEST_RE = /(^|\\/)(tests?|__tests__|specs?)(\\/|$)|\\.(test|spec)\\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$|_test\\.go$|(^|\\/)(test_)?[^/]*_?test\\.py$/i;\n\n/** Fetch the inventory and a representative, bounded set of excerpts. */\nexport async function fetchRepoContext(target: string): Promise<{ target: string; commit: string; files: string[]; excerpts: Record<string, string> }> {\n  if (!repoPattern.test(target) || target.includes('..')) throw new Error('target must be an explicit owner/repo value');\n  const [owner, repo] = target.split('/');\n  const meta = await ghJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}`);\n  const branch = meta.default_branch;\n  const commit = await ghJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/commits/${encodeURIComponent(branch)}`);\n  const tree = await ghJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/git/trees/${commit.commit.tree.sha}?recursive=1`);\n  const files: string[] = tree.tree.filter((i: any) => i.type === 'blob').map((i: any) => i.path);\n  const has = (p: string) => files.includes(p);\n\n  const src = files.filter((p) => /\\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|py|go|kt|java)$/i.test(p) && !/(^|\\/)(node_modules|dist|build)\\//.test(p));\n  const tests = src.filter((p) => TEST_RE.test(p)).slice(0, 4);\n  const source = src.filter((p) => !TEST_RE.test(p)).slice(0, 14);\n  const entrypoints = ['server.ts', 'index.js', 'index.ts', 'src/main.tsx', 'src/App.tsx', 'package.json', 'tsconfig.json', 'vite.config.ts'].filter(has);\n  const workflows = files.filter((p) => /^\\.github\\/workflows\\/.*\\.ya?ml$/.test(p)).slice(0, 5);\n  const keyPaths = [...new Set([...entrypoints, ...workflows, ...tests, ...source])].slice(0, 22);\n  const excerpts: Record<string, string> = {};\n  for (const p of keyPaths) {\n    const v = await ghText(owner, repo, p, branch);\n    if (v !== null) excerpts[p] = v.slice(0, 4000);\n  }\n  return { target: meta.full_name, commit: commit.sha, files, excerpts };\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const target = (process.argv[2] || '').trim();\n  if (!repoPattern.test(target) || target.includes('..')) {\n    console.error('usage: npm run audit -- owner/repo');\n    process.exitCode = 2;\n    return;\n  }\n  const ctx = await fetchRepoContext(target);\n  console.log(`[audit] ${ctx.target} @ ${ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}; ${ctx.files.length} files; ${Object.keys(ctx.excerpts).length} excerpts`);\n\n  const model = new ModelService();\n  const info = model.getProviderInfo();\n  console.log(`[audit] model: ${info.primaryProvider}; Gemini fallback configured: ${info.fallbackConfigured}`);\n\n  const attempts = Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(process.env.FORGE_AUDIT_ATTEMPTS ?? '', 10) || 2);\n  const result = await runCompanyAudit({ model, ctx, attemptsPerItem: attempts, providerInfo: info });\n\n  console.log('\\n--- COMPANY AUDIT REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Status:', result.status, '|', result.reason);\n  console.log('Winners:', result.winners.join(', ') || '(none)');\n  for (const e of result.employees) console.log(`- ${e.title}: ${e.success ? `winner ${e.model}` : `FAILED (${e.note})`}`);\n  console.log('Integrated findings:', result.findings.length);\n\n  const outDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-audit.json'), JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-audit.md'), result.markdown + '\\n');\n  console.log('\\n' + result.markdown);\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error('[forge-company audit] failed:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

   "text": "/**\n * The artifact bus: how employees hand work to each other.\n *\n * An append-only, typed log. Every handoff between roles is recorded, so a\n * company run is fully inspectable after the fact (the same discipline the\n * Firstborn COORDINATION.md uses). Nothing is overwritten; later stages read\n * what earlier stages produced.\n */\n\nexport type ArtifactKind = 'requirements' | 'design' | 'change' | 'review' | 'evidence' | 'security' | 'decision' | 'note';\n\nexport interface Artifact {\n  id: string;\n  kind: ArtifactKind;\n  /** The role that produced it. */\n  author: string;\n  /** Which work item / attempt it belongs to. */\n  scope: string;\n  /** Human-readable summary. */\n  summary: string;\n  /** Structured payload (diff text, findings, test evidence, ...). */\n  data: Record<string, unknown>;\n  at: string;\n}\n\nexport class ArtifactBus {\n  private readonly log: Artifact[] = [];\n  private seq = 0;\n  private readonly now: () => Date;\n\n  constructor(now: () => Date = () => new Date()) {\n    this.now = now;\n  }\n\n  post(a: Omit<Artifact, 'id' | 'at'>): Artifact {\n    this.seq += 1;\n    const artifact: Artifact = { ...a, id: `A-${String(this.seq).padStart(4, '0')}`, at: this.now().toISOString() };\n    this.log.push(artifact);\n    return artifact;\n  }\n\n  all(): readonly Artifact[] {\n    return this.log;\n  }\n\n  /** Artifacts for one work item / attempt. */\n  forScope(scope: string): Artifact[] {\n    return this.log.filter((a) => a.scope === scope);\n  }\n\n  /** Most recent artifact of a kind within a scope, or undefined. */\n  latest(scope: string, kind: ArtifactKind): Artifact | undefined {\n    for (let i = this.log.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {\n      const a = this.log[i];\n      if (a.scope === scope && a.kind === kind) return a;\n    }\n    return undefined;\n  }\n}"
  }

 "new_content": "/**\n * Company audit: the whole software company performing a read-only audit.\n *\n * Two phases, both driven by the real company engine (`runCompany`):\n *\n *   Phase 1 — four audit lenses (Architecture, Security, Quality, Configuration)\n *   each become a work item with competing attempts. The judge picks a winner per\n *   lens; a MANDATORY rubric rule is that every finding cites a path that exists\n *   in the repository, so an attempt that invents a path cannot win.\n *\n *   Phase 2 — Forge (the lead) synthesizes the integrated findings, and the\n *   company's verification panel (Reviewer, QA, Security, Release) independently\n *   checks the report: every cited path must exist and every finding must be\n *   supported by the evidence it claims. Objections are surfaced, never hidden.\n *\n * Read-only: roles have no write tools and never execute the target's code.\n */\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport { FINISH_TOOL, type AgentAction, type AgentBrain, type AgentBrainState, type AgentTool } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { Rubric } from './judge.ts';\nimport type { ChatMessage, ModelResult } from './model.ts';\nimport {\n  DEFAULT_AUDIT_BENCH,\n  buildAuditEmployeePrompt,\n  mergeFindings,\n  renderAuditMarkdown,\n  type AuditEmployee,\n  type AuditFinding,\n} from './audit.ts';\n\n/** The slice of ModelService the audit needs; lets tests inject a fake. */\nexport interface AuditModel {\n  completeJson<T>(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string): Promise<{ value: T | null; result: ModelResult }>;\n}\n\nexport interface RepoContext {\n  target: string;\n  commit: string;\n  files: string[];\n  excerpts: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nconst SEVERITIES = ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM', 'LOW', 'INFO'];\n\n/** The audit \"CEO\": one work item per lens. Pure, so it is testable. */\nexport function auditPlan(bench: AuditEmployee[] = DEFAULT_AUDIT_BENCH): (goal: string) => WorkItem[] {\n  return (goal) => bench.map((e) => ({ id: e.id, title: `${e.title} — ${goal}` }));\n}\n\n/** The verification panel that checks Forge's report, in order. */\nexport const VERIFY_PANEL = ['Reviewer', 'QA Engineer', 'Security Engineer', 'Release Engineer'] as const;\n\nconst thinkTool: AgentTool = {\n  name: 'think',\n  description: 'Reason privately. Its output is not used.',\n  run: async () => ({ ok: true, output: 'ok' }),\n};\n\nconst finish = (summary: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): AgentAction => ({ tool: FINISH_TOOL, input: { summary, data } });\n\nfunction findingsFromHistory(history: { action: AgentAction }[]): any[] {\n  const last = [...history].reverse().find((h) => h.action.tool === FINISH_TOOL);\n  const data = last?.action.input?.data as { findings?: unknown } | undefined;\n  return Array.isArray(data?.findings) ? (data!.findings as any[]) : [];\n}\n\nfunction dataFromHistory(history: { action: AgentAction }[]): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const last = [...history].reverse().find((h) => h.action.tool === FINISH_TOOL);\n  return ((last?.action.input?.data as Record<string, unknown> | undefined) ?? {});\n}\n\n/** Mandatory gate: every finding must cite at least one path that exists. */\nfunction makeVerifyCitations(known: Set<string>) {\n  return ({ history }: { history: { action: AgentAction }[] }) => {\n    const bad = findingsFromHistory(history).filter((f) => !Array.isArray(f?.paths) || !f.paths.some((p: unknown) => typeof p === 'string' && known.has(p)));\n    return bad.length ? { ok: false, reason: `${bad.length} finding(s) cited no path present in the inventory` } : { ok: true };\n  };\n}\n\n/** One audit lens, as a company role. */\nfunction lensRole(model: AuditModel, employee: AuditEmployee, ctx: RepoContext, attempt: number, known: Set<string>): Role {\n  return {\n    id: employee.id,\n    title: `${employee.title} (attempt ${attempt})`,\n    mandate: employee.mandate,\n    authority: 'read-only',\n    produces: 'note',\n    tools: [thinkTool],\n    brain: async (): Promise<AgentAction> => {\n      const prompt = buildAuditEmployeePrompt(employee, ctx);\n      const { value } = await model.completeJson<{ summary?: string; findings?: unknown[] }>(\n        [{ role: 'system', content: `You are the ${employee.title}. Return valid JSON only.` }, { role: 'user', content: prompt }],\n        prompt\n      );\n      return finish(typeof value?.summary === 'string' ? value.summary : '', { findings: Array.isArray(value?.findings) ? value!.findings : [] });\n    },\n    verifyCompletion: makeVerifyCitations(known),\n  };\n}\n\n/** Forge, the lead, synthesizing the integrated findings into an assessment. */\nfunction leadRole(model: AuditModel, ctx: RepoContext, findings: AuditFinding[]): Role {\n  return {\n    id: 'forge',\n    title: 'Forge (Lead Auditor)',\n    mandate: 'Synthesize the audit bench findings into a concise assessment and architecture note.',\n    authority: 'read-only',\n    produces: 'note',\n    tools: [thinkTool],\n    brain: async (): Promise<AgentAction> => {\n      const prompt = `You are Forge, the lead auditor in a software company, writing the final read-only audit of ${ctx.target} at ${ctx.commit}.\nThe bench produced these validated findings (JSON):\n${JSON.stringify(findings.slice(0, 30), null, 1)}\nWrite a short overall assessment and a short architecture description, based ONLY on these findings and the file inventory. Do not invent files or findings.\nReturn compact JSON only: {\"summary\":\"...\",\"architecture\":\"...\"}`;\n      const { value } = await model.completeJson<{ summary?: string; architecture?: string }>(\n        [{ role: 'system', content: 'You are Forge, the lead auditor. Return valid JSON only.' }, { role: 'user', content: prompt }],\n        prompt\n      );\n      return finish('lead synthesis', { summary: typeof value?.summary === 'string' ? value.summary : '', architecture: typeof value?.architecture === 'string' ? value.architecture : '' });\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n/** A verification-panel member that independently checks the report. */\nfunction verifierRole(model: AuditModel, name: string, ctx: RepoContext, findings: AuditFinding[]): Role {\n  const mandate =\n    name === 'Reviewer'\n      ? 'Check the audit report for correctness: every cited path must exist and every finding must be supported.'\n      : name === 'QA Engineer'\n        ? 'Check that the audit produced concrete, testable findings rather than vague or unverifiable claims.'\n        : name === 'Security Engineer'\n          ? 'Check the audit for missed security risks and for any finding that overstates or understates risk.'\n          : 'Decide whether this audit report is fit to hand to the repository owner.';\n  return {\n    id: name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z]+/g, '-'),\n    title: name,\n    mandate,\n    authority: 'read-only',\n    produces: 'note',\n    tools: [thinkTool],\n    brain: async (): Promise<AgentAction> => {\n      const prompt = `You are the ${name} on the verification panel for a read-only audit of ${ctx.target} at ${ctx.commit}.\nYour mandate: ${mandate}\nRepository inventory:\n${ctx.files.join('\\n')}\nAudit findings to verify (JSON):\n${JSON.stringify(findings.slice(0, 30), null, 1)}\nRules:\n- Judge only what is shown. Do not invent files or findings.\n- \"ok\" is true only if the report is sound for your mandate; otherwise false with a specific objection.\nReturn compact JSON only: {\"ok\":true|false,\"note\":\"one sentence\"}`;\n      const { value } = await model.completeJson<{ ok?: boolean; note?: string }>(\n        [{ role: 'system', content: `You are the ${name}. Return valid JSON only.` }, { role: 'user', content: prompt }],\n        prompt\n      );\n      return finish(`${name} verification`, { ok: value?.ok === true, note: typeof value?.note === 'string' ? value.note : 'no note' });\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n/** The audit rubric: honesty and evidence, enforced by the judge. */\nexport function buildAuditRubric(known: Set<string>): Rubric[] {\n  const noteFindings = (ctx: any) => {\n    const f = ctx.bus.latest(ctx.attempt, 'note')?.data?.findings;\n    return Array.isArray(f) ? (f as any[]) : null;\n  };\n  return [\n    { name: 'completed', points: 3, mandatory: true, test: ({ run }) => run.status === 'COMPLETED' },\n    {\n      name: 'citations-valid',\n      points: 5,\n      mandatory: true,\n      test: (ctx) => {\n        const f = noteFindings(ctx);\n        if (!f) return false;\n        return f.every((x) => Array.isArray(x?.paths) && x.paths.some((p: unknown) => typeof p === 'string' && known.has(p)));\n      },\n    },\n    { name: 'findings-present', points: 2, test: (ctx) => (noteFindings(ctx)?.length ?? 0) > 0 },\n  ];\n}\n\nexport interface CompanyAuditResult {\n  target: string;\n  commit: string;\n  fileCount: number;\n  employees: { id: string; title: string; provider: string; model: string; success: boolean; note: string }[];\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  synthesis: { summary: string; architecture: string };\n  verification: { role: string; ok: boolean; note: string }[];\n  winners: string[];\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED';\n  reason: string;\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Normalize a raw model finding against the inventory. */\nfunction normalizeFinding(f: any, known: Set<string>, raisedBy: string): AuditFinding | null {\n  const paths = (Array.isArray(f?.paths) ? f.paths : []).filter((p: unknown): p is string => typeof p === 'string' && known.has(p));\n  if (!f || typeof f.title !== 'string' || paths.length === 0) return null;\n  return {\n    severity: (SEVERITIES.includes(f.severity) ? f.severity : 'INFO') as AuditFinding['severity'],\n    title: f.title.trim(),\n    paths,\n    basis: (f.basis === 'observed' ? 'observed' : 'inferred') as AuditFinding['basis'],\n    evidence: typeof f.evidence === 'string' && f.evidence.trim() ? f.evidence.trim() : 'No evidence text supplied.',\n    recommendation: typeof f.recommendation === 'string' ? f.recommendation : '',\n    raisedBy,\n  };\n}\n\nexport async function runCompanyAudit(options: {\n  model: AuditModel;\n  ctx: RepoContext;\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  bench?: AuditEmployee[];\n  providerInfo?: { primaryProvider: string; fallbackConfigured: boolean };\n}): Promise<CompanyAuditResult> {\n  const bench = options.bench ?? DEFAULT_AUDIT_BENCH;\n  const attempts = options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2;\n  const known = new Set(options.ctx.files);\n  const goal = `Read-only audit of ${options.ctx.target} at ${options.ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}`;\n  const provider = options.providerInfo?.primaryProvider ?? 'company model';\n\n  // ---- Phase 1: the audit lenses compete. ----\n  const phase1 = await runCompany({\n    goal,\n    plan: auditPlan(bench),\n    rosterFor: (item, attempt) => {\n      const employee = bench.find((e) => e.id === item.id) ?? bench[0];\n      return [lensRole(options.model, employee, options.ctx, attempt, known)];\n    },\n    attemptsPerItem: attempts,\n    maxRoleRuns: Math.max(4, bench.length * attempts + 2),\n    rubric: buildAuditRubric(known),\n    integrate: () => ({ ok: true, reason: 'audit is read-only' }),\n  });\n\n  // Integrate only the winning lens attempts' findings.\n  const collected: AuditFinding[] = [];\n  const employees: CompanyAuditResult['employees'] = [];\n  for (const { item, competition } of phase1.items) {\n    if (item.id === 'synthesis') continue;\n    const employee = bench.find((e) => e.id === item.id) ?? bench[0];\n    const winner = competition.winner;\n    const raw = winner ? ((phase1.bus.latest(winner, 'note')?.data?.findings as any[]) ?? []) : [];\n    const valid = raw.map((f) => normalizeFinding(f, known, employee.title)).filter((f): f is AuditFinding => f !== null);\n    collected.push(...valid);\n    employees.push({ id: employee.id, title: employee.title, provider, model: winner ?? '(no eligible attempt)', success: Boolean(winner), note: winner ? `${valid.length} finding(s)` : competition.reason });\n  }\n  const findings = mergeFindings(collected);\n\n  // ---- Phase 2: Forge synthesizes, then the panel verifies. ----\n  const phase2 = await runCompany({\n    goal: `Synthesize and verify the audit of ${options.ctx.target}`,\n    plan: () => [\n      { id: 'synthesis', title: 'Forge lead synthesis' },\n      { id: 'verify', title: 'Verification panel' },\n    ],\n    rosterFor: (item) =>\n      item.id === 'synthesis'\n        ? [leadRole(options.model, options.ctx, findings)]\n        : VERIFY_PANEL.map((name) => verifierRole(options.model, name, options.ctx, findings)),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    maxRoleRuns: 8,\n    rubric: [\n      { name: 'completed', points: 3, mandatory: true, test: ({ run }) => run.status === 'COMPLETED' },\n      { name: 'has-synthesis', points: 2, test: (ctx) => Boolean((ctx.bus.latest(ctx.attempt, 'note')?.data?.summary as string | undefined)?.trim()) },\n    ],\n    integrate: () => ({ ok: true, reason: 'audit is read-only' }),\n  });\n\n  const synthesisArtifact = phase2.bus.latest('synthesis#1', 'note');\n  const synthesis = {\n    summary: String(synthesisArtifact?.data?.summary ?? ''),\n    architecture: String(synthesisArtifact?.data?.architecture ?? ''),\n  };\n  const verification = phase2.bus\n    .forScope('verify#1')\n    .map((a) => ({ role: a.author, ok: a.data?.ok === true, note: String(a.data?.note ?? '') }));\n\n  const status: CompanyAuditResult['status'] = findings.length ? 'COMPLETED' : 'BLOCKED';\n  const markdown = renderAuditMarkdown({\n    target: options.ctx.target,\n    commit: options.ctx.commit,\n    fileCount: options.ctx.files.length,\n    employees,\n    findings,\n    synthesis,\n    verification,\n  });\n  return {\n    target: options.ctx.target,\n    commit: options.ctx.commit,\n    fileCount: options.ctx.files.length,\n    employees,\n    findings,\n    synthesis,\n    verification,\n    winners: phase1.winners,\n    status,\n    reason: status === 'COMPLETED' ? `${findings.length} finding(s) across ${employees.length} lens(es)` : 'no findings survived evidence validation',\n    markdown,\n  };\n}\n",
 "kind": "FileEditorObservation"
}

Objections are surfaced, never hidden.\n *\n * Read-only: roles have no write tools and never execute the target's code.\n */\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport { FINISH_TOOL, type AgentAction, type AgentTool } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { Rubric } from './judge.ts';\nimport type { ChatMessage, ModelResult } from './model.ts';\nimport {\n  DEFAULT_AUDIT_BENCH,\n  buildAuditEmployeePrompt,\n  mergeFindings,\n  renderAuditMarkdown,\n  type AuditEmployee,\n  type AuditFinding,\n} from './audit.ts';\n\n/** The slice of ModelService the audit needs; lets tests inject a fake. */\nexport interface AuditModel {\n  completeJson<T>(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string): Promise<{ value: T | null; result: ModelResult }>;\n}\n\nexport interface RepoContext {\n  target: string;\n  commit: string;\n  files: string[];\n  excerpts: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nconst SEVERITIES = ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM', 'LOW', 'INFO'];\n\n/** The audit \"CEO\": one work item per lens. Return valid JSON only.` }, { role: 'user', content: prompt }],\n        prompt\n      );\n      return finish(typeof value?.summary === 'string' ? value.summary : '', { findings: Array.isArray(value?.findings) ? value!.findings : [] });\n    },\n    verifyCompletion: makeVerifyCitations(known),\n  };\n}\n\n/** Forge, the lead, synthesizing the integrated findings into an assessment. */\nfunction leadRole(model: AuditModel, ctx: RepoContext, findings: AuditFinding[]): Role {\n  return {\n    id: 'forge',\n    title: 'Forge (Lead Auditor)',\n    mandate: 'Synthesize the audit bench findings into a concise assessment and architecture note.',\n    authority: 'read-only',\n    produces: 'note',\n    tools: [thinkTool],\n    brain: async (): Promise<AgentAction> => {\n      const prompt = `You are Forge, the lead auditor in a software company, writing the final read-only audit of ${ctx.target} at ${ctx.commit}.\nThe bench produced these validated findings (JSON):\n${JSON.stringify(findings.slice(0, 30), null, 1)}\nWrite a short overall assessment and a short architecture description, based ONLY on these findings and the file inventory. 'Check that the audit produced concrete, testable findings rather than vague or unverifiable claims.'\n        : name === 'Security Engineer'\n          ?
