   "text": "========== src/company/company.ts ==========\n/**\n * The company: one goal in, an integrated result out.\n *\n * The supervisor decomposes the goal into work items, runs a *competition* on\n * each (several independent attempts), judges them on evidence, then integrates\n * only the winners and re-verifies the whole. Everything is bounded by a\n * company-wide budget and recorded on the artifact bus.\n */\nimport { ArtifactBus } from './bus.ts';\nimport { runTeam, type TeamRun } from './team.ts';\nimport { judgeCompetition, DEFAULT_RUBRIC, type Competition, type Rubric } from './judge.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\n\nexport interface WorkItem {\n  id: string;\n  title: string;\n}\n\nexport interface CompanyOptions {\n  goal: string;\n  /** Decomposition (the \"CEO\"): goal -> work items. Pure, so it is testable. */\n  plan: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Different attempts may differ. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** How many independent attempts compete per work item. Default 2. */\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  /** Company-wide ceiling on total role-runs, so the org cannot run away. */\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  bus?: ArtifactBus;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  rubric?: Rubric[];\n  /** Files under change at the start of the run. */\n  changes?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** A real directory mutating roles write into, so changes reflect disk. */\n  workspaceDir?: string;\n  /** Final gate: given the winners' merged changes, may the company ship? */\n  integrate?: (state: { goal: string; winners: string[]; changes: Record<string, string>; bus: ArtifactBus }) => { ok: boolean; reason: string };\n}\n\nexport interface CompanyRun {\n  goal: string;\n  items: { item: WorkItem; competition: Competition }[];\n  /** Changes from the winning attempt of every work item. */\n  integratedChanges: Record<string, string>;\n  winners: string[];\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED';\n  reason: string;\n  bus: ArtifactBus;\n}\n\nexport async function runCompany(options: CompanyOptions): Promise<CompanyRun> {\n  const { goal, plan, rosterFor } = options;\n  const attemptsPerItem = Math.max(1, options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2);\n  const maxRoleRuns = Math.max(1, options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40);\n  const bus = options.bus ?? new ArtifactBus();\n  const rubric = options.rubric ?? DEFAULT_RUBRIC;\n\n  const items = plan(goal);\n  const results: { item: WorkItem; competition: Competition }[] = [];\n  let integratedChanges: Record<string, string> = { ...(options.changes ?? {}) };\n  const winners: string[] = [];\n  let roleRuns = 0;\n\n  for (const item of items) {\n    const runs: { attempt: string; run: TeamRun }[] = [];\n    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attemptsPerItem; attempt += 1) {\n      if (roleRuns >= maxRoleRuns) {\n        return { goal, items: results, integratedChanges, winners, status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `company budget exhausted (${maxRoleRuns} role-runs)`, bus };\n      }\n      const roster = rosterFor(item, attempt);\n      roleRuns += roster.length;\n      const attemptId = `${item.id}#${attempt}`;\n      const run = await runTeam({\n        goal,\n        workItem: item.title,\n        scope: attemptId,\n        roster,\n        bus,\n        limits: options.limits,\n        changes: integratedChanges,\n        workspaceDir: options.workspaceDir,\n      });\n      runs.push({ attempt: attemptId, run });\n    }\n\n    const competition = judgeCompetition(item.title, runs, bus, rubric);\n    results.push({ item, competition });\n\n    if (!competition.winner) {\n      return { goal, items: results, integratedChanges, winners, status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no eligible attempt for \"${item.title}\"`, bus };\n    }\n    winners.push(competition.winner);\n    const winning = runs.find((r) => r.attempt === competition.winner)!.run;\n    integratedChanges = { ...integratedChanges, ...winning.changes };\n    bus.post({\n      kind: 'decision',\n      author: 'supervisor',\n      scope: competition.winner,\n      summary: competition.reason,\n      data: { workItem: item.title, winner: competition.winner, scorecards: competition.scorecards },\n    });\n  }\n\n  const verdict = options.integrate\n    ? options.integrate({ goal, winners, changes: integratedChanges, bus })\n    : { ok: true, reason: 'all work items resolved and integrated' };\n\n  return {\n    goal,\n    items: results,\n    integratedChanges,\n    winners,\n    status: verdict.ok ? 'COMPLETED' : 'BLOCKED',\n    reason: verdict.reason,\n    bus,\n  };\n}\n\n========== src/company/roles.ts ==========\n/**\n * Roles: the employees. A role is the hardened loop with a mandate, a scoped\n * toolset, an authority level, and a brain. The roster below is the default\n * company; callers can compose their own.\n */\nimport type { AgentBrain, AgentTool, Authorization } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { ArtifactBus, ArtifactKind } from './bus.ts';\n\nexport type RoleId = 'pm' | 'architect' | 'implementer' | 'reviewer' | 'qa' | 'security' | 'docs' | 'release' | (string & {});\n\n/** What a role is allowed to change. */\nexport type Authority = 'read-only' | 'branch-write';\n\nexport interface RoleInput {\n  /** The company goal. */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The specific work item this role is acting on. */\n  workItem: string;\n  /** The scope id for artifacts produced here. */\n  scope: string;\n  /** Everything produced so far for this scope, oldest first. */\n  artifacts: readonly import('./bus.ts').Artifact[];\n  /** Files currently under change (for reviewers/QA). */\n  changes?: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nexport interface RoleResult {\n  /** Did the role finish its mandate? */\n  ok: boolean;\n  /** Artifact kind this role emits. */\n  kind: ArtifactKind;\n  summary: string;\n  data: Record<string, unknown>;\n  /** Steps taken (for evidence). */\n  steps: number;\n  reason?: string;\n}\n\nexport interface Role {\n  id: RoleId;\n  title: string;\n  mandate: string;\n  authority: Authority;\n  /** Which artifact kind this role consumes, if any. */\n  consumes?: ArtifactKind;\n  /** Which artifact kind this role produces. */\n  produces: ArtifactKind;\n  /** Tools this role may use (built by the caller, scoped to the workspace). */\n  tools: AgentTool[];\n  /** The decision-maker. Deterministic in tests; model-backed in production. */\n  brain: AgentBrain;\n  authorize?: Authorization;\n  limits?: import('../kernel/loop.ts').LoopLimits;\n  /** Independent gate on this role's completion (e.g. \"a test must pass first\"). */\n  verifyCompletion?: (state: { goal: string; summary: string; history: import('../kernel/loop.ts').LoopStep[] }) => { ok: boolean; reason?: string };\n}\n\n/** The default roster: a small but complete software company. */\nexport const DEFAULT_ROSTER: { id: RoleId; title: string; mandate: string; authority: Authority; consumes?: ArtifactKind; produces: ArtifactKind }[] = [\n  { id: 'pm', title: 'Product Manager', mandate: 'Turn the goal into testable requirements.', authority: 'read-only', produces: 'requirements' },\n  { id: 'architect', title: 'Architect', mandate: 'Design the change and name the files it touches.', authority: 'read-only', consumes: 'requirements', produces: 'design' },\n  { id: 'implementer', title: 'Implementer', mandate: 'Write the change and make the checks pass.', authority: 'branch-write', consumes: 'design', produces: 'change' },\n  { id: 'reviewer', title: 'Reviewer', mandate: 'Read the change and find correctness flaws.', authority: 'read-only', consumes: 'change', produces: 'review' },\n  { id: 'qa', title: 'QA Engineer', mandate: 'Run the real checks and record evidence.', authority: 'branch-write', consumes: 'change', produces: 'evidence' },\n  { id: 'security', title: 'Security Engineer', mandate: 'Attack the change for escapes and unsafe writes.', authority: 'read-only', consumes: 'change', produces: 'security' },\n  { id: 'release', title: 'Release Engineer', mandate: 'Decide whether the change may ship.', authority: 'read-only', consumes: 'evidence', produces: 'decision' },\n];\n\nexport function findRole(roster: Role[], id: RoleId): Role | undefined {\n  return roster.find((r) => r.id === id);\n}\n\nexport type { ArtifactBus };\n\n========== src/company/team.ts ==========\n/**\n * Teams: an ordered roster that works one job together.\n *\n * Each role runs the hardened loop with its own mandate, tools and authority,\n * then posts its artifact to the shared bus. Later roles read what earlier roles\n * produced, which is how the employees \"integrate\" — the handoff is explicit and\n * typed, never implicit.\n */\nimport { runAgentLoop, FINISH_TOOL, type AgentAction, type LoopLimits } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport type { ArtifactBus } from './bus.ts';\nimport type { Role, RoleInput, RoleResult } from './roles.ts';\n\nexport interface TeamRun {\n  workItem: string;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  results: { role: string; result: RoleResult }[];\n  /** Files under change after the team ran (for downstream judging). */\n  changes: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nexport interface TeamOptions {\n  /** The whole-company goal. */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The work item this team owns. */\n  workItem: string;\n  /** The scope id for artifacts (usually `${workItem}#${attempt}`). */\n  scope: string;\n  /** The ordered roster. */\n  roster: Role[];\n  /** Shared artifact bus. */\n  bus: ArtifactBus;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Files under change; a mutating role may add to this. */\n  changes?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Stop the whole team if a role fails (default: true for producers of change). */\n  stopOnFailure?: boolean;\n  /** A directory a mutating role writes real files into, so the change map reflects disk. */\n  workspaceDir?: string;\n}\n\n/** Derive a role result from the loop's terminal action. */\nfunction interpret(role: Role, actions: AgentAction[], status: string, reason: string): RoleResult {\n  const finish = [...actions].reverse().find((a) => a.tool === FINISH_TOOL);\n  const data = (finish?.input?.data as Record<string, unknown> | undefined) ?? {};\n  const summary = (finish?.input?.summary as string | undefined) ?? reason;\n  return {\n    ok: status === 'COMPLETED',\n    kind: role.produces,\n    summary,\n    data,\n    steps: actions.length,\n    reason: status === 'COMPLETED' ? undefined : reason,\n  };\n}\n\nexport async function runTeam(options: TeamOptions): Promise<TeamRun> {\n  const { goal, workItem, scope, roster, bus } = options;\n  const stopOnFailure = options.stopOnFailure ?? true;\n  const changes: Record<string, string> = { ...(options.changes ?? {}) };\n  const results: { role: string; result: RoleResult }[] = [];\n\n  for (const role of roster) {\n    const input: RoleInput = {\n      goal,\n      workItem,\n      scope,\n      artifacts: bus.forScope(scope),\n      changes: { ...changes },\n    };\n\n    // Give the brain the upstream artifacts and the files already under change.\n    const memory = JSON.stringify({\n      upstream: input.artifacts.map((a) => ({ kind: a.kind, author: a.author, summary: a.summary, data: a.data })),\n      changes: input.changes,\n    });\n\n    const loop = await runAgentLoop({\n      goal: `${role.title}: ${role.mandate} [${workItem}]`,\n      tools: role.tools,\n      brain: (state) => role.brain({ ...state, memory: state.memory }),\n      authorize: role.authorize,\n      limits: role.limits ?? options.limits,\n      workspace: scope,\n      memory,\n      verifyCompletion: role.verifyCompletion,\n    });\n\n    const result = interpret(role, loop.steps.map((s) => s.action), loop.status, loop.reason);\n\n    // QA evidence is derived from the commands the role actually ran, never from a\n    // self-reported claim: a check counts only if the loop observed it pass.\n    if (role.produces === 'evidence') {\n      const observed = loop.steps\n        .filter((s) => s.action.tool === 'run_check')\n        .map((s) => ({ name: String(s.action.input?.command ?? 'check'), status: s.observation.ok ? 'PASSED' : 'FAILED' }));\n      if (observed.length) result.data = { ...result.data, checks: observed };\n    }\n\n    // A mutating role records the files it changed. `files` must be a path->content\n    // map; a plain list of touched names (e.g. from a design) is not a change.\n    const wrote = result.data.files;\n    if (wrote && typeof wrote === 'object' && !Array.isArray(wrote)) {\n      Object.assign(changes, wrote as Record<string, string>);\n    }\n    // Capture files the role actually wrote to disk, so the change map reflects\n    // real writes even when the brain did not enumerate them in its finish data.\n    if (options.workspaceDir) {\n      for (const step of loop.steps) {\n        if (step.action.tool !== 'write_file' || !step.observation.ok) continue;\n        const rel = step.action.input?.path;\n        if (typeof rel !== 'string') continue;\n        try {\n          changes[rel] = readFileSync(path.join(options.workspaceDir, rel), 'utf8');\n        } catch {\n          /* file vanished; skip */\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    bus.post({ kind: role.produces, author: role.id, scope, summary: result.summary, data: { ...result.data, changes: { ...changes } } });\n    results.push({ role: role.id, result });\n\n    if (!result.ok && stopOnFailure) {\n      return { workItem, status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `${role.id} failed: ${result.reason ?? result.summary}`, results, changes };\n    }\n  }\n\n  const failed = results.some((r) => !r.result.ok);\n  return {\n    workItem,\n    status: failed ? 'BLOCKED' : 'COMPLETED',\n    reason: failed ? 'one or more roles failed' : 'team completed the work item',\n    results,\n    changes,\n  };\n}\n\n========== src/company/role-tools.ts ==========\n/**\n * Role tools: the real workspace tools each employee is handed.\n *\n * Reads are always available. Only `branch-write` roles get `write_file` and\n * `run_check`, and a mutation is refused unless its path is inside the role's\n * allowed roots. Every write is recorded so the team's change map reflects disk.\n */\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools, type AgentTool } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\n\nexport interface RoleToolsOptions {\n  /** The real directory this role works in. */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** True for `branch-write` roles. */\n  canMutate: boolean;\n  /** Relative path prefixes a write is confined to. ```
{
 "command": "create",
 "path": "/workspace/project/Firstborn/src/company/deliver.ts",
 "file_text": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against. Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks. Defaults to its package.json test/lint scripts. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Findings this run set out to fix (carried into the report and the PR body). */\n  findings?: AuditFinding[];\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ?? '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length ? r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.prUrl ? ['', `## Pull request`, `- ${r.prUrl}`] : []),\n    '',\n    '## Guarantees',\n    '- The change was committed to an isolated `forge/` branch, never to the base branch.',\n    '- The pull request is opened, never merged.',\n    '- The run is BLOCKED unless there was a real diff and every available check passed.',\n  ];\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n\nexport async function deliverChange(options: DeliveryOptions): Promise<DeliveryResult> {\n  const git = options.git ?? realGit();\n  const baseBranch = options.baseBranch ?? 'main';\n  const push = options.push ?? true;\n  const findings = options.findings ?? [];\n\n  const base: DeliveryResult = {\n    target: options.target,\n    baseBranch,\n    baseCommit: options.commit,\n    branch: options.branch,\n    headCommit: null,\n    status: 'BLOCKED',\n    reason: '',\n    changedFiles: [],\n    checks: [],\n    findings,\n    markdown: '',\n  };\n  const finish = (partial: Partial<DeliveryResult>): DeliveryResult => {\n    const merged = { ...base, ...partial };\n    return { ...merged, markdown: renderDeliveryMarkdown(merged) };\n  };\n\n  if (!options.branch.startsWith('forge/')) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to use branch \"${options.branch}\"; delivery branches must start with \"forge/\"` });\n  }\n  if (options.branch === baseBranch) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to deliver to the base branch \"${baseBranch}\"` });\n  }\n  if (!options.token) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'no token supplied; cannot clone, push, or open a pull request' });\n  }\n\n  // 1. Clone the target pinned at the audited commit.\n  const dir = options.workspaceDir;\n  const url = authedUrl(options.target, options.token);\n  const init = await git.run(['init', '-q', dir]);\n  if (init.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git init failed: ${redact(init.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['remote', 'add', 'origin', url], dir);\n  const fetch = await git.run(['fetch', '--depth', '1', 'origin', options.commit], dir);\n  if (fetch.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `could not fetch ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}: ${redact(fetch.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  const checkout = await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '--detach', 'FETCH_HEAD'], dir);\n  if (checkout.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `checkout of the audited commit failed: ${redact(checkout.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '-b', options.branch], dir);\n\n  // Commits need an identity; use the agent's, never the operator's.\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.name', 'openhands'], dir);\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.email', 'openhands@all-hands.dev'], dir);\n\n  // 2. What checks may we run? Only the target's own.\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir);\n  if (!Object.keys(authorized).length) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'the target declares no test or lint script, so no change can be verified; refusing to push unverified work' });\n  }\n\n  // 3. Run the implementation team inside the clone.\n  const company = await runCompany({\n    goal: options.goal,\n    plan: options.plan ?? ((g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }]),\n    rosterFor: options.rosterFor,\n    attemptsPerItem: options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2,\n    maxRoleRuns: options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40,\n    limits: options.limits,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    changes: {},\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({\n      ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0,\n      reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'the team produced no change',\n    }),\n  });\n\n  // 4. Refuse to continue without a real, non-empty diff against the base commit.\n  const diff = await git.run(['diff', '--name-only', options.commit], dir);\n  const changedFiles = diff.stdout.split('\\n').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);\n  if (!changedFiles.length) {\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no change was produced (company: ${company.reason})` });\n  }\n\n  // 5. Run the target's real checks. A failing check stops delivery.\n  const install = existsSync(path.join(dir, 'package-lock.json')) ? 'npm ci' : 'npm install';\n  const installResult = await runCommand(install, dir);\n  const checks: DeliveryResult['checks'] = [];\n  if (installResult.status === 'FAILED') {\n    checks.push({ name: 'install', status: 'FAILED', output: redact(installResult.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `dependency install failed: ${installResult.output.split('\\n')[0] ?? Run the implementation team inside the clone.\n  const company = await runCompany({\n    goal: options.goal,\n    plan: options.plan ?? It is not merged automatically._',\n  ].join('\\n');\n  let pr: { url: string; number: number } | undefined;\n  if (options.openPr) {\n    try {\n      pr = await options.openPr({ target: options.target, head: options.branch, base: baseBranch, title: `forge: ${options.goal}`, body, token: options.token });\n    } catch (err) {\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `branch pushed, but opening the pull request failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`, headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return finish({ status: 'COMPLETED', reason: `pushed ${changedFiles.length} file(s) to ${options.branch}${pr ? ` and opened PR #${pr.number}` : ''}`, headCommit, changedFiles, checks, prUrl: pr?.url, prNumber: pr?.number });\n}\n",
 "kind": "FileEditorObservation"
}

 "file_text": "/**\n * Repository context: read a target repository's inventory and key excerpts.\n *\n * Read-only. Fetches metadata, the file tree, and a bounded set of source/config\n * excerpts at the default branch's head commit. Shared by the audit CLI and the\n * delivery CLI so both look at the same commit the same way.\n */\nconst TOKEN = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN || '';\nconst repoPattern = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/;\n\nexport interface RepoContext {\n  target: string;\n  commit: string;\n  files: string[];\n  excerpts: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nexport async function ghJson(url: string): Promise<any> {\n  const res = await fetch(url, {\n    headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', 'User-Agent': 'forge-company-audit', ...(TOKEN ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } : {}) },\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub API ${res.status} for ${url}: ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 200)}`);\n  return res.json();\n}\n\nexport async function ghText(owner: string, repo: string, filePath: string, ref: string): Promise<string | null> {\n  try {\n    const encoded = filePath.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/');\n    const data = await ghJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/contents/${encoded}?ref=${encodeURIComponent(ref)}`);\n    if (data.type !== 'file' || typeof data.content !== 'string') return null;\n    return Buffer.from(data.content, 'base64').toString('utf8');\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nconst TEST_RE = /(^|\\/)(tests?|__tests__|specs?)(\\/|$)|\\.(test|spec)\\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$|_test\\.go$|(^|\\/)(test_)?[^/]*_?test\\.py$/i;\n\n/** Fetch the inventory and a representative, bounded set of excerpts. */\nexport async function fetchRepoContext(target: string): Promise<RepoContext> {\n  if (!repoPattern.test(target) || target.includes('..')) throw new Error('target must be an explicit owner/repo value');\n  const [owner, repo] = target.split('/');\n  const meta = await ghJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}`);\n  const branch = meta.default_branch;\n  const commit = await ghJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/commits/${encodeURIComponent(branch)}`);\n  const tree = await ghJson(`https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/git/trees/${commit.commit.tree.sha}?recursive=1`);\n  const files: string[] = tree.tree.filter((i: any) => i.type === 'blob').map((i: any) => i.path);\n  const has = (p: string) => files.includes(p);\n\n  const src = files.filter((p) => /\\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|py|go|kt|java)$/i.test(p) && !/(^|\\/)(node_modules|dist|build)\\//.test(p));\n  const tests = src.filter((p) => TEST_RE.test(p)).slice(0, 4);\n  const source = src.filter((p) => !TEST_RE.test(p)).slice(0, 14);\n  const entrypoints = ['server.ts', 'index.js', 'index.ts', 'src/main.tsx', 'src/App.tsx', 'package.json', 'tsconfig.json', 'vite.config.ts'].filter(has);\n  const workflows = files.filter((p) => /^\\.github\\/workflows\\/.*\\.ya?ml$/.test(p)).slice(0, 5);\n  const keyPaths = [...new Set([...entrypoints, ...workflows, ...tests, ...source])].slice(0, 22);\n  const excerpts: Record<string, string> = {};\n  for (const p of keyPaths) {\n    const v = await ghText(owner, repo, p, branch);\n    if (v !== null) excerpts[p] = v.slice(0, 4000);\n  }\n  return { target: meta.full_name, commit: '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length ? r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.prUrl ? ['', `## Pull request`, `- ${r.prUrl}`] : []),\n    '',\n    '## Guarantees',\n    '- The change was committed to an isolated `forge/` branch, never to the base branch.',\n    '- The pull request is opened, never merged.',\n    '- The run is BLOCKED unless there was a real diff and every available check passed.',\n  ];\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n\nexport async function deliverChange(options: DeliveryOptions): Promise<DeliveryResult> {\n  const git = options.git ?? realGit();\n  const baseBranch = options.baseBranch ?? 'main';\n  const push = options.push ?? true;\n  const findings = options.findings ?? [];\n\n  const base: DeliveryResult = {\n    target: options.target,\n    baseBranch,\n    baseCommit: options.commit,\n    branch: options.branch,\n    headCommit: null,\n    status: 'BLOCKED',\n    reason: '',\n    changedFiles: [],\n    checks: [],\n    findings,\n    markdown: '',\n  };\n  const finish = (partial: Partial<DeliveryResult>): DeliveryResult => {\n    const merged = { ...base, ...partial };\n    return { ...merged, markdown: renderDeliveryMarkdown(merged) };\n  };\n\n  if (!options.branch.startsWith('forge/')) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to use branch \"${options.branch}\"; delivery branches must start with \"forge/\"` });\n  }\n  if (options.branch === baseBranch) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to deliver to the base branch \"${baseBranch}\"` });\n  }\n  if (!options.token) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'no token supplied; cannot clone, push, or open a pull request' });\n  }\n\n  // 1. Clone the target pinned at the audited commit.\n  const dir = options.workspaceDir;\n  const url = options.remoteUrl ?? authedUrl(options.target, options.token);\n  const init = await git.run(['init', '-q', dir]);\n  if (init.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git init failed: ${redact(init.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['remote', 'add', 'origin', url], dir);\n  const fetch = await git.run(['fetch', '--depth', '1', 'origin', options.commit], dir);\n  if (fetch.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `could not fetch ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}: ${redact(fetch.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  const checkout = await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '--detach', 'FETCH_HEAD'], dir);\n  if (checkout.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `checkout of the audited commit failed: ${redact(checkout.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '-b', options.branch], dir);\n\n  // Commits need an identity; use the agent's, never the operator's.\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.name', 'openhands'], dir);\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.email', 'openhands@all-hands.dev'], dir);\n\n  // 2. What checks may we run? Only the target's own.\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir);\n  if (!Object.keys(authorized).length) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'the target declares no test or lint script, so no change can be verified; refusing to push unverified work' });\n  }\n\n  // Prepare dependencies before the team works, so QA can run the target's real\n  // checks during the run. 'npm ci' : 'npm install';\n    const installResult = await runCommand(install, dir);\n    if (installResult.status === 'FAILED') {\n      checks.push({ name: 'install', status: 'FAILED', output: redact(installResult.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `dependency install failed: ${installResult.output.split('\\n')[0] ?? 'unknown'}`, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 3. Run the implementation team inside the clone.\n  const company = await runCompany({\n    goal: options.goal,\n    plan: options.plan ?? ((g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }]),\n    rosterFor: options.rosterFor,\n    attemptsPerItem: options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2,\n    maxRoleRuns: options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40,\n    limits: options.limits,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    changes: {},\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({\n      ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0,\n      reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'the team produced no change',\n    }),\n  });\n\n  // 4. Refuse to continue without a real, non-empty diff against the base commit.\n  const diff = await git.run(['diff', '--name-only', options.commit], dir);\n  const changedFiles = diff.stdout.split('\\n').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);\n  if (!changedFiles.length) {\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no change was produced (company: ${company.reason})`, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 5. Run the target's real checks. A failing check stops delivery.\n  for (const name of Object.keys(authorized)) {\n    const res = await runCommand(authorized[name], dir);\n    checks.push({ name, status: res.status, output: redact(res.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n    if (res.status === 'FAILED') {\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `check \"${name}\" failed; refusing to push a broken change`, changedFiles, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 6. Only install when the target declares dependencies; a\n  // lockfile-less install on a dependency-free target would add files to the diff.\n  const checks: DeliveryResult['checks'] = [];\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  let hasDeps = false;\n  if (existsSync(pkgPath)) {\n    try {\n      const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { dependencies?: Record<string, string>; devDependencies?: Record<string, string> };\n      hasDeps = Object.keys(pkg.dependencies ?? {}).length > 0 || Object.keys(pkg.devDependencies ?? {}).length > 0;\n    } catch {\n      hasDeps = false;\n    }\n  }\n  if (hasDeps) {\n    const install = existsSync(path.join(dir, 'package-lock.json')) ? 'npm ci' : 'npm install';\n    const installResult = await runCommand(install, dir);\n    if (installResult.status === 'FAILED') {\n      checks.push({ name: 'install', status: 'FAILED', output: redact(installResult.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `dependency install failed: ${installResult.output.split('\\n')[0] ?? 'unknown'}`, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 3. Run the implementation team inside the clone.\n  const company = await runCompany({\n    goal: options.goal,\n    plan: options.plan ?? ((g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }]),\n    rosterFor: options.rosterFor,\n    attemptsPerItem: options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2,\n    maxRoleRuns: options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40,\n    limits: options.limits,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    changes: {},\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({\n      ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0,\n      reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'the team produced no change',\n    }),\n  });\n\n  // 4. Refuse to continue without a real, non-empty diff against the base commit.\n  //    Stage first: `git diff` ignores new files, so a change that adds a file\n  //    would otherwise look empty. node_modules is excluded locally (via\n  //    .git/info/exclude) so an install never leaks into the change even when the\n  //    target has no .gitignore of its own.\n  const excludeRel = (await git.run(['rev-parse', '--git-path', 'info/exclude'], dir)).stdout.trim();\n  if (excludeRel) {\n    const excludeAbs = path.isAbsolute(excludeRel) ? excludeRel : path.join(dir, excludeRel);\n    try {\n      const current = existsSync(excludeAbs) ? readFileSync(excludeAbs, 'utf8') : '';\n      if (!/^node_modules\\/?$/m.test(current)) {\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(excludeAbs), { recursive: true });\n        appendFileSync(excludeAbs, `${current.endsWith('\\n') || !current ? '' : '\\n'}node_modules/\\n`);\n      }\n    } catch {\n      /* best effort; the commit step will surface a real failure */\n    }\n  }\n  const add = await git.run(['add', '-A'], dir);\n  if (add.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git add failed: ${redact(add.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, checks });\n  const diff = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--name-only', options.commit], dir);\n  const changedFiles = diff.stdout.split('\\n').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);\n  if (!changedFiles.length) {\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no change was produced (company: ${company.reason})`, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 5. Run the target's real checks. A failing check stops delivery.\n  for (const name of Object.keys(authorized)) {\n    const res = await runCommand(authorized[name], dir);\n    checks.push({ name, status: res.status, output: redact(res.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n    if (res.status === 'FAILED') {\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `check \"${name}\" failed; refusing to push a broken change`, changedFiles, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 6. Commit and push an isolated branch.\n  const message = `forge: ${options.goal}\\n\\nProposed by the Forge software company from an audit of ${options.target} at ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}.\\n\\nCo-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev>`;\n  const commit = await git.run(['commit', '-q', '-m', message], dir);\n  if (commit.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git commit failed: ${redact(commit.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, changedFiles, checks });\n  const head = await git.run(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], dir);\n  const headCommit = head.stdout.trim();\n\n  if (!push) {\n    return finish({ status: 'COMPLETED', reason: 'built and verified locally (push disabled)', headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  const pushResult = await git.run(['push', 'origin', `HEAD:refs/heads/${options.branch}`], dir);\n  if (pushResult.code !== 0) {\n    return finish({ reason: `git push failed: ${redact(pushResult.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 7. Open the pull request (never merge).\n  const body = [\n    `The Forge software company audited \\`${options.target}\\` at \\`${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}\\` and proposes this change.`,\n    '',\n    '## What this addresses',\n    ...(findings.length ? findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification',\n    ...checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`),\n    '',\n    '_This pull request was opened by an AI agent (Forge / OpenHands) on behalf of the repository owner. Then subsequent roles get finish. So no file written.

I need per-role counters. Let me fix: create the brain inside the map with its own counter.

Let me rewrite the addFile function so each role gets its own closure with its own index.

'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '0.0.0' };\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (v !== '1.0.0') { console.error('expected 1.0.0, got ' + v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: 'index.js', content: opts.bad ? 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n' : \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\" } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n' : \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\" } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir: string, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}) {\n  return (_item: WorkItem, attempt: number): Role[] => {\n    const base = rosterFor(attempt, opts);\n    return base.map((r) => ({ ...r, tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }) }));\n  };\n}\n\ntest('resolveAuthorizedCommands reads only the target\\'s declared scripts', () => {\n  const dir = tmp('pkg-');\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ scripts: { test: 'node --test', build: 'vite build' } }));\n  assert.deepEqual(resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir), { test: 'npm test' });\n  const empty = tmp('pkg-');\n  assert.deepEqual(resolveAuthorizedCommands(empty), {});\n});\n\ntest('delivery pushes a real, verified change to a real remote branch', async () => {\n  const { remoteDir, commit } = seedRemote();\n  const work = tmp('deliver-work-');\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: 'local/seed',\n    goal: 'bump the version',\n    commit,\n    branch: 'forge/deliver-test',\n    workspaceDir: work,\n    token: 'unused-in-local-test',\n    remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    push: true,\n    openPr: async () => ({ url: 'https://example.test/pr/1', number: 1 }),\n  });\n\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'COMPLETED', result.reason);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.changedFiles, ['index.js']);\n  assert.equal(result.checks.find((c) => c.name === 'test')?.status, 'PASSED');\n  assert.equal(result.prNumber, 1);\n\n  // The branch is really on the remote, and the change is really in it.\n  const remoteHead = git(['rev-parse', `refs/heads/forge/deliver-test`], remoteDir);\n  assert.equal(remoteHead, result.headCommit);\n  const show = git(['show', `refs/heads/forge/deliver-test:index.js`], remoteDir);\n  assert.match(show, /1\\.0\\.0/);\n  // The base branch was never touched.\n  assert.equal(git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'], remoteDir), commit);\n});\n\ntest('delivery refuses to push when the target\\'s own check fails', async () => {\n  const { remoteDir, commit } = seedRemote();\n  const work = tmp('deliver-work-');\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: 'local/seed',\n    goal: 'break the version',\n    commit,\n    branch: 'forge/broken',\n    workspaceDir: work,\n    token: 'unused-in-local-test',\n    remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work, { bad: true }),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    push: true,\n  });\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'BLOCKED');\n  assert.match(result.reason, /check \"test\" failed/);\n  // No branch was created on the remote.\n  const branches = git(['branch', '--list'], remoteDir);\n  assert.doesNotMatch(branches, /forge\\/broken/);\n});\n\ntest('delivery detects a change that only adds a new file', async () => {\n  const { remoteDir, commit } = seedRemote({ testScript: 'node --test' });\n  const work = tmp('deliver-work-');\n  const addFile = (_item: WorkItem, _attempt: number): Role[] => {\n    return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => {\n      const script: AgentAction[] =\n        r.id === 'implementer'\n [\n              { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: 'NEW.md', content: '# new\\n' } },\n              { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'added a file', data: { files: { 'NEW.md': '# new\\n' } } } },\n            ]\n          : r.id === 'qa'\n            ? [\n                { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n                { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the check', data: {} } },\n              ]\n            : [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: r.id, data: r.id === 'security' ? { clean: true } : r.id === 'reviewer' ? { blockers: 0 } : {} } }];\n      let i = 0;\n      return {\n        ...r,\n        tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: work, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }),\n        brain: (async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)]) as AgentBrain,\n      };\n    });\n  };\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: 'local/seed', goal: 'add a file', commit, branch: 'forge/add-only',\n    workspaceDir: work, token: 'unused-in-local-test', remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: addFile, attemptsPerItem: 1, push: true,\n    openPr: async () => ({ url: 'https://example.test/pr/2', number: 2 }),\n  });\n  // `git diff` alone would miss an untracked file; the run must still see it.\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'COMPLETED', result.reason);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.changedFiles, ['NEW.md']);\n  const remoteHead = git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/forge/add-only'], remoteDir);\n  assert.equal(remoteHead, result.headCommit);\n});\n\ntest('delivery refuses a branch that is not under forge/', async () => {\n  const { remoteDir, commit } = seedRemote();\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: 'local/seed', goal: 'x', commit, branch: 'main', workspaceDir: tmp('w-'),\n    token: 't', remoteUrl: remoteDir, rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(tmp('w-')), push: false,\n  });\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'BLOCKED');\n  assert.match(result.reason, /must start with \"forge\\/\"|base branch/);\n});\n\ntest('delivery refuses to push a change it cannot verify (no checks declared)', async () => {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'no-scripts' }));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), 'module.exports = {};\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n\n  const work = tmp('deliver-work-');\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: 'local/seed', goal: 'x', commit, branch: 'forge/nochecks', workspaceDir: work,\n    token: 't', remoteUrl: remoteDir, rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work), push: true,\n  });\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'BLOCKED');\n  assert.match(result.reason, /no test or lint script/);\n});\n",

---

## 1. Rotate the leaked token

A token was embedded in this workspace's `git remote` URL (I removed it and sanitized the URL, but it appeared in terminal output, so it must be treated as exposed).

**Link:** https://github.com/settings/tokens

- Click that link. You'll see two tabs: **Tokens (classic)** and **Fine-grained tokens**.
- Check both tabs for a token that would have been used for this repo. If you don't recognize it, or it's the one that was in the remote, click it → **Delete** (or **Revoke**).
- If you can't tell which one it was, the safe move is: revoke all tokens you don't actively need, then create a fresh one in step 3.

> Rotating = delete the old one and create a new one. GitHub tokens cannot be "changed in place"; you revoke and replace.

---

## 2. Tell me which scratch repo to use

**Link:** https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug?tab=repositories

- Look at your repo list. Tell me the name of the repo I should use for the live cross-repo test.

---

## 3. Add the `FORGE_DELIVER_TOKEN` secret

This is the token the workflow uses to push a branch and open a PR **on another repo**. The built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot do that — it only reaches this repo.

### 3a. Create the token
**Link:** https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new

- **Token name:** `FORGE_DELIVER_TOKEN`
- **Expiration:** 90 days (or your preference)
- **Repository access:** *Only select repositories* → pick the scratch repo from step 2
- **Permissions** (under "Repository permissions"):
  - **Contents** → **Read and write**
  - **Pull requests** → **Read and write**
  - **Metadata** → Read (auto-selected)
- Click **Generate token** and **copy it** (you won't see it again).

> Simpler alternative if fine-grained gives you trouble: create a **classic** token at https://github.com/settings/tokens/new with the single **`repo`** scope. Broader, but works everywhere.

### 3b. Add it to the repo
**Link:** https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn/settings/secrets/actions

- Click **New repository secret**
- **Name:** `FORGE_DELIVER_TOKEN` (exactly this — capital letters and underscores)

- Click **Add secret**

If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against. Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ?? 'main';\n  const push = options.push ?? true;\n  const findings = options.findings ?? [];\n\n  const base: DeliveryResult = {\n    target: options.target,\n    baseBranch,\n    baseCommit: options.commit,\n    branch: options.branch,\n    headCommit: null,\n    status: 'BLOCKED',\n    reason: '',\n    changedFiles: [],\n    checks: [],\n    findings,\n    markdown: '',\n  };\n  const finish = (partial: Partial<DeliveryResult>): DeliveryResult => {\n    const merged = { ...base, ...partial };\n    return { ...merged, markdown: renderDeliveryMarkdown(merged) };\n  };\n\n  if (!options.branch.startsWith('forge/')) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to use branch \"${options.branch}\"; delivery branches must start with \"forge/\"` });\n  }\n  if (options.branch === baseBranch) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to deliver to the base branch \"${baseBranch}\"` });\n  }\n  if (!options.token) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'no token supplied; cannot clone, push, or open a pull request' });\n  }\n\n  // 1. Clone the target pinned at the audited commit.\n  const dir = options.workspaceDir;\n  const url = options.remoteUrl ?? authedUrl(options.target, options.token);\n  const init = await git.run(['init', '-q', dir]);\n  if (init.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git init failed: ${redact(init.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['remote', 'add', 'origin', url], dir);\n  const fetch = await git.run(['fetch', '--depth', '1', 'origin', options.commit], dir);\n  if (fetch.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `could not fetch ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}: ${redact(fetch.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  const checkout = await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '--detach', 'FETCH_HEAD'], dir);\n  if (checkout.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `checkout of the audited commit failed: ${redact(checkout.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '-b', options.branch], dir);\n\n  // Commits need an identity; use the agent's, never the operator's.\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.name', 'openhands'], dir);\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.email', 'openhands@all-hands.dev'], dir);\n\n  // 2. What checks may we run? Only the target's own.\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir);\n  if (!Object.keys(authorized).length) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'the target declares no test or lint script, so no change can be verified; refusing to push unverified work' });\n  }\n\n  // Prepare dependencies before the team works, so QA can run the target's real\n  // checks during the run. Only install when the target declares dependencies; a\n  // lockfile-less install on a dependency-free target would add files to the diff.\n  const checks: DeliveryResult['checks'] = [];\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  let hasDeps = false;\n  if (existsSync(pkgPath)) {\n    try {\n      const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { dependencies?: Record<string, string>; devDependencies?: Record<string, string> };\n      hasDeps = Object.keys(pkg.dependencies ?? {}).length > 0 || Object.keys(pkg.devDependencies ?? {}).length > 0;\n    } catch {\n      hasDeps = false;\n    }\n  }\n  if (hasDeps) {\n    const install = existsSync(path.join(dir, 'package-lock.json')) ? 'unknown'}`, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 3. Run the implementation team inside the clone.\n  const company = await runCompany({\n    goal: options.goal,\n    plan: options.plan ?? ((g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }]),\n    rosterFor: options.rosterFor,\n    attemptsPerItem: options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2,\n    maxRoleRuns: options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40,\n    limits: options.limits,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    changes: {},\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({\n      ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0,\n      reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'the team produced no change',\n    }),\n  });\n\n  // 4. Refuse to continue without a real, non-empty diff against the base commit.\n  //    Stage first: `git diff` ignores new files, so a change that adds a file\n  //    would otherwise look empty. node_modules is excluded locally (via\n  //    .git/info/exclude) so an install never leaks into the change even when the\n  //    target has no .gitignore of its own.\n  const excludeRel = (await git.run(['rev-parse', '--git-path', 'info/exclude'], dir)).stdout.trim();\n  if (excludeRel) {\n    const excludeAbs = path.isAbsolute(excludeRel) ? excludeRel : path.join(dir, excludeRel);\n    try {\n      const current = existsSync(excludeAbs) ? readFileSync(excludeAbs, 'utf8') : '';\n      if (!/^node_modules\\/?$/m.test(current)) {\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(excludeAbs), { recursive: true });\n        appendFileSync(excludeAbs, `${current.endsWith('\\n') || !current ? '' : '\\n'}node_modules/\\n`);\n      }\n    } catch {\n      /* best effort; the commit step will surface a real failure */\n    }\n  }\n  const add = await git.run(['add', '-A'], dir);\n  if (add.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git add failed: ${redact(add.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, checks });\n  const diff = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--name-only', options.commit], dir);\n  const changedFiles = diff.stdout.split('\\n').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);\n  if (!changedFiles.length) {\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no change was produced (company: ${company.reason})`, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 5. Run the target's real checks. Open the pull request (never merge).\n  const body = [\n    `The Forge software company audited \\`${options.target}\\` at \\`${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}\\` and proposes this change.`,\n    '',\n    '## What this addresses',\n    ...(findings.length ? findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification',\n    ...checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`),\n    '',\n    '_This pull request was opened by an AI agent (Forge / OpenHands) on behalf of the repository owner. But `package.json` isn't in the second seed, so `npm install`... hasDeps false, authorized = resolveAuthorizedCommands reads package.json — but the second seed has no package.json! So `resolveAuthorizedCommands` returns {} → BLOCKED with "no test or lint script", not "already fails". That's the wrong reason.

 "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === Run the target's real checks. A failing check stops delivery.\n  for (const name of Object.keys(authorized)) {\n    const res = await runCommand(authorized[name], dir);\n    checks.push({ name, status: res.status, output: redact(res.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n    if (res.status === 'FAILED') {\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `check \"${name}\" failed; refusing to push a broken change`, changedFiles, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 6. Commit and push an isolated branch.\n  const message = `forge: ${options.goal}\\n\\nProposed by the Forge software company from an audit of ${options.target} at ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}.\\n\\nCo-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev>`;\n  const commit = await git.run(['commit', '-q', '-m', message], dir);\n  if (commit.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git commit failed: ${redact(commit.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, changedFiles, checks });\n  const head = await git.run(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], dir);\n  const headCommit = head.stdout.trim();\n\n  if (!push) {\n    return finish({ status: 'COMPLETED', reason: 'built and verified locally (push disabled)', headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  const pushResult = await git.run(['push', 'origin', `HEAD:refs/heads/${options.branch}`], dir);\n  if (pushResult.code !== 0) {\n    return finish({ reason: `git push failed: ${redact(pushResult.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 7. Open the pull request (never merge).\n  const body = [\n    `The Forge software company audited \\`${options.target}\\` at \\`${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}\\` and proposes this change.`,\n    '',\n    '## What this addresses',\n    ...(findings.length ? findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification',\n    ...checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`),\n    '',\n    '_This pull request was opened by an AI agent (Forge / OpenHands) on behalf of the repository owner.  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against. Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Override the clone/push URL (tests point this at a local bare repo). */\n  remoteUrl?: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks. Defaults to its package.json test/lint scripts. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Findings this run set out to fix (carried into the report and the PR body). */\n  findings?: AuditFinding[];\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ?? '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length ? r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.prUrl ? Clone the target pinned at the audited commit.\n  const dir = options.workspaceDir;\n  const url = options.remoteUrl ?? authedUrl(options.target, options.token);\n  const init = await git.run(['init', '-q', dir]);\n  if (init.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git init failed: ${redact(init.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['remote', 'add', 'origin', url], dir);\n  const fetch = await git.run(['fetch', '--depth', '1', 'origin', options.commit], dir);\n  if (fetch.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `could not fetch ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}: ${redact(fetch.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  const checkout = await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '--detach', 'FETCH_HEAD'], dir);\n  if (checkout.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `checkout of the audited commit failed: ${redact(checkout.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '-b', options.branch], dir);\n\n  // Commits need an identity; use the agent's, never the operator's.\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.name', 'openhands'], dir);\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.email', 'openhands@all-hands.dev'], dir);\n\n  // 2. Only the target's own.\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir);\n  if (!Object.keys(authorized).length) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'the target declares no test or lint script, so no change can be verified; refusing to push unverified work' });\n  }\n\n  // Prepare dependencies before the team works, so QA can run the target's real\n  // checks during the run. Retry once and record which\n    // command actually worked, rather than failing a target that its own team\n    // can still test.\n    if (installResult.status === 'FAILED' && /ERESOLVE|peer dep|Conflicting peer/i.test(installResult.output)) {\n      installCmd = `${installCmd} --legacy-peer-deps`;\n      installResult = await runCommand(installCmd, dir);\n    }\n    if (installResult.status === 'FAILED') {\n      checks.push({ name: 'install', status: 'FAILED', output: redact(installResult.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `dependency install failed: ${installResult.output.split('\\n')[0] ?? 'unknown'}`, checks });\n    }\n    checks.push({ name: installCmd === 'npm ci' || installCmd === 'npm install' ? 'install' : `install (${installCmd})`, status: 'PASSED', output: '' });\n  }\n\n  // Establish the baseline: if the target's checks already fail at the base\n  // commit, a later failure cannot be attributed to the company's change, so\n  // refuse up front rather than take blame (or credit) for a pre-existing break.\n  for (const name of Object.keys(authorized)) {\n    const base = await runCommand(authorized[name], dir);\n    checks.push({ name: `baseline:${name}`, status: base.status, output: redact(base.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n    if (base.status === 'FAILED') {\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `the target's \"${name}\" check already fails at ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}; cannot verify a change against a broken baseline`, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 3. ((g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }]),\n    rosterFor: options.rosterFor,\n    attemptsPerItem: options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2,\n    maxRoleRuns: options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40,\n    limits: options.limits,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    changes: {},\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({\n      ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0,\n      reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'the team produced no change',\n    }),\n  });\n\n  // 4. Refuse to continue without a real, non-empty diff against the base commit.\n  //    Stage first: `git diff` ignores new files, so a change that adds a file\n  //    would otherwise look empty. node_modules is excluded locally (via\n  //    .git/info/exclude) so an install never leaks into the change even when the\n  //    target has no .gitignore of its own.\n  const excludeRel = (await git.run(['rev-parse', '--git-path', 'info/exclude'], dir)).stdout.trim();\n  if (excludeRel) {\n    const excludeAbs = path.isAbsolute(excludeRel) ? excludeRel : path.join(dir, excludeRel);\n    try {\n      const current = existsSync(excludeAbs) ? readFileSync(excludeAbs, 'utf8') : '';\n      if (!/^node_modules\\/?$/m.test(current)) {\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(excludeAbs), { recursive: true });\n        appendFileSync(excludeAbs, `${current.endsWith('\\n') || !current ? '' : '\\n'}node_modules/\\n`);\n      }\n    } catch {\n      /* best effort; the commit step will surface a real failure */\n    }\n  }\n  const add = await git.run(['add', '-A'], dir);\n  if (add.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git add failed: ${redact(add.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, checks });\n  const diff = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--name-only', options.commit], dir);\n  const changedFiles = diff.stdout.split('\\n').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);\n  if (!changedFiles.length) {\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no change was produced (company: ${company.reason})`, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 5. const SHADOW_MAX_DELETIONS = Math.max(0, Number.parseInt(process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_MAX_DELETIONS ?? '', 10) || 30);
const SHADOW_RATIO = 0.5;
const numstat = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--numstat', options.commit], dir);
const destructive: string[] = [];
for (const line of numstat.stdout.split('\n')) {
  const [addedRaw, deletedRaw, ...rest] = line.split('\t');
  const file = rest.join('\t');
  if (!file || addedRaw === '-' || deletedRaw === '-') continue;
  const added = Number(addedRaw), deleted = Number(deletedRaw);
  if (deleted > SHADOW_MAX_DELETIONS && deleted > added / Math.max(1, SHADOW_RATIO)) destructive.push(file);
}
if (destructive.length) {
  return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `refusing a change that deletes most of: ${destructive.join(', ')}; a partial read can silently gut a file`, changedFiles, checks });
}
```
