Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ?? '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length ? r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.prUrl ? ['', `## Pull request`, `- ${r.prUrl}`] : []),\n    '',\n    '## Guarantees',\n    '- The change was committed to an isolated `forge/` branch, never to the base branch.',\n    '- The pull request is opened, never merged.',\n    '- The run is BLOCKED unless there was a real diff and every available check passed.',\n  ];\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n\nexport async function deliverChange(options: DeliveryOptions): Promise<DeliveryResult> {\n  const git = options.git ?? realGit();\n  const baseBranch = options.baseBranch ?? 'main';\n  const push = options.push ?? true;\n  const findings = options.findings ?? [];\n\n  const base: DeliveryResult = {\n    target: options.target,\n    baseBranch,\n    baseCommit: options.commit,\n    branch: options.branch,\n    headCommit: null,\n    status: 'BLOCKED',\n    reason: '',\n    changedFiles: [],\n    checks: [],\n    findings,\n    markdown: '',\n  };\n  const finish = (partial: Partial<DeliveryResult>): DeliveryResult => {\n    const merged = { ...base, ...partial };\n    return { ...merged, markdown: renderDeliveryMarkdown(merged) };\n  };\n\n  if (!options.branch.startsWith('forge/')) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to use branch \"${options.branch}\"; delivery branches must start with \"forge/\"` });\n  }\n  if (options.branch === baseBranch) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to deliver to the base branch \"${baseBranch}\"` });\n  }\n  if (!options.token) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'no token supplied; cannot clone, push, or open a pull request' });\n  }\n\n  // 1. Clone the target pinned at the audited commit.\n  const dir = options.workspaceDir;\n  const url = options.remoteUrl ?? authedUrl(options.target, options.token);\n  const init = await git.run(['init', '-q', dir]);\n  if (init.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git init failed: ${redact(init.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['remote', 'add', 'origin', url], dir);\n  const fetch = await git.run(['fetch', '--depth', '1', 'origin', options.commit], dir);\n  if (fetch.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `could not fetch ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}: ${redact(fetch.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  const checkout = await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '--detach', 'FETCH_HEAD'], dir);\n  if (checkout.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `checkout of the audited commit failed: ${redact(checkout.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '-b', options.branch], dir);\n\n  // Commits need an identity; use the agent's, never the operator's.\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.name', 'openhands'], dir);\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.email', 'openhands@all-hands.dev'], dir);\n\n  // 2. What checks may we run? Only the target's own.\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir);\n  if (!Object.keys(authorized).length) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'the target declares no test or lint script, so no change can be verified; refusing to push unverified work' });\n  }\n\n  // Prepare dependencies before the team works, so QA can run the target's real\n  // checks during the run. Only install when the target declares dependencies; a\n  // lockfile-less install on a dependency-free target would add files to the diff.\n  const checks: DeliveryResult['checks'] = [];\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  let hasDeps = false;\n  if (existsSync(pkgPath)) {\n    try {\n      const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { dependencies?: Record<string, string>; devDependencies?: Record<string, string> };\n      hasDeps = Object.keys(pkg.dependencies ?? {}).length > 0 || Object.keys(pkg.devDependencies ?? {}).length > 0;\n    } catch {\n      hasDeps = false;\n    }\n  }\n  if (hasDeps) {\n    let installCmd = existsSync(path.join(dir, 'package-lock.json')) ? 'npm ci' : 'npm install';\n    let installResult = await runCommand(installCmd, dir);\n    // Some real projects have a peer-dependency conflict that only\n    // `--legacy-peer-deps` resolves (Amina is one). Retry once and record which\n    // command actually worked, rather than failing a target that its own team\n    // can still test.\n    if (installResult.status === 'FAILED' && /ERESOLVE|peer dep|Conflicting peer/i.test(installResult.output)) {\n      installCmd = `${installCmd} --legacy-peer-deps`;\n      installResult = await runCommand(installCmd, dir);\n    }\n    if (installResult.status === 'FAILED') {\n      checks.push({ name: 'install', status: 'FAILED', output: redact(installResult.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `dependency install failed: ${installResult.output.split('\\n')[0] ?? 'unknown'}`, checks });\n    }\n    checks.push({ name: installCmd === 'npm ci' || installCmd === 'npm install' ? 'install' : `install (${installCmd})`, status: 'PASSED', output: '' });\n  }\n\n  // Establish the baseline: if the target's checks already fail at the base\n  // commit, a later failure cannot be attributed to the company's change, so\n  // refuse up front rather than take blame (or credit) for a pre-existing break.\n  for (const name of Object.keys(authorized)) {\n    const base = await runCommand(authorized[name], dir);\n    checks.push({ name: `baseline:${name}`, status: base.status, output: redact(base.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n    if (base.status === 'FAILED') {\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `the target's \"${name}\" check already fails at ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}; cannot verify a change against a broken baseline`, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 3. Run the implementation team inside the clone.\n  const company = await runCompany({\n    goal: options.goal,\n    plan: options.plan ?? ((g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }]),\n    rosterFor: options.rosterFor,\n    attemptsPerItem: options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2,\n    maxRoleRuns: options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40,\n    limits: options.limits,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    changes: {},\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({\n      ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0,\n      reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'the team produced no change',\n    }),\n  });\n\n  // 4. Refuse to continue without a real, non-empty diff against the base commit.\n  //    Stage first: `git diff` ignores new files, so a change that adds a file\n  //    would otherwise look empty. node_modules is excluded locally (via\n  //    .git/info/exclude) so an install never leaks into the change even when the\n  //    target has no .gitignore of its own.\n  const excludeRel = (await git.run(['rev-parse', '--git-path', 'info/exclude'], dir)).stdout.trim();\n  if (excludeRel) {\n    const excludeAbs = path.isAbsolute(excludeRel) ? excludeRel : path.join(dir, excludeRel);\n    try {\n      const current = existsSync(excludeAbs) ? readFileSync(excludeAbs, 'utf8') : '';\n      if (!/^node_modules\\/?$/m.test(current)) {\n        mkdirSync(path.dirname(excludeAbs), { recursive: true });\n        appendFileSync(excludeAbs, `${current.endsWith('\\n') || !current ? '' : '\\n'}node_modules/\\n`);\n      }\n    } catch {\n      /* best effort; the commit step will surface a real failure */\n    }\n  }\n  const add = await git.run(['add', '-A'], dir);\n  if (add.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git add failed: ${redact(add.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, checks });\n  const diff = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--name-only', options.commit], dir);\n  const changedFiles = diff.stdout.split('\\n').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);\n  if (!changedFiles.length) {\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no change was produced (company: ${company.reason})`, checks });\n  }\n\n  // A free model that reads a truncated file will happily write back a tiny\n  // fragment, silently deleting the rest. Tests and lint do not catch a gutted\n  // README or config, so a \"verified\" run can still be destructive. Refuse a\n  // change that removes most of a file that still exists. Whole-file deletions\n  // (a clear intent) and small edits are allowed.\n  const numstat = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--numstat', options.commit], dir);\n  const gutted: string[] = [];\n  for (const line of numstat.stdout.split('\\n')) {\n    const [addedRaw, deletedRaw, ...rest] = line.split('\\t');\n    const file = rest.join('\\t');\n    if (!file || addedRaw === '-' || deletedRaw === '-') continue;\n    if (!existsSync(path.join(dir, file))) continue;\n    const added = Number(addedRaw);\n    const deleted = Number(deletedRaw);\n    if (deleted > 30 && deleted > added * 2) gutted.push(`${file} (-${deleted}/+${added})`);\n  }\n  if (gutted.length) {\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `refusing a change that deletes most of: ${gutted.join(', ')}; a partial read can silently gut a file`, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 5. Run the target's real checks. Commit and push an isolated branch.\n  const message = `forge: ${options.goal}\\n\\nProposed by the Forge software company from an audit of ${options.target} at ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}.\\n\\nCo-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev>`;\n  const commit = await git.run(['commit', '-q', '-m', message], dir);\n  if (commit.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git commit failed: ${redact(commit.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, changedFiles, checks });\n  const head = await git.run(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], dir);\n  const headCommit = head.stdout.trim();\n\n  if (!push) {\n    return finish({ status: 'COMPLETED', reason: 'built and verified locally (push disabled)', headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  const pushResult = await git.run(['push', 'origin', `HEAD:refs/heads/${options.branch}`], dir);\n  if (pushResult.code !== 0) {\n    return finish({ reason: `git push failed: ${redact(pushResult.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 7.  "old_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: 'index.js', content: opts.bad ? 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n' : \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\" } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n' : \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\" } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir: string, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}) {\n  return (_item: WorkItem, attempt: number): Role[] => {\n    const base = rosterFor(attempt, opts);\n    return base.map((r) => ({ ...r, tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }) }));\n  };\n}\n\ntest('resolveAuthorizedCommands reads only the target\\'s declared scripts', () => {\n  const dir = branch: 'forge/deliver-test',\n    workspaceDir: work,\n    token: 'unused-in-local-test',\n    remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    push: true,\n    openPr: async () => ({ url: 'https://example.test/pr/1', number: 1 }),\n  });\n\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'COMPLETED', result.reason);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.changedFiles, really in it.\n  const remoteHead = git(['rev-parse', `refs/heads/forge/deliver-test`], remoteDir);\n  assert.equal(remoteHead, result.headCommit);\n  const show = git(['show', `refs/heads/forge/deliver-test:index.js`], remoteDir);\n  assert.match(show, /1\\.1\\.0/);\n  // The base branch was never touched.\n  assert.equal(git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'], remoteDir), remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work, { bad: true }),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    push: true,\n  });\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'BLOCKED');\n  "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: 'index.js', content: opts.bad ? 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n' : \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\" } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n' : \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\" } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir: string, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}) {\n  return (_item: WorkItem, attempt: number): Role[] => {\n    const base = rosterFor(attempt, opts);\n    return base.map((r) => ({ ...r, tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }) }));\n  };\n}\n\ntest('resolveAuthorizedCommands reads only the target\\'s declared scripts', () => {\n  const dir =    "text": "/**\n * Role tools: the real workspace tools each employee is handed.\n *\n * Reads are always available. Only `branch-write` roles get `write_file` and\n * `run_check`, and a mutation is refused unless its path is inside the role's\n * allowed roots. Every write is recorded so the team's change map reflects disk.\n */\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools, type AgentTool } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\n\nexport interface RoleToolsOptions {\n  /** The real directory this role works in. */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** True for `branch-write` roles. */\n  canMutate: boolean;\n  /** Relative path prefixes a write is confined to. Defaults to the whole workspace. */\n  allowedRoots?: string[];\n  /** Authorized verification commands: label -> command. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_COMMANDS: Record<string, string> = {\n  test: 'npm test',\n  lint: 'npm run lint',\n};\n\nexport function buildRoleTools(options: RoleToolsOptions): AgentTool[] {\n  const roots = options.allowedRoots?.length ? options.allowedRoots : [''];\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? DEFAULT_COMMANDS;\n\n  const base = buildWorkspaceTools({\n    workspace: options.workspaceDir,\n    allowMutation: options.canMutate,\n    authorizedCommands: authorized,\n    runner: (command, cwd) => runCommand(command, cwd),\n  });\n\n  return base.map((tool) => {\n    if (tool.name !== 'write_file') return tool;\n    const original = tool.run;\n    return {\n      ...tool,\n      run: async (input, ctx) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        if (!roots.some((root) => root === '' || rel === root || rel.startsWith(root.endsWith('/') ? root : root + '/'))) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the allowed roots (${roots.join(', ')}): ${rel}` };\n        }\n        return original(input, ctx);\n      },\n    };\n  });\n}"

```ts
tools.push({
  name: 'edit_file',
  description: 'Replace a unique snippet in an existing file. Input: {"path":"...","old_string":"...","new_string":"..."}. Prefer this over write_file for existing files. Mutating.',
  mutating: true,
  run: async (input) => {
    const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';
    const oldStr = typeof input.old_string === 'string' ? input.old_string : '';
    const newStr = typeof input.new_string === 'string' ? input.new_string : '';
    if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires a "path".' };
    if (!oldStr) return { ok: false, output: 'edit_file requires a non-empty "old_string".' };
    const abs = resolveInWorkspace(workspace, rel);
    if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to edit outside the workspace: ${rel}` };
    try {
      if (!existsSync(abs)) return { ok: false, output: `No such file: ${rel} (use write_file to create it)` };
      const current = readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');
      const first = current.indexOf(oldStr);
      if (first === -1) return { ok: false, output: `old_string not found in ${rel}. Read the file and copy the exact text.` };
      if (current.indexOf(oldStr, first + oldStr.length) !== -1) return { ok: false, output: `old_string is not unique in ${rel}; include more surrounding context.` };
      writeFileSync(abs, current.slice(0, first) + newStr + current.slice(first + oldStr.length));
      return { ok: true, output: `Edited ${rel} (${oldStr.length} -> ${newStr.length} chars).` };
    } catch (err) {
      return { ok: false, output: `Edit failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };
    }
  },
});
```

DEFAULT_COMMANDS;\n\n  const base = buildWorkspaceTools({\n    workspace: options.workspaceDir,\n    allowMutation: options.canMutate,\n    authorizedCommands: authorized,\n    runner: (command, cwd) => runCommand(command, cwd),\n  });\n\n  return base.map((tool) => {\n    if (tool.name !== 'write_file' && tool.name !== 'edit_file') return tool;\n    const original = tool.run;\n    return {\n      ...tool,\n      run: async (input, ctx) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        if (!roots.some((root) => root === '' || rel === root || rel.startsWith(root.endsWith('/') ? root : root + '/'))) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the allowed roots (${roots.join(', ')}): ${rel}` };\n        }\n        return original(input, ctx);\n      },\n    };\n  });\n}\n",
 "kind": "FileEditorObservation"
}

### MessageEvent — role: `user` — source: `user` — id: `048e5630-eadd-4368-a3eb-71b3812fb5fa` — 2026-10-15T11:17:55.882326

```
TASK: Fix the delivery path so it can never destroy a file and still report success. Work on repo madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn.


BRANCH RULES
- Base your work on branch forge/company-deliver (PR #94). Push new commits to it, or open a PR stacked on it. Do not push to main. Do not merge anything.
- Do not touch secrets or tokens. Never print a token.


WHAT HAPPENED (evidence, verify it yourself)
- Delivery run produced PR #96 (closed, unmerged), branch forge/deliver-cd8f9eae-mv9fqrxp.
- Goal given: "Add a single line to the top of README.md ... (do not change anything else)".
- Result: README.md went +2 / -239. The file was cut off mid-word at "what it gets back, and what evidence accompa". The PR body said install, test and lint all PASSED.
- So the pipeline reported success on a destroyed file.


ROOT CAUSE
1. src/kernel/loop.ts, buildWorkspaceTools: the only mutation tool is write_file. It overwrites the whole file with whatever string the model returns. read_file has no cap, so the model read the full README, then retyped only about 400 characters of it into write_file.
2. src/company/role-tools.ts wraps write_file and only checks allowed path roots. It never compares old content with new.
3. scripts/deliver.ts, ROLE_SEQUENCE.implementer, literally instructs the model to "write_file with the corrected content".
4. src/company/deliver.ts only verifies that the diff is non-empty and that the target's test and lint pass. Neither check reads the README. Nothing checks that the diff matches the goal.
5. loop.ts verifyCompletion defaults to always OK.


REQUIRED CHANGES (do all of them)


A. Add an exact-anchor edit tool (src/kernel/loop.ts)
- New mutating tool edit_file. Input: {path, old_str, new_str}.
- old_str must occur exactly once in the current file. Zero matches or multiple matches: return ok:false with a clear message. Do not write.
- Use the existing resolveInWorkspace for path safety.
- Return the number of lines added and removed in the observation.


B. Stop whole-file overwrite of existing files
- write_file may only create files that do not exist yet.
- If the path exists, refuse with: "File exists. Use edit_file." Do not add a bypass flag.
- Make the same change in src/company/role-tools.ts so the wrapper stays consistent.


C. Fix the implementer instructions (scripts/deliver.ts)
- Change ROLE_SEQUENCE.implementer to: read_file, then edit_file with minimal anchors, then run_check "test", then finish.
- Say explicitly: never retype a whole file.


D. Add a shrink and size guard in deliver.ts
- After "git add -A", compute per-file stats against the base commit using "git diff --cached --numstat <commit>".
- Block delivery (status BLOCKED) when any modified existing file has deletions greater than additions plus 20 AND deletions above 30% of its original line count.
- Also block when the total deletions across the change exceed 5x total additions and exceed 50 lines.
- The block reason must name the file, additions, deletions and the original line count.
- Make the thresholds constants at the top of the file, with an optional override in DeliveryOptions.
- Run this check BEFORE the target's test and lint, and also record it in the report under "Checks" so it is visible.


E. Make "success" mean the goal was met, not just "builds"
- Add an optional DeliveryOptions.expect field. It holds a list of assertions the final diff must satisfy. Examples: {file:"README.md", addedLinesContain:"Verified by the Forge software company.", maxDeletions:0}.
- scripts/deliver.ts gets a matching --expect-file, --expect-contains and --max-deletions option.
- If an expectation is present and not met, status is BLOCKED.
- Pass a verifyCompletion into runCompany/the loop that refuses "finish" unless at least one edit_file call succeeded and run_check "test" passed after the last edit.


F. Detect truncated model output
- If ModelService exposes a finish reason or token-limit signal, treat length-truncated output as a failed attempt. Do not apply it.
- If it does not expose one, add a note to the report listing this as a known gap. Do not silently skip it.


G. Fix a security issue in .github/workflows/company-deliver.yml
- The step runs: npx tsx scripts/deliver.ts "${{ inputs.target_repo }}" "${{ inputs.goal }}". This interpolates input text directly into a shell command.
- Pass the inputs through env: variables (TARGET_REPO, GOAL) and reference them as "$TARGET_REPO" and "$GOAL".
- Also decode HTML entities such as &gt; in the goal before use. The #96 title shows the goal arrived as "&gt;".


TESTS (add to tests/, use real git and a real temp filesystem like tests/deliver.test.ts does)
1. edit_file: unique match edits correctly; zero matches rejected; two or more matches rejected; a file outside the workspace rejected.
2. write_file: creating a new file works; overwriting an existing file is refused.
3. REGRESSION for #96: seed a bare repo with a 242-line README. Use a scripted roster that tries to write a 400-character version of it. Assert the overwrite is refused. Then a second variant that gets around the tool but still shrinks the file: assert deliverChange returns BLOCKED with the shrink reason and that no branch exists on the remote.
4. Positive case: a scripted edit_file adds one line at the top of the 242-line README. Assert the diff is exactly +1 / -0, status COMPLETED, and the expect assertion passes.
5. expect: a change that violates maxDeletions:0 is BLOCKED.
6. All existing tests must still pass. Report the exact count (it was 220 passed / 0 failed on #94).


PROOF REQUIRED BEFORE YOU REPORT DONE
- Run npm run lint, npm run build and npm test. Paste the real counts.
- Re-run the exact #96 task through the real delivery workflow with a real model (not --scripted): add one line "> Verified by the Forge software company." to the top of README.md, do not change anything else. Run it with --expect-contains and --max-deletions 0.
- Show: the PR link, the diff stat, and the workflow run URL. The diff must be +1 / -0 on README.md only. Close that proof PR afterwards and say so.
- If the real-model run fails or is blocked, report that exactly. Do not claim success. A BLOCKED result is better than a bad PR.


REPORTING RULES
- Separate what you verified by running it from what you inferred.
- List every honest gap, including anything you could not test.
- Do not call something proven unless you executed it.
- Do not widen scope. Do not refactor unrelated code. Do not change the keyless/keyed model policy in this task.
- Note that the token exposed in the earlier workspace git remote (COORDINATION entry -04) still needs rotating by the owner. Do not handle that token.


DONE MEANS: all tests green, the +1/-0 README live proof shown with links, and the regression test that reproduces #96 now fails safe. so that's cloud opinion on what's going on now check it and tell me should should we implement an adopt this or not

**Adopt it — it's ~90% right and points at a real, reproduced defect.** But four of its items are wrong or stale, and if you implement them as written you'll build guards that don't fire and "fix" a bug that doesn't exist. So: adopt the *intent*, correct the *details*.

## The four corrections (this is the valuable part)

**1. Item F is unbuildable, and it targets the wrong bug.** `ModelResult` has no finish-reason field, so there is nothing to check — the spec even anticipates this. More importantly: #96 was **not** truncation. The model returned complete, valid JSON and *chose* to write a 400-char file. So truncation-detection would not have caught #96. The mechanism that *would* have caught it is B + D + A, which the spec also asks for. **Do F as the honest note only; don't pretend it's a guard.**

**2. Item G's `&gt;` claim is false.** I pulled PR #96's title: it reads `...README.md: '> Verified by the Forge software company.'` — the `>` arrived intact. Decoding HTML entities is unnecessary and slightly dangerous (it would corrupt any legitimate goal that genuinely contains `&gt;`). **Do the env-var passing (real shell-injection hardening); drop the entity decode.**

**3. Item D's thresholds don't fire on the worst case.** The rule `deletions > additions + 20 AND deletions > 30%` **misses a pure-deletion edit** (`additions = 0` → `0 > 0+20` is false → no block). That's exactly the destructive case. Use `deletions > additions` as the third clause. Also note D's whole-file-delete carve-out: spec says block "modified existing files" — deleting a file entirely is not "modified", so it escapes D (my existing guard deliberately allows intentional deletions). Worth stating explicitly so it's a decision, not an accident.

**4. That's probably fine, but it means "the pipeline can never destroy a file" is only true for the company path unless you also harden `agent/tools.ts`. Don't claim the broader guarantee.

Defaults to maxRuntimeMs. */\n  maxCallMs?: number;\n}\n\nexport type Authorization = (action: AgentAction, ctx: LoopContext) => { allowed: boolean; reason?: string };\n\nexport interface LoopResult {\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  steps: LoopStep[];\n  reason: string;\n}\n\nexport const FINISH_TOOL = 'finish';\n\nexport function loadLoopLimits(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): LoopLimits {\n  const int = (name: string, fallback: number, min: number, max: number) => {\n    const parsed = Number.parseInt(env[name] ?? '', 10);\n    if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;\n    return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, parsed));\n  };\n  return {\n    maxSteps: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_STEPS', 12, 1, 100),\n    maxRuntimeMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_RUNTIME_MS', 10 * 60 * 1000, 10_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n    maxCallMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_CALL_MS', 2 * 60 * 1000, 1_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n  };\n}\n\nasync function withDeadline<T>(promise: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {\n  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;\n  try {\n    return await Promise.race([\n      promise,\n      new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {\n        timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${label} exceeded its ${ms}ms deadline`)), ms);\n      }),\n    ]);\n  } finally {\n    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface RunLoopOptions {\n  goal: string;\n  tools: AgentTool[];\n  brain: AgentBrain;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  authorize?: Authorization;\n  workspace?: string;\n  memory?: string;\n  now?: () => number;\n  onStep?: (step: LoopStep) => void;\n  verifyCompletion?: (state: { goal: string; summary: string; history: LoopStep[] }) => { ok: boolean; reason?: string };\n}\n\nexport async function runAgentLoop(options: RunLoopOptions): Promise<LoopResult> {\n  const { goal, tools, brain, authorize, workspace = 'loop', memory } = options;\n  const limits = options.limits ?? loadLoopLimits();\n  const now = options.now ?? Date.now;\n  const startedAt = now();\n  const maxCallMs = limits.maxCallMs ?? limits.maxRuntimeMs;\n  const byName = new Map(tools.map((t) => [t.name, t]));\n  const catalog = tools.map((t) => ({ name: t.name, description: t.description }));\n  const steps: LoopStep[] = [];\n\n  for (let step = 1; step <= limits.maxSteps; step += 1) {\n    if (now() - startedAt > limits.maxRuntimeMs) {\n      return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached (${limits.maxRuntimeMs}ms); stopping safely.` };\n    }\n    const remaining = Math.max(1, limits.maxRuntimeMs - (now() - startedAt));\n    const deadlineMs = Math.min(maxCallMs, remaining);\n\n    let action: AgentAction;\n    try {\n      action = await withDeadline(brain({ goal, history: steps, tools: catalog, memory }), deadlineMs, 'Brain call');\n    } catch (err) {\n      const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      if (/deadline/.test(message)) {\n        return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached: ${message}; stopping safely.` };\n      }\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: `Brain failed: ${message}` };\n    }\n\n    if (!action || typeof action.tool !== 'string') {\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: 'Brain returned no usable action.' };\n    }\n\n    const ctx: LoopContext = { goal, workspace, step, deadlineMs };\n\n    if (action.tool === FINISH_TOOL) {\n      const summary = typeof action.input?.summary === 'string' ? action.input.summary : 'Goal reported complete.';\n      const verdict = options.verifyCompletion ? options.verifyCompletion({ goal, summary, history: steps }) : { ok: true };\n      if (verdict.ok) {\n        steps.push({ index: step, action, observation: { ok: true, output: summary } });\n        return { status: 'COMPLETED', steps, reason: summary };\n      }\n      const refused: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation: { ok: false, output: `Completion refused: ${verdict.reason ?? Reads and\n * writes go through the symlink-aware resolver; `run_check` is a bounded shell\n * runner restricted to an allowlist.\n */\nexport interface WorkspaceToolsOptions {\n  workspace: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  runner?: (command: string, cwd: string) => Promise<{ status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }>;\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_AUTHORIZED: Record<string, string> = {\n  test: 'npm test',\n  lint: 'npm run lint',\n};\n\nexport function buildWorkspaceTools(options: WorkspaceToolsOptions): AgentTool[] {\n  const { workspace, allowMutation = false } = options;\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? It is self-contained on purpose so Forge-the-company carries\n * its own engine and never depends on the Firstborn repository.\n *\n * Hardening carried over from the Firstborn review (PR #83):\n * - a per-call deadline, so a hung brain or tool cannot defeat the ceiling;\n * - an optional completion verifier, so `finish` is not automatically success;\n * - symlink-aware workspace containment for every file read and write.\n */\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, realpathSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\n\nexport interface ToolObservation {\n  ok: boolean;\n  output: string;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopContext {\n  goal: string;\n  workspace: string;\n  step: number;\n  deadlineMs?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentTool {\n  name: string;\n  description: string;\n  mutating?: boolean;\n  run(input: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: LoopContext): Promise<ToolObservation>;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentAction {\n  tool: string;\n  input?: Record<string, unknown>;\n}\n\nexport interface LoopStep {\n  index: number;\n  action: AgentAction;\n  observation: ToolObservation;\n}\n\nexport interface AgentBrainState {\n  goal: string;\n  history: LoopStep[];\n  tools: { name: string; description: string }[];\n  memory?: string;\n}\n\nexport type AgentBrain = (state: AgentBrainState) => Promise<AgentAction>;\n\nexport interface LoopLimits {\n  maxSteps: number;\n  maxRuntimeMs: number;\n  /** Ceiling (ms) for a single brain or tool call. Defaults to maxRuntimeMs. */\n  maxCallMs?: number;\n}\n\nexport type Authorization = (action: AgentAction, ctx: LoopContext) => { allowed: boolean; reason?: string };\n\nexport interface LoopResult {\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  steps: LoopStep[];\n  reason: string;\n}\n\nexport const FINISH_TOOL = 'finish';\n\nexport function loadLoopLimits(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): LoopLimits {\n  const int = (name: string, fallback: number, min: number, max: number) => {\n    const parsed = Number.parseInt(env[name] ?? '', 10);\n    if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;\n    return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, parsed));\n  };\n  return {\n    maxSteps: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_STEPS', 12, 1, 100),\n    maxRuntimeMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_RUNTIME_MS', 10 * 60 * 1000, 10_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n    maxCallMs: int('FORGE_LOOP_MAX_CALL_MS', 2 * 60 * 1000, 1_000, 60 * 60 * 1000),\n  };\n}\n\nasync function withDeadline<T>(promise: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {\n  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;\n  try {\n    return await Promise.race([\n      promise,\n      new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {\n        timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${label} exceeded its ${ms}ms deadline`)), ms);\n      }),\n    ]);\n  } finally {\n    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface RunLoopOptions {\n  goal: string;\n  tools: AgentTool[];\n  brain: AgentBrain;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  authorize?: Authorization;\n  workspace?: string;\n  memory?: string;\n  now?: () => number;\n  onStep?: (step: LoopStep) => void;\n  verifyCompletion?: (state: { goal: string; summary: string; history: LoopStep[] }) => { ok: boolean; reason?: string };\n}\n\nexport async function runAgentLoop(options: RunLoopOptions): Promise<LoopResult> {\n  const { goal, tools, brain, authorize, workspace = 'loop', memory } = options;\n  const limits = options.limits ?? loadLoopLimits();\n  const now = options.now ?? Date.now;\n  const startedAt = now();\n  const maxCallMs = limits.maxCallMs ?? limits.maxRuntimeMs;\n  const byName = new Map(tools.map((t) => [t.name, t]));\n  const catalog = tools.map((t) => ({ name: t.name, description: t.description }));\n  const steps: LoopStep[] = [];\n\n  for (let step = 1; step <= limits.maxSteps; step += 1) {\n    if (now() - startedAt > limits.maxRuntimeMs) {\n      return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached (${limits.maxRuntimeMs}ms); stopping safely.` };\n    }\n    const remaining = Math.max(1, limits.maxRuntimeMs - (now() - startedAt));\n    const deadlineMs = Math.min(maxCallMs, remaining);\n\n    let action: AgentAction;\n    try {\n      action = await withDeadline(brain({ goal, history: steps, tools: catalog, memory }), deadlineMs, 'Brain call');\n    } catch (err) {\n      const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      if (/deadline/.test(message)) {\n        return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Runtime ceiling reached: ${message}; stopping safely.` };\n      }\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: `Brain failed: ${message}` };\n    }\n\n    if (!action || typeof action.tool !== 'string') {\n      return { status: 'FAILED', steps, reason: 'Brain returned no usable action.' };\n    }\n\n    const ctx: LoopContext = { goal, workspace, step, deadlineMs };\n\n    if (action.tool === FINISH_TOOL) {\n      const summary = typeof action.input?.summary === 'string' ? action.input.summary : 'Goal reported complete.';\n      const verdict = options.verifyCompletion ? options.verifyCompletion({ goal, summary, history: steps }) : { ok: true };\n      if (verdict.ok) {\n        steps.push({ index: step, action, observation: { ok: true, output: summary } });\n        return { status: 'COMPLETED', steps, reason: summary };\n      }\n      const refused: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation: { ok: false, output: `Completion refused: ${verdict.reason ?? 'not permitted'}` } };\n        steps.push(s);\n        options.onStep?.(s);\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n\n    let observation: ToolObservation;\n    try {\n      observation = await withDeadline(tool.run(action.input ?? {}, ctx), deadlineMs, `Tool \"${action.tool}\"`);\n    } catch (err) {\n      observation = { ok: false, output: `Tool \"${action.tool}\" threw: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n    }\n    const s: LoopStep = { index: step, action, observation };\n    steps.push(s);\n    options.onStep?.(s);\n  }\n\n  return { status: 'BLOCKED', steps, reason: `Step ceiling reached (${limits.maxSteps}); stopping safely.` };\n}\n\n// --- Workspace-safe file tools ------------------------------------------------\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nexport function safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `rel` under `ws` and confirm the real path stays inside the workspace.\n * Lexical checks miss a symlink inside the workspace that points outside it, so\n * the target and its deepest existing ancestor are resolved through the real FS.\n */\nexport function resolveInWorkspace(ws: string, rel: string): string | null {\n  const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n  if (!safe) return null;\n  let root: string;\n  try {\n    root = realpathSync(ws);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const abs = path.join(root, safe);\n  const inside = (real: string) => real === root || real.startsWith(root + path.sep);\n\n  let probe = path.dirname(abs);\n  while (!existsSync(probe)) {\n    const next = path.dirname(probe);\n    if (next === probe) break;\n    probe = next;\n  }\n  try {\n    if (!inside(realpathSync(probe))) return null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  if (existsSync(abs)) {\n    try {\n      if (!inside(realpathSync(abs))) return null;\n    } catch {\n      return null;\n    }\n  }\n  return abs;\n}\n\n/**\n * A minimal, real, workspace-contained toolset every employee shares. DEFAULT_AUTHORIZED;\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read a file inside the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\"}. Input: {\"thought\":\"...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input) => ({ ok: true, output: `Noted: ${typeof input.thought === 'string' ? input.thought : '(empty)'}` }),\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'write_file',\n      description: 'Create a NEW file in the workspace. Input: {\"path\":\"...\",\"content\":\"...\"}. Refuses to overwrite an existing file — use edit_file for that. Mutating.',\n      mutating: true,\n      run: async (input) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        const content = typeof input.content === 'string' ? input.content : '';\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'write_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const abs = resolveInWorkspace(workspace, rel);\n        if (!abs) return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the workspace: ${rel}` };\n        if (existsSync(abs)) return { ok: false, output: `File exists. Use edit_file.` };\n        try {\n          mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });\n          writeFileSync(abs, content);\n          return { ok: true, output: `Wrote ${content.length} byte(s) to ${rel}.` };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Write failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    });\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description: 'Replace a unique snippet in an existing file. value : '';\n}\n\nconst MAX_FILE_BYTES = 200_000;\nconst MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 200;\nconst MAX_SCAN_FILES = 2_000;\n\n/** Resolve a real workspace directory, or null when the loop has none. */\nfunction workspaceDir(ws: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!ws) return null;\n  try {\n    if (existsSync(ws) && statSync(ws).isDirectory()) return ws;\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** Reject paths that escape the workspace (absolute or `..` traversal). */\nfunction safeRelative(rel: string): string | null {\n  if (!rel) return null;\n  if (path.isAbsolute(rel)) return null;\n  const normalized = path.normalize(rel);\n  if (normalized.startsWith('..') || normalized.includes(`..${path.sep}`)) return null;\n  return normalized;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve `rel` under `ws` and confirm the result stays inside the workspace.\n * Lexical checks alone cannot catch a symlink inside the workspace that points\n * outside it, so the parent directory is resolved through the real filesystem.\n * Returns the absolute path, or null when the target escapes or cannot be\n * resolved safely.\n */\nfunction resolveInWorkspace(ws: string, rel: string): string | null {\n  const safe = safeRelative(rel);\n  if (!safe) return null;\n  let root: string;\n  try {\n    root = realpathSync(ws);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const abs = path.join(root, safe);\n\n  const inside = (real: string) => real === root || real.startsWith(root + path.sep);\n\n  // The deepest existing ancestor is the only part that can contain a symlink;\n  // realpath resolves every symlinked component along the way. Mutating tools are enabled only when `allowMutation` is\n * true; otherwise they are omitted so the brain cannot even see a state-changing\n * capability it is not permitted to use.\n */\nexport function buildForgeTools(options: {\n  owner: string;\n  repo: string;\n  ref?: string;\n  token?: string;\n  allowMutation?: boolean;\n  /** Absolute path to the mission workspace, when one exists. */\n  workspace?: string;\n  /** Include the real-browser tools (open/view/click/type/scroll/extract/close). */\n  allowBrowser?: boolean;\n}): AgentTool[] {\n  const github = new GitHubService(options.token);\n  const runner = new TestRunnerService();\n  const ref = options.ref ?? 'main';\n  const ws = workspaceDir(options.workspace);\n\n  const readRepoFile = async (rel: string): Promise<string | null> => {\n    if (ws) {\n      const abs = resolveInWorkspace(ws, rel);\n      if (!abs) return null;\n      try {\n        if (existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isFile()) return readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');\n      } catch {\n        /* fall through to GitHub */\n      }\n    }\n    const file = await github.fetchFile(options.owner, options.repo, rel, ref);\n    return file ? file.content : null;\n  };\n\n  const listPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => {\n    if (ws) return walkFiles(ws);\n    return github.listRepositoryFiles(options.owner, options.repo, ref);\n  };\n\n  const tools: AgentTool[] = [\n    {\n      name: 'list_files',\n      description: 'List repository file paths (recursive). Read-only.',\n      run: async (): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const files = await listPaths();\n        if (files.length === 0) return { ok: false, output: 'No files found.' };\n        const shown = files.slice(0, 80);\n        return { ok: true, output: `${files.length} files total. First ${shown.length}:\\n${shown.join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'read_file',\n      description: 'Read one file by exact repository path. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const rel = str(input, 'path');\n        if (!rel) return { ok: false, output: 'read_file requires a \"path\".' };\n        const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n        if (content === null) return { ok: false, output: `File not found: ${rel}` };\n        return { ok: true, output: content.slice(0, MAX_FILE_BYTES) };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'search',\n      description:\n        'Search file contents by regular expression (like grep). Input: {\"pattern\":\"...\", \"glob\":\"*.ts\" (optional)}. Returns matching file:line: text. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const pattern = str(input, 'pattern');\n        if (!pattern) return { ok: false, output: 'search requires a \"pattern\" (regular expression).' };\n        let re: RegExp;\n        try {\n          re = new RegExp(pattern, 'i');\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Invalid pattern: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        }\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        const matcher = glob && !matchesAll(glob) ? globToRegExp(glob) : null;\n        const paths = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        const matches: string[] = [];\n        let scanned = 0;\n        for (const rel of paths) {\n          if (matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES || scanned >= MAX_SCAN_FILES) break;\n          scanned += 1;\n          const content = await readRepoFile(rel);\n          if (content === null) continue;\n          const lines = content.split('\\n');\n          for (let i = 0; i < lines.length && matches.length < MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES; i += 1) {\n            if (re.test(lines[i])) matches.push(`${rel}:${i + 1}: ${lines[i].trim().slice(0, 200)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No matches for /${pattern}/ in ${paths.length} file(s).` };\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          output: `${matches.length} match(es)${matches.length >= MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES ? ' (capped)' : ''}:\\n${matches.join('\\n')}`,\n        };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'find_files',\n      description:\n        'Find files by glob pattern, e.g. {\"glob\":\"src/**/*.ts\"} or {\"glob\":\"*.json\"}. Returns matching paths. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const glob = str(input, 'glob');\n        if (!glob) return { ok: false, output: 'find_files requires a \"glob\".' };\n        const matcher = matchesAll(glob) ? null : globToRegExp(glob);\n        const matches = (await listPaths()).filter((p) => (matcher ? matcher.test(p) : true));\n        if (matches.length === 0) return { ok: true, output: `No files match ${glob}.` };\n        return { ok: true, output: `${matches.length} file(s):\\n${matches.slice(0, 100).join('\\n')}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'think',\n      description:\n        'Record a reasoning step without changing anything (use to plan before acting). Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const thought = str(input, 'thought');\n        if (!thought) return { ok: false, output: 'think requires a \"thought\".' };\n        return { ok: true, output: `Noted: ${thought.slice(0, 1000)}` };\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'fetch_url',\n      description:\n        'Fetch the text of an http(s) URL (e.g. docs, a raw file). Input: {\"url\":\"https://...\"}. Read-only.',\n      run: async (input): Promise<ToolObservation> => {\n        const url = str(input, 'url');\n        if (!/^https?:\\/\\//i.test(url)) return { ok: false, output: 'fetch_url requires an http(s) \"url\".' };\n        const controller = new AbortController();\n        const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15_000);\n        try {\n          const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, headers: { 'user-agent': 'forge-agent' } });\n          const text = await res.text();\n          return { ok: res.ok, output: `HTTP ${res.status}\\n${text.slice(0, 20_000)}` };\n        } catch (error) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Fetch failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` };\n        } finally {\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n  ];\n\n  if (options.allowMutation) {\n    tools.push({\n      name: 'edit_file',\n      description:\n        'Apply exact-anchor edits to a file. 'up' : 'down';\n        try {\n          return { ok: true, output: renderSnapshot(await browser.scroll(direction)) };\n        } catch (err) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `browser_scroll failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: 'browser_extract',\n      description: 'Return the visible text of the current page, optionally only sentences matching a regex. Requires GITHUB_TOKEN with `repo` scope (contents + pull requests).\n */\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { ModelService } from '../src/company/model.ts';\nimport { modelBrain } from '../src/company/brains.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport { deliverChange, type PullRequestOpener } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { fetchRepoContext } from '../src/company/repo-context.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\n\nconst TOKEN = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN || '';\nconst repoPattern = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/;\n\n/** The one tool sequence each role follows, so the model executes rather than wanders. */\nconst ROLE_SEQUENCE: Record<string, string[]> = {\n  pm: ['finish with your requirements artifact (data.items = acceptance criteria)'],\n  architect: ['read_file on the files named in the goal', 'finish with your design artifact (data.design, data.files)'],\n  implementer: ['read_file on each file you will change', 'write_file with the corrected content', 'run_check the \"test\" command', 'finish with your change artifact'],\n  reviewer: ['read_file on the changed file', 'finish with your review artifact (data.blockers = number)'],\n  qa: ['run_check the \"test\" command', 'run_check the \"lint\" command', 'finish with your evidence artifact'],\n  security: ['read_file on the changed file', 'finish with your security artifact (data.clean = boolean)'],\n  release: ['finish with your decision artifact (data.ship = boolean)'],\n};\n\nfunction modelRoster(model: ModelService, workspaceDir: string): (item: { id: string; title: string }, attempt: number) => Role[] {\n  return (_item, attempt) =>\n    DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n      id: r.id,\n      title: r.title,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      authority: r.authority,\n      consumes: r.consumes,\n      produces: r.produces,\n      tools: buildRoleTools({\n        workspaceDir,\n        canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write',\n        allowedRoots: [''],\n      }),\n      brain: modelBrain(model, {\n        role: `${r.title} (attempt ${attempt})`,\n        mandate: r.mandate,\n        sequence: ROLE_SEQUENCE[r.id],\n        artifactHint: `Emit your \"${r.produces}\" artifact in data.`,\n      }),\n    }));\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster for offline plumbing tests (`--scripted`). The\n * implementer makes a trivial, verifiable edit and QA records the check it\n * really ran; the rest of the roster is evidence-only. It proves the delivery\n * path (clone → team → checks → branch → push → PR) without needing model keys.\n */\nfunction scriptedRoster(workspaceDir: string): (item: { id: string; title: string }, attempt: number) => Role[] {\n  const EDIT_PATH = 'FORGE-DELIVERY-PROBE.md';\n  const content = `# Forge delivery probe\\n\\nThis file was written by the Forge software company to prove the delivery path end to end.\\n`;\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const scripts: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n      implementer: [\n        { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: EDIT_PATH, content } },\n        { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'wrote the probe file', data: { files: { [EDIT_PATH]: content } } } },\n      ],\n      qa: [\n        { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n        { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'lint' } },\n        { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the checks', data: {} } },\n      ],\n      security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes', data: { clean: true } } }],\n      reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n      release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n      pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: probe the path', data: { items: ['probe file exists'] } } }],\n      architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'add one file', data: { files: [EDIT_PATH] } } }],\n    };\n    const script = scripts[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return () =>\n    DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n      id: r.id,\n      title: r.title,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      authority: r.authority,\n      consumes: r.consumes,\n      produces: r.produces,\n      tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write', allowedRoots: [''] }),\n      brain: brain(r.id),\n    }));\n}\n\nconst openPr: PullRequestOpener = async ({ target, head, base, title, body, token }) => {\n  const res = await fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${target}/pulls`, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'User-Agent': 'forge-company-deliver' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ title, head, base, body }),\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub PR API ${res.status}: ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 200)}`);\n  const data = (await res.json()) as { html_url: string; number: number };\n  return { url: data.html_url, number: data.number };\n};\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const args = process.argv.slice(2);\n  const scripted = args.includes('--scripted');\n  const positional = args.filter((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));\n  const target = (positional[0] || '').trim();\n  const goal = positional.slice(1).join(' ').trim() || 'Address the audit findings.';\n  if (!repoPattern.test(target) || target.includes('..')) {\n    console.error('usage: npm run deliver -- [--scripted] owner/repo \"goal\"');\n    process.exitCode = 2;\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const ctx = await fetchRepoContext(target);\n  console.log(`[deliver] ${ctx.target} @ ${ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}; goal: ${goal}`);\n\n  const model = scripted ? null : new ModelService();\n  if (model) {\n    const info = model.getProviderInfo();\n    console.log(`[deliver] model: ${info.primaryProvider}; Gemini fallback configured: ${info.fallbackConfigured}`);\n  } else {\n    console.log('[deliver] scripted roster (deterministic; proves the delivery path, not model quality)');\n  }\n\n  const workspaceDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'forge-deliver-'));\n  const branch = `forge/deliver-${ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}-${Date.now().toString(36)}`;\n\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: ctx.target,\n    goal,\n    commit: ctx.commit,\n    branch,\n    workspaceDir,\n    token: TOKEN,\n    rosterFor: model ? modelRoster(model, workspaceDir) : scriptedRoster(workspaceDir),\n    attemptsPerItem: Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_ATTEMPTS ?? '', 10) || 1),\n    push: process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_PUSH !== 'false',\n    openPr,\n  });\n\n  const outDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-delivery.json'), JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-delivery.md'), result.markdown + '\\n');\n\n  console.log('\\n--- COMPANY DELIVERY REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Status:', result.status, '|', result.reason);\n  console.log('Branch:', result.branch, '| head:', result.headCommit ?? '(none)');\n  console.log('Changed files:', result.changedFiles.join(', ') || '(none)');\n  for (const c of result.checks) console.log(`- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`);\n  if (result.prUrl) console.log('PR:', result.prUrl);\n  console.log('\\n' + result.markdown);\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error('[forge-company deliver] failed:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

((g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }]),\n    rosterFor: options.rosterFor,\n    attemptsPerItem: options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2,\n    maxRoleRuns: options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40,\n    limits: options.limits,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    changes: {},\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({\n      ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0,\n      reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'the team produced no change',\n    }),\n  });\n\n  // 4. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Omit to consider every changed file. */\n  file?: string;\n  /** Added lines must contain this substring somewhere in the diff. */\n  addedLinesContain?: string;\n  /** Fail if any changed file deletes more than this many lines. */\n  maxDeletions?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against.  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Omit to consider every changed file. */\n  file?: string;\n  /** Added lines must contain this substring somewhere in the diff. */\n  addedLinesContain?: string;\n  /** Fail if any changed file deletes more than this many lines. */\n  maxDeletions?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against. Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Override the clone/push URL (tests point this at a local bare repo). */\n  remoteUrl?: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks. Defaults to its package.json test/lint scripts. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Assertions the final diff must satisfy for the run to count as success. */\n  expect?: DeliveryExpectation[];\n  /** Override the shrink-guard thresholds (tests use this to force a trip). */\n  thresholds?: {\n    minDeletions?: number;\n    deletionRatio?: number;\n    additionMargin?: number;\n    totalMinDeletions?: number;\n    totalDeletionMultiple?: number;\n  };\n  /** Findings this run set out to fix (carried into the report and the PR body). */\n  findings?: AuditFinding[];\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  /** How each expectation was judged, so the report shows the goal was checked. */\n  expected: { assertion: string; met: boolean; detail: string }[];\n  /** Known limitations of this run that no check can cover. */\n  gaps: string[];\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ??
