 "old_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Omit to consider every changed file. */\n  file?: string;\n  /** Added lines must contain this substring somewhere in the diff. */\n  addedLinesContain?: string;\n  /** Fail if any changed file deletes more than this many lines. */\n  maxDeletions?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against. Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Override the clone/push URL (tests point this at a local bare repo). */\n  remoteUrl?: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks. Defaults to its package.json test/lint scripts. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Assertions the final diff must satisfy for the run to count as success. */\n  expect?: DeliveryExpectation[];\n  /** Override the shrink-guard thresholds (tests use this to force a trip). */\n  thresholds?: {\n    minDeletions?: number;\n    deletionRatio?: number;\n    additionMargin?: number;\n    totalMinDeletions?: number;\n    totalDeletionMultiple?: number;\n  };\n  /** Findings this run set out to fix (carried into the report and the PR body). */\n  findings?: AuditFinding[];\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  /** How each expectation was judged, so the report shows the goal was checked. */\n  expected: { assertion: string; met: boolean; detail: string }[];\n  /** Known limitations of this run that no check can cover. */\n  gaps: string[];\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ?? '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length ? r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.prUrl ? If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks.  "old_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Omit to consider every changed file. */\n  file?: string;\n  /** Added lines must contain this substring somewhere in the diff. */\n  addedLinesContain?: string;\n  /** Fail if any changed file deletes more than this many lines. */\n  maxDeletions?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against. Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Override the clone/push URL (tests point this at a local bare repo). */\n  remoteUrl?: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks. Defaults to its package.json test/lint scripts. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Assertions the final diff must satisfy for the run to count as success. */\n  expect?: DeliveryExpectation[];\n  /** Override the shrink-guard thresholds (tests use this to force a trip). */\n  thresholds?: {\n    minDeletions?: number;\n    deletionRatio?: number;\n    additionMargin?: number;\n    totalMinDeletions?: number;\n    totalDeletionMultiple?: number;\n  };\n  /** Findings this run set out to fix (carried into the report and the PR body). */\n  findings?: AuditFinding[];\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  /** How each expectation was judged, so the report shows the goal was checked. */\n  expected: { assertion: string; met: boolean; detail: string }[];\n  /** Known limitations of this run that no check can cover. */\n  gaps: string[];\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ??  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Override the clone/push URL (tests point this at a local bare repo). */\n  remoteUrl?: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks. Defaults to its package.json test/lint scripts. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Assertions the final diff must satisfy for the run to count as success. */\n  expect?: DeliveryExpectation[];\n  /** Override the shrink-guard thresholds (tests use this to force a trip). */\n  thresholds?: {\n    minDeletions?: number;\n    deletionRatio?: number;\n    additionMargin?: number;\n    totalMinDeletions?: number;\n    totalDeletionMultiple?: number;\n  };\n  /** Findings this run set out to fix (carried into the report and the PR body). */\n  findings?: AuditFinding[];\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  /** How each expectation was judged, so the report shows the goal was checked. */\n  expected: { assertion: string; met: boolean; detail: string }[];\n  /** Known limitations of this run that no check can cover. */\n  gaps: string[];\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ?? '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length ? r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.expected.length\n      ? [\n          '',\n          '## Goal assertions (what \"success\" required)',\n          ...r.expected.map((e) => `- ${e.met ? 'MET' : 'NOT MET'} — ${e.assertion}: ${e.detail}`),\n        ]\n      : []),\n    ...(r.gaps.length ? ['', '## Known gaps', ...r.gaps.map((g) => `- ${g}`)] : []),\n    ...(r.prUrl ? ['', `## Pull request`, `- ${r.prUrl}`] : []),\n    '',\n    '## Guarantees',\n    '- The change was committed to an isolated `forge/` branch, never to the base branch.',\n    '- The pull request is opened, never merged.',\n    '- The run is BLOCKED unless there was a real diff, the goal assertions were met, and every available check passed.',\n  ];\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n\nexport async function deliverChange(options: DeliveryOptions): Promise<DeliveryResult> {\n  const git = options.git ?? realGit();\n  const baseBranch = options.baseBranch ?? 'main';\n  const push = options.push ?? true;\n  const findings = options.findings ?? [];\n  const expect = options.expect ?? [];\n  const t = {\n    minDeletions: options.thresholds?.minDeletions ?? SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN,\n    totalMinDeletions: options.thresholds?.totalMinDeletions ?? TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS,\n    totalDeletionMultiple: options.thresholds?.totalDeletionMultiple ?? TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE,\n  };\n\n  const base: DeliveryResult = {\n    target: options.target,\n    baseBranch,\n    baseCommit: options.commit,\n    branch: options.branch,\n    headCommit: null,\n    status: 'BLOCKED',\n    reason: '',\n    changedFiles: [],\n    checks: [],\n    expected: [],\n    gaps: [\n      'Truncated model output cannot be detected: ModelResult exposes no finish reason or token-limit signal, so an output cut off at the token limit is treated as a complete action.',\n    ],\n    findings,\n    markdown: '',\n  };\n  const finish = (partial: Partial<DeliveryResult>): DeliveryResult => {\n    const merged = { ...base, ...partial };\n    return { ...merged, markdown: renderDeliveryMarkdown(merged) };\n  };\n\n  if (!options.branch.startsWith('forge/')) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to use branch \"${options.branch}\"; delivery branches must start with \"forge/\"` });\n  }\n  if (options.branch === baseBranch) {\n    return finish({ reason: `refusing to deliver to the base branch \"${baseBranch}\"` });\n  }\n  if (!options.token) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'no token supplied; cannot clone, push, or open a pull request' });\n  }\n\n  // 1. Clone the target pinned at the audited commit.\n  const dir = options.workspaceDir;\n  const url = options.remoteUrl ?? authedUrl(options.target, options.token);\n  const init = await git.run(['init', '-q', dir]);\n  if (init.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git init failed: ${redact(init.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['remote', 'add', 'origin', url], dir);\n  const fetch = await git.run(['fetch', '--depth', '1', 'origin', options.commit], dir);\n  if (fetch.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `could not fetch ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}: ${redact(fetch.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  const checkout = await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '--detach', 'FETCH_HEAD'], dir);\n  if (checkout.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `checkout of the audited commit failed: ${redact(checkout.stderr, options.token).trim()}` });\n  await git.run(['checkout', '-q', '-b', options.branch], dir);\n\n  // Commits need an identity; use the agent's, never the operator's.\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.name', 'openhands'], dir);\n  await git.run(['config', 'user.email', 'openhands@all-hands.dev'], dir);\n\n  // 2. What checks may we run? Only the target's own.\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir);\n  if (!Object.keys(authorized).length) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'the target declares no test or lint script, so no change can be verified; refusing to push unverified work' });\n  }\n\n  // Prepare dependencies before the team works, so QA can run the target's real\n  // checks during the run. Only install when the target declares dependencies; a\n  // lockfile-less install on a dependency-free target would add files to the diff.\n  const checks: DeliveryResult['checks'] = [];\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  let hasDeps = false;\n  if (existsSync(pkgPath)) {\n    try {\n      const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { dependencies?: Record<string, string>; devDependencies?: Record<string, string> };\n      hasDeps = Object.keys(pkg.dependencies ?? {}).length > 0 || Object.keys(pkg.devDependencies ?? {}).length > 0;\n    } catch {\n      hasDeps = false;\n    }\n  }\n  if (hasDeps) {\n    let installCmd = existsSync(path.join(dir, 'package-lock.json')) ? Retry once and record which\n    // command actually worked, rather than failing a target that its own team\n    // can still test.\n    if (installResult.status === 'FAILED' && /ERESOLVE|peer dep|Conflicting peer/i.test(installResult.output)) {\n      installCmd = `${installCmd} --legacy-peer-deps`;\n      installResult = await runCommand(installCmd, dir);\n    }\n    if (installResult.status === 'FAILED') {\n      checks.push({ name: 'install', status: 'FAILED', output: redact(installResult.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `dependency install failed: ${installResult.output.split('\\n')[0] ?? Run the implementation team inside the clone.\n  const company = await runCompany({\n    goal: options.goal,\n    plan: options.plan ?? ((g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }]),\n    rosterFor: options.rosterFor,\n    attemptsPerItem: options.attemptsPerItem ?? 2,\n    maxRoleRuns: options.maxRoleRuns ?? 40,\n    limits: options.limits,\n    workspaceDir: dir,\n    changes: {},\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({\n      ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0,\n      reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'the team produced no change',\n    }),\n  });\n\n  // 4. '' : '\\n'}node_modules/\\n`);\n      }\n    } catch {\n      /* best effort; the commit step will surface a real failure */\n    }\n  }\n  const add = await git.run(['add', '-A'], dir);\n  if (add.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git add failed: ${redact(add.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, checks });\n  const diff = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--name-only', options.commit], dir);\n  const changedFiles = diff.stdout.split('\\n').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);\n  if (!changedFiles.length) {\n    return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `no change was produced (company: ${company.reason})`, checks });\n  }\n\n  // A free model that reads a file and writes back only a fragment silently\n  // deletes the rest. This guard runs before the target's\n  // checks and blocks any change that shrinks an existing file or the change as a\n  // whole. Whole-file deletions (a clear intent) are left to the checks.\n  const numstat = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--numstat', options.commit], dir);\n  const stats: { file: string; added: number; deleted: number; originalLines: number }[] = [];\n  for (const line of numstat.stdout.split('\\n')) {\n    const [addedRaw, deletedRaw, ...rest] = line.split('\\t');\n    const file = rest.join('\\t');\n    if (!file || addedRaw === '-' || deletedRaw === '-') continue;\n    const abs = path.join(dir, file);\n    if (!existsSync(abs)) continue; // a whole-file deletion; not a \"modification\"\n    const original = await git.run(['show', `${options.commit}:${file}`], dir);\n    const originalLines = original.code === 0 ? original.stdout.split('\\n').length : 0;\n    stats.push({ file, added: Number(addedRaw), deleted: Number(deletedRaw), originalLines });\n  }\n\n  const shrinkViolations: string[] = [];\n  let totalAdded = 0;\n  let totalDeleted = 0;\n  for (const s of stats) {\n    totalAdded += s.added;\n    totalDeleted += s.deleted;\n    if (s.deleted > s.added + t.additionMargin && s.deleted > t.deletionRatio * s.originalLines && s.deleted > t.minDeletions) {\n      shrinkViolations.push(`${s.file} (+${s.added}/-${s.deleted} of ${s.originalLines} original line(s))`);\n    }\n  }\n  const totalShrunk = totalDeleted > t.totalDeletionMultiple * totalAdded && totalDeleted > t.totalMinDeletions;\n  if (shrinkViolations.length || totalShrunk) {\n    const detail = shrinkViolations.length\n      ? `files: ${shrinkViolations.join(', ')}`\n      : `the change deletes ${totalDeleted} line(s) and adds ${totalAdded} in total`;\n    checks.push({ name: 'shrink-guard', status: 'FAILED', output: detail });\n    return finish({\n      status: 'BLOCKED',\n      reason: `refusing a change that destroys existing content (${detail}); a partial read can silently gut a file`,\n      changedFiles,\n      checks,\n    });\n  }\n  checks.push({ name: 'shrink-guard', status: 'PASSED', output: `${stats.length} modified file(s); no file shrinks beyond the guard` });\n\n  // 5. '' : diffText;\n    return chunk\n      .split('\\n')\n      .filter((l) => l.startsWith('+') && !l.startsWith('+++'))\n      .join('\\n');\n  };\n  for (const e of expect) {\n    const label = [e.file ? `file=${e.file}` : 'any file', e.addedLinesContain ? `added~=\"${e.addedLinesContain}\"` : '', e.maxDeletions !== undefined ? `maxDeletions=${e.maxDeletions}` : '']\n      .filter(Boolean)\n      .join(' ');\n    let met = true;\n    let detail = 'ok';\n    if (e.addedLinesContain !== undefined) {\n      const added = addedLinesFor(e.file);\n      met = added.includes(e.addedLinesContain);\n      detail = met ? `added lines contain ${JSON.stringify(e.addedLinesContain)}` : `added lines do not contain ${JSON.stringify(e.addedLinesContain)}`;\n    }\n    if (met && e.maxDeletions !== undefined) {\n      const considered = e.file ? stats.filter((s) => s.file === e.file) : stats;\n      const worst = considered.reduce((m, s) => Math.max(m, s.deleted), 0);\n      met = worst <= e.maxDeletions;\n      detail = met ? `max deletions ${worst} <= ${e.maxDeletions}` : `deletes ${worst} line(s), over the allowed ${e.maxDeletions}`;\n    }\n    expected.push({ assertion: label, met, detail });\n  }\n  const unmet = expected.filter((e) => !e.met);\n  if (unmet.length) {\n    checks.push({ name: 'expect', status: 'FAILED', output: unmet.map((e) => `${e.assertion}: ${e.detail}`).join('; ') });\n    return finish({\n      status: 'BLOCKED',\n      reason: `the change does not meet the goal assertion(s): ${unmet.map((e) => `${e.assertion} (${e.detail})`).join('; ')}`,\n      changedFiles,\n      checks,\n      expected,\n    });\n  }\n  if (expected.length) checks.push({ name: 'expect', status: 'PASSED', output: `${expected.length} assertion(s) met` });\n\n  // 6. Run the target's real checks. A failing check stops delivery.\n  for (const name of Object.keys(authorized)) {\n    const res = await runCommand(authorized[name], dir);\n    checks.push({ name, status: res.status, output: redact(res.output, options.token).slice(0, 2000) });\n    if (res.status === 'FAILED') {\n      return finish({ status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `check \"${name}\" failed; refusing to push a broken change`, changedFiles, checks });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 6. Commit and push an isolated branch.\n  const message = `forge: ${options.goal}\\n\\nProposed by the Forge software company from an audit of ${options.target} at ${options.commit.slice(0, 8)}.\\n\\nCo-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev>`;\n  const commit = await git.run(['commit', '-q', '-m', message], dir);\n  if (commit.code !== 0) return finish({ reason: `git commit failed: ${redact(commit.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, changedFiles, checks });\n  const head = await git.run(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], dir);\n  const headCommit = head.stdout.trim();\n\n  if (!push) {\n    return finish({ status: 'COMPLETED', reason: 'built and verified locally (push disabled)', headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  const pushResult = await git.run(['push', 'origin', `HEAD:refs/heads/${options.branch}`], dir);\n  if (pushResult.code !== 0) {\n    return finish({ reason: `git push failed: ${redact(pushResult.stderr, options.token).trim()}`, headCommit, changedFiles, checks });\n  }\n\n  // 7.  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Omit to consider every changed file. */\n  file?: string;\n  /** Added lines must contain this substring somewhere in the diff. */\n  addedLinesContain?: string;\n  /** Fail if any changed file deletes more than this many lines. */\n  maxDeletions?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against. Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Override the clone/push URL (tests point this at a local bare repo). */\n  remoteUrl?: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. /**
 * Bind the implementer's "finish" to real evidence: it may only finish once an
 * edit_file actually changed a file and the target's "test" check passed after
 * that edit. A stub that merely claims completion is refused.
 */
function withEvidenceGate(rosterFor: DeliveryOptions['rosterFor']): DeliveryOptions['rosterFor'] {

          if (!testAfter) return { ok: false, reason: 'run the "test" check after your last edit before finishing' };

        },
      };
    });
}

original.stdout.split('\\n').length : 0;\n    stats.push({ file, added: Number(addedRaw), deleted: Number(deletedRaw), originalLines });\n  }\n\n  const shrinkViolations: string[] = [];\n  let totalAdded = 0;\n  let totalDeleted = 0;\n  for (const s of stats) {\n    totalAdded += s.added;\n    totalDeleted += s.deleted;\n    if (s.deleted > s.added + t.additionMargin && s.deleted > t.deletionRatio * s.originalLines && s.deleted > t.minDeletions) {\n      shrinkViolations.push(`${s.file} (+${s.added}/-${s.deleted} of ${s.originalLines} original line(s))`);\n    }\n  }\n  const totalShrunk = totalDeleted > t.totalDeletionMultiple * totalAdded && totalDeleted > t.totalMinDeletions;\n  if (shrinkViolations.length || totalShrunk) {\n    const detail = shrinkViolations.length\n      ?  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Override the clone/push URL (tests point this at a local bare repo). */\n  remoteUrl?: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks. Defaults to its package.json test/lint scripts. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Assertions the final diff must satisfy for the run to count as success. */\n  expect?: DeliveryExpectation[];\n  /** Override the shrink-guard thresholds (tests use this to force a trip). */\n  thresholds?: {\n    minDeletions?: number;\n    deletionRatio?: number;\n    additionMargin?: number;\n    totalMinDeletions?: number;\n    totalDeletionMultiple?: number;\n  };\n  /** Findings this run set out to fix (carried into the report and the PR body). */\n  findings?: AuditFinding[];\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  /** How each expectation was judged, so the report shows the goal was checked. */\n  expected: { assertion: string; met: boolean; detail: string }[];\n  /** Known limitations of this run that no check can cover. */\n  gaps: string[];\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length ? r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.expected.length\n      ? [\n          '',\n          '## Goal assertions (what \"success\" required)',\n          ...r.expected.map((e) => `- ${e.met ? 'MET' : 'NOT MET'} — ${e.assertion}: ${e.detail}`),\n        ]\n      : []),\n    ...(r.gaps.length ? ['', '## Known gaps', ...r.gaps.map((g) => `- ${g}`)] : []),\n    ...(r.prUrl ? A stub that merely claims completion is\n * refused, and the loop gives the role another turn instead.\n */\nfunction withEvidenceGate(rosterFor: DeliveryOptions['rosterFor']): DeliveryOptions['rosterFor'] {\n  return (item, attempt) =>\n    rosterFor(item, attempt).map((role) => {\n      if (role.id !== 'implementer' || role.verifyCompletion) return role;\n      return {\n        ...role,\n        verifyCompletion: ({ history }: { history: LoopStep[] }) => {\n          const mutations = history.filter((h) => (h.action.tool === 'edit_file' || h.action.tool === 'write_file') && h.observation.ok);\n          if (!mutations.length) return { ok: false, reason: 'no file was actually changed yet; make the change before finishing' };\n          const lastMutation = mutations[mutations.length - 1].index;\n          const testAfter = history.some(\n            (h) => h.action.tool === 'run_check' && h.action.input?.command === 'test' && h.observation.ok && h.index > lastMutation,\n          );\n          if (!testAfter) return { ok: false, reason: 'run the \"test\" check after your last change, then finish' };\n          return { ok: true };\n        },\n      };\n    });\n}\n\nexport async function deliverChange(options: DeliveryOptions): Promise<DeliveryResult> {\n  const git = options.git ?? realGit();\n  const baseBranch = options.baseBranch ?? 'main';\n  const push = options.push ?? true;\n  const findings = options.findings ?? [];\n  const expect = options.expect ?? [];\n  const t = {\n    minDeletions: options.thresholds?.minDeletions ??  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means.  "old_content": "/**\n * forge-company deliver CLI — audit a target, then deliver a verified fix.\n *\n *   npm run deliver -- <owner/repo> \"goal\"\n *\n * Read the target, run the software company's implementation team inside a clone\n * pinned at the audited commit, run the target's own checks, and open a pull\n * request on an isolated `forge/` branch. It never merges and never touches the\n * base branch. Requires GITHUB_TOKEN with `repo` scope (contents + pull requests).\n */\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { ModelService } from '../src/company/model.ts';\nimport { modelBrain } from '../src/company/brains.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport { deliverChange, type PullRequestOpener, type DeliveryExpectation } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { fetchRepoContext } from '../src/company/repo-context.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\n\nconst TOKEN = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN || '';\nconst repoPattern = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/;\n\n/** The one tool sequence each role follows, so the model executes rather than wanders. */\nconst ROLE_SEQUENCE: Record<string, string[]> = {\n  pm: ['finish with your requirements artifact (data.items = acceptance criteria)'],\n  architect: ['read_file on the files named in the goal', 'finish with your design artifact (data.design, data.files)'],\n  implementer: [\n    'read_file on each file you will change',\n    'edit_file with minimal anchors: old_str is a small unique snippet copied exactly from what you read, new_str is the replacement',\n    'never retype a whole file — you may only have seen part of it',\n    'run_check the \"test\" command',\n    'finish with your change artifact',\n  ],\n  reviewer: ['read_file on the changed file', 'finish with your review artifact (data.blockers = number)'],\n  qa: ['run_check the \"test\" command', 'run_check the \"lint\" command', 'finish with your evidence artifact'],\n  security: ['read_file on the changed file', 'finish with your security artifact (data.clean = boolean)'],\n  release: ['finish with your decision artifact (data.ship = boolean)'],\n};\n\nfunction modelRoster(model: ModelService, workspaceDir: string): (item: { id: string; title: string }, attempt: number) => Role[] {\n  return (_item, attempt) =>\n    DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n      id: r.id,\n      title: r.title,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      authority: r.authority,\n      consumes: r.consumes,\n      produces: r.produces,\n      tools: buildRoleTools({\n        workspaceDir,\n        canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write',\n        allowedRoots: [''],\n      }),\n      brain: modelBrain(model, {\n        role: `${r.title} (attempt ${attempt})`,\n        mandate: r.mandate,\n        sequence: ROLE_SEQUENCE[r.id],\n        artifactHint: `Emit your \"${r.produces}\" artifact in data.`,\n      }),\n    }));\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster for offline plumbing tests (`--scripted`). The\n * implementer makes a trivial, verifiable edit and QA records the check it\n * really ran; the rest of the roster is evidence-only. It proves the delivery\n * path (clone → team → checks → branch → push → PR) without needing model keys.\n */\nfunction scriptedRoster(workspaceDir: string): (item: { id: string; title: string }, attempt: number) => Role[] {\n  const EDIT_PATH = 'FORGE-DELIVERY-PROBE.md';\n  const content = `# Forge delivery probe\\n\\nThis file was written by the Forge software company to prove the delivery path end to end.\\n`;\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const scripts: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n      implementer: [\n        { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: EDIT_PATH, content } },\n        { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'wrote the probe file', data: { files: { [EDIT_PATH]: content } } } },\n      ],\n      qa: [\n        { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n        { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'lint' } },\n        { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the checks', data: {} } },\n      ],\n      security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes', data: { clean: true } } }],\n      reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n      release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n      pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: probe the path', data: { items: ['probe file exists'] } } }],\n      architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'add one file', data: { files: [EDIT_PATH] } } }],\n    };\n    const script = scripts[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return () =>\n    DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n      id: r.id,\n      title: r.title,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      authority: r.authority,\n      consumes: r.consumes,\n      produces: r.produces,\n      tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write', allowedRoots: [''] }),\n      brain: brain(r.id),\n    }));\n}\n\nconst openPr: PullRequestOpener = async ({ target, head, base, title, body, token }) => {\n  const res = await fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${target}/pulls`, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'User-Agent': 'forge-company-deliver' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ title, head, base, body }),\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub PR API ${res.status}: ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 200)}`);\n  const data = (await res.json()) as { html_url: string; number: number };\n  return { url: data.html_url, number: data.number };\n};\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const args = process.argv.slice(2);\n  const scripted = args.includes('--scripted');\n  const valueFlags = new Set(['--expect-file', '--expect-contains', '--max-deletions']);\n  const flags: Record<string, string> = {};\n  const positional: string[] = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {\n    const a = args[i];\n    if (valueFlags.has(a)) {\n      flags[a] = args[i + 1] ?? '';\n      i += 1;\n    } else if (!a.startsWith('--')) {\n      positional.push(a);\n    }\n  }\n  const target = (positional[0] || '').trim();\n  const goal = positional.slice(1).join(' ').trim() || 'Address the audit findings.';\n  if (!repoPattern.test(target) || target.includes('..')) {\n    console.error('usage: npm run deliver -- [--scripted] [--expect-file <path>] [--expect-contains <text>] [--max-deletions <n>] owner/repo \"goal\"');\n    process.exitCode = 2;\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const expect: DeliveryExpectation[] = [];\n  if (flags['--expect-contains'] !== undefined) {\n    const maxDeletions = flags['--max-deletions'] !== undefined ? Number.parseInt(flags['--max-deletions'], 10) : undefined;\n    expect.push({\n      file: flags['--expect-file'] || undefined,\n      addedLinesContain: flags['--expect-contains'],\n      maxDeletions: Number.isNaN(maxDeletions as number) ? undefined : maxDeletions,\n    });\n  } else if (flags['--max-deletions'] !== undefined) {\n    const maxDeletions = Number.parseInt(flags['--max-deletions'], 10);\n    expect.push({ file: flags['--expect-file'] || undefined, maxDeletions: Number.isNaN(maxDeletions) ? undefined : maxDeletions });\n  }\n\n  const ctx = await fetchRepoContext(target);\n  console.log(`[deliver] ${ctx.target} @ ${ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}; goal: ${goal}`);\n\n  const model = scripted ? null : new ModelService();\n  if (model) {\n    const info = model.getProviderInfo();\n    console.log(`[deliver] model: ${info.primaryProvider}; Gemini fallback configured: ${info.fallbackConfigured}`);\n  } else {\n    console.log('[deliver] scripted roster (deterministic; proves the delivery path, not model quality)');\n  }\n\n  const workspaceDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'forge-deliver-'));\n  const branch = `forge/deliver-${ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}-${Date.now().toString(36)}`;\n\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: ctx.target,\n    goal,\n    commit: ctx.commit,\n    branch,\n    workspaceDir,\n    token: TOKEN,\n    rosterFor: model ? modelRoster(model, workspaceDir) : scriptedRoster(workspaceDir),\n    attemptsPerItem: Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_ATTEMPTS ?? '', 10) || 1),\n    push: process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_PUSH !== 'false',\n    expect,\n    openPr,\n  });\n\n  const outDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-delivery.json'), JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-delivery.md'), result.markdown + '\\n');\n\n  console.log('\\n--- COMPANY DELIVERY REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Status:', result.status, '|', result.reason);\n  console.log('Branch:', result.branch, '| head:', result.headCommit ?? '(none)');\n  console.log('Changed files:', result.changedFiles.join(', ') || '(none)');\n  for (const c of result.checks) console.log(`- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`);\n  if (result.prUrl) console.log('PR:', result.prUrl);\n  console.log('\\n' + result.markdown);\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error('[forge-company deliver] failed:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

function seedReadmeRepo(): { remoteDir: string; commit: string; readme: string } {
  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-readme-');
  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);
  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-readme-');
  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'readme-target', scripts: { test: 'node pass.js' } }, null, 2));
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\n');
  const readme = Array.from({ length: 242 }, (_, i) => `line ${i + 1} of the readme`).join('\n') + '\n';
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'README.md'), readme);

  git(['-c','user.name=seed','-c','user.email=seed@example.com','commit','-q','-m','seed'], seedDir);
  const commit = git(['rev-parse','HEAD'], seedDir);
  git(['push','-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);
  return { remoteDir, commit, readme };
}

 "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ? 'version: 123' : \"version: '1.1.0'\" } },\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? badContent : goodContent } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir: string, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}) {\n  return (_item: WorkItem, attempt: number): Role[] => {\n    const base = rosterFor(attempt, opts);\n    return base.map((r) => ({ ...r, tools: branch: 'forge/deliver-test',\n    workspaceDir: work,\n    token: 'unused-in-local-test',\n    remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    push:  "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ?   title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir:  "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ? 'version: 123' : \"version: '1.1.0'\" } },\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? badContent : goodContent } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir:
