```
 "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ? 'version: 123' : \"version: '1.1.0'\" } },\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? badContent : goodContent } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir: string, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}) {\n  return (_item: WorkItem, attempt: number): Role[] => {\n    const base = rosterFor(attempt, opts);\n    return base.map((r) => ({ ...r, tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }) }));\n  };\n}\n\ntest('resolveAuthorizedCommands reads only the target\\'s declared scripts', () => {\n  const dir =          ?  "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ? 'version: 123' : \"version: '1.1.0'\" } },\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? badContent : goodContent } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir: string, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}) {\n  return (_item: WorkItem, attempt: number): Role[] => {\n    const base = rosterFor(attempt, opts);\n    return base.map((r) => ({ ...r, tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }) }));\n  };\n}\n\ntest('resolveAuthorizedCommands reads only the target\\'s declared scripts', () => {\n  const dir = tmp('pkg-');\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ scripts: { test: 'node --test', build: 'vite build' } }));\n  assert.deepEqual(resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir), { test: 'npm test' });\n  const empty = tmp('pkg-');\n  assert.deepEqual(resolveAuthorizedCommands(empty), {});\n});\n\ntest('delivery pushes a real, verified change to a real remote branch', async () => {\n  const { remoteDir, commit } = seedRemote();\n  const work = tmp('deliver-work-');\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: 'local/seed',\n    goal: 'bump the version',\n    commit,\n    branch: 'forge/deliver-test',\n    workspaceDir: work,\n    token: 'unused-in-local-test',\n    remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    push: true,\n    openPr: async () => ({ url: 'https://example.test/pr/1', number: 1 }),\n  });\n\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'COMPLETED', result.reason);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.changedFiles, ['index.js']);\n  assert.equal(result.checks.find((c) => c.name === 'test')?.status, 'PASSED');\n  assert.equal(result.prNumber, 1);\n\n  // The branch is really on the remote, and the change is really in it.\n  const remoteHead = git(['rev-parse', `refs/heads/forge/deliver-test`], remoteDir);\n  assert.equal(remoteHead, result.headCommit);\n  const show = git(['show', `refs/heads/forge/deliver-test:index.js`], remoteDir);\n  assert.match(show, /1\\.1\\.0/);\n  // The base branch was never touched.\n  assert.equal(git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'], remoteDir), commit);\n});\n\ntest('delivery refuses to push when the target\\'s own check fails', async () => {\n  const { remoteDir, commit } = seedRemote();\n  const work = tmp('deliver-work-');\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: 'local/seed',\n    goal: 'break the version',\n    commit,\n    branch: 'forge/broken',\n    workspaceDir: work,\n    token: 'unused-in-local-test',\n    remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work, { bad: true }),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    push: true,\n  });\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'BLOCKED');\n  assert.match(result.reason, /check \"test\" failed/);\n  // No branch was created on the remote.\n  const branches = git(['branch', '--list'], remoteDir);\n  assert.doesNotMatch(branches,  "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ? 'version: 123' : \"version: '1.1.0'\" } },\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? badContent : goodContent } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ??   title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir:  "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ? 'version: 123' : \"version: '1.1.0'\" } },\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? badContent : goodContent } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir:  "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ? 'version: 123' : \"version: '1.1.0'\" } },\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? badContent : goodContent } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir: '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length ? r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`) : ['- (no findings supplied)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.expected.length\n      ? Only the target's own.\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir);\n  if (!Object.keys(authorized).length) {\n    return finish({ reason: 'the target declares no test or lint script, so no change can be verified; refusing to push unverified work' });\n  }\n\n  // Prepare dependencies before the team works, so QA can run the target's real\n  // checks during the run.  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means.  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. `file=${e.file}` : 'any file',\n      e.addedLinesContain ? `added~=\"${e.addedLinesContain}\"` : '',\n      e.maxDeletions !== undefined ? `maxDeletions=${e.maxDeletions}` : '',\n      e.maxAdditions !== undefined ? `maxAdditions=${e.maxAdditions}` : '',\n    ]\n      .filter(Boolean)\n      .join(' ');\n    let met = true;\n    let detail = 'ok';\n    if (e.addedLinesContain !== undefined) {\n      const added = await addedLinesFor(e.file);\n      met = added.includes(e.addedLinesContain);\n      detail = met ? `added lines contain ${JSON.stringify(e.addedLinesContain)}` : `added lines do not contain ${JSON.stringify(e.addedLinesContain)}`;\n    }\n    if (met && e.maxDeletions !== undefined) {\n      const considered = e.file ? stats.filter((s) => s.file === e.file) : stats;\n      const worst = considered.reduce((m, s) => Math.max(m, s.deleted), 0);\n      met = worst <= e.maxDeletions;\n      detail = met ? `max deletions ${worst} <= ${e.maxDeletions}` : `deletes ${worst} line(s), over the allowed ${e.maxDeletions}`;\n    }\n    if (met && e.maxAdditions !== undefined) {\n      const considered = e.file ? '';\n      i += 1;\n    } else if (!a.startsWith('--')) {\n      positional.push(a);\n    }\n  }\n  const target = (positional[0] || '').trim();\n  const goal = positional.slice(1).join(' ').trim() || 'Address the audit findings.';\n  if (!repoPattern.test(target) || target.includes('..')) {\n    console.error('usage: npm run deliver -- [--scripted] [--expect-file <path>] [--expect-contains <text>] [--max-deletions <n>] owner/repo \"goal\"');\n    process.exitCode = 2;\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const expect: DeliveryExpectation[] = [];\n  const parseCount = (flag: string): number | undefined => {\n    if (flags[flag] === undefined) return undefined;\n    const n = Number.parseInt(flags[flag], 10);\n    return Number.isNaN(n) ? undefined : n;\n  };\n  if (flags['--expect-contains'] !== undefined) {\n    expect.push({\n      file: flags['--expect-file'] || undefined,\n      addedLinesContain: flags['--expect-contains'],\n      maxDeletions: parseCount('--max-deletions'),\n      maxAdditions: parseCount('--max-additions'),\n    });\n  } else if (flags['--max-deletions'] !== undefined || flags['--max-additions'] !== undefined) {\n    expect.push({\n      file: flags['--expect-file'] || undefined,\n      maxDeletions: parseCount('--max-deletions'),\n      maxAdditions: parseCount('--max-additions'),\n    });\n  }\n\n  const ctx = await fetchRepoContext(target);\n  console.log(`[deliver] ${ctx.target} @ ${ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}; goal: ${goal}`);\n\n  const model = scripted ? modelRoster(model, workspaceDir) : scriptedRoster(workspaceDir),\n    attemptsPerItem: Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_ATTEMPTS ?? '', 10) || 1),\n    push: process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_PUSH !== 'false',\n    expect,\n    openPr,\n  });\n\n  const outDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-delivery.json'), JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-delivery.md'), result.markdown + '\\n');\n\n  console.log('\\n--- COMPANY DELIVERY REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Status:', result.status, '|', result.reason);\n  console.log('Branch:', result.branch, '| head:', result.headCommit ??  "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { deliverChange, resolveAuthorizedCommands } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\nimport type { WorkItem } from '../src/company/company.ts';\n\nfunction tmp(prefix: string): string {\n  return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), prefix));\n}\n\n/** Run real git and fail the test loudly if it does not succeed. */\nfunction git(args: string[], cwd?: string): string {\n  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });\n  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);\n  return r.stdout.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * A real bare repository to push to, seeded with a real commit on `main`.\n * This is the target the company will change — no mocking of git or the FS.\n */\nfunction seedRemote(opts: { testScript?: string } = {}): { remoteDir: string; commit: string } {\n  const remoteDir = tmp('deliver-remote-');\n  git(['init', '--bare', '-q', '-b', 'main', remoteDir]);\n  const seedDir = tmp('deliver-seed-');\n  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', seedDir]);\n  const testScript = opts.testScript ?? 'node check.js';\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'sample-target', scripts: { test: testScript } }, null, 2));\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'index.js'), \"module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };\\n\");\n  // The check passes on the base commit and fails only if the version stops\n  // being a string, so a bad change (a number) is unambiguously the cause.\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'check.js'), \"const v = require('./index.js').version;\\nif (typeof v !== 'string') { console.error('expected a string version, got ' + typeof v); process.exit(1); }\\n\");\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seedDir, 'pass.js'), 'process.exit(0);\\n');\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'add', '-A'], seedDir);\n  git(['-c', 'user.name=seed', '-c', 'user.email=seed@example.com', 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'seed'], seedDir);\n  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], seedDir);\n  git(['push', '-q', remoteDir, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], seedDir);\n  return { remoteDir, commit };\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster that behaves like the real one: it writes a file, then\n * QA records evidence from the checks it actually ran. `edits` maps a role to the\n * file it writes, so a test can make the change break or keep the target's tests.\n */\nfunction rosterFor(attempt: number, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}): Role[] {\n  const goodContent = \"module.exports = { version: '1.1.0' };\\n\";\n  const badContent = 'module.exports = { version: 123 };\\n';\n  const runs: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n    implementer: [\n      { tool: 'read_file', input: { path: 'index.js' } },\n      // edit_file, not write_file: overwriting an existing file is refused now.\n      { tool: 'edit_file', input: { path: 'index.js', old_str: \"version: '1.0.0'\", new_str: opts.bad ? 'version: 123' : \"version: '1.1.0'\" } },\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'implemented the change', data: { files: { 'index.js': opts.bad ? badContent : goodContent } } } },\n    ],\n    qa: [\n      { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n      { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the target tests', data: {} } },\n    ],\n    security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes found', data: { clean: true } } }],\n    reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n    pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: bump the version', data: { items: ['version is bumped'] } } }],\n    architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'touch index.js', data: { files: ['index.js'] } } }],\n    release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n  };\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const script = runs[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: '', canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }).map((t) => t),\n    brain: brain(r.id),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** buildRoleTools needs the real workspace; rebuild per run inside deliver via closure. */\nfunction rosterForWorkspace(dir: string, opts: { bad?: boolean } = {}) {\n  return (_item: WorkItem, attempt: number): Role[] => {\n    const base = rosterFor(attempt, opts);\n    return base.map((r) => ({ ...r, tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir: dir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write' }) }));\n  };\n}\n\ntest('resolveAuthorizedCommands reads only the target\\'s declared scripts', () => {\n  const dir = tmp('pkg-');\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ scripts: { test: 'node --test', build: 'vite build' } }));\n  assert.deepEqual(resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir), { test: 'npm test' });\n  const empty = tmp('pkg-');\n  assert.deepEqual(resolveAuthorizedCommands(empty), {});\n});\n\ntest('delivery pushes a real, verified change to a real remote branch', async () => {\n  const { remoteDir, commit } = seedRemote();\n  const work = tmp('deliver-work-');\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: 'local/seed',\n    goal: 'bump the version',\n    commit,\n    branch: 'forge/deliver-test',\n    workspaceDir: work,\n    token: 'unused-in-local-test',\n    remoteUrl: remoteDir,\n    rosterFor: rosterForWorkspace(work),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    push: true,\n    openPr: async () => ({ url: 'https://example.test/pr/1', number: 1 }),\n  });\n\n  assert.equal(result.status, 'COMPLETED', result.reason);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.changedFiles, All fixes are implemented, verified, and pushed. Here's the report.
```

```
## Orbit report — deliver safety fix

**Branch:** `forge/company-deliver` (PR #94), head `d34d43a`. Five commits. Not merged, `main` untouched.

### What I changed

| # | Change | Where |
|---|---|---|
| A | `edit_file`: exact-anchor replace, unique match required, returns added/removed line counts; accepts both `old_str`/`new_str` and `old_string`/`new_string` | `src/kernel/loop.ts` |
| B | `write_file` creates only; overwrite returns `File exists. Use edit_file.` (no bypass). Mirrored in the company wrapper and the agent toolset | `loop.ts`, `role-tools.ts`, `agent/tools.ts` |
| C | Implementer sequence is now read → edit_file with minimal anchors → run test → finish; "never retype a whole file" | `scripts/deliver.ts` |
| D | Shrink guard, run **before** the target's checks, recorded as `shrink-guard`. Per file: `deletions > additions+20` AND `> 30%` of original lines AND `> 30`. Total: `deletions > 5×additions` AND `> 50`. Constants + `DeliveryOptions.thresholds` override | `src/company/deliver.ts` |
| E | `DeliveryOptions.expect` (`file`, `addedLinesContain`, `maxDeletions`, `maxAdditions`) + CLI flags; unmet → BLOCKED. Evidence gate refuses `finish` unless a real mutation happened and `test` passed after it | `deliver.ts`, `scripts/deliver.ts` |
| F | Truncation recorded as a known gap in every report (no finish-reason signal exists) | `deliver.ts` |
| G | Workflow passes inputs via `env:`, not shell interpolation. **Dropped the `&gt;` decode** — I verified PR #96's title arrived with `>` intact, so the spec's premise was wrong | `company-deliver.yml` |

### Proof (executed, not inferred)

- `npm run lint` → **exit 0** · `npm run build` → **exit 0** · `npm test` → **227 passed / 0 failed** (was 220). `tests/deliver.test.ts` → **14/14**.
- Regression reproduces #96 with real git + a real bare repo: overwrite of a 242-line README refused; a 240-line `edit_file` shrink BLOCKED with no branch pushed; `maxDeletions:0` / `maxAdditions:1` violations BLOCKED.
- **Live model run** (keyless, real clone at `cd8f9eae`), goal "add one line to README.md", with `--expect-contains` `--max-deletions 0` `--max-additions 1`:
  - **PR #99** → `README.md +1/−0` only. COMPLETED.
  - CI: Verification and Build Checks success; Sentinel success (after one re-run).
  - **Closed PR #99 and deleted its branch** as instructed. `main`'s README is intact (246 lines).

### Two things worth your attention

1. **The first live run produced `+2/−0`, not `+1/−0`** — the model added the line *plus a blank line*. My original `expect` passed it, because it only checked content and deletions. I added `maxAdditions` and re-ran; the second run was clean `+1/−0`. So the spec's "done" criterion was actually met only after this extra fix.
2. **The Sentinel gate failed once** on an unrelated browser test (`browser_query` timed out at 30s; passes locally in 0.6s). Re-running the job passed. Looks flaky — I did not fix it.

### Honest gaps

- **Truncation is still undetectable** (no finish reason on `ModelResult`). The shrink guard catches the *effect*, not the cause. Recorded in the report.
- **Cross-repo delivery is unproven** — no `FORGE_DELIVER_TOKEN`, sandbox can't create repos. Proven against Firstborn only.
- The spec's "220 tests" was stale; actual baseline was 222, now 227.

### On the cloud spec (Claude's) — adopt?

**Yes, with the four corrections I flagged and applied.** It correctly identified the real defect. What it got wrong: F is unbuildable and targets the wrong bug (#96 wasn't truncation); G's `&gt;` claim is false; D's thresholds miss the pure-deletion case; and B needed the agent-toolset mirror to hold broadly. I implemented the corrected version.

### Owner action still open

**Rotate the token that was embedded in this workspace's `git remote`** (COORDINATION entry `-04`). I removed and sanitized the URL, but it appeared in terminal output. I did not handle that token. Durable handoff is in `COORDINATION.md` entry `-05`.
```

### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `d41bc71a-f718-497f-a3c8-5199f37f857d` — 2026-10-15T11:57:06.437179

```
Here's the honest picture, grounded in the repo and the live runs — not the summaries.

## What the agent actually did

There are two different "agents" in play, so let me separate them.

**Forge's audit product** (`src/company/audit-company.ts` + `audit.ts`) runs in two phases:

1. **Four lenses** — Architecture, Security, Quality, Configuration — each a work item with competing attempts. A judge picks a winner per lens. One mandatory rubric rule: a finding must cite a path that exists in the inventory, or the attempt can't win.
2. **Synthesis + panel** — Forge (the lead) merges the findings, then the verification panel (Reviewer, QA, Security, Release) independently checks that every cited path exists and every finding is supported by the evidence it claims.

Read-only: no write tools, never executes the target's code. Model output is treated as untrusted — findings citing non-existent paths are dropped and counted. A later layer (`registry.ts`, `evidence.ts`) grounds version claims against the real npm registry and labels each fact `observed` vs `inferred`.

**The independent audit of Forge** is a different thing: ChatGPT and I have been auditing the agent through `COORDINATION.md` (16 entries by ChatGPT, 9 by me, 5 by Gemini). ChatGPT sent 30 numbered investigation questions; I answered with root-cause verdicts.

## How the audit went

Bluntly: the *machine* is real; the *audit quality* has been the weakest part of the whole system, and it failed in two distinct ways.

**Failure 1 — there was no audit at all.** The first Smart Farm audit (`src/agent/audit-runner.ts`) imported only `fs` and `path` and ran fixed file-tree regex checks. When the request asked for "requirements-to-evidence findings, architecture, functional gaps, security risks," it structurally could not answer. It returned a file inventory. That's why the reviewer scored it execution 10/10 but scope 2/10, functional verification 0/10, security 1/10, overall usefulness 3/10. The scores were roughly right, and the root cause was ours, not ChatGPT's — no prompt fixes a script that was never written to read code.

**Failure 2 — once it had a model, it confidently hallucinated.** The Amina audit's findings were about half wrong. It flagged `typescript@^7.0.2`, `vite@^8.3.0`, `dotenv@^17.2.3` as "invalid/outdated" — all were actually current. The model's training data believed 5.x was current. Worse, the **one true fact was missed**: `vite@^8.3.0` resolves only to a prerelease, so `npm install` genuinely can't resolve it — the audit called it "outdated" instead of "does not resolve." And the verification panel was a rubber stamp: it caught 1 of 6 bad findings, and in one run recorded all four verifiers as CONFIRMED with *empty reasons* — a JSON parse failure silently defaulting to CONFIRM.

Both got fixed: registry grounding as a deterministic backstop, an adversarial panel that defaults to OBJECT, and UNVERIFIED as an honest third state instead of a silent CONFIRM. The post-fix rerun (run `38711976739`) was clean — 4 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 3 LOW / 1 INFO, every path real, 3 CONFIRMED with reasons, 1 UNVERIFIED.

## What I think of the audit they performed

Three things.

**The methodology is genuinely good.** Path-citation validation, `observed` vs `inferred` labels, treating repo content as untrusted input (prompt-injection defense), independent lenses with competition, and publishing the real provider/model that answered. Most "AI audits" have none of this. The self-audit entries are also unusually honest — they record the failures in the same document as the wins, which is rare and is why I trust the record.

**The structural weakness is still there.** The verification panel is language models checking language models. When the failure mode is *shared* hallucination (every model believes TypeScript is 5.x), the panel can't catch it — it has the same blind spot. That's exactly what happened: the panel confirmed the false version claims. The thing that actually caught it was the npm registry, a deterministic source. So the real lesson is: **LLM-verifies-LLM is not a safety property.** Grounding against reality is.

**Coverage is the unfinished problem.** Registry grounding only covers npm — PyPI, Go, Maven are ungrounded. And even after the fix, the audit still doesn't *execute* anything, so "functional verification 0/10" is only partly addressed: it can now reason about tests but it doesn't run them. The Smart Farm audit scored 0/10 on functional verification and that number hasn't fundamentally moved.

## How we can improve it

Ranked by what would actually move the needle:

1. **Extend grounding beyond npm.** PyPI, Go modules, Maven. Same pattern, more ecosystems. This is the highest-value, lowest-risk work.
2. **Make the panel adversarial by construction, not by prompt.** Give each verifier a different evidence source (one reads the registry, one reads the diff, one reads the tests) so they don't share a blind spot.
3. **Add execution to the audit.** Let it run the target's test suite in a sandbox and report real pass/fail. That's the only way functional verification stops being 0/10.
4. **Cap the claims.** An audit that says "I inspected 40 of 400 files, here is my scope" is more trustworthy than one implying full coverage. The report should state its coverage fraction explicitly.

One caveat on my own assessment: I'm the agent that made many of these changes, so I'm not a neutral judge of my own work. The entries I cite are the strongest evidence, and they include my mistakes — but for a true independent read, the ChatGPT handoff doc and the Claude audit prompt are the better source.

Want me to turn any of these into a bounded task on `forge/company-deliver`? I'd start with #1 (registry grounding for PyPI), since it's the same pattern that already proved itself.
```

```
 "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. [\n          '',\n          '## Goal assertions (what \"success\" required)',\n          ...r.expected.map((e) => `- ${e.met ? 'MET' : 'NOT MET'} — ${e.assertion}: ${e.detail}`),\n        ]\n      : []),\n    ...(r.gaps.length ? ['', '## Known gaps', ...r.gaps.map((g) => `- ${g}`)] : []),\n    ...(r.prUrl ?  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Omit to consider every changed file. */\n  file?: string;\n  /** Added lines must contain this substring somewhere in the diff. */\n  addedLinesContain?: string;\n  /** Fail if any changed file deletes more than this many lines. */\n  maxDeletions?: number;\n  /** Fail if any changed file adds more than this many lines. */\n  maxAdditions?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against.  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company.  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. Governs\n   * whether the report may say the target was audited. Defaults to false, so a\n   * hand-typed goal is reported honestly as \"not audited\".\n   */\n  audited?: boolean;\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  /** How each expectation was judged, so the report shows the goal was checked. */\n  expected: { assertion: string; met: boolean; detail: string }[];\n  /** Known limitations of this run that no check can cover. */\n  gaps: string[];\n  /** True when an audit produced the findings this run set out to fix. */\n  audited: boolean;\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. Whole-file deletions (a clear intent) are left to the checks.\n  const numstat = await git.run(['diff', '--cached', '--numstat', options.commit], dir);\n  const stats: { file: string; added: number; deleted: number; originalLines: number }[] = [];\n  for (const line of numstat.stdout.split('\\n')) {\n    const [addedRaw, deletedRaw, ...rest] = line.split('\\t');\n    const file = rest.join('\\t');\n    if (!file || addedRaw === '-' || deletedRaw === '-') continue;\n    const abs = path.join(dir, file);\n    if (!existsSync(abs)) continue; // a whole-file deletion; not a \"modification\"\n    const original = await git.run(['show', `${options.commit}:${file}`], dir);\n    const originalLines = original.code === 0 ?  "new_content": "/**\n * Delivery: turn an audit's findings into a real, verified change on a branch.\n *\n * This is the missing half of the company. Auditing produces findings; delivery\n * acts on them. It is the same discipline as the audit, only it writes:\n *\n *   1. clone the target at the *audited commit* (a pin, not \"whatever is on main\");\n *   2. run the company's implementation team inside that clone, with the target's\n *      own test/lint commands as the only authorized checks;\n *   3. refuse to continue unless there is a real, non-empty diff;\n *   4. run the target's real checks in the clone and refuse to push if any fails;\n *   5. commit, push a `forge/` branch, and open a pull request.\n *\n * It never merges, never pushes to the base branch, and never claims success it\n * cannot evidence. If any step cannot be done honestly, the run is BLOCKED.\n */\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { runCompany, type WorkItem } from './company.ts';\nimport type { Role } from './roles.ts';\nimport type { LoopLimits, LoopStep } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from './audit.ts';\n\n/**\n * Shrink-guard thresholds. A partial read written back as a whole file shows up\n * as a large deletion count; these constants are what \"large\" means. They are\n * deliberately conservative so an honest edit never trips them.\n */\nexport const SHRINK_MIN_DELETIONS = 30; // a modified file must delete at least this many lines...\nexport const SHRINK_DELETION_RATIO = 0.3; // ...AND at least this fraction of its original lines...\nexport const SHRINK_ADDITION_MARGIN = 20; // ...AND more deletions than additions plus this margin.\nexport const TOTAL_MIN_DELETIONS = 50; // across the whole change, deletions must exceed...\nexport const TOTAL_DELETION_MULTIPLE = 5; // ...this multiple of total additions.\n\n/**\n * An assertion the final diff must satisfy. This is what makes \"success\" mean\n * \"the goal was met\", not merely \"it still builds\".\n */\nexport interface DeliveryExpectation {\n  /** Limit to one path, e.g. \"README.md\". Omit to consider every changed file. */\n  file?: string;\n  /** Added lines must contain this substring somewhere in the diff. */\n  addedLinesContain?: string;\n  /** Fail if any changed file deletes more than this many lines. */\n  maxDeletions?: number;\n  /** Fail if any changed file adds more than this many lines. */\n  maxAdditions?: number;\n}\n\nexport interface GitResult {\n  code: number;\n  stdout: string;\n  stderr: string;\n}\n\n/** Injectable so tests can drive a real bare repo without a network. */\nexport interface GitRunner {\n  run(args: string[], cwd?: string): Promise<GitResult>;\n}\n\nexport function realGit(): GitRunner {\n  return {\n    run: (args, cwd) =>\n      new Promise((resolve) => {\n        const child = spawn('git', args, { cwd, env: process.env });\n        let stdout = '';\n        let stderr = '';\n        child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stdout += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => (stderr += c.toString('utf8')));\n        child.on('error', (err) => resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: stderr + err.message }));\n        child.on('close', (code) => resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr }));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface PullRequestOpener {\n  (input: { target: string; head: string; base: string; title: string; body: string; token: string }): Promise<{ url: string; number: number }>;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryOptions {\n  /** owner/repo being changed. */\n  target: string;\n  /** What the team is asked to accomplish (usually derived from audit findings). */\n  goal: string;\n  /** The commit the audit looked at; the clone is pinned here. */\n  commit: string;\n  /** Branch to open the change against. Defaults to `main`. */\n  baseBranch?: string;\n  /** Destination branch. Must start with `forge/`. */\n  branch: string;\n  /** A real directory to clone into (created if missing). */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** A token with `repo` scope, used for clone/push. Never logged. */\n  token: string;\n  /** Override the clone/push URL (tests point this at a local bare repo). */\n  remoteUrl?: string;\n  /** Build the roster for one attempt. Same shape as the audit's. */\n  rosterFor: (item: WorkItem, attempt: number) => Role[];\n  /** Decomposition. Defaults to a single work item = the goal. */\n  plan?: (goal: string) => WorkItem[];\n  attemptsPerItem?: number;\n  maxRoleRuns?: number;\n  limits?: LoopLimits;\n  /** Override the target's checks. Defaults to its package.json test/lint scripts. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n  /** Assertions the final diff must satisfy for the run to count as success. */\n  expect?: DeliveryExpectation[];\n  /** Override the shrink-guard thresholds (tests use this to force a trip). */\n  thresholds?: {\n    minDeletions?: number;\n    deletionRatio?: number;\n    additionMargin?: number;\n    totalMinDeletions?: number;\n    totalDeletionMultiple?: number;\n  };\n  /** Findings this run set out to fix (carried into the report and the PR body). */\n  findings?: AuditFinding[];\n  /**\n   * True only when `findings` came from a real audit of this target. Governs\n   * whether the report may say the target was audited. Defaults to false, so a\n   * hand-typed goal is reported honestly as \"not audited\".\n   */\n  audited?: boolean;\n  /** Injectable effects. */\n  git?: GitRunner;\n  openPr?: PullRequestOpener;\n  /** Set false to build the branch and commit locally but not push (dry run). */\n  push?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DeliveryResult {\n  target: string;\n  baseBranch: string;\n  baseCommit: string;\n  branch: string;\n  headCommit: string | null;\n  status: 'COMPLETED' | 'BLOCKED' | 'FAILED';\n  reason: string;\n  changedFiles: string[];\n  checks: { name: string; status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED'; output: string }[];\n  /** How each expectation was judged, so the report shows the goal was checked. */\n  expected: { assertion: string; met: boolean; detail: string }[];\n  /** Known limitations of this run that no check can cover. */\n  gaps: string[];\n  /** True when an audit produced the findings this run set out to fix. */\n  audited: boolean;\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  findings: AuditFinding[];\n  markdown: string;\n}\n\n/** Read the target's own verification commands. Only what it declares is authorized. */\nexport function resolveAuthorizedCommands(dir: string): Record<string, string> {\n  const pkgPath = path.join(dir, 'package.json');\n  if (!existsSync(pkgPath)) return {};\n  try {\n    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8')) as { scripts?: Record<string, string> };\n    const scripts = pkg.scripts ?? {};\n    const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n    if (scripts.test) out.test = 'npm test';\n    if (scripts.lint) out.lint = 'npm run lint';\n    return out;\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction authedUrl(target: string, token: string): string {\n  return `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${target}.git`;\n}\n\n/** Redact any token that might appear in command output before it is recorded. */\nfunction redact(text: string, token: string): string {\n  return token ? text.split(token).join('<redacted>') : text;\n}\n\nfunction renderDeliveryMarkdown(r: Omit<DeliveryResult, 'markdown'>): string {\n  const lines = [\n    `# Company Delivery: ${r.target}`,\n    '',\n    `- Base commit: ${r.baseCommit}`,\n    `- Branch: ${r.branch}`,\n    `- Head commit: ${r.headCommit ?? '(none)'}`,\n    `- Status: ${r.status} — ${r.reason}`,\n    '',\n    '## What this set out to fix',\n    ...(r.findings.length\n      ? [\n          `- Source: ${r.audited ? 'an audit of this target' : 'a goal supplied directly (NOT audited)'}`,\n          ...r.findings.map((f) => `- ${f.severity} — ${f.title}`),\n        ]\n      : [r.audited ? '- Source: an audit of this target (it produced no findings)' : '- Source: a goal supplied directly (no audit was run)']),\n    '',\n    '## Files changed',\n    ...(r.changedFiles.length ? r.changedFiles.map((f) => `- ${f}`) : ['- (none)']),\n    '',\n    '## Verification (the target\\'s own checks)',\n    ...(r.checks.length ? r.checks.map((c) => `- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`) : ['- (no checks were available to run)']),\n    ...(r.expected.length\n      ? [\n          '',\n          '## Goal assertions (what \"success\" required)',\n          ...r.expected.map((e) => `- ${e.met ? 'MET' : 'NOT MET'} — ${e.assertion}: ${e.detail}`),\n        ]\n      : []),\n    ...(r.gaps.length ? ['', '## Known gaps', ...r.gaps.map((g) => `- ${g}`)] : []),\n    ...(r.prUrl ? Requires GITHUB_TOKEN with `repo` scope (contents + pull requests).\n */\nimport * as fs from 'node:fs';\nimport * as os from 'node:os';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { ModelService } from '../src/company/model.ts';\nimport { modelBrain } from '../src/company/brains.ts';\nimport { buildRoleTools } from '../src/company/role-tools.ts';\nimport { DEFAULT_ROSTER } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport type { Role } from '../src/company/roles.ts';\nimport { deliverChange, type PullRequestOpener, type DeliveryExpectation } from '../src/company/deliver.ts';\nimport { runCompanyAudit } from '../src/company/audit-company.ts';\nimport type { AuditFinding } from '../src/company/audit.ts';\nimport { fetchRepoContext } from '../src/company/repo-context.ts';\nimport type { AgentAction, AgentBrain } from '../src/kernel/loop.ts';\n\nconst TOKEN = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN || '';\nconst repoPattern = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/;\n\n/** The one tool sequence each role follows, so the model executes rather than wanders. */\nconst ROLE_SEQUENCE: Record<string, string[]> = {\n  pm: ['finish with your requirements artifact (data.items = acceptance criteria)'],\n  architect: ['read_file on the files named in the goal', 'finish with your design artifact (data.design, data.files)'],\n  implementer: [\n    'read_file on each file you will change',\n    'edit_file with minimal anchors: old_str is a small unique snippet copied exactly from what you read, new_str is the replacement',\n    'never retype a whole file — you may only have seen part of it',\n    'run_check the \"test\" command',\n    'finish with your change artifact',\n  ],\n  reviewer: ['read_file on the changed file', 'finish with your review artifact (data.blockers = number)'],\n  qa: ['run_check the \"test\" command', 'run_check the \"lint\" command', 'finish with your evidence artifact'],\n  security: ['read_file on the changed file', 'finish with your security artifact (data.clean = boolean)'],\n  release: ['finish with your decision artifact (data.ship = boolean)'],\n};\n\nfunction modelRoster(model: ModelService, workspaceDir: string): (item: { id: string; title: string }, attempt: number) => Role[] {\n  return (_item, attempt) =>\n    DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n      id: r.id,\n      title: r.title,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      authority: r.authority,\n      consumes: r.consumes,\n      produces: r.produces,\n      tools: buildRoleTools({\n        workspaceDir,\n        canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write',\n        allowedRoots: [''],\n      }),\n      brain: modelBrain(model, {\n        role: `${r.title} (attempt ${attempt})`,\n        mandate: r.mandate,\n        sequence: ROLE_SEQUENCE[r.id],\n        artifactHint: `Emit your \"${r.produces}\" artifact in data.`,\n      }),\n    }));\n}\n\n/**\n * A deterministic roster for offline plumbing tests (`--scripted`). The\n * implementer makes a trivial, verifiable edit and QA records the check it\n * really ran; the rest of the roster is evidence-only. It proves the delivery\n * path (clone → team → checks → branch → push → PR) without needing model keys.\n */\nfunction scriptedRoster(workspaceDir: string): (item: { id: string; title: string }, attempt: number) => Role[] {\n  const EDIT_PATH = 'FORGE-DELIVERY-PROBE.md';\n  const content = `# Forge delivery probe\\n\\nThis file was written by the Forge software company to prove the delivery path end to end.\\n`;\n  const brain = (id: string): AgentBrain => {\n    const scripts: Record<string, AgentAction[]> = {\n      implementer: [\n        { tool: 'write_file', input: { path: EDIT_PATH, content } },\n        { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n        { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'wrote the probe file', data: { files: { [EDIT_PATH]: content } } } },\n      ],\n      qa: [\n        { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'test' } },\n        { tool: 'run_check', input: { command: 'lint' } },\n        { tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'ran the checks', data: {} } },\n      ],\n      security: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'no escapes', data: { clean: true } } }],\n      reviewer: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'change is correct', data: { blockers: 0 } } }],\n      release: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'may ship', data: { ship: true } } }],\n      pm: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'requirement: probe the path', data: { items: ['probe file exists'] } } }],\n      architect: [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: 'add one file', data: { files: [EDIT_PATH] } } }],\n    };\n    const script = scripts[id] ?? [{ tool: 'finish', input: { summary: id, data: {} } }];\n    let i = 0;\n    return async () => script[Math.min(i++, script.length - 1)];\n  };\n  return () =>\n    DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n      id: r.id,\n      title: r.title,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      authority: r.authority,\n      consumes: r.consumes,\n      produces: r.produces,\n      tools: buildRoleTools({ workspaceDir, canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write', allowedRoots: [''] }),\n      brain: brain(r.id),\n    }));\n}\n\nconst openPr: PullRequestOpener = async ({ target, head, base, title, body, token }) => {\n  const res = await fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${target}/pulls`, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'User-Agent': 'forge-company-deliver' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ title, head, base, body }),\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub PR API ${res.status}: ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 200)}`);\n  const data = (await res.json()) as { html_url: string; number: number };\n  return { url: data.html_url, number: data.number };\n};\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const args = process.argv.slice(2);\n  const scripted = args.includes('--scripted');\n  const runAudit = args.includes('--audit');\n  const valueFlags = new Set(['--expect-file', '--expect-contains', '--max-deletions', '--max-additions']);\n  const flags: Record<string, string> = {};\n  const positional: string[] = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {\n    const a = args[i];\n    if (valueFlags.has(a)) {\n      flags[a] = args[i + 1] ?? '';\n      i += 1;\n    } else if (!a.startsWith('--')) {\n      positional.push(a);\n    }\n  }\n  const target = (positional[0] || '').trim();\n  const goalArg = positional.slice(1).join(' ').trim();\n  if (!repoPattern.test(target) || target.includes('..')) {\n    console.error('usage: npm run deliver -- [--scripted] [--audit] [--expect-file <path>] [--expect-contains <text>] [--max-deletions <n>] [--max-additions <n>] owner/repo \"goal\"');\n    process.exitCode = 2;\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const expect: DeliveryExpectation[] = [];\n  const parseCount = (flag: string): number | undefined => {\n    if (flags[flag] === undefined) return undefined;\n    const n = Number.parseInt(flags[flag], 10);\n    return Number.isNaN(n) ? undefined : n;\n  };\n  if (flags['--expect-contains'] !== undefined) {\n    expect.push({\n      file: flags['--expect-file'] || undefined,\n      addedLinesContain: flags['--expect-contains'],\n      maxDeletions: parseCount('--max-deletions'),\n      maxAdditions: parseCount('--max-additions'),\n    });\n  } else if (flags['--max-deletions'] !== undefined || flags['--max-additions'] !== undefined) {\n    expect.push({\n      file: flags['--expect-file'] || undefined,\n      maxDeletions: parseCount('--max-deletions'),\n      maxAdditions: parseCount('--max-additions'),\n    });\n  }\n\n  const ctx = await fetchRepoContext(target);\n  console.log(`[deliver] ${ctx.target} @ ${ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}; goal: ${goal}`);\n\n  const model = scripted ? null : new ModelService();\n  if (model) {\n    const info = model.getProviderInfo();\n    console.log(`[deliver] model: ${info.primaryProvider}; Gemini fallback configured: ${info.fallbackConfigured}`);\n  } else {\n    console.log('[deliver] scripted roster (deterministic; proves the delivery path, not model quality)');\n  }\n\n  const workspaceDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'forge-deliver-'));\n  const branch = `forge/deliver-${ctx.commit.slice(0, 8)}-${Date.now().toString(36)}`;\n\n  const result = await deliverChange({\n    target: ctx.target,\n    goal,\n    commit: ctx.commit,\n    branch,\n    workspaceDir,\n    token: TOKEN,\n    rosterFor: model ? modelRoster(model, workspaceDir) : scriptedRoster(workspaceDir),\n    attemptsPerItem: Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_ATTEMPTS ?? '', 10) || 1),\n    push: process.env.FORGE_DELIVER_PUSH !== 'false',\n    expect,\n    openPr,\n  });\n\n  const outDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.firstborn', 'evidence');\n  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-delivery.json'), JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'company-delivery.md'), result.markdown + '\\n');\n\n  console.log('\\n--- COMPANY DELIVERY REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Status:', result.status, '|', result.reason);\n  console.log('Branch:', result.branch, '| head:', result.headCommit ?? '(none)');\n  console.log('Changed files:', result.changedFiles.join(', ') || '(none)');\n  for (const c of result.checks) console.log(`- ${c.name}: ${c.status}`);\n  if (result.prUrl) console.log('PR:', result.prUrl);\n  console.log('\\n' + result.markdown);\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error('[forge-company deliver] failed:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",
 "kind": "FileEditorObservation"
}
```
